grammar.title: 打招呼和介绍自己 (Greetings and Self-introduction)

examples.en: What would you like for breakfast?
examples.cn: 你早餐想吃什么？
你喜欢茶还是咖啡？
examples.en: Do you like tea or coffee?

grammar.explain:
这两个问句都用于询问对方的偏好或意愿，但在语境和含义上有所区别。

**Do you like...?** 用于询问对方是否普遍喜欢某种事物，表达的是一种长期的偏好或习惯。答案通常是肯定或否定的。

**What would you like...?** 是 “What would you like to have/eat/drink...?” 的简略形式，用于礼貌地询问对方此时此地想要什么，表达的是一种即时的选择或请求。它通常用于点餐、提供选择或询问对方的需求。答案通常是具体的选择。

grammar.title: I have a/an + [身体部位] + ache / I have a + [症状]
grammar.explain:
这个句型用于表达身体不适或疾病。它可以用来表示“我感到……痛”或“我患有……”。

- 当你感到某个部位疼痛时，可以使用“I have a/an + 身体部位 + ache”。例如，headache（头痛）、stomachache（胃痛）、backache（背痛）。
- 当你表达其他症状时，可以使用“I have a + 症状”。例如，a fever（发烧）、a sore throat（喉咙痛）、a cold（感冒）。

grammar.title: I feel + [形容词] / I don't feel + [形容词]
grammar.explain:
这个句型用来描述你的感受。你可以用它来表达“我感觉……”或者“我感觉不……”。

- 当你感觉不舒服时，常用形容词有 sick, unwell, tired, dizzy。
- 当你感觉好转时，常用形容词有 better, well, good, great。

Best,
Mei

reading.en: Last night was Halloween — my first one. Mark bought a big orange pumpkin from the store. He put it on the table.
reading.cn: 昨晚是万圣节——我的第一个万圣节。马克从商店买了一个橙色的大南瓜。他把它放在桌上。
reading.note: 💡 Halloween / pumpkin / put — past simple of put (no change!)

reading.en: Mark cut the pumpkin. We took out the seeds. Sara made eyes and a mouth. Tom said, "Now it is a jack-o'-lantern!"
reading.cn: 马克切开南瓜。我们把瓜瓤掏出来。莎拉做了眼睛和嘴。汤姆说："现在它是个杰克灯了！"
reading.note: 💡 cut / seeds / mouth / jack-o'-lantern — Halloween 必备词

reading.cn: 我装扮成一个鬼——一块白床单，挖两个洞当眼睛。孩子们大笑："你看起来好搞笑！"
reading.note: 💡 dressed up / ghost / sheet / hole — basic costume vocab

reading.cn: 七点钟，门铃响了。三个穿着戏服的小孩站在门口。他们大喊："不给糖就捣蛋！"
reading.note: rang (ring 不规则过去) / stood (stand 不规则过去) / Trick or treat — Halloween 习俗

reading.en: Sara handed each kid two pieces of candy. One little girl looked at me. She said in Chinese, "你好!" Her mom is from Shanghai.
reading.cn: 莎拉给每个孩子发了两颗糖。一个小女孩看着我，用中文说："你好！"她妈妈来自上海。
reading.note: 💡 handed / candy / piece — past simple in narrative

reading.en: I gave her three extra pieces. I felt so happy. America is big — but home is everywhere if you look.
reading.cn: 我多给了她三颗糖。我感到非常开心。美国很大——但只要你愿意看，家在到处。
reading.note: 💡 extra / everywhere — gave (give 不规则过去) / closing reflection

reading.en: Today in class, Ms. Park asks, "What's your favorite season?"
reading.cn: 今天课上，Park 老师问："你最喜欢哪个季节？"
reading.note: 💡 favorite / season — What's = What is

reading.en: Hyun-Woo says, "I love summer. I love the beach."
reading.cn: Hyun-Woo 说："我爱夏天。我爱海滩。"
reading.note: love + 季节 / love + 名词 — 复用 L1#14 角色

reading.en: Lucia says, "I love spring. The flowers are beautiful in Brazil."
reading.cn: Lucia 说："我爱春天。巴西的花开得很美。"
reading.note: 💡 spring / flower — beautiful (复用 L1#5)

reading.en: It's my turn. I say, "My favorite is autumn — fall in America. The Beijing leaves were red and gold."
reading.cn: 轮到我了。我说："我最喜欢秋天——美国说 fall。北京的树叶是红色和金色的。"
reading.note: 💡 autumn / fall / leaves / red / gold — 美式 fall = 英式 autumn / were 复用过去时

reading.en: Ms. Park smiles. "Yes! Autumn here can be pretty too. We'll see soon."
reading.cn: Park 老师笑了。"是的！这边的秋天也很美。等等就能看到。"
reading.note: 💡 pretty / soon — 'll = will / We'll see soon

reading.en: I look out the window. The Berkeley trees are starting to turn. I miss home a little — but only a little.
reading.cn: 我望向窗外。伯克利的树正在变色。我有点想家——但只是一点点。

grammar.explain: 现在完成时用来表示从过去某个时间点开始，一直持续到现在或对现在有影响的动作或状态。当我们需要强调持续的时间长度时，常用 "for" 加上一段时间；当我们需要强调开始的时间点时，常用 "since" 加上一个具体时间点。

examples.en: Mei has been in the U.S. for three months.

examples.cn: 我从2020年开始学习英语。
examples.en: I have studied English since 2020.

grammar.title: 现在完成时 (Present Perfect) + for/since

grammar.explain: 一般过去时用来描述在过去某个时间点发生并结束的动作或事件。常常与表示过去时间的词一起使用，如 "ago", "yesterday", "last week" 等。
grammar.title: 一般过去时 (Simple Past)

grammar.title: 一般现在时 (Simple Present)
grammar.explain: 一般现在时用来描述现在的事实、习惯性动作或普遍真理。它也可以用来描述现在持续的状态。

reading.en: Three months ago, I came to America. Today I sit on a hill in Berkeley. I look at the sunset. I think about everything.
reading.cn: 三个月前我来到美国。今天我坐在伯克利的一座小山上。我看着日落。我想起了所有的事。
reading.note: three months ago + came (PAST) / sit + look + think (PRESENT) — 时态对比开篇

reading.en: In August, I had no friends here. I was scared. I did not know how to use a fork. I did not know the bus.
reading.cn: 八月时我在这里一个朋友也没有。我很害怕。我不会用叉子。我也不会坐公交。
reading.note: PAST: had / was / did not know — Mei 三个月前的样子

reading.en: Now I have Linda and Mark. I have Anna. I have a good cafe near my classes. I am working on my English every day.
reading.cn: 现在我有琳达和马克。有安娜。在课程附近有一家不错的咖啡馆。我每天都在练英语。
reading.note: PRESENT: have / am working — "现在的我" / every day

reading.en: Tonight I will call my mom in China. I will tell her, "I am OK. I am safe. I am happy." She is going to be proud.
reading.cn: 今晚我会给中国的妈妈打电话。我会告诉她："我很好。我很安全。我很开心。"她会为我骄傲。
reading.note: FUTURE: will call / will tell / is going to be proud — 三种将来表达

reading.en: Tomorrow I am going to the library to study. Next week I am going to look at one more apartment. There are many things ahead.
reading.cn: 明天我要去图书馆学习。下周我要再去看一套公寓。前面还有很多事。

grammar.explain: 在超市购物时，我们经常需要询问商品的具体位置。最常见的表达是 “Excuse me, where can I find…?” （打扰一下，请问…在哪里？）或者 “Where is…?”（…在哪里？）。回答时，可以用 “It’s in aisle…” （它在…通道）或 “It’s next to…” （它在…旁边）来指明位置。

grammar.title: Making a polite request: “I'd like...”

examples.cn: 我想要一袋苹果。
examples.en: I'd like a bag of apples, please.

examples.cn: 我想用现金支付。
examples.en: I'd like to pay with cash.

examples.cn: 我想要一杯中杯咖啡。
examples.en: I'd like a medium coffee.

grammar.explain: “I'd like...” 是 “I would like...” 的缩写，表示“我想要…”，是一种非常客气、自然的表达方式，比直接说 “I want…” 更委婉有礼。在点餐、购物等场景中非常常用。

examples.cn: 我想要一杯咖啡，谢谢。
examples.en: I'd like a coffee, please.

examples.cn: 我想要两杯咖啡，谢谢。
examples.en: I'd like two coffees, please.
I'd like a cup of tea, please.
examples.cn: 我想要一杯茶，谢谢。

grammar.explain: 在咖啡店或其他地方点餐时，我们可以使用“I'd like...”这个句型，表示“我想要……”。这是一个礼貌的表达。在请求的最后加上“please”会让你的话语更客气。
grammar.title: Ordering with 'I'd like...' and 'please'

grammar.explain: 当你需要询问别人的饮品偏好，例如是否加牛奶或糖时，可以使用以下句型。这些通常在点咖啡或茶时用到。

examples.cn: 你需要牛奶吗？
examples.en: Do you need milk?

examples.cn: 你想要糖吗？
examples.en: Do you want sugar?
One needs milk, no sugar.
examples.cn: 一杯需要牛奶不加糖。

grammar.title: 礼貌地邀请和回应 (Inviting and Responding Politely)

grammar.explain: 'Should' 是一个情态动词，用来表示建议、义务或推测。它的后面总是跟动词原形。

grammar.title: How was...? (询问过去经历)
grammar.explain: 我们用 “How was...?” 来询问某人对过去的经历或感受的看法。通常后面接一个名词，表示询问的是这个名词所代表的事物、事件或时间段。比如课文中的 “How was your weekend?” 就是询问“你的周末怎么样？”。
在回答 “How was...?” 的问题时，我们通常用 “It was + 形容词” 来描述。形容词可以是 positive (great, good)、negative (bad, terrible) 或 neutral (okay, busy)。

grammar.explain:
在描述交通或到达某个地方时，我们经常会用到“to get to”和“to take”。

**To get to:** 表示“到达某个地方”。它强调的是抵达目的地的动作或结果。

**To take:** 表示“走（某条路/交通工具）”或“乘坐（某种交通工具）”。它强调的是选择的路线或方式。

grammar.title: 现在完成时：持续动作 (Present Perfect: Continuous Actions)
grammar.explain: 现在完成时可以用来描述一个从过去开始，一直持续到现在，并且可能还会继续进行的动作或状态。我们经常与表示时间段的 for (表示持续了多久) 和 since (表示从什么时候开始) 搭配使用。核心句型: I have worked there for one year. 我在那里工作一年了。
for 后面接一段时间的长度，表示“持续了多久”；since 后面接一个具体的起始时间点，表示“从……开始”。

grammar.explain: 英语中，名词可以分为可数名词和不可数名词。可数名词是指可以数数的名词，有单数和复数形式。不可数名词是指不能数数的名词，通常没有复数形式，不能直接用数字来修饰。
grammar.title: 可数名词 (Countable Nouns) 和不可数名词 (Uncountable Nouns)
点餐句型: I'd like...

grammar.explain: 在餐厅点餐时，通常用 "I'd like..." 来表达“我想要…”。这是一种非常礼貌和常用的表达方式。 "I'd like" 是 "I would like" 的缩写。

在点餐时，我们会用到 a/an, some 和 any。
* a/an 用于修饰单数可数名词。
* some 用于肯定句中，修饰复数可数名词或不可数名词，表示“一些”。
* any 用于疑问句和否定句中，修饰复数可数名词或不可数名词，表示“任何”或“一些”。

grammar.title: If it rains, I'll stay home. (第一条件句)
grammar.explain:
第一条件句用来谈论当前或将来可能发生的情况及其导致的结果。它由两部分组成：一个 'if' 从句（条件）和一个主句（结果）。

**结构：**
If + 主语 + 动词现在时态 (if 从句), 主语 + will + 动词原形 (主句)

**If 从句:** 描述条件。动词用一般现在时。
**主句:** 描述结果。动词用 'will' + 动词原形。

grammar.title: Asking Questions in a Formal Setting (例如在机场)
grammar.explain:
在机场等正式场合询问信息时，我们通常使用更礼貌的表达方式，例如“May I…?”、“Could you please…?” 或 “Would you like…?”，而不是直接的“Can I…?”。

**May I …?**： 用于请求允许，比“Can I…?”更正式。
**Could you please …?**： 用于请求对方帮忙，表达更委婉。

grammar.explain:
在英语中，might, may 和 could 都可以用来表示对未来或当前事态的“可能性”推测。它们都属于情态动词 (modal verbs)。

1.  **Might**: 表示可能性相对较低，或者语气比较不确定。它通常用于表达一种猜测。
    *   结构：主语 + might + 动词原形
2.  **May**: 与 might 相似，也表示可能性，但有时被认为可能性略高于 might，或者语气更正式一些。在口语中，may 和 might 经常可以互换使用，差别不大。
    *   结构：主语 + may + 动词原形
3.  **Could**: 也可以表示可能性，尤其是在疑问句和否定句中，它可以指“也许会”或“可能不是”。在表示可能性时，could 和 might/may 意思相近，但 could 还可以表示“能力”。
    *   结构：主语 + could + 动词原形

grammar.explain:
当我们要转述别人说的话时，我们常常使用间接引语。直接引语是引用原话，而间接引语是转述内容。当主句是过去时，间接引语中的时态通常也要做相应的变化（退一步时态）。

核心句型：I'm tired. → She said she was tired.

examples.cn: 直接引语：“我累了。” → 间接引语：她说她累了。
examples.en: Direct: "I am tired." → Reported: She said she was tired.
Direct: "I am hungry." → Reported: He told me he was hungry.
examples.cn: 直接引语：“我饿了。” → 间接引语：他告诉我他饿了。
直接引语：“我们很高兴。” → 间接引语：他们说他们很高兴。
examples.en: Direct: "We are happy." → Reported: They said they were happy.
Direct: "I need a coffee." → Reported: She mentioned she needed a coffee.
examples.cn: 直接引语：“我需要一杯咖啡。” → 间接引语：她提到她需要一杯咖啡。

grammar.title: Say vs. Tell
grammar.explain:
在间接引语中，say 和 tell 都可以用来引导转述，但它们的用法略有不同。

- Say 后面可以直接跟转述内容，或跟 that 从句。
- Tell 后面通常需要先跟一个宾语（告诉某人），然后再跟转述内容或 that 从句。

grammar.explain:
反意疑问句（Question Tags）是在陈述句后加上一个简短的疑问句，用来征求对方的同意或确认某事。它的构成通常是：陈述句，+ 助动词/情态动词 + 主语代词？

- 如果陈述句是肯定的，反意疑问句通常用否定形式。
- 如果陈述句是否定的，反意疑问句通常用肯定形式。
- 助动词（如 be, do, have）或情态动词（如 can, will, must）要与陈述句中的动词保持一致。
- 主语要用代词形式指代陈述句的主语。

本课核心句型 “It's cold, isn't it?” 就是一个典型的反意疑问句。

grammar.explain:
在英语中，我们经常使用“be + 形容词 + 介词”的结构来表达某人擅长、不擅长或对某事感兴趣。本课主要学习如何使用形容词 good, bad, terrible 搭配介词 at，后面可以跟动名词（-ing 形式）或名词，用来表达“擅长做某事”或“不擅长做某事”。

- **be good at** + 动名词/名词：表示“擅长于……”
- **be bad at** + 动名词/名词：表示“不擅长于……”
- **be terrible at** + 动名词/名词：表示“对……很糟糕/非常不擅长……”

这个结构非常实用，在日常对话中经常出现。

grammar.explain:
在英语中，当我们要表达某事“必须被完成”、“应该被送达”等时，我们会使用情态动词 (modal verbs) 与被动语态 (passive voice) 结合的结构。这个结构是：

情态动词 (modal verb) + be + 动词的过去分词 (past participle)

常用的情态动词包括 must（必须）、should（应该）、can（可以）、may（可能）等。被动语态强调动作的承受者，而不是动作的发出者。

examples.en: This report must be done by Friday.

examples.en: The email should be sent by noon.

examples.cn: 会议可以改期到下周。

cannot (或 can't): 不能

grammar.title: 形容词的顺序 (Order of Adjectives)
grammar.explain:
当多个形容词修饰一个名词时，它们通常遵循一定的顺序。这个顺序可以帮助我们更自然、清晰地描述事物。记住这个顺序能让你的英语表达更地道。常见的顺序是：
1. 评价/看法 (Opinion)：beautiful, comfortable, unique
2. 大小 (Size)：small, big, large
3. 形状 (Shape)：round, oval
4. 新旧 (Age)：old, new, antique
5. 颜色 (Color)：red, blue, white
6. 材质 (Material)：wooden, metal, velvet
7. 来源/国籍 (Origin)：American, Chinese
8. 目的 (Purpose)：sleeping (bag), reading (corner)

例：a beautiful old wooden chair (一张漂亮的旧木椅)。

grammar.explain:
这是一个非常常用的英语祝福语和赠送礼物的表达。在生日、节日或任何需要送礼物表示心意的时候都可以使用。其中，“Happy birthday!”是直接的祝福语，表达“生日快乐！”；“Here's a gift for you.”是表示“这是给你的礼物”的意思。“Here's”是“Here is”的缩写，后面加单数名词；如果要送多件礼物，可以说“Here are some gifts for you.”。

这个句型可以推广到其他场合：
- Happy New Year! Here's a present for you. (新年快乐！这是送你的礼物。)
- Happy Anniversary! Here's a card for you. (周年快乐！这是送你的贺卡。)
- Here's a little something for you. (这是给你的一点小东西。—— 更随意的表达)

grammar.explain:
这句话用来表达收到礼物或帮助时，感到对方太客气了，不应该这么费心。它表示一种礼貌的推辞，但内心是感激的。在中文里，我们常说“你太客气了！”或者“你不用这么麻烦的！”。

这个表达的完整形式是 “You didn't have to do that!”，在口语中常被缩短为 “You didn't have to!”。

examples.cn: A：我给你带了些花。B：哦，你太客气了！
examples.en: A: I brought you some flowers. B: Oh, you didn't have to!

examples.cn: A：我为你做了晚饭。B：你不用这么麻烦的！不过谢谢你。
examples.en: A: I cooked dinner for you. B: You didn't have to! But thank you.

examples.cn: A：这是我为你的帮助准备的一点小东西。B：哦，你真的不用这么客气的！

grammar.title: Thank you for...
grammar.explain:
这个句型表示感谢某人做了某事。后面可以跟名词或动名词（动词的 ing 形式）。它是表达感谢非常常用且礼貌的方式。

例句：
- Thank you for the gift. (谢谢你的礼物。)
- Thank you for coming. (谢谢你的到来。)
- Thank you for helping me. (谢谢你帮助我。)

grammar.title: 现在完成进行时 (Present Perfect Continuous)
grammar.explain:
现在完成进行时表示一个动作从过去某个时间开始，一直持续到现在，并且可能还会继续下去。它强调动作的持续性。

结构：subject + have/has + been + verb-ing

常与 for (持续多长时间) 或 since (从某个时间点开始) 连用。

examples.en: I've been waiting here for 30 minutes.
examples.cn: 我在这里已经等了30分钟了。（强调持续的等待）

examples.en: I've waited for you.
examples.cn: 我等你等过了。（强调等待这个事实，可能已经结束）

grammar.title: 现在完成进行时 vs. 现在完成时
grammar.explain:
现在完成进行时强调动作的持续性和过程，而现在完成时则强调动作的结果或完成。

现在完成进行时: "I've been reading this book." (我一直在读这本书，可能还没读完)
现在完成时: "I've read this book." (我已经读完这本书了)

output.cn: 写一小段话，描述你童年时期经常做的事情。描述两到三项活动，以及你对它们的感受。至少各使用一次 "used to" 和 "would"。

grammar.explain:
在英语中，我们用 "used to" 和 "would" 来描述过去经常发生但现在不再发生的事情，或者过去的习惯。它们都表示“过去常常”或“以前会”。

**Used to:**
1. 可以描述过去经常发生的动作（习惯）。
   例如：I used to play basketball every day. (我以前每天都打篮球。)
2. 可以描述过去的状态（非动作性动词），而 "would" 通常不可以。
   例如：I used to live in a small town. (我以前住在一个小镇。) - 这里不能用 "would"。

examples.en: I used to play tennis a lot when I was young.
examples.cn: 我年轻时经常打网球。

examples.en: She used to have long hair.
examples.cn: 她以前留长发。

examples.en: There used to be a bookstore here.
examples.cn: 这里以前有家书店。

grammar.title: Used to vs. Would: 描述过去的习惯和状态
Would: 描述过去的重复性动作
grammar.explain:
Would 主要用于描述过去反复发生的动作或习惯，但它不能用于描述过去的状态。它通常用在叙述故事或回忆时，让描述更生动。

**Would (强调重复性动作):**
1. 只能描述过去重复性的动作，不能描述状态。
   例如：Every Sunday, we would go to the park. (每个星期天，我们都会去公园。)
2. 常与时间短语（如 every day, often, sometimes）一起使用，表示频率。

examples.cn: 我小时候，奶奶每晚都会给我讲故事。
examples.en: When I was a child, my grandmother would tell me stories every night.
We would often go fishing together.
examples.cn: 我们以前经常一起去钓鱼。
夏天的时候，我们总是会在湖里游泳。
examples.en: In the summer, we would always swim in the lake.

grammar.title: 总结区别:
grammar.explain:
**Used to 可以描述动作和状态，would 只能描述动作。**

- **Used to** 可以替换 **would** 来描述重复性动作。
  例如：I used to play basketball. = I would play basketball. (✓)

- **Would 不可以** 替换 **used to** 来描述状态。
  例如：I used to live in a small town. ≠ I would live in a small town. (✕)

grammar.title: That's a wrap! (口语化表达“结束了/搞定了”)
grammar.explain: “That's a wrap!”是一个非常地道的口语表达，意思是“这就结束了”、“圆满完成了”或者“搞定了”。它常用于宣布一项任务、活动或项目已经成功结束。在电影制作中，当一天的拍摄或整个电影拍摄完成时，导演会说“That's a wrap!”。在日常生活中，当完成某项工作或学习阶段后，也可以用它来表达事情的完成。

examples.en: After two years, my A2 English course is a wrap!

grammar.title: 过去完成时 (Past Perfect)
grammar.explain: 过去完成时表示在过去某个时间点或动作之前已经完成的动作或状态。它通常用于强调动作的先后顺序，即“在...之前”已经发生的事情。其构成是 'had + 动词的过去分词 (past participle)'。

examples.cn: 她说她已经决定了。（“决定”发生在“说”之前）
examples.en: She said she had already decided.

examples.cn: 他到的时候，我已经完成工作了。（“完成工作”发生在“他到”之前）
examples.en: I had already finished my work when he arrived.

output.sample: November 20th. It's been a terrible week. Johnsy had caught pneumonia, and the doctor had given us very little hope. Though I tried to cheer her up, she had made up her mind that she wouldn't get well. She keeps looking at the ivy vine. grammar.title: 让步连接词: Though / Although / Even though

examples.cn: 虽然很冷，琼西还是看着窗外。
examples.en: Though it was cold, Johnsy still looked out the window.

examples.en: Even though the vine was almost bare, Johnsy still clung to the idea of the last leaf.

grammar.explain:
这些连接词用于引出让步状语从句，表示与主句内容相反或出乎意料的情况。它们的意思相近，都表示“尽管”、“虽然”。

- **Though**：可以用于句首、句中或句尾，相对口语化。
- **Although**：通常用于句首，语气比 though 稍正式。
- **Even though**：语气最强，强调“即使”或“尽管如此”的意思。

**核心句型示例：**
Though she had little hope, Sue never gave up trying to encourage Johnsy.

examples.cn: 在苏来之前，医生已经给了她很少的希望。
examples.en: The doctor had given her little hope before Sue arrived.

grammar.title: 过去完成时 (Past Perfect)
grammar.explain:
过去完成时表示在过去某个时间点之前已经完成的动作。它常用于叙述故事，表明事件发生的先后顺序。

结构：had + 动词过去分词 (V-ed/V3)

**核心句型示例：**
Johnsy had made up her mind that she was not going to get well.

reading.en: In a small studio in Greenwich Village lived two young painters: Sue and Johnsy. It was Johnsy who fell ill that November — pneumonia, the doctor said. Never had a winter felt so heavy.
reading.cn: 格林威治村一间小画室里，住着两位年轻画家：苏和琼西。那年十一月生病的是琼西——肺炎，医生说。冬天从未让人觉得这般沉重。
reading.note: It was Johnsy who... — cleft sentence (KEY focus) / Never had... — negative inversion

reading.en: Lying in bed, Johnsy stared at the brick wall outside. An old ivy vine clung there. "When the last leaf falls," she whispered, "I will go too." It was this strange belief that frightened Sue most of all.
reading.cn: 琼西躺在床上，盯着窗外的砖墙。一株老常春藤攀在墙上。"等最后一片叶子掉了，"她小声说，"我也就走了。"让苏最害怕的，正是这个奇怪的念头。
reading.note: It was this strange belief that... — cleft for emphasis

reading.en: Behind their building lived old Behrman, a failed painter who, for forty years, had been talking about the masterpiece he would one day paint. Not once had he begun it.
reading.cn: 他们楼后住着老贝尔曼，一个失败的画家，四十年来一直说着自己有一天要画的那幅杰作。可他一次都没动笔。
reading.note: Not once had he begun it — negative inversion (KEY focus)

reading.en: When Sue told him about Johnsy, Behrman cursed loudly. "Why do you let her have such fool ideas?" he said. But it was clear, even then, that he had been moved.
reading.cn: 苏把琼西的事告诉他，贝尔曼大声咒骂。"你怎么由她生这种傻念头？"他说。可即便那时，谁都看得出，他已经动了心。
reading.note: It was clear that... — cleft for confirmation

reading.en: That night, the storm came. Rain hammered the window. Wind tore at the wall. By morning, only one leaf remained on the vine — and Johnsy lay watching it. "When it falls," she said, "so will I."
reading.cn: 那一夜，暴风雨来了。雨敲打着窗户。风撕扯着墙。到早晨，藤上只剩一片叶子——琼西躺着看着它。"它一落，"她说，"我也就走了。"
reading.note: Rain hammered... + so will I — emphatic structures

reading.en: But the leaf did not fall that day. Nor did it fall the next. Each morning, Johnsy looked, and there it still was — green, hanging on. Slowly, her will to live returned.
reading.cn: 可那片叶子那天没掉。第二天也没掉。每天早上，琼西看出去，它还在那儿——绿色的，还挂着。慢慢地，她活下去的意志回来了。
reading.note: Nor did it fall... — negative inversion ('nor + auxiliary + subject')

reading.en: On the third day, the doctor said she would live. "Now I must go to see Behrman," he added. "Yesterday, the old man was admitted to the hospital with pneumonia. Out he had gone the night of the storm — God knows where."
reading.cn: 到第三天，医生说她能挺过来了。"现在我得去看贝尔曼，"他又说，"昨天，那位老先生因为肺炎被送进了医院。暴风雨那夜他出了门——天晓得去了哪里。"
reading.note: Out he had gone... — fronted adverbial for emphasis

reading.en: Two days later, Sue came to Johnsy. "There is something I must show you," she said. They went to the window. Sue pointed at the leaf. "Look closely. It has not moved in the wind. Not once has it shaken since the storm."
reading.cn: 两天后，苏来到琼西身边。"有件事我必须给你看，"她说。她们走到窗前。苏指着那片叶子。"仔细看。它在风里一动也没动过。从那夜暴风雨以来，它一次都没颤过。"
reading.note: Not once has it shaken — negative inversion in present perfect

reading.en: It was Behrman, Sue explained, who had painted the leaf on the wall the night of the storm. Yellow and green and brown, leaf-veins drawn fine — done in the freezing rain, by lantern. "That," Sue said quietly, "was his masterpiece."
reading.cn: 苏解释说，是贝尔曼在暴风雨那一夜把那片叶子画在墙上的。黄、绿、棕，叶脉描得细致——在结冰的雨里画出来，借着一盏灯笼的光。"那，"苏轻声说，"是他的杰作。"
reading.note: Closing — It was Behrman who... — cleft + 'That was his masterpiece' = emphatic

grammar.title: 被动语态 (The Passive Voice): The decision was made together.
grammar.explain: 被动语态用于强调动作的承受者而不是动作的发出者。在标题句 "The decision was made together" 中，我们更关注“决定”本身以及它是如何被做出的，而不是谁做了这个决定。常见的被动语态结构是：主语 + be动词 + 过去分词。
动词 discuss 表示“讨论”，后面直接跟讨论的内容，不需要加介词。例如，我们讨论一个计划，就用 discuss a plan，而不需要 discuss about a plan。

* agree on sth.: 就某事达成一致
* agree to do sth.: 同意做某事
* agree that clause: 同意一个事实或观点

grammar.title: 叙事时态混搭 (Narrative Tense Blending)
grammar.explain:
在讲述过去发生的故事或经历时，我们经常会混用不同的过去时态，以清晰地表达事件发生的顺序、背景和持续性。

**核心句型一：一般过去时 (Simple Past) - 描述主要动作或事件。**

**核心句型二：过去进行时 (Past Continuous) - 描述过去某个时间点正在进行或作为背景的动作。**

**核心句型三：过去完成时 (Past Perfect) - 描述在另一个过去动作之前已经完成的动作。**

examples.cn: 我当时正在写报告，这时客户打来了电话。
examples.en: I **was working** on the report when the client **called**.

examples.cn: 当我加入团队时，他们已经完成了第一阶段。
examples.en: By the time I **joined** the team, they **had already completed** phase one.

examples.cn: 他解释说，他那天早些时候遇到了一个技术问题。
examples.en: He **explained** that he **had encountered** a technical issue earlier that day.

Could you please provide information on the eligibility criteria and the application deadline for the upcoming academic year? Your guidance on this matter would be greatly appreciated. Thank you for your time and consideration.

listening.audio: Ivan Dmitrich, a middle-class man who lived with his family on a small income, went to bed early one evening. After dinner, he read the newspaper. He remembered that his wife had a lottery ticket, bought many weeks ago. She had forgotten all about it. He wondered, "What if we actually win?" The series was 9,499, and the number was 26. He quickly looked at the newspaper to check the winning list. "Good heavens! 9,499 is there! And 26 is also there!" He couldn't believe his eyes. His wife, Masha, was sitting at the table, folding laundry. He handed her the newspaper. Masha's face turned pale. "It is our ticket!" she cried. They both started to imagine their new life. They would buy an estate with the money, maybe a house and some land. They would travel, eat delicious food, and live a life of luxury. Their excitement grew. But then, a different thought came to Ivan. "What if Masha tries to take all the money for herself?" he wondered. He started to feel annoyed with her. Masha, in turn, began to think about how Ivan might spend the money on his hobbies, ignoring her needs. They started to argue about how the money would be spent, even before they officially had it. "It's my ticket!" Masha shouted. "I bought it!" Ivan replied, "But I work hard to earn the money that bought it!" Their dreams of a happy, rich life together quickly turned into anger and resentment. The dream of the lottery win had ruined their peaceful evening.

reading.en: Ivan and his wife Masha lived a comfortable life. One evening Ivan opened the newspaper and saw the lottery results. Masha had bought a ticket months ago. "What's the number, dear?" he asked casually. "9499, series 26," she said. "I'll just check." His finger ran down the column. He stopped.
reading.cn: Ivan 和妻子 Masha 过着舒适的生活。一天傍晚，Ivan 打开报纸看到了彩票结果。Masha 几个月前买过一张票。"亲爱的，什么号码？"他随便问。"9499，第 26 组，"她说。"我来查一下。"他的手指顺着那一栏滑下。他停住了。
reading.note: had bought — past perfect (复习) / casually 💡 = 随意地

reading.en: Series 26 had won. Ivan looked at the number. He could not bring himself to look at the digits — not yet. "Don't tell me," Masha whispered. They sat in silence for a moment. "It is said that the prize this year is 75,000 rubles," Ivan finally said.
reading.cn: 第 26 组中奖了。Ivan 盯着号码。他还不敢看那几个数字——还不敢。"先别说，"Masha 低声说。他们沉默了一会儿。"据说今年的奖金是 75,000 卢布，"Ivan 终于说道。
reading.note: It is said that — 非人称被动（KEY focus）/ could not bring himself to look = 不忍/不敢去看

reading.en: Ivan began to dream. He imagined a country house — quiet evenings, mushroom hunting, swimming in the river. He saw himself as a calm gentleman, respected by neighbors. "I am supposed to like fishing," he thought, "and I think I really do." He felt years younger. The future looked golden.
reading.cn: Ivan 开始幻想。他想象一栋乡间别墅——安静的晚上、采蘑菇、在河里游泳。他看见自己成了一位被邻居尊敬的从容绅士。"我应该是个喜欢钓鱼的人，"他想，"而且我确实喜欢。"他感觉年轻了好多岁。未来一片金黄。
reading.note: I am supposed to like — 非人称被动 (KEY focus·人们认为/被期望) / respected by — 被动

reading.en: Then he glanced at his wife. She, too, was smiling. Her eyes shone. Ivan suddenly remembered: the ticket was Masha's. The money was hers. "She is known to be careful with money," he thought. "But she will probably travel without me. She might give it all to her relatives. Yes, that's exactly what she'll do."
reading.cn: 然后他瞥了妻子一眼。她也在笑。她的眼睛在闪。Ivan 忽然想起来：彩票是 Masha 的。钱是她的。"大家都知道她对钱很谨慎，"他想。"但她大概会自己一个人去旅行——把钱全分给她的亲戚。对，她肯定会这样做。"
reading.note: She is known to be — 非人称被动（KEY focus·大家都知道）/ exactly what she'll do — 内心独白

reading.en: He looked at her again, but now coldly. Her smile was greedy. Her relatives were the worst. "It is believed that money changes everyone," Ivan said bitterly. "Look at you already!" Masha looked surprised. "I was thinking the same about you," she replied. "You'd spend it on yourself."
reading.cn: 他又看了她一眼，但现在带着寒意。她的笑容看上去贪婪。她的亲戚是最差的一类人。"人们都相信钱会改变一个人，"Ivan 苦涩地说。"看看你！"Masha 露出意外的表情。"我也正这么想你呢，"她回答。"你只会把钱花在自己身上。"
reading.note: It is believed that — 非人称被动（KEY focus·人们都相信）/ greedy 💡 = 贪婪的

reading.en: They argued for ten minutes. Then Ivan looked at the ticket again. He read the digits carefully. The number was 9498, not 9499. They had not won at all. The kitchen suddenly looked small. The walls suddenly looked dirty. They sat there, two people who, an hour earlier, had been content.
reading.cn: 他们吵了十分钟。然后 Ivan 又看了看彩票。他仔细读了那几个数字。号码是 9498，不是 9499。他们根本没中。厨房忽然显得小。墙壁忽然显得脏。他们坐在那里——两个一小时前还心满意足的人。
reading.note: had not won / had been content — past perfect / 故事关键反转：根本没中

grammar.title: 定语从句 (Relative Clauses) - 用 which 引导非限制性定语从句
grammar.explain: 定语从句用来修饰名词或代词，提供更多信息。非限制性定语从句提供补充信息，即使没有它，句子的主句意思也是完整的。它通常用逗号与主句隔开，修饰物时常用 "which" 引导。

grammar.title: 投诉表达 - 礼貌地反映问题
grammar.explain: 虽然本课场景是愉快的感恩节,但为了单元主题的完整性,我们也学习一些关于“投诉”的礼貌表达。在日常生活中,如果遇到需要反映问题的情况,我们可以用这些句型。

output.sample: Hey Lily! Guess what? I just had my first Thanksgiving dinner, and it was amazing! The Walkers are so nice. We had a huge turkey and tons of other delicious food. My favorite was definitely the stuffing, which was Mrs. Walker's secret recipe. It was so flavorful! And the whole dinner, which lasted for almost four hours, was full of laughter. I'm so full and happy now! Hope you had a great day too!

grammar.title: 使役动词：let / make / help + 宾语 + 动词原形
grammar.explain: 在英语中，let, make, help 这三个词被称为使役动词。它们后面通常会带一个宾语（接收动作的人或物），然后宾语后面直接跟动词原形（base form of the verb），表示“让/使/帮助某人做某事”。

grammar.title: 动词原形的用法回顾
grammar.explain: 动词原形是指动词最基本的形式，不加任何词尾变化（如-s, -ed, -ing）。在使役动词 let, make, help 后面，宾语之后直接使用动词原形。

grammar.title: 用 regret 表达后悔
grammar.explain: 动词 regret 后面可以接动名词 (V-ing) 或者不定式 (to V)。当 regret 后接动名词时，表示对过去做过或没做过的事情感到后悔。当 regret 后接不定式时，通常表示对接下来要说的事情感到遗憾或抱歉（比较正式）。

grammar.explain:
当我们需要转述别人说的话，特别是命令或请求时，我们通常使用“间接命令”结构。核心句型是：
Subject + tell/ask + Object + (not) to + Verb (原形)

examples.cn: 她对我说：“别担心。” → 她让我别担心。
examples.en: She told me, “Don't worry.” → She told me not to worry.

examples.cn: 他对我说：“请在这里等。” → 他让我等在那里。
examples.en: He said to me, “Please wait here.” → He asked me to wait there.

examples.cn: 老师告诉我们：“完成作业。” → 老师让我们完成作业。
examples.en: The teacher told us, “Finish your homework.” → The teacher told us to finish our homework.

grammar.title: 间接命令 (Reported Commands)

grammar.explain: 在间接命令中，常常用到动词不定式 (to + 动词原形) 来表示被转述的动作或请求。

reading.en: Della had exactly one dollar and eighty-seven cents. The arrival of Christmas was less than twenty-four hours away.
reading.cn: 黛拉手里只有一块八毛七。圣诞节的到来，已经只剩不到二十四个小时。
reading.note: Nominalization (arrival)

reading.en: For weeks, her preparation for this day had been a single goal: a gift worthy of her husband Jim. Their poverty was real, but her devotion was greater.
reading.cn: 几个星期以来，她为这天做的所有准备只有一件事：找一份配得上丈夫吉姆的礼物。他们的贫穷是真实的，但她对他的爱意，比贫穷更深。
reading.note: Nominalization × 3 (preparation, poverty, devotion)

reading.en: In all their possessions, two things were of great value. Jim's gold watch had been his father's, and his grandfather's. Della's brown hair fell below her knees, with the soft shine of a brown waterfall.
reading.cn: 他们家里所有的东西里，只有两样真正贵重。吉姆的金表，是父亲、爷爷传下来的。黛拉的栗色长发垂到膝下，闪着像褐色瀑布一样柔和的光。
reading.note: Nominalization (possessions)

reading.en: Her decision came without hesitation. She stopped at a shop whose sign read "Madame Sofronie. Hair Goods of All Kinds." Twenty dollars later, she walked out — her head cold and her purse full.
reading.cn: 她做这个决定时几乎没有犹豫。她在一家招牌写着「索弗朗夫人 · 各种发制品」的店门口停下，走了进去。二十块钱之后，她走出来——头顶发凉，钱包却满了。
reading.note: Nominalization × 2 (decision, hesitation)

reading.en: With the money, she bought a platinum watch chain for Jim. The chain's simplicity and quietness were exactly right. Like Jim, it had value without showiness.
reading.cn: 她用这笔钱给吉姆买了一条铂金表链。这条链子的简洁与低调正合适。像吉姆这个人——它有价值，但不张扬。
reading.note: Nominalization × 4 (simplicity, quietness, value, showiness)

reading.en: When Jim came home that evening, his reaction was strange. It was not anger, nor disappointment, nor displeasure. It was a kind of stillness Della had never seen on his face before.
reading.cn: 傍晚吉姆回家时，他的反应很奇怪。不是生气，不是失望，也不是不悦。那是一种黛拉从未在他脸上见过的安静。
reading.note: Nominalization × 5 (reaction, anger, disappointment, displeasure, stillness)

reading.en: Slowly, he placed a small package on the table. Inside were the combs Della had been admiring in a shop window for months — beautiful tortoise-shell combs, perfect for her long hair. Her realization came like cold water.
reading.cn: 他慢慢把一个小包放在桌上。里面是几把黛拉对着橱窗看了几个月的发梳——漂亮的玳瑁发梳，正适合她的长发。她明白过来的那一刻，像被冷水浇了一身。
reading.note: Nominalization (realization)

reading.en: "I sold the watch," Jim said, "to buy your combs." His confession needed no further explanation. Their two sacrifices — made out of love — had cancelled each other out exactly.
reading.cn: 「我把表卖了，」吉姆说，「为了给你买梳子。」他的坦白不需要再多解释什么。他们出于爱做的两个牺牲，正好相互抵消。
reading.note: Nominalization × 3 (confession, explanation, sacrifices)

reading.en: This is the wisdom of the Magi: of all the gifts in the world, those that look the most foolish are sometimes the wisest. The exchange of useless treasures, given in devotion, is itself the gift.
reading.cn: 这就是麦琪的智慧：在世上所有礼物中，那些看起来最傻的，有时候恰恰是最有智慧的。两件没用的宝物在彼此间交换——只因为爱——这件事本身，就是真正的礼物。
reading.note: Closing aphorism — nominalization-rich (wisdom, exchange, devotion)

output.sample: The most impressive aspect of the story for me is the selfless love between Della and Jim. They both gave up their most prized possessions just to buy a gift for the other, which shows how much they cherished each other. It’s a powerful message that true love is about sacrifice, not about the material value of gifts. Their actions, though seemingly foolish, were the wisest because they were driven by pure love.

listening.audio: Mei is studying for the GRE, a very important and challenging exam for her graduate school application. She’s at her desk, surrounded by textbooks and notes, trying to focus on complex math problems. Suddenly, her phone rings. She sighs, seeing her father’s name on the caller ID. This is the third time he’s called today. Mei loves her dad, but his frequent calls are becoming a major distraction. She really needs to concentrate. She answers, trying to sound cheerful. “Hi, Dad! Everything okay?” Her father launches into a long story about his day. Mei tries to listen patiently, but her eyes keep drifting back to her textbooks. She feels a rising sense of frustration. After the call, Mei puts her phone on silent. “I wish he would stop calling so much,” she mutters to herself. “I wish I could just focus on my studies.” She knows he means well, but she wishes he understood how demanding this exam is.

listening.audio: Mei was trying to study for her English test in her room. Her roommate, Vivi, was listening to music without headphones, and singing along loudly. Mei tried to ignore it at first, but the music was too loud. She took a deep breath and decided to talk to Vivi. 'Vivi,' Mei said politely, 'I'm really trying to focus on my studies, but the music is making it hard for me to concentrate.' Vivi took off her headphones, looking surprised. 'Oh, I'm so sorry, Mei! I didn't realize it was bothering you. I can turn it down, or use my headphones.' Mei smiled. 'Headphones would be great, if you don't mind. I really appreciate it.' Vivi nodded. 'No problem at all! I totally understand. I'll be more careful next time.' Mei felt relieved. It was a small step, but an important one in learning to live with a roommate.

listening.audio: It’s the night before Mei’s application deadline. She’s been working on her essay for hours, but she still feels like it’s not perfect. She sighs, looking at the clock. It’s already 11 PM. “If only I had more time,” she mumbles to herself. “Then I could review everything one more time, maybe even rewrite a paragraph. I wish I had started earlier. Now I’m so stressed.” She thinks about all the other things she could have done. “If only I hadn’t spent so much time on social media this week. If only I had focused more in class instead of daydreaming. I regret wasting so much time.” Mei takes a deep breath. She knows there’s no turning back now. “It is what it is. I just need to submit it. I wish I felt more confident, but I’ve done my best.”

reading.cn: "你怎么敢把我喝的水弄浑！"狼吼道。小羊被这问题吓了一跳——抬头礼貌地回答："先生，水从您那儿流到我这儿。我在您下面很远的地方喝。我不可能让您的水变浑。"狼不肯认输——又试了一次。
reading.note: make my drinking water muddy — 使役 make + 宾语 + 形容词（KEY focus）/ surprised by the question — 过去分词短语作定语 / refusing to lose — 现在分词短语

reading.en: "You called me names last year — I haven't forgotten." The lamb, looking confused, replied, "Last year I was not even born." The wolf, growing angrier, tried a third time. "Then it must have been your father. He had me chased out of his pasture five years ago. I never forget such things."
reading.cn: "你去年还骂过我——我没忘。"小羊看上去很困惑："去年我还没出生呢。"狼越来越生气——第三次试："那一定是你父亲。五年前他让人把我赶出他的牧场。这种事我从不忘。"
reading.note: looking confused — 现在分词短语 / He had me chased out — 使役 have（让/被某人做某事）（KEY focus）/ growing angrier — 现在分词

reading.en: "I have never had any father chase you," the lamb said gently. "Sir, please ask my mother — she is just over the hill. We are peaceful sheep. We have never had anyone harmed in our flock." Hearing this, the wolf snarled and stepped closer to the trembling lamb.
reading.cn: "我从没让任何父亲赶过您，"小羊温和地说。"先生，请问问我母亲——她就在山那边。我们是平和的羊。我们从没有让羊群里任何人受过伤。"听到这话，狼咆哮起来——朝颤抖的小羊走近一步。
reading.note: have any father chase you — 使役 have / We have never had anyone harmed — 使役 have + 过去分词（被动 KEY focus）/ Hearing this — 现在分词

reading.en: "You and your kind, having stolen our forest, our streams, our grass for years, deserve to be punished. I do not need a real reason — only a reason that sounds good enough to others. Believe me, I have had thousands of meals this way."
reading.cn: "你们这种人——多年来偷了我们的森林、溪水、草场——活该受惩罚。我不需要真正的理由——只需要一个对别人听起来还说得过去的理由。相信我——我用这种办法吃了几千顿饭。"
reading.note: having stolen our forest — 完成式分词短语（KEY focus）/ have had thousands of meals — 使役 have（吃，复数概念）

reading.en: Having waited long enough for an excuse, the wolf jumped on the lamb and made his meal. The moral, told by Aesop in two thousand years of retelling, is simple: a tyrant will always have his reasons; what he needs is the strength to act, not the truth to support him. Reasons can be made up. Power cannot.
reading.cn: 等够了一个借口——狼扑上小羊——结束了它的饭。这个寓言——Aesop 讲了两千年——道理很简单：暴君永远找得到理由；他需要的是动手的力量——不是支持他的真相。理由可以编出来。力量编不出来。
reading.note: Having waited long enough — 完成式分词（KEY focus）/ told by Aesop — 过去分词短语作定语 / made his meal = 让它成为他的一餐（使役 make）

expressions.scene: 当狼对小羊的行为感到愤怒和不满时使用。
当狼不愿听小羊的解释，坚持自己的观点时使用。
描述一个人是否能被说服或接受道理时使用。
字面意思是指弄浑水，引申意可以指搅浑局面，使事情复杂化。
感到口渴时，去喝水来解渴。

quiz.q: 根据故事，狼为什么声称小羊弄浑了水？
小羊反驳狼的理由是什么？
狼为什么对小羊说“六个月前，你侮辱了我爸爸！”？
options: 小羊确实侮辱了它的爸爸。
狼只是想找个吃掉小羊的借口。
狼的爸爸真的被侮辱了。

quiz.q: “I won't have you spoiling my drink!”这句话中，“have”是哪个使役动词的用法？

listening.audio: One hot summer day, a hungry and thirsty wolf decided to quench his thirst at a clear stream. As he was about to drink, he noticed a little lamb further downstream, also enjoying the cool water. "How dare you!" growled the wolf, his eyes blazing with anger. "You are muddying my drinking water! I won't have you spoiling my drink!" The innocent lamb, trembling with fear, replied, "But, kind sir, that's impossible. The water flows from you to me. I couldn't possibly muddy your water, as it starts from your end." The wolf, however, was not one to be reasoned with. "No matter!" he snarled. "Six months ago, you insulted my father!" The lamb, confused, protested, "But six months ago, I wasn't even born!" The wolf, finding no true fault with the lamb, still would not let it go. "Well, if it wasn't you, it was your brother!" he cried. "I have no brother," said the lamb. "Then," said the wolf, "it was your ancestor! Be that as it may, I'm not going without my dinner!" And without another word, he fell upon the poor, helpless lamb and devoured it.

examples.cn: 我不会让你把我的水弄脏！ (have + 宾语 + 现在分词，表示容忍或允许某事发生)
examples.en: I won't **have you spoiling** my drink!
The wolf **made the lamb tremble** with fear.
examples.cn: 狼让小羊吓得发抖。 (make + 宾语 + 动词原形，表示强迫或导致某事发生)
我父母让我自己选择衣服。(let + 宾语 + 动词原形，表示允许某事发生)
examples.en: My parents **let me choose** my own clothes.

grammar.title: 使役动词 (Causative Verbs): let, have, make
grammar.explain: 使役动词用于表达“让/使某人做某事”的句型。在《狼与小羊》的故事中，狼试图“让小羊承担责任”，或者“使小羊的水变浑”。

grammar.title: 分词短语 (Participial Phrases) 作状语
grammar.explain: 分词短语（现在分词或过去分词构成）可以作状语，修饰主句的谓语或整个句子，说明原因、时间、方式或伴随情况。它们使得句子更简洁生动。

examples.cn: 因为害怕而发抖，无辜的小羊回答说…… (现在分词短语作状语，表示伴随状态或原因)
examples.en: **Trembling with fear**, the innocent lamb replied...

examples.cn: 因为又饿又渴，狼寻找一条小溪。(现在分词短语作原因状语)
examples.en: **Being hungry and thirsty**, the wolf looked for a stream.

examples.cn: 看到小羊后，狼的眼睛燃烧着怒火。(现在分词短语作时间状语)
examples.en: **Seeing the lamb**, the wolf's eyes blazed with anger.

examples.cn: 小羊，正在享受着凉水，一开始没注意到狼。(现在分词短语作定语，修饰 lamb)
examples.en: The lamb, **enjoying the cool water**, didn't notice the wolf at first.
The **growling** wolf tried to blame the lamb.
examples.cn: 咆哮的狼试图责怪小羊。(现在分词作定语修饰 wolf)
受惊的小羊迅速离开了。(过去分词作定语修饰 lamb)
examples.en: The **frightened** lamb quickly moved away.

grammar.title: 分词短语 (Participial Phrases) 作定语
grammar.explain: 分词短语也可以作定语，修饰名词或代词，相当于一个定语从句。在《狼与小羊》的故事中，我们可以用分词短语来描述事物的特征。

output.sample: The wolf was extremely cruel and unjust. Being consumed by hunger, he made up various excuses to blame the innocent lamb. He wouldn't let the lamb explain itself, showing no mercy. His actions, driven by pure selfishness, allowed him to devour the lamb without a second thought.
output.prompt: 你认为狼的行为可以用哪个词来形容？请用英文写一段话，至少包含一个使役动词和一个分词短语。
output.cn: 你认为狼的行为可以用哪个词来形容？请用英文写一段话，至少包含一个使役动词和一个分词短语。

examples.cn: 做完作业后，我出去玩了。
examples.en: Having finished my homework, I went out to play.

examples.cn: 努力学习后，她轻松通过了考试。
examples.en: Having studied hard, she passed the exam easily.

examples.cn: 因为累了，他早早地睡了。
examples.en: Being tired, he went to bed early.

examples.cn: 她灿烂地笑着接过了奖项。
examples.en: Smiling brightly, she accepted the award.

grammar.title: Using Participle Phrases for Cause and Effect / Time
grammar.explain:
本课的核心句型 “Having waited for weeks, I finally got the email.” 中， “Having waited for weeks” 是一个分词短语，用作状语，说明主句动作发生的原因或者时间顺序。它可以用来简化句子，使表达更紧凑，常用于表示：
1. 完成某事后发生另一个动作。
2. 某事导致了另一个结果。

grammar.title: Mixed Conditionals (Third Conditional + Present Result)
grammar.explain: 在一些情况下，我们谈论过去未发生的事情对现在造成的影响。这叫做混合条件句，结合了第三条件句（If + had + P.P.）和第二条件句（would + V）。

examples.cn: 如果我大学时学习更努力，我现在就会有一份更好的工作了。（过去未发生，现在有影响）
examples.en: If I had studied harder in college, I would have a better job now.

examples.cn: 如果梅没有申请那所大学，她今天就不会庆祝她的录取了。（过去未发生，现在有影响）
examples.en: If Mei hadn't applied to that university, she wouldn't be celebrating her admission today.

examples.cn: 如果他没错过航班，他现在就在巴黎了。
examples.en: If he hadn't missed the flight, he would be in Paris right now.

examples.cn: 我还在等公司回复我的工作申请。
examples.en: I'm still waiting to hear back from the company about my job application.

examples.cn: 你收到房东关于公寓的回复了吗？
examples.en: Did you hear back from the landlord about the apartment?

examples.cn: 梅终于收到大学的回复，非常兴奋。
examples.en: Mei was so excited to finally hear back from the university.

grammar.title: Phrasal Verb: 'Hear back from'
grammar.explain: “Hear back from” 是一个常用短语动词，意思是“收到（某人或机构的）回复”。这在申请大学、工作或其他需要等待官方回复的场景中非常常见。

output.sample: Having waited for months, I finally received the acceptance letter from my dream university. My heart was pounding, and I felt incredibly relieved. When I saw 'Congratulations!', a huge smile spread across my face. I immediately called my parents to share the good news. All my hard work has paid off!

output.cn: 想象一下你收到大学录取通知书的那一刻，或者其他你期待已久的好消息。描述一下你当时的心情、你看到了什么、做了什么。

reading.en: Wei is at school. Anna is at work. I am alone in the apartment, my finger hovering over the link.

reading.en: Holding my breath, I click. The page loads. "Congratulations — you've been admitted."
reading.cn: 屏住呼吸,我点了一下。页面加载。"恭喜——你被录取了。"

listening.audio: Dear Anna, as I prepare to leave, I find myself thinking about how much you've helped me during my stay here. It feels like just yesterday I arrived, a bit lost and unsure. But it was you who welcomed me with open arms and made me feel at home. There were times when I faced challenges, and it was your encouragement that kept me going. It was your advice that guided me through difficult situations. And when I felt truly down, it was your kindness that lifted my spirits. Honestly, it was Anna who saved me. I will cherish every memory we've made. Thank you for everything. This journey in the UK would not have been the same without you.

grammar.title: 强调句型: It is/was...who/that...

examples.cn: 是安娜救了我。（强调了“Anna”这个主语）

examples.cn: 是你的善良让我振作起来。（强调了“your kindness”这个主语）
examples.en: It was your kindness that lifted my spirits.

examples.cn: 我是在去年访问的伦敦。（强调了“last year”这个时间状语）
examples.en: It was last year that I visited London.

grammar.explain: 当我们想要强调句子的某个部分（比如主语、宾语或时间状语）时，可以使用“It is/was...who/that...”句型。被强调的部分放在is/was和who/that之间。

grammar.title: 动名词作主语
grammar.explain: 动词的-ing形式（动名词）可以在句子中作主语，表示一个动作或行为。

examples.cn: 如果我有更多时间，我会去旅行更多。（条件句）

examples.cn: 我小时候经常去看望我的祖父母。（过去常常）

grammar.title: 情态动词 'would' 的用法
grammar.explain: 'would' 可以用于表示条件句中的结果，或者表示过去常常发生的事情。

reading.en: Anna is starting nursing school. I am starting graduate school. We have less time now.

grammar.explain: 这个句型用于强调“一……就……”的意思，表示一个动作紧接着另一个动作发生。结构是：Hardly/Scarcely/Barely + had + 主语 + 动词过去分词 + when/before + 句子（一般过去时）。这是一种倒装句型，when 和 before 可以互换。

reading.cn: 让我给你讲讲 Rosemary Fell 的故事。首先要说的是，Rosemary 又有钱、又年轻、又时髦。她和丈夫 Philip 住在伦敦一栋大房子里——有仆人、孩子、司机。下雨的下午——她去 Curzon 街的奢侈店购物。
reading.note: Let me walk you through — 演示开场（KEY focus）/ To begin with — 三段式信号词（KEY focus）

reading.en: First of all, let me describe the setting. One February day, Rosemary went into a small antique shop. The owner showed her a tiny enamel box. "It's twenty-eight guineas," he said softly. She liked it but asked him to keep it for her — she'd think it over. Outside the shop, the rain had started.
reading.cn: 首先说说背景。二月里的一天——Rosemary 走进一家小古董店。店主拿出一个小巧的珐琅盒给她看。"二十八几尼，"他轻声说。她喜欢——但请他先替她留着——她要再想想。出店时——外面已经开始下雨。
reading.note: First of all — 演示信号词（KEY focus）/ Let me describe — 演示信号 / setting / antique 💡 = 古董

reading.en: Now let's move to the second part. As Rosemary stood by her car, a thin, pale young woman approached her and whispered, "Madam, may I have the price of a cup of tea?" Rosemary, on impulse, said something extraordinary: "Will you come home with me to my house and have tea?" The girl was too tired to refuse.
reading.cn: 现在讲第二部分。Rosemary 站在车旁时——一个又瘦又苍白的年轻女人走过来低声说："夫人，给我一杯茶的钱好吗？"Rosemary 一时冲动——说了不寻常的一句："愿意跟我回家——喝杯茶吗？"那女孩太累了——拒绝不了。
reading.note: Now let's move to — 演示信号词（KEY focus·过渡）/ on impulse 💡 = 一时冲动

reading.en: Moving on to the climax — Rosemary brought the girl, whose name was Miss Smith, into her warm sitting room. She gave her tea, sandwiches, and a brandy. "How adventurous of me," Rosemary thought. She felt thrilled, almost like the heroine of a Russian novel. The girl ate slowly, saying nothing.
reading.cn: 讲到高潮部分——Rosemary 把这个女孩——叫 Smith 小姐——带进她暖和的客厅。她给她茶、三明治、白兰地。"我真有冒险精神，"Rosemary 心想。她兴奋得——简直像俄国小说里的女主角。那女孩慢慢吃着——一句话也不说。
reading.note: Moving on to — 演示信号词（KEY focus·递进）/ adventurous 💡 = 有冒险精神的 / heroine 💡 = 女主角

reading.en: At this point, Philip walked in. He stared at the strange girl. He took Rosemary aside. "Who is she?" he asked quietly. "She's so pretty — strikingly so. I haven't been so struck for years." He smiled. "You can't keep her. It's quite impossible. But she's lovely." He went back to his study.
reading.cn: 讲到这里——Philip 进来了。他盯着这个陌生女孩看。他把 Rosemary 拉到一边。"她是谁？"他低声问。"她真漂亮——惊艳的那种漂亮。我好多年没这么吃惊过了。"他笑了。"你不能留她——这绝不可能。但她真好看。"他回了书房。
reading.note: At this point — 演示信号词（KEY focus·此刻）/ strikingly 💡 = 惊人地

reading.en: Finally, here's how it ended. Rosemary went to her room, opened her purse, and gave the girl five pounds. She sent her away politely. Then she stood in front of the mirror, fixed her hair, and walked into Philip's study. "Philip," she said, smiling, "may I have that little box I told you about? Twenty-eight guineas — am I pretty?"
reading.cn: 最后说说结局。Rosemary 走进自己房间——打开钱包——给了女孩五英镑。礼貌地送她走了。然后她站在镜子前——整理头发——走进 Philip 的书房。"Philip，"她笑着说，"可以让我买那个小盒子吗？我跟你说过的那个——二十八几尼——我漂亮吗？"
reading.note: Finally / here's how it ended — 演示信号词（KEY focus·收尾）/ 故事关键反转：Rosemary 嫉妒，赶走了女孩

output.sample: Rosemary led Miss Smith into her opulent drawing-room. "Do sit down," she said, gesturing towards a plush armchair. "I'll have Cook bring us some tea. Are you terribly hungry, dear? We have some dainty pastries." Miss Smith, still a little bewildered, murmured her thanks. Rosemary felt a rush of satisfaction. It was exquisite to be a benevolent hostess, extending her generosity to someone so utterly in need. The silver teapot arrived, steaming gently, and Rosemary poured two cups. "Tell me, Miss Smith," she began, "where are you from? Why do you have nowhere to go?"
output.prompt: 请以 "A Cup of Tea" 故事中的 Rosemary 为主角，续写一个短篇故事。故事内容可以围绕她和 Miss Smith 共度下午茶的场景展开，描述她们的对话、Rosemary 的内心活动，以及她对这次“冒险”的感受。请在故事中体现至少一个本课学到的词汇（如 delighted, exquisite, hostess, dainty, generosity）和至少一个实用表达（如 Could you spare a moment?, I'm terribly hungry., nowhere to go.）。
output.cn: 请以 "A Cup of Tea" 故事中的 Rosemary 为主角，续写一个短篇故事。故事内容可以围绕她和 Miss Smith 共度下午茶的场景展开，描述她们的对话、Rosemary 的内心活动，以及她对这次“冒险”的感受。请在故事中体现至少一个本课学到的词汇（如 delighted, exquisite, hostess, dainty, generosity）和至少一个实用表达（如 Could you spare a moment?, I'm terribly hungry., nowhere to go.）。

listening.audio: One rainy afternoon, Rosemary was shopping in a small antique shop. She saw a tiny, exquisite enamel box. "How much is this?" she asked. The shopkeeper replied, "Twenty-eight guineas, madam." Rosemary hesitated. It was more than she expected. Just then, a young woman, shivering and poorly dressed, entered the shop. "Excuse me, could you spare a moment?" she whispered to Rosemary. "I'm terribly hungry, and I have nowhere to go." A sudden idea delighted Rosemary. "Come home with me," she said impulsively. "You shall have a cup of tea, and perhaps something to eat." The young woman, whose name was Miss Smith, looked surprised but gratefully accepted. Rosemary imagined herself as a benevolent hostess, sharing her warmth and generosity. This unexpected rescue felt like a truly grand adventure, a deviation from her perfectly ordered, somewhat boring life.

grammar.title: 强调句 (Cleft Sentences)
grammar.explain: 强调句用于突出句子中的某个部分，通常使用 "It is/was... that/who..." 的结构。

在文学作品和日常叙述中，使用信号词可以帮助读者或听者更好地理解故事的结构和事件的进展。典型的三段式信号词可以是：
导入 (Introduction): "One day...", "Once upon a time...", "It began when..."
发展 (Development): "Suddenly...", "Meanwhile...", "As a result..."
结局 (Conclusion): "Eventually...", "In the end...", "Finally..."

listening.audio: After settling into her new apartment, Mei decided to write down a list. This list outlines her new life, she thought. She wanted to organize her thoughts and goals. First, she listed her daily routine: wake up early, exercise, work on her projects, and explore the neighborhood. Next, she wrote down essential items for her apartment, like a comfortable chair and some plants. Mei also included a section for new opportunities. I want to join a local book club and volunteer, she noted. She knew it would take time to adjust, but having a clear outline made her feel more confident about her new beginning. Her list was not just tasks, it was a vision. It helped her see how each step would contribute to the life she envisioned in San Francisco.

listening.audio: Mei sat by her window, looking out at the new city. It was beautiful, but also very different. She thought about her hometown and smiled sadly. 'I ______ the bookstore,' she whispered to herself. There was a small bookstore in her old neighborhood, a place she visited almost every week. It wasn't just a shop; it was a quiet corner where she could spend hours browsing books, enjoying the smell of old paper, and finding new stories. The friendly owner always had a recommendation for her. In this new city, there were big modern bookstores, but they didn't feel the same. They lacked the familiar warmth and personal touch. Mei realized it wasn't just the books she missed; it was the entire experience, the sense of community, and the comfort of a familiar place. She knew she needed to explore and find new favorite spots here, but for now, the memory of her old bookstore brought a bittersweet feeling. It was a reminder of home, a place she cherished.

grammar.title: 非限制性定语从句
grammar.explain: 非限制性定语从句用来补充说明先行词，它与先行词的关系不紧密，通常用逗号隔开，即使去掉也不影响主句的意义。

reading.en: True! nervous, very, very dreadfully nervous I had been and am. But why will you say that I am mad? Listen — observe how calmly, how healthily I can tell you the whole story.
reading.cn: 没错！我紧张，非常、非常可怕地紧张过，现在仍然紧张。可你为什么偏说我疯了？听着——你看我能多平静、多正常地把整件事讲给你听。
reading.note: True! — emphatic interjection / 'very, very dreadfully' — repetition for emphasis (KEY focus)

reading.en: It is impossible to say how the idea first entered my brain — but, once conceived, it haunted me day and night. I loved the old man. He had never wronged me. He had never given me insult. But there was his eye — yes, it was his eye!
reading.cn: 我说不清这念头是怎么钻进我脑子里的——但一旦冒出来，便日夜缠着我。我爱那位老人。他从没害过我。从没冒犯过我。但他有那只眼睛——对，就是那只眼睛！
reading.note: Past perfect (had wronged) + emphatic repetition ('his eye — yes, it was his eye!')

reading.en: One of his eyes resembled that of a vulture — a pale blue eye, with a film over it. Whenever it fell upon me, my blood ran cold. Slowly, very slowly — I made up my mind to take the life of the old man, and rid myself of the eye for ever.
reading.cn: 他的一只眼睛像秃鹫的——苍蓝色，覆着一层翳。每当那只眼落在我身上，我的血就发凉。慢慢地，非常慢——我下定决心要取那位老人的性命，永远摆脱那只眼。
reading.note: Slowly, very slowly — adverb repetition for pacing (KEY focus)

reading.en: Now this is the point — you fancy me mad. Madmen know nothing. But you should have seen me. You should have seen how wisely I proceeded — with what caution, with what foresight, with what dissimulation I went to work!
reading.cn: 听好——你以为我疯了。疯子什么都不懂。可你真该看看我。真该看看我是多么聪明地动手——多么谨慎、多么有远见、多么会掩饰！
reading.note: should have seen — modal perfect (L44 review) + 'with what... with what... with what...' — anaphora (KEY focus)

reading.en: For seven nights I opened the old man's door — slowly, slowly, just enough to put my head in. And every night I shone a single ray of lantern-light upon his eye. Every night the eye was closed. The eye was the offense, not the man.
reading.cn: 整整七夜，我都打开那位老人的房门——慢慢地、慢慢地，刚好够把头探进去。每一夜，我都把一束灯笼光打在他的眼上。每一夜，那只眼都是闭着的。冒犯我的是那只眼，不是那个人。
reading.note: Past simple narrative + repetition ('every night... every night...')

reading.en: On the eighth night, the eye was open — open and looking at me. Fury seized me. I rushed in. I dragged him to the floor. In an instant, it was done. The old man was dead.
reading.cn: 第八夜，那只眼睁开了——睁开着，看着我。狂怒攫住了我。我冲了进去。把他拽倒在地。一瞬间，事情就完了。老人死了。
reading.note: Sequence of short sentences — Poe's escalation technique

reading.en: I dismembered the body. I hid it under the floorboards. So cleverly had I done my work that no human eye — not even his — could have detected anything wrong. At four o'clock, the police came. I led them through the house, calm as a stone.
reading.cn: 我把尸体处理了。我藏在地板下。我做得如此巧妙，连人的眼睛——甚至他的——也察觉不出任何不对。凌晨四点，警察来了。我领他们走过整间屋子，镇定得像块石头。
reading.note: So cleverly had I done... — so + adverb inversion (L52 review)

reading.en: We sat. They chatted. But after a while, my head began to ache, and I fancied a ringing in my ears. It was a low, dull, quick sound — much like a watch makes when wrapped in cotton. I knew that sound. It grew louder — louder — louder. Why would they not be gone?
reading.cn: 我们坐下。他们闲聊。可没多久，我的头开始痛，我觉得耳朵里有一阵嗡鸣。那是一种低沉、闷哑、急促的声响——很像怀表用棉花裹住时的声音。我认得这声音。它越响越大——越响越大——越响越大。他们怎么还不走？
reading.note: Repetition 'louder — louder — louder' (KEY focus) + free indirect (Why would they not be gone?)

reading.en: "Villains!" I shrieked. "Dissemble no more! I admit the deed! Tear up the planks! — here, here! — it is the beating of his hideous heart!" — and I had betrayed myself by the tell-tale heart that was, all along, my own.
reading.cn: "恶棍！"我尖叫。"别再装了！我承认！撬开地板！——这里，这里！——是他那颗可憎的心还在跳！"——我被那颗告密的心出卖了，而那颗心，从头到尾，是我自己的。
reading.note: Closing — repetition ('here, here!') + final irony

listening.audio: Priya found Mei sitting alone in her room, tears silently streaming down her face. Mei had just received terrible news from home, and her world felt like it was falling apart. She was heartbroken and couldn't stop crying. Priya didn't say much at first. She just sat next to Mei, offering a quiet, comforting presence. After a while, Mei looked up, her eyes red and swollen. "It's just… so much to handle," Mei whispered. Priya gently put an arm around her. "I'm so sorry you're going through this, Mei. Remember what I always say? Real friends show up when it matters. I'm here for you, whatever you need." Mei leaned into Priya, finding warmth and support. "Thank you, Priya. It means a lot to know you're here." Priya just held her, letting Mei cry until she felt a little better. Sometimes, just having a friend by your side is all the comfort you need.

grammar.explain:
'Should' 用于表达建议、责任或预期。'Shouldn't' 是 'should not' 的缩写，用于表达不建议做的事情或不应该发生的事情。 

核心用法：

*   **建议或义务：** 你应该做某事 (You should do something.)
*   **不建议或不应该：** 你不应该做某事 (You shouldn't do something.)
*   **预期（较少见在此级别）：** 某事应该发生 (Something should happen.)

grammar.explain:

核心用法：

*   **强调行为本身：** 尤其是当这个行为作为句子的主题时。
*   **通常指一般性的行为或习惯：** 而不是某个特定的、一次性发生的动作。

listening.audio: It was late October, and Mei was feeling tired. She had been working hard, studying for her English classes, and helping with chores at her host family's home. Every morning she woke up early and her days were full. She often felt a little dizzy. Mei sat down with her journal, thinking about her past few weeks. "I'm always busy," she wrote. "Rest isn't a luxury. It's a necessity, especially when I'm studying a new language and living in a new culture. I shouldn't feel guilty about taking a break." She realized she was feeling overwhelmed and close to burnout. Mei decided to make a change. She made a new schedule that included specific times for relaxation. She talked to her host mother, Mrs. Smith, about her feelings, and Mrs. Smith was very understanding. "Mei, you're right. Everyone needs time to recharge," Mrs. Smith said. From then on, Mei started taking more breaks. She would read a book, listen to music, or just sit quietly for a while. She noticed a big difference. She felt more energetic and focused. Her English studies even improved because she wasn't so tired all the time. Mei learned that taking care of herself was just as important as working hard.

reading.en: The policeman walked his beat as midnight approached. The wind was cold, the streets nearly empty. While most citizens were home asleep, he was still on duty.
reading.cn: 午夜将近，警察走着他的巡逻线。风很冷，街上几乎没人。当大多数市民都在家睡觉时，他还在值勤。
reading.note: While + clause — contrast of simultaneous states (KEY focus)

reading.en: In a darkened doorway stood a man, an unlit cigar in his mouth. As the policeman approached, the man spoke quickly. "It's all right, officer — I'm waiting for a friend. Twenty years ago tonight, I had dinner here with my best friend, Jimmy."
reading.cn: 一个昏暗的门洞里站着一个人，嘴里叼着一支没点燃的雪茄。警察走近时，那人迅速开口。"没事，警官——我在等一个朋友。二十年前的今晚，我和我最好的朋友吉米在这里吃过饭。"
reading.note: In a darkened doorway stood... — fronted adverbial inversion (L52 review)

reading.en: "We made a pact," Bob continued, striking a match. "No matter where life took us, we would meet right here, twenty years to the night. Jimmy stayed in New York. I went West."
reading.cn: "我们立了个誓，"鲍勃接着说，划亮一根火柴。"不管人生把我们带到哪里，二十年后的这一晚，我们都要回到这儿见面。吉米留在了纽约。我去了西部。"
reading.note: striking a match — present participle (L51 review)

reading.en: By the light of the match, the policeman saw a face — a man with sharp, pale eyes and a small white scar near the right eyebrow. While Bob talked happily of his Western fortune, the officer's expression had changed. But Bob, glowing with anticipation, did not notice.
reading.cn: 火柴的光照在那人的脸上——一双锐利的、苍白的眼睛，右眉边一道细细的白色伤疤。当鲍勃兴致勃勃地讲他在西部发家的事时，警察的神情已经变了。可鲍勃满怀期待，没注意到。
reading.note: While Bob talked... — contrast clause / glowing with anticipation — participial (L51 review)

reading.en: "I made it big in the West," Bob said. "Money, business, everything. Jimmy was a slow, plain sort of fellow — by comparison, I always thought I'd be the one to amount to something."
reading.cn: "我在西部干出了大名堂，"鲍勃说。"钱、生意，什么都有。吉米是个慢吞吞、不起眼的家伙——比起来，我一直觉得能有出息的会是我。"
reading.note: By comparison... — contrast preposition (KEY focus)

reading.en: The policeman wished Bob luck and walked on. Twenty minutes later, another man approached the doorway, in a long overcoat, collar turned up. "Bob, is that you?" he asked. "Jimmy!" Bob cried. They shook hands warmly.
reading.cn: 警察祝鲍勃好运，便走开了。二十分钟后，另一个人走近门洞，穿着长大衣，领子翻起来。"鲍勃，是你吗？"他问。"吉米！"鲍勃喊。两人热情地握了手。
reading.note: Sequence of action — narrative continuity

reading.en: Walking arm in arm, the two men crossed the street, talking of old times. Whereas Bob spoke loudly and laughed often, the other man was quiet, glancing sideways from time to time.
reading.cn: 两人挽着胳膊穿过街，聊着过去的事。鲍勃声音洪亮、时不时大笑，而另一人却很安静，时不时朝侧面瞥一眼。
reading.note: Whereas + clause — formal contrast (KEY focus)

reading.en: Beneath a streetlamp, Bob looked closely at the man for the first time. He stopped walking. "You're not Jimmy," he said slowly. "Jimmy had a Roman nose. Yours is a pug nose. In contrast to him, you're —" He froze.
reading.cn: 在一盏路灯下，鲍勃第一次仔细看了那人一眼。他停下脚步。"你不是吉米，"他慢慢说。"吉米是罗马鼻。你的是塌鼻子。和他比起来，你——"他僵住了。
reading.note: In contrast to him... — contrast preposition (KEY focus)

reading.en: The man pulled out a badge. "You're under arrest, Bob. Chicago wired us. Jimmy Wells was the policeman you spoke with twenty minutes ago. He recognized you when you struck the match. Unlike a stranger, he could not arrest you himself. He left a note." The note read: "Bob, I was at the appointed place on time. — Jimmy."
reading.cn: 那人掏出警徽。"你被捕了，鲍勃。芝加哥发了电报。吉米·韦尔斯就是二十分钟前和你说话的那个警察。你划火柴时他认出了你。和一个陌生人不同的是，他没法亲自逮捕你。他留下了一张纸条。"纸条上写着："鲍勃，我准时到了约定的地方。——吉米。"
reading.note: Unlike a stranger... — contrast preposition (KEY focus) + closing aphorism

listening.audio: Linda usually doesn't pay much attention to her health. She feels fine most of the time. But recently, she had her annual medical check-up. The results showed a minor issue: an irregular heartbeat, also known as arrhythmia. The doctor said, "It's not severe, but we need to monitor it. Technology shapes how we live, especially in healthcare now. There are many new ways to track your health." Linda was a bit worried but also curious. The doctor recommended a wearable device to monitor her heart rhythm daily. "This watch can collect data on your heart rate and alert you if there's anything unusual," the doctor explained. "It's a great example of how technology allows for early detection and prevention." Linda thought about it. She realized that technology could indeed help her manage her health better. She decided to try the wearable device. She hoped it would help her understand her body and keep her healthy. A few weeks later, Linda began to use the wearable device. It recorded her heart rate and activity levels. She could see real-time data on her phone. One day, the watch sent an alert: abnormal heart rate. The doctor confirmed that the watch helped catch a subtle change that might have been missed otherwise. "See, technology shapes how we live and extends to how we manage our health. This early detection is very important," the doctor stated. Linda was relieved and grateful. She learned that technology is not just about entertainment; it's also a powerful tool for personal health management.

listening.audio: It was a quiet Tuesday evening. I was sitting at my desk, deep in revision for my history exam. The house was still, except for the gentle hum of my laptop. Suddenly, my phone buzzed loudly on the table. It was my mom. I picked it up, expecting her to remind me about something trivial. But her voice was shaky. "The news broke while I was studying," she began, "Grandma had a stroke." My heart dropped. I couldn't believe what I was hearing. "Is she okay? Is she conscious?" I asked, my own voice trembling. Mom said, "She's in the hospital. The doctors are taking care of her. We're waiting for an update." I felt a mix of shock and worry. My grandma is usually so strong and healthy. I immediately packed a small bag and headed to the hospital. When I saw her, she was pale but trying to smile. It was a huge relief to see her conscious, even though she was still weak. I stayed by her side, holding her hand, for a long time that night.

listening.audio: Have you ever thought about the magic of small habits? It's like compound interest, but for your life. Imagine you want to read more. Instead of trying to read a whole book in one go, start with just one page a day. It seems like a tiny step, right? But if you are consistent, that one page a day will compound. In a month, you've read about 30 pages. In a year, over 365 pages – that's often more than one book! The magic isn't in the size of the habit, but in its consistency and the power of compounding. This principle applies to everything: learning a new language, getting fit, or even saving money. Don't underestimate the power of starting small. Sustainable habits are built not on grand gestures, but on consistent, tiny actions that compound over time, creating incredible momentum. So, what small habit can you start today that will compound into something great tomorrow?

reading.en: Mei wanted to learn English. For years, she had told herself she would start "when she had time" — when work slowed down, when the weekend came, when life was less busy. But weekends turned into more weekends. Years passed. She still could not introduce herself in English without panic.
reading.cn: 美想学英语。几年来——她一直对自己说——"等有时间"再开始——等工作不忙了、等周末了、等生活没那么乱了。但周末变成一个又一个周末。几年过去。她仍然无法不慌张地用英语自我介绍。
reading.note: had told herself / had time / Years passed — narrative tense mix / she still could not — 现在能力否定

reading.en: Then one day she changed her approach. "I will not wait for time," she said. "I will give myself ten minutes a day. Just ten." Ten minutes felt small — almost too small to matter. But that was the point. Big goals had crushed her before. A small goal she could keep.
reading.cn: 然后有一天她换了思路。"我不等时间了，"她说。"我每天给自己十分钟。就十分钟。"十分钟感觉很小——小到几乎无足轻重。但那正是关键。之前——大目标把她压垮了。小目标——她守得住。
reading.note: Big goals had crushed her before — past perfect / A small goal she could keep — 倒装强调 / approach 💡 = 方式

reading.en: On day one, she watched a three-minute YouTube video and copied two sentences. On day fifteen, she felt comfortable saying "Could you say that again, please?" On day sixty, she watched her first short film without subtitles. The progress, measured day by day, looked tiny. Measured month by month, it became real.
reading.cn: 第一天——她看了三分钟 YouTube 视频——抄了两句话。第十五天——她敢轻松地说"麻烦再说一遍"。第六十天——她看了第一部不带字幕的短片。进步——一天一天地看——很小。一个月一个月地看——它就成真了。
reading.note: measured day by day — 过去分词短语作状语（KEY focus）/ measured month by month — 同上

reading.en: Mei learned three principles. First, the rule of small steps: each habit must be small enough that you cannot say no. Second, the rule of compounding: tiny actions, repeated daily, build something nothing-big-on-day-one can. Third, the rule of identity: you are not what you say — you are what you do every day.
reading.cn: 美学到了三条原则。第一——小步原则：每个习惯都要小到——你无法说'不'。第二——复利原则：微小动作——每天重复——能建出'第一天什么都不大'的东西所建不出的。第三——身份原则：你不是你说的——你是你每天做的。
reading.note: tiny actions, repeated daily — 过去分词作定语 / 三条原则结构清晰：first / second / third / compounding 💡 = 复利的

reading.en: Compared with her friend Lei, who had bought ten language apps and used none of them for more than a week, Mei had advanced far. Lei had wished for fluent English. Mei had practiced ten minutes daily. After a year, Mei could speak. Lei could not. The difference was not talent. It was structure.

reading.note: Compared with her friend — 过去分词短语作开头（KEY focus）/ Lei, who had bought ten apps — 非限定性定语从句 / had wished / had practiced — past perfect

reading.en: Today Mei runs a small English club at her workplace. She tells new members: "Pick something you can do even on your worst day. Then do it on your worst day. The trick is not motivation. The trick is making the first step so small that motivation does not get a vote." Small habits, compounding over time, make a different person.

But now, seeing how worried her dad looked, Mei knew it was time to stop. “Dad, I know we disagree, but there's no use arguing anymore. Mom needs us to be strong, not fighting.” Her dad looked at her, his eyes red-rimmed and tired. “You're right, Mei. You're absolutely right. I'm just so exhausted and worried.” Mei reached for his hand. “I know, Dad. We'll get through this together. No matter what happens, we're a team.” Her dad squeezed her hand, a small, grateful smile touching his lips. “A team. Yes. And perhaps we can discuss the options calmly later, when we both have clearer heads.” Mei nodded. It was a small step, but a hopeful one.

reading.en: Then she saw it: a small cat trying to hide under a green table. The cat was pressing itself against the table to keep dry, but the rain was dripping from above. "I'm going to get that cat," she said. The husband did not look up from his book. "Don't get wet," he said.

listening.audio: The American couple was in Italy, and it was raining. The wife, George, stood at the window, looking out. "I'm going down to get that cat," she said to her husband, George. "The poor kitty is wet in the rain." Her husband didn't look up from his book. George went downstairs. The innkeeper stood in the doorway, helping a maid with something. He greeted George warmly. "It's raining hard," he said. George went out to the porch. There was a cat, trying to make itself small under a wet table. George reached out, but the cat moved away. Then, the innkeeper's maid came out with an umbrella. "I'll help you, signora," she said, holding the umbrella over George. But when they got to the table, the cat was gone. George returned upstairs, disappointed. "I couldn't find it," she told her husband. "It was gone." Later, there was a knock on their door. The innkeeper's maid stood there, holding a large, beautiful cat. "The innkeeper asked me to bring this to you, signora," she said.

grammar.title: 混合条件句 (Mixed Conditionals)
grammar.explain: 混合条件句结合了不同时态的条件句。常见的形式是：如果过去发生了某事（与过去事实相反的假设），那么现在会是何种情况（对现在情况的假设）。

examples.cn: 如果我带了伞，我现在就不会湿了。 (过去：没带伞，现在：湿了)
examples.en: If I had brought an umbrella, I wouldn't be wet now.

examples.cn: 如果她找到了那只猫，她现在就会很高兴。 (过去：没找到猫，现在：不高兴)
examples.en: If she had found the cat, she would be happy now.

grammar.title: 过去完成时与一般现在时的结合

output.sample: In my experience, "The more I rest, the better I do" is absolutely true. During college, I used to pull all-nighters before exams, thinking that more study time meant better grades. However, I often felt exhausted and couldn't focus during the actual exam. My mind was foggy, and I made silly mistakes. Later, I changed my approach. I made sure to get at least 7-8 hours of sleep before big exams and scheduled short breaks during study sessions. To my surprise, I felt much more alert, my memory improved, and I could recall information more easily. Even with fewer "study hours" logged, the quality of my learning and my performance significantly improved. It taught me that a well-rested mind is the best tool for effective learning and problem-solving.

output.sample:
Entry: April 25th

It's hard to believe how fast time flies. This spring has been a whirlwind of new experiences, and I'm so grateful for every moment. As I look ahead to the next year, I'm starting to think about where I might be. 

I'm not entirely sure where I'll end up—maybe I'll stay in this city, or perhaps I’ll explore a new country. The possibilities are endless, and that's both exciting and a little daunting. 

Regardless of where I end up, I know I want to keep learning and growing. I want to embrace new challenges, meet interesting people, and continue to step out of my comfort zone. I hope to carry with me the openness and curiosity I’ve found this spring. I want to cherish every new experience and build a life that feels authentic to me, no matter the location. The journey itself is what matters most.

reading.en: Framton Nuttel was a man whose nerves needed rest. His sister had given him letters of introduction to several country families.
reading.cn: 弗兰顿·纳特尔是个神经紧张、需要静养的人。他姐姐给了他几封介绍信，让他去拜访几户乡下人家。
reading.note: Reduced relative + past perfect

reading.en: In a country house, he was met by Mrs. Sappleton's fifteen-year-old niece, Vera. "My aunt will be down in fifteen minutes," she said. "Until then, I must do my best to entertain you."
reading.cn: 在一栋乡下房子里，他被萨普尔顿太太那位十五岁的侄女维拉接待。"我姑姑十五分钟之内就下来，"她说。"在那之前，我得尽量让你不无聊。"
reading.note: Direct speech opener

reading.en: Vera asked whether Framton knew her aunt at all. Framton replied that he knew almost nothing about her — just her name and address.
reading.cn: 维拉问弗兰顿对她姑姑究竟了解多少。弗兰顿回答说，他几乎什么也不知道——只知道她的名字和地址。
reading.note: Reported speech: asked whether / replied that (L47 KEY focus)

reading.en: "Then I should tell you the great tragedy," Vera said softly. She pointed to the open French window. "Three years ago, my aunt's husband and her two younger brothers went out that window to hunt. They never returned. They drowned in a bog."
reading.cn: "那我应该把那场大悲剧告诉你，"维拉轻声说。她指着那扇开着的落地窗。"三年前，我姑姑的丈夫和她两个弟弟从那扇窗户出去打猎。他们再也没回来。他们都陷进沼泽淹死了。"
reading.note: Past simple narrative + 'never returned' (emphatic)

reading.en: Vera said her aunt still expected them to walk back through the window any minute. "That is why," Vera whispered, "the window is kept open until dusk every evening — even now."
reading.cn: 维拉说，姑姑仍然以为他们随时会从那扇窗户走回来。"所以，"维拉低声说，"每天傍晚天黑之前，那扇窗都开着——一直到现在。"
reading.note: Reported speech: said her aunt expected... (backshift)

reading.en: Mrs. Sappleton came in and apologized for being late. She told Framton that her husband and brothers would be home from hunting any moment. "They always come in through that window," she said cheerfully.
reading.cn: 萨普尔顿太太进来，为自己来晚了道歉。她告诉弗兰顿，她丈夫和弟弟随时可能打完猎回家。"他们总是从那扇窗户进来，"她快活地说。
reading.note: Reported speech: told Framton that + would (future-in-past)

reading.en: Framton listened in horror. He believed Mrs. Sappleton was suffering from a delusion — believing the dead would walk in. Then, through the open window, three figures appeared, carrying guns.
reading.cn: 弗兰顿越听越恐惧。他以为萨普尔顿太太得了妄想症——以为死人会走回来。这时，三个身影从那扇开着的窗户走了进来，肩上扛着猎枪。
reading.note: Believed + that-clause (reported belief) + sequence

reading.en: Framton ran. He did not stop running until he reached the road. Mrs. Sappleton's husband was puzzled. "What a strange man," he said. "He bolted as if he had seen a ghost."
reading.cn: 弗兰顿跑了。他一口气跑到马路上才停下。萨普尔顿先生很困惑。"这人真奇怪，"他说。"跑得跟见了鬼一样。"
reading.note: did not + V until + reached + 'as if + had seen' (subjunctive simile)

reading.en: Vera explained, with a face of innocent regret, that Framton had a horror of dogs — once, in India, he had been chased into a graveyard by a pack of pariah dogs. Romance at short notice was her specialty.
reading.cn: 维拉一脸天真的惋惜，解释说弗兰顿见不得狗——有一次在印度，他被一群野狗追进了一座墓地。"临时即兴编故事"是她的拿手好戏。
reading.note: Closing aphorism — Saki's famous line

listening.audio: Framton Nuttel was visiting the Sappletons. He hoped the quiet country life would calm his nerves. Mrs. Sappleton was not in the room yet, so his niece, Vera, entertained him. Vera pointed to a large French window that was open. “Through that window, three years ago to a day, her husband and her two young brothers went off for their day’s shooting,” said Vera, “and they never came back. Their bodies were never recovered. And the window is kept open every evening until dark, in case they should return.” Framton listened with growing horror. Suddenly, Mrs. Sappleton entered and cheerfully spoke of her husband and brothers returning soon through that very window. Framton looked at Vera, who calmly watched the window. Just then, three figures walked across the lawn towards the window. Framton, seeing ghosts, grabbed his hat and stick and ran out as fast as he could. Mrs. Sappleton was confused. “He saw the spaniel and thought it was a ghost!” Vera said.

listening.audio: Mei received an offer to be a research assistant. Her host mother said, "Congratulations are in order! I knew you could do it." Mei was very excited about the news. They decided to celebrate her success tonight.

reading.en: Many years ago, at a dinner party, a banker and a young lawyer began to argue about prison. The banker said that life imprisonment was crueler than the death penalty. The lawyer disagreed: "To live somehow is better than not to live at all." The banker shouted, "I bet you two million rubles you couldn't stay in solitary confinement for five years!" "Make it fifteen," said the lawyer.
reading.cn: 许多年前——在一次晚宴上——一个银行家和一个年轻律师争论起监狱来。银行家说终身监禁比死刑更残酷。律师不同意："无论怎样活着——也好过完全不活。"银行家喊道："我赌你两百万卢布——你五年单独监禁都待不下！""那就十五年吧，"律师说。
reading.note: argued about — argue + about + topic / would be (虚拟·非现实建议) / 'I bet you ...' — informal challenge structure

reading.en: And so the bet began. The lawyer was locked in a small room in the banker's garden. He was allowed books, music, wine, and letters — but no contact with people. For the first year, he read light novels and played the piano. He often complained.
reading.cn: 于是赌局开始了。律师被锁在银行家花园里的一间小屋里。他可以有书、音乐、酒、信件——但不能和任何人接触。第一年——他读些轻松的小说——弹钢琴。他常常抱怨。
reading.note: was locked / was allowed — past simple passive (B1 重点) / for the first year — for + 时段

reading.en: By the second year, music had stopped. He read only the classics. By the fifth year, he wrote that he wanted no more wine — that he had not touched it in months. By the tenth year, he was reading the Bible, then philosophy, then six hundred volumes of every kind of book.
reading.cn: 到了第二年——音乐停了。他只读经典。到了第五年——他写信说不要再送酒了——他已经几个月没碰它了。到了第十年——他在读《圣经》——然后哲学——然后六百卷各类书籍。
reading.note: by + 时间 — 到...为止 / had stopped, had not touched — past perfect for prior states / he wrote that — reported speech

reading.en: Fifteen years passed. On the eve of the final day, the banker — who had lost most of his fortune — could not pay the two million. "If he wins, I'll be ruined," he thought. "But if he dies before tomorrow night, I'll keep everything." He took a key and went into the garden.
reading.cn: 十五年过去了。最后一天的前夕——银行家——他已经输掉了大部分财产——拿不出那两百万。"如果他赢——我就完了，"他想。"但如果他在明晚之前死掉——我就什么都保得住。"他拿了一把钥匙——走进花园。
reading.note: had lost — past perfect / 'If he wins, I'll be ruined' — first conditional (现实条件) / 'If he dies, I'll keep' — first conditional with sinister intent

reading.en: Through the small window, the banker saw a thin man at a table, asleep over a letter. The lawyer's hair had turned grey, his hands looked like an old man's hands. The banker read the letter quietly. In it, the lawyer wrote that he had read everything, had seen everything in books, and had come to despise the wealth that men killed each other for.
reading.cn: 透过那扇小窗——银行家看见一个瘦弱的人趴在桌上——在一封信上睡着了。律师的头发已经变白——双手像个老人的手。银行家悄悄读了那封信。信中——律师写道：他已经读完了一切——在书里见过了一切——已经鄙视那种人们为了它而互相残杀的财富。
reading.note: had turned, had read, had come to — past perfect chain / 'wealth that men killed each other for' — relative clause

reading.en: "I despise your money," the lawyer had written, "and to show I do, I will leave this room five hours before the bet ends. So I will lose. So I am free." The banker kissed the strange man's head and wept. He had been ready to do something terrible — and instead, the man's words had saved them both.
reading.cn: "我鄙视你的钱，"律师写道。"为了证明这一点——我会在赌约结束前五小时离开这个房间。所以我输了。所以我自由了。"银行家亲了亲那陌生人的头——哭了。他差一点就做了可怕的事——可律师的话——救了他们两个人。
reading.note: to show I do — purpose infinitive / had been ready / had saved — past perfect for the moment-of-realization timeline

output.cn: 请结合课文内容，思考律师的人生选择，并用英语表达你的看法。例如，他获得了什么？失去了什么？
output.sample: I think the lawyer's fifteen years of solitude for the bet was worth it in some ways, but not in others. He gained immense knowledge and wisdom from reading and studying, which allowed him to understand the world differently. This experience transformed him from a materialistic young man to someone who despised worldly wealth. However, he lost fifteen valuable years of his youth and social interaction. While he gained intellectual wealth, he sacrificed human connection and direct experience of life outside his confinement. Perhaps true wisdom also encompasses the understanding of human relationships and the complexities of society, which he missed during his isolation. So, while he gained a lot, I wouldn't say it was entirely worth it.
output.prompt: 你认为律师为赌约而选择的十五年独处生活是值得的吗？为什么？请用英文写一段话，阐述你的观点。

grammar.title: 高级连接词: Though/Although/Even though

listening.audio: Mary Maloney was six months pregnant. She was a happy woman, well-pleased with her husband, Patrick. He was a detective. One evening, Patrick came home and drank a large whiskey. He told Mary something that shocked her. She couldn't believe what she heard. Mary went to the cellar to get a leg of lamb for dinner. In a daze, she came back upstairs. Patrick was standing with his back to her, looking out the window. Without thinking, Mary hit him on the back of the head with the frozen lamb. He fell to the floor, dead. Mary quickly thought about what to do. She put the lamb in the oven. Then she went to the store, pretending to be normal. When she came back, she called the police. "My husband is dead!" she cried. Detectives arrived. They searched the house but found no murder weapon. Mary offered them the cooked lamb. "You gentlemen must be hungry," she said. The police ate the evidence, discussing how mysterious the case was. Mary Maloney smiled.

grammar.title: 强调句：It was ... that/who...
grammar.explain: 强调句用来突出句子中的某个部分，如主语、宾语或状语。结构是“It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who + 句子的其余部分”。that 用于强调物或人都可，who 专用于强调人。
