grammar.title: 省略表目的的介词 for
grammar.explain: 在某些口语或非正式的书面语中，表示目的的介词“for”有时可以省略，尤其是当目的非常明确时。但这并非所有情况都适用，通常限于表示“为了（做某事）”的结构，后面跟着动名词。

examples.cn: 她去地窖拿羊腿做晚餐。（原始句）
examples.en: She went to the cellar to get a leg of lamb for dinner.

examples.cn: 她去地窖拿羊腿晚餐。（省略 for，但此处 for 引导的是目的状语，省略后意思略有变化，变成 lamb dinner 这个词组）
examples.en: She went to the cellar to get a leg of lamb dinner.

examples.cn: 她去商店假装正常。（这里 for 并未省略，也不是 for dinner）
examples.en: She went to the store pretending to be normal.

grammar.title: 得体表达：委婉拒绝或提出请求
grammar.explain: 在英语交流中，尤其是情境像故事中 Mary 邀请侦探们吃饭时，即使对方是警察，为了显得礼貌和得体，也会使用一些委婉的表达方式。例如，使用情态动词 'must' 来表达一种推测性但带有关怀的建议，而不是直接命令。

examples.cn: “先生们一定饿了，”她说道。（委婉的建议，表示关怀）
examples.en: "You gentlemen must be hungry," she said.

examples.cn: 您能否告诉我发生了什么？（委婉地提出问题）
examples.en: Could you perhaps tell me what happened?

examples.cn: 恐怕我帮不了你。（委婉地拒绝）
examples.en: I'm afraid I can't help you with that.

expressions.scene: Mary was well-pleased with her husband.
She came back upstairs in a daze after hearing the news.
Without thinking, Mary hit him with the lamb.
The police found no evidence of foul play.
The detectives discussed how mysterious the case was.

reading.en: Mary Maloney was waiting for her husband to come home from work. The room was warm, the curtains drawn. Her sewing was on the table. She felt happy and calm. Her husband Patrick was a police detective, and she loved him more than anything.
reading.cn: 玛丽·马洛尼在等丈夫下班回家。屋里很暖和——窗帘拉上了。她的针线活放在桌上。她感到开心又平静。丈夫帕特里克是个警察侦探——她爱他胜过一切。
reading.note: story setup: warm domestic scene before the twist / past continuous: 'was waiting' / detective 💡 = 侦探

reading.en: When he came in, she said, "Hello, darling." He poured himself a strong drink. "Sit down," he told her. "I have something to tell you." She replied softly that she would listen. He explained, in a quick voice, that he was leaving her. He admitted there was someone else.
reading.cn: 他进来时——她说："亲爱的，你回来了。"他给自己倒了一杯烈酒。"坐下，"他对她说。"我有件事要告诉你。"她轻声回答说她会听。他用很快的语气解释——他要离开她了。他承认——他有别人了。
reading.note: reporting verbs cluster (KEY focus): said / told / replied / explained / admitted / 'there was someone else' — common phrasing

reading.en: Mary said nothing. She walked into the kitchen. From the freezer she took out a large frozen leg of lamb. She would cook it for dinner, she told herself. She carried it back into the living room. Patrick was standing with his back to her, looking at the window.
reading.cn: 玛丽什么都没说。她走进厨房。她从冷冻柜里拿出一只大块的冷冻羊腿。她对自己说——她要把它煮了当晚饭。她拿着它走回客厅。帕特里克背对着她——望着窗户。
reading.note: she would cook — past future / told herself — reflexive reporting / leg of lamb 💡 — 整句双关：羊腿

reading.en: She brought the lamb high above her head and hit him on the back of the head. He fell instantly. She put the lamb in the oven, set the temperature, and went out to the grocery store. "Hello, Sam!" she said brightly. "I need some peas. Patrick wants his dinner waiting when he gets home."
reading.cn: 她把羊腿高高举过头顶——朝他后脑砸下去。他立刻倒下。她把羊腿放进烤箱——设好温度——然后去了杂货店。"嗨，山姆！"她开朗地说。"我要些豌豆。帕特里克回家时——希望饭已经摆好了。"
reading.note: the murder hidden in domesticity / 'brightly' — adverb tone / fake present tense to keep alibi

reading.en: When she got home, she pretended to discover the body and called the police. The detectives — Patrick's own colleagues — searched the house carefully. They asked her many questions. They wondered what could have killed him. They couldn't find any weapon. "Whatever it was," one detective said, "it must be on the premises."
reading.cn: 她回家后——假装发现了尸体——给警察打了电话。侦探们——帕特里克自己的同事们——仔细搜查了房子。他们问了她很多问题。他们想——能是什么杀了他呢。他们找不到任何凶器。"不管那是什么，"一个侦探说。"它一定还在现场。"
reading.note: wondered / asked — reporting / could have killed (modal perfect) / on the premises = 在现场

reading.en: Mary, who was crying, suggested they have something to eat. "There's a leg of lamb in the oven," she said. "Please. Eat it for me." The detectives sat at the kitchen table and ate. "Whatever was used," one said with his mouth full, "the killer probably took it with him." In the next room, Mary began to laugh.
reading.cn: 玛丽哭着——建议他们吃点东西。"烤箱里有一只羊腿，"她说。"求求你们。替我吃了它吧。"侦探们坐到厨房桌前——吃了起来。"不管用的是什么——"一个嘴里塞满了食物地说。"凶手大概把它带走了。"隔壁房间里——玛丽笑了起来。
reading.note: suggested they have — suggest + that-clause (subjunctive trace) / 'with his mouth full' — preposition + adj phrase / the perfect twist: they ate the murder weapon

output.cn: 请描述 Mary Maloney 微笑的原因，并评价她的计划。
output.sample: Mary Maloney smiled because her plan worked perfectly. The detectives, unknowingly, ate the murder weapon, meaning there was no physical evidence left to connect her to the crime. She successfully framed the situation as a tragic accident, escaping blame. Her plan was indeed perfect in its execution; it was clever, ruthless, and ultimately effective in achieving her goal of avoiding punishment.
output.prompt: 你认为 Mary Maloney 在故事最后微笑的原因是什么？你觉得她的计划完美吗？请用英语回答，不少于 50 词。

grammar.explain: “fed up with” 用于表达对某人、某事或某种情况的厌烦或忍无可忍。它后面可以接名词、代词或动名词（-ing 形式）。

Using 'Drop out' and 'Tough it out'
grammar.explain: 'Drop out' 意思是“中途退出，退学”。'Tough it out' 意思是“坚持下去，挺过去”，通常指在困难时期。

reading.en: Final year. Statistics class. Three hours twice a week.
reading.cn: 最后一年。统计课。一周两次,每次三小时。
reading.note: 💡 final year / statistics — 学院词

reading.en: The professor reads slides. He never explains. He gets impatient when we ask questions.
reading.cn: 教授念 PPT。从不解释。我们问问题他还不耐烦。
reading.note: 💡 reads slides / never explains / impatient — B1 高级现在时叙述

reading.en: After two months, I am fed up. I tell Priya, "I'm fed up with this class. Three hours of slides."
reading.cn: 两个月后,我受够了。我对 Priya 说:"这门课我受够了。三小时的 PPT。"
reading.note: 💡 FED UP WITH · B1 习语·"受够了"

reading.en: She listens. "Have you written to him? Politely. Specifically."
reading.cn: 她听着。"你给他写信了吗?礼貌地。具体地。"
reading.note: 💡 written to him / politely / specifically — Priya 给具体策略·复用 L3#42 风格

reading.en: I haven't. I sit down and write. I name three concepts I am unclear on. I ask if he can spend ten minutes after class.
reading.cn: 我没。我坐下来写。我列出三个我没搞懂的概念。我问他能不能下课后给我十分钟。
reading.note: 💡 name + 名词 / unclear on / spend ten minutes — 复用 specifically + B1 学院

reading.en: He replies in an hour. "Yes. After Thursday's class." Sometimes complaining feels easier than asking. But asking is what changes things.
reading.cn: 他一小时后回:"好。周四下课后。"有时候抱怨比请教更容易。但请教才能改变事情。
reading.note: 💡 complaining / easier than asking — closing reflection·B1 高级 + 复用 "asking is professional" L3#64

listening.audio: Mei felt a knot of anxiety tighten in her stomach. It was her final year, and the workload was relentless. Especially "Advanced Calculus." The professor, Dr. Miller, was brilliant but demanding. Mei was constantly falling behind, even with extra study sessions. "I'm fed up with this class," she mumbled to her friend, Lisa, during a coffee break. "I just can't seem to grasp the concepts." Lisa nodded sympathetically. "I know, Mei. It's really tough. But you've come so far. Don't let this one class get you down. Maybe we can study together tonight?" Mei sighed. "I appreciate it, Lisa, but I'm just so overwhelmed. I've even thought about dropping out of this course." Lisa's eyes widened. "No way! You're so close to graduating! You just need to tough it out for a few more months." Mei leaned back, feeling the weight of her frustration. "I know, I know. It's just... I'm really fed up with feeling like I'm not smart enough." Lisa put a hand on Mei's arm. "That's not true, Mei. You're incredibly smart. This class is just a beast. We'll figure it out together. You're not alone."

output.sample: I'm fed up with the endless meetings at work. They always take up so much time and don't seem to lead anywhere productive. When I feel this way, I usually try to take a short break, maybe go for a walk, and then come back to my tasks with a clearer mind. Sometimes I also talk to my colleagues about it to see if they feel the same way and if we can find a solution together.

output.sample: My friend, Lily, recently opened her own small café. It was a dream she had worked on for years. The design of the café is brilliant—it's so cozy and welcoming. And her coffee, oh my gosh, it's truly exceptional! When I visited for the first time, I felt so proud of her. She really poured her heart into it, and it stands out from all the other cafés in the area. It's truly something special to see her dream come true. I told her, "You must be so proud of yourself! This is a brilliant achievement!"

That's a big

listening.audio: Mei was scrolling through her phone, sipping her morning tea. "Wow!" she exclaimed, a huge smile spreading across her face. Her host mother, Mrs. Peterson, looked up from her newspaper. "What's so exciting, dear?" "It's my sister, Wei! She won the school writing contest! And the article says, 'The story written by Wei is brilliant!'" Mei beamed, showing her phone screen to Mrs. Peterson. Mrs. Peterson leaned closer to read. "Oh, that's wonderful news, Mei! You must be so proud of her." "I am! I always knew she was a very creative writer. But 'brilliant'... that's a big compliment." "Indeed. To have your work described as brilliant is truly something special. It means it stands out, it's exceptional," Mrs. Peterson explained. "You should definitely call her and congratulate her."

reading.en: Wei's school sends me a copy of the school magazine. Wei wrote the cover story.
reading.cn: 薇学校给我寄了一本校刊。封面文章是薇写的。
reading.note: 💡 magazine / cover story — 复用 L3#56 学校认可

reading.en: The story, written by my fifteen-year-old sister, is brilliant.
reading.cn: 这篇故事——是我十五岁妹妹写的——写得真出彩。
reading.note: 💡 PASSIVE PARTICIPIAL · written by + 人 — 复用 L3#28 分词短语 + 升级被动

reading.en: It's about a girl who moves between two countries. The girl carries her grandmother's tea cup in her bag.
reading.cn: 故事讲一个女孩在两个国家之间穿梭。她包里装着奶奶的茶杯。
reading.note: 💡 a girl who / between two countries — 复用 "two homes" 主题 / 复用 L3#51 grandma 茶杯

reading.en: I read it three times. The girl is not me. But the tea cup is.
reading.cn: 我读了三遍。那个女孩不是我。但茶杯是。
reading.note: 💡 not me / but the tea cup is — closing reflection·B1 简短抒情

reading.en: I FaceTime Wei. "You wrote about us." She is quiet. "I wrote what I knew."
reading.cn: 我视频薇。"你写的是我们。"她沉默了:"我写的是我熟悉的。"
reading.note: 💡 wrote about us / wrote what I knew — 复用 quiet (L3#8) / 关系从句 what I knew

reading.en: Stories belong to whoever can write them down. My sister is now telling our story too.
reading.cn: 故事属于能把它写下来的人。我妹妹现在也在讲我们的故事。
reading.note: 💡 BELONG TO WHOEVER · 复用 whoever (L3#24) / closing reflection·B1 高级抒情

grammar.explain: “It is/was... that...” 是一种强调句型，用来强调句子的某个部分，如主语、宾语、时间状语、地点状语等。被强调的部分放在 "It is/was" 和 "that" 之间。
grammar.title: 强调句型：It is/was... that...

正是在昨天她赢得了比赛。（强调时间状语）

grammar.explain: "Brilliant" 在这里表示“极好的，非常棒的，出彩的”，常用来形容作品、想法、表现等。比 "good" 或 "great" 更有强调的意味。
grammar.title: 形容词 "brilliant" 的用法

那是个绝妙的主意！

fillBlanks.sentence: The children loved to play in the giant's ______.
fillBlanks.cn: 孩子们喜欢在巨人的花园里玩耍。

fillBlanks.sentence: The giant was very ______.
fillBlanks.cn: 巨人非常自私。

fillBlanks.sentence: He built a high ______ around his garden.
fillBlanks.cn: 他在花园周围筑起一道高墙。

fillBlanks.cn: 只有在自私的巨人的花园里，仍然是冬天。

reading.en: When the Giant returned home, he found the children playing in his garden. He had been away visiting his Cornish friend for seven years. By the time he came back, his garden had become the children's favorite place.
reading.cn: 巨人回家时，发现孩子们正在他的花园里玩。他离家走访康沃尔的朋友已有七年。等他回来时，他的花园已经成了孩子们最喜欢的地方。
reading.note: had been away + V-ing (duration to past) + by the time + past perfect

reading.en: "My own garden is my own garden," the Giant roared. "I will allow nobody to play in it but myself." He built a high wall around it and put up a sign: TRESPASSERS WILL BE PROSECUTED.
reading.cn: "我的花园是我的花园，"巨人怒吼。"除了我自己，谁都不许在里面玩。"他在花园四周筑起高墙，立了块牌子：闯入者必究。
reading.note: Direct speech + future passive (will be prosecuted)

reading.en: Once the wall had been built, Spring no longer came to that garden. Snow covered the grass. The North Wind moved in. Hail came every day. Only Winter remained — for the Giant had refused everyone else.
reading.cn: 墙一建好，春天就不再光顾那座花园了。雪铺满草地。北风搬了进来。冰雹每天都来。只有冬天留了下来——因为巨人把别人都拒之门外了。
reading.note: Once + past perfect passive (had been built) + 'for' (= because)

reading.en: One morning, the Giant heard music. A linnet was singing outside his window. He had not heard birdsong for so long that he thought spring had returned to the world. Through a small hole in the wall, the children had crept back in. Their laughter had brought spring with them.
reading.cn: 一天早晨，巨人听到了音乐。一只朱顶雀在窗外唱歌。他已经太久没听到鸟鸣，以为春天回到了人间。原来孩子们从墙上一个小洞钻了回来。他们的笑声把春天也带回来了。
reading.note: Multiple past perfects: had not heard / had returned / had crept / had brought (KEY focus)

reading.en: Every tree had blossomed except one — in the corner stood a small child who could not reach the lowest branch. The Giant lifted him gently. The tree burst into flower at once. The boy threw his arms around the Giant's neck and kissed him.
reading.cn: 除了角落里那一棵，每棵树都开了花。角落里有个小男孩，够不到最低的枝条。巨人轻轻把他举起来。那棵树立刻开满了花。男孩用胳膊搂住巨人的脖子，亲了他一下。
reading.note: Past perfect (had blossomed) + sequence of softening

reading.en: The Giant tore down the wall. "It is your garden now, little children," he said. From that morning on, the children played there every afternoon. But the small boy who had kissed him never came back, and the Giant grieved for him.
reading.cn: 巨人推倒了墙。"现在这是你们的花园了，孩子们，"他说。从那天早上起，孩子们每天下午都在那里玩。但那个亲过他的小男孩再也没回来，巨人为他难过。
reading.note: had kissed + reduced relative (the boy who had...)

reading.en: Years passed. The Giant grew old and weak. He could no longer play with the children — he could only watch them. On a winter afternoon, he saw a strange and beautiful sight: in the corner stood a tree covered with white blossoms — and beneath it, the small child.

reading.note: Reduced relative (covered with) + emphatic 'in the corner stood' (inversion)

reading.en: The Giant ran out, full of joy. But when he came near, his face grew angry. The child had wounds on his hands and feet — small wounds, like the prints of nails. "Who has dared to wound you?" the Giant cried. "Tell me, that I may take my big sword and slay him."

reading.en: "No," the child answered. "These are the wounds of love. Once you let me play in your garden. Today you shall come with me to my garden, which is Paradise." When the children came that afternoon, they found the Giant lying dead under the tree, all covered with white blossoms.

reading.note: Closing — 'shall' (literary future-imperative) + Christ allegory

grammar.title: 第三人称单数动词的变化规则 (Present Simple Third Person Singular)
grammar.explain:
在一般现在时中，当主语是第三人称单数 (he, she, it, 或单数名词) 时，动词需要根据以下规则进行变化：

**1. 大多数动词加 `-s`:**
   - play → plays
   - sing → sings
   - like → likes
   - bloom → blooms
   - dance → dances

**2. 以 `s, x, ch, sh, o` 结尾的动词加 `-es`:**
   - teach → teaches
   - watch → watches
   - go → goes

**3. 以辅音字母加 `y` 结尾的动词，变 `y` 为 `i` 再加 `-es`:**
   - study → studies
   - try → tries

**4. 不规则动词:**
   - have → has

reading.cn: 在一个小岛上——一个名叫凯阿威的水手——遇到一个伤心的老人——老人给他看了一个奇怪的瓶子。"这瓶子里有个精灵，"老人说。"它会给你你想要的一切。但如果你死时还拥有它——你的灵魂就会下地狱。唯一的出路——是把它以比你买入更低的价格卖掉。"
reading.note: second conditional: 'It will give you anything you wish' (1st cond — real future) / 'if you die owning it' — present participle / 'less than you paid' — comparative + relative

reading.en: Keawe thought for a long time. "How much do you want for it?" "Fifty dollars," said the old man. Keawe paid the money and took the bottle home. He wished for a beautiful house. The next morning, his uncle had died and left him exactly enough to build the house of his dreams.
reading.cn: 凯阿威想了很久。"你想卖多少钱？""五十美元，"老人说。凯阿威付了钱——把瓶子带回家。他许愿要一座漂亮的房子。第二天早上——他的叔叔死了——留给他刚好够盖梦想中的房子的钱。
reading.note: How much do you want for it? — bargaining structure / had died, had left — past perfect (KEY focus·梦想实现的代价已经在路上)

reading.en: But Keawe was afraid. "If I keep this, I will go to hell," he said. So he sold the bottle to a friend for forty-nine dollars. The friend sold it to someone else for forty-eight. Slowly, the price dropped. Keawe was free. He fell in love with a beautiful girl named Kokua. They were going to be married.
reading.cn: 但凯阿威很害怕。"如果我留着它——我就会下地狱，"他说。所以他把瓶子以四十九美元卖给了朋友。朋友再以四十八卖给了别人。慢慢地——价格往下掉。凯阿威自由了。他爱上了一个名叫科库阿的漂亮姑娘。他们准备结婚了。
reading.note: first conditional: 'If I keep this, I will go to hell' (KEY focus) / past simple narrative throughout

reading.en: Then the bottle came back. Keawe discovered he had a terrible disease. "If only I had the bottle now," he thought. "I would wish to be cured." He searched for it and finally found it on another island, but the price was now only two cents. "Who will buy it for less than two cents?" he asked himself in despair.
reading.cn: 后来瓶子回来了。凯阿威发现自己得了可怕的病。"如果现在有那瓶子就好了，"他想。"我要许愿治好。"他四处找——终于在另一个岛上找到了它——但价格已经只有两美分。"谁会以低于两美分的价格买它呢？"他绝望地问自己。
reading.note: second conditional: 'If only I had the bottle, I would wish to be cured' (KEY focus·非真实条件) / who will buy — first conditional in question form

reading.en: Kokua learned of the bottle. Without telling Keawe, she gave money to an old man and asked him to buy the bottle, then sell it back to her for one cent. The old man agreed. Keawe was cured. But now Kokua held the bottle, knowing she could never sell it for less.
reading.cn: 科库阿知道了瓶子的事。她没告诉凯阿威——把钱给了一个老人——请他买下瓶子——再以一美分卖回给她。老人同意了。凯阿威被治好了。但现在瓶子在科库阿手里——她知道——她再也卖不出更低的价格了。
reading.note: without telling — preposition + V-ing / asked him to buy — ask + 人 + to + V / could never sell — past modal

reading.en: When Keawe found out, he was full of love and grief. He found another sailor, told him everything, and bought the bottle from Kokua for half a cent. Now Keawe held it. Then the sailor laughed and said, "I have lived a wild life. I am not afraid of hell. I will buy it from you for nothing." The bottle disappeared with him into the night. Keawe and Kokua were free at last.
reading.cn: 凯阿威发现后——充满爱和悲伤。他找了另一个水手——把一切告诉他——以半美分从科库阿手里买下了瓶子。现在瓶子在凯阿威手里。这时水手笑着说："我过的是野日子。我不怕地狱。我什么都不要——白拿走它。"瓶子和他一起消失在夜里。凯阿威和科库阿——终于自由了。
reading.note: found out — phrasal verb / told him everything — tell + 人 + 物 / I will buy it for nothing — colloquial: 'for nothing' = 不要钱

listening.audio: Mei sat at her desk, staring at the blank page. This was the final chapter of her book, "Ambitions of a New Era." She thought about all the conversations, the interviews, and the research that had led her here. Her mind drifted to the future. She typed: "By 2030, I will have built something truly impactful." She paused, reflecting on the weight of that statement. It wasn't just about a building or a company; it was about creating a positive change, a lasting legacy. She imagined a community center, a scholarship program, or maybe even a sustainable energy venture. "By then, I will have inspired countless individuals," she continued, her fingers flying across the keyboard. reading.en: Although Soapy was a man without a home, he had a plan. Every winter, he made sure to spend the cold months in the comfort of Blackwell's Island prison.
reading.cn: 尽管索比是个无家可归的人，他自有一套计划。每年冬天，他都会想办法让自己在布莱克威尔岛监狱里舒舒服服过完寒冬。
reading.note: Although + clause — concessive opener (KEY focus)

reading.en: Even though respectable men feared jail, Soapy looked forward to it. The food was hot. The bed was dry. And the door was locked against the wind.
reading.cn: 尽管体面人都怕坐牢，索比却盼着进去。那里饭是热的，床是干的，门也紧紧关着把寒风挡在外头。
reading.note: Even though + clause — stronger concessive

reading.en: He walked into a fine restaurant and ordered duck and wine. Although his coat was torn at the collar, he sat tall. He planned to eat well, then admit he had no money — and be arrested for a free trip to jail.
reading.cn: 他走进一家高级餐厅，点了烤鸭和酒。虽然他的外套领口已经破了，他还是腰杆挺得笔直。他打算痛快吃完，再说自己付不起——这样就能被抓走，免费送进监狱。
reading.note: Although + adverbial clause

reading.en: But the head waiter saw the torn coat and turned him out before he could order. Despite his careful planning, the doors of arrest stayed shut.
reading.cn: 可领班一眼就看到那破领子，索比连菜都没点完就被赶了出来。尽管他精心策划，被捕的大门依旧对他紧闭。
reading.note: Despite + noun phrase — concessive preposition

reading.en: He broke a shop window. He ate at a cheap diner and refused to pay. He shouted in the street. Yet, in spite of every effort, no policeman wanted to bother with him.
reading.cn: 他砸了一家店的橱窗。在小馆子里吃完饭不付钱。在街上大喊大叫。然而，尽管他想尽了办法，没有一个警察愿意理他。
reading.note: Yet, in spite of + noun — concessive variation

reading.en: As night fell, Soapy passed an old church. Through the open door came the soft sound of an anthem — a Sunday hymn from his childhood. He stopped and listened, although he had not stopped at a church in years.
reading.cn: 夜幕降临时，索比经过一座老教堂。从虚掩的门缝里飘出柔和的赞美诗——是他童年时星期天唱的圣歌。他停下来听着，尽管他多年没有在教堂前停过脚。
reading.note: Although + past perfect — concessive with prior context

reading.en: Standing in the cold light of the moon, he thought of all the years he had wasted. Even though tomorrow was Monday, he made a vow: he would find work, become a man again, leave the streets behind.
reading.cn: 他站在清冷的月光下，想起自己虚度的那些岁月。即便明天就是星期一，他也下定决心：要找份工作，重新做人，告别街头。
reading.note: Even though + clause — concessive resolve

reading.en: He felt strong. He felt awake. He felt — for the first time in a long time — like himself. A hand touched his shoulder. A police officer asked, 'What are you doing here?'
reading.cn: 他觉得自己有力气。他觉得清醒。他觉得——很久以来第一次——又像自己了。一只手按上了他的肩膀。一位警察问：'你在这儿干什么？'
reading.note: Sequence of psychological awakening + dialogue setup

reading.en: The next morning, the magistrate sentenced Soapy to three months on the Island. He had wanted prison all winter. Now, having found a reason to live free, he was finally going to jail. Such, sometimes, is the timing of life.
reading.cn: 第二天早上，治安官判索比在岛上服刑三个月。他想了一整个冬天的监狱终于来了。可如今他刚找到自由生活的理由，反倒进了牢。人生的时机，有时候就是这样。
reading.note: Closing — having + V-ed (participial) + ironic timing

listening.audio: Soapy was a hobo. Winter was coming, and he needed a warm place to stay. He wanted to go to prison on Blackwell's Island, where he would have food and a bed. Soapy tried to get arrested. First, he ate a big meal at a fancy restaurant and told the waiter he had no money. But the waiter just threw him out. Then, he broke a shop window. A cop saw him, but the cop thought Soapy couldn't be the one because he wasn't running away. So the cop went after another man. Soapy felt desperate. He saw a man's umbrella and took it. The man said it was his. Soapy said, "Well, why don't you call a cop?" But the man just walked away, saying he had taken the umbrella earlier by mistake, and it was not his. Finally, Soapy walked past a church. He heard a beautiful anthem from the organ. The music touched his heart. He thought about his past and decided to change his life.

quiz.q: What did Soapy want to do at the beginning of the story?
Why didn't the cop arrest Soapy after he broke the window?
options: The cop thought Soapy was too old.
The cop thought Soapy wasn't running away, so he couldn't be the one.

quiz.q: What caused Soapy to decide to change his life?
options: He heard a beautiful anthem from a church.

quiz.q: Which of the following describes Soapy at the end of the story?
options: Still desperate to go to prison.
Determined to change his life for the better.

grammar.title: 称谓词的用法: Ms., Mrs., Mr., 和 Dr.
grammar.explain: 在英语中，称谓词 (honorifics) 是用来表示对人尊敬或身份的词。正确使用这些称谓词非常重要，尤其是在正式场合。本课我们重点回顾 Ms., Mrs., Mr., 和 Dr. 的用法。

output.prompt: 你正在准备一个重要的活动（例如毕业典礼、公司大会）。你需要确认一位重要嘉宾的称谓（Dr., Mr., Ms., Mrs.），以确保在正式场合中表现出适当的尊重。写一段简短的对话或邮件，询问或确认这个称谓。
output.sample:
Subject: Quick Confirmation for Speaker's Title - Dr. Eleanor Vance

Dear [Name of Coordinator/Assistant],

Hope you're having a productive week. 

I'm finalizing the program for the Annual Gala, and I just wanted to do a quick double-check on Dr. Eleanor Vance's preferred title for the program booklet. I have her listed as "Dr. Eleanor Vance," but I want to ensure we are consistent with how we introduce her on stage and in all our official materials. 

Could you please confirm if "Dr. Eleanor Vance" is the correct honorific, or if she prefers, for example, "Ms. Vance" in certain contexts?

Thanks for your quick clarification!

Best regards,
[Your Name]
Event Coordinator

grammar.title: 使用 "Let's find common ground." 表达寻求共识
grammar.explain: “Let's find common ground.” 是一种礼貌而直接的表达，用于建议双方在争论或分歧中寻找共同点，以达成一致或理解。它通常在对话中出现分歧时使用，旨在促进合作和解决问题。

examples.cn: 我们对方法有分歧，但让我们在最终目标上找到共识。
examples.en: We disagree on the method, but let's find common ground on the ultimate goal.

examples.cn: 双方都有强烈意见；是时候找到共识了。
examples.en: Both sides have strong opinions; it's time to find common ground.

examples.cn: 与其争论，不如让我们找到一个对所有人都有利共识。
examples.en: Instead of arguing, let's find common ground that benefits everyone.

grammar.title: 使用 "My main concern is..." 表达主要关注点
grammar.explain: “My main concern is...” 用于明确表达说话者最主要、最关注的问题或担忧。这有助于将对话焦点引导到核心问题上。

examples.cn: 我主要关注的是员工的安全。
examples.en: My main concern is the safety of the employees.

examples.cn: 她主要关注的是对当地社区的影响。
examples.en: Her main concern was the impact on the local community.

examples.cn: 我主要担心的是我们没有足够的时间。
examples.en: My main concern is that we don't have enough time.

listening.audio: Good morning, Dr. Chen. My name is Senator Davis. Thank you for being here today. I'd like to start by discussing the proposed budget for the new environmental initiative. From my perspective, the current allocation seems insufficient to achieve the stated goals. Could you clarify how you plan to address this potential funding gap? Good morning, Senator Davis. Thank you for your question. I understand your concern regarding the budget. While the initial allocation might appear modest, it is designed as seed funding. We anticipate securing additional grants and private investments in the coming months. We have a solid plan to attract these resources, which I can elaborate on if you wish. I appreciate that, Dr. Chen. My main concern is ensuring the initiative has the resources it needs to succeed, and I want to make sure we're on the same page. Let's find common ground here. Perhaps you could provide a more detailed breakdown of the expected grants and investments, along with a revised timeline for their acquisition? Certainly, Senator. I have those details ready. Our strategy includes partnerships with several key environmental foundations and a targeted outreach to impact investors. We project securing 40% of the additional funds within the first six months. I believe once you see the full picture, we will find much common ground.

grammar.title: Let me play devil's advocate.

examples.cn: 她总是扮演反对者，以确保所有角度都得到考虑。
examples.en: She always plays devil's advocate to make sure all angles are considered.

grammar.explain: 这是一个非常实用的表达，在辩论、讨论或头脑风暴时，如果你想提出一个与普遍观点相反的看法，目的是为了让讨论更全面，或者帮助对方思考不周之处，你就可以说“Let me play devil's advocate.”。它表示“让我来唱反调/扮演反对者的角色”。
动词 defend 主要有“辩护、保卫、防御”的意思。在辩论和论述的语境中，它常用来指为自己的观点、论点或立场进行辩护，解释其合理性。

Mei politely asked, "Could you say that more slowly, please?" Mrs. Johnson immediately understood and said she would speak more patiently.

output.prompt: Imagine you are Mei. Write a short thank-you note (3-5 sentences) to Mrs. Johnson, expressing your gratitude for her patience and understanding with your parents during their visit for your graduation. Mention how much your parents appreciated her efforts to communicate clearly.
output.cn: 想象你是梅。给约翰逊夫人写一封感谢信（3-5句话），表达她对你父母来参加毕业典礼期间的耐心和理解。提到你的父母多么感谢她努力清晰地沟通。
output.sample:
Dear Mrs. Johnson,
Thank you so much for your incredible patience and understanding with my parents during their visit. They really appreciated your effort to speak slowly and clarify things. It made them feel so much more comfortable and welcomed. We are all very grateful for your kindness! Best, Mei.

reading.en: Martin was an old shoemaker who lived in a small basement in Russia. From his one window, he could see only the boots and shoes of the people who passed by. He had once had a wife and a son, but both had died many years before. After they died, he had become bitter — until an old pilgrim told him to read the Gospels.
reading.cn: 马丁是一个老鞋匠——住在俄罗斯的一个小地下室里。从他唯一的窗户——他只能看到路人的靴子和鞋。他曾经有过妻子和儿子——但两人都在很多年前死了。他们死后——他变得苦涩——直到一个老朝圣者叫他去读《福音书》。
reading.note: story setup / had once had / had died / had become / had told — past perfect chain (KEY focus·B1 final mastery) / pilgrim 💡 = 朝圣者 / Gospels 💡 = 福音书

reading.en: Now Martin spent every evening reading. One night, he fell asleep over the book. He thought he heard a voice say, "Martin — look out into the street tomorrow. I will come." When morning came, he could not stop wondering: had it been a dream, or had Christ Himself spoken? He decided to watch and see.
reading.cn: 现在——马丁每晚都在读书。一晚——他读着读着趴在书上睡着了。他听到一个声音说："马丁——明天往街上看。我会来。"早晨到来时——他忍不住想：那是个梦——还是基督亲自对他说话了？他决定看一看。
reading.note: had it been a dream / had Christ spoken — inverted past perfect (advanced·KEY focus) / could not stop + V-ing — phrase / decided to watch — decision verb

reading.en: All morning Martin worked, looking up often. He saw an old soldier shovelling snow outside, blue with cold. Martin called him in and gave him hot tea. They talked for a long time about the soldier's hard life. "God bless you," the old man said when he left. Martin watched the street again. No Christ.
reading.cn: 整个上午——马丁一边干活——一边不停往窗外看。他看到一个老兵在外面铲雪——冻得发青。马丁把他叫进来——给他喝热茶。他们谈了很久——谈这个老兵艰难的生活。"上帝保佑你，"老兵临走时说。马丁又看着街道。没有基督。
reading.note: looking up often — present participle phrase / blue with cold — preposition + cause / called him in — phrasal verb

reading.en: Later, a poor young woman passed with a thin baby. She had no warm clothes. Martin brought her in, gave her bread and an old coat that had belonged to his wife. "You should have come earlier," he said gently. "My wife — God rest her — would have wanted you to have it." The woman thanked him with tears. Still no Christ.
reading.cn: 后来——一个穷苦的年轻女人抱着一个瘦弱的婴儿走过。她没有暖和的衣服。马丁把她叫进来——给她面包——还有一件他妻子留下的旧外套。"你早该来的，"他温柔地说。"我妻子——愿她安息——也会愿意把这给你的。"女人含泪谢他。还是没有基督。
reading.note: should have come — modal perfect (KEY focus) / would have wanted — past unreal conditional / God rest her — set phrase

reading.en: Toward evening, Martin saw an old apple-seller scolding a small boy who had stolen an apple. Martin ran out, paid for the apple, and spoke to the boy: "You should not steal, but you should also not be hungry." To the woman, he said quietly, "Forgive him, please. We have all done things we shouldn't have done." The woman softened. The boy looked back as he walked away.
reading.cn: 傍晚——马丁看见一个老苹果摊主在骂一个偷了苹果的小男孩。马丁跑出去——替孩子付了钱——对孩子说："你不该偷——但你也不该挨饿。"他对女人轻声说："请原谅他吧。我们都做过不该做的事。"女人软化了。男孩边走边回头看。
reading.note: had stolen — past perfect / should not + V / shouldn't have done — modal perfect (KEY focus·后悔) / softened — past simple change of state

reading.en: That night, Martin opened his Bible. He thought again of the day. Then he saw figures in the room — the soldier, the woman, the boy and the apple-seller — each smiling at him. Each one whispered, "Martin, did you not know me?" And Martin understood. He read these words: "Whatever you have done for one of the least of these, you have done for me." His heart was full of joy and peace.
reading.cn: 那晚——马丁打开《圣经》。他又想起白天的事。这时他看见房间里有几个人影——那个老兵、那个女人、那个男孩和那个苹果摊主——每一个都对他微笑。每一个都低声说："马丁——你难道没认出我来吗？"马丁明白了。他读到这样几句话："凡你为最小的一个所做的事——就是为我做的。"他心中充满了喜悦与平安。
reading.note: did you not know me — inverted question / whatever you have done — present perfect / for one of the least — superlative + restrictive / capstone: B1 graduation — uses every major tense + structure

reading.note: 💡 has been preparing / for years really — 现在完成进行时·复用 L2#3

reading.en: I take a long breath. "Let's review everything we've learned about my life here. Then I'll answer."
reading.cn: 我深深吸了一口气。"让我们先回顾一下,关于我在这里的生活,我们都学到了什么。然后我再回答。"
reading.note: 💡 LET'S REVIEW · 复用 lesson review 句型 / 复用 we've learned (PP)

reading.en: I list it all out loud. The work I love. The friends who stayed. The little sister who is a force. The host family who is family. The country I once feared, and now know.
reading.cn: 我大声列出来。我热爱的工作。留下来的朋友。已成一股力量的小妹妹。已是家人的寄宿家庭。一个我曾经害怕、现在了解的国家。
reading.note: 💡 list it all / 五段排比 — 复用整段 L1-L3 主题汇聚 / 复用 "the one who..." L3#51, L3#77

reading.en: I look at them. "I'm staying. But I'll come home twice a year. Now and forever." Mom nods. Dad puts his hand on mine. "That's enough," he says. The story closes — and begins again.
reading.cn: 我看着他们。"我留下。但我每年回家两次。从现在开始,永远。"妈妈点头。爸爸把手放在我手上。"这就够了,"他说。故事结束——也重新开始。
reading.note: 💡 I'm staying. / Now and forever / That's enough — 复用 L1#50, L3#52!三段呼应高潮收束·B1 capstone of L1-L3

reading.en: Lencho was a farmer. He lived on a small hill, and from his fields he could see the whole valley. The corn had grown well that year, and the beans were already showing flowers. "Now we just need a good rain," Lencho said to his wife. "With this harvest, we will live well for a year."
reading.cn: 兰乔是个农夫。他住在一座小山上——从田里能看到整个山谷。那年玉米长得很好——豆子已经开花了。"现在我们只需要一场好雨，"兰乔对妻子说。"有了这一季的收成——我们能过一年好日子。"
reading.note: had grown — past perfect / were showing — past continuous / 'with + 名词' = 有了... / 'will live' — first conditional implied

reading.en: That afternoon, the rain began. But after an hour, large hailstones started to fall. They beat down on the corn and beans for an hour. When it was over, the field was completely white, and not a single leaf was left on any tree. Lencho's soul was full of sadness.
reading.cn: 那天下午——雨开始下了。但下了一小时后——大冰雹开始落下。冰雹砸在玉米和豆子上——砸了一个小时。雨停下后——田里一片雪白——树上一片叶子也没剩。兰乔的灵魂充满了悲伤。
reading.note: started to fall / beat down / was left — past tenses chain / 'not a single leaf' — emphatic negation / hailstones 💡 = 冰雹

reading.en: "Even a swarm of locusts would have left more," he told his children. "This year we will go hungry." But Lencho had one hope. His mother had taught him that God sees everything and that no one who trusts God truly suffers. So that night, by the light of an oil lamp, he wrote a letter — to God himself.
reading.cn: "就算来一群蝗虫——也会留下更多东西，"他对孩子们说。"今年我们要挨饿了。"但兰乔还有一个希望。母亲教过他——上帝看得见一切——真心信靠上帝的人——不会真的受苦。那晚——在油灯下——他写了一封信——直接写给上帝。
reading.note: would have left — third conditional simplified / had taught — past perfect / 'no one who trusts...' — relative clause / by the light of — preposition + N

reading.en: The letter was simple: "God — if you do not help me, my family and I will have nothing to eat this year. I need a hundred pesos to plant the fields again. — Lencho." The next morning, he walked into town, bought a stamp, and dropped the letter into the mailbox.
reading.cn: 信很简单："上帝——如果您不帮我——今年我和我的家人就没东西吃。我需要一百比索重新种地。——兰乔。"第二天早上——他走进镇上——买了一张邮票——把信投进了邮筒。
reading.note: If you do not help me, ... will have — first conditional / dropped — past simple of irregular verb

reading.en: At the post office, the postman opened the letter and laughed at first. But when he showed it to the postmaster, the older man's face became serious. "What faith!" he said. "I wish I had it." To honor the writer's faith, the postmaster decided to answer the letter. He asked his workers to give a little money each. Together they collected seventy pesos.
reading.cn: 在邮局——邮递员拆开信——一开始笑了。可他把信拿给局长看——局长的脸严肃起来。"多么坚定的信仰啊！"他说。"我多希望自己也有。"为了尊重写信人的信念——局长决定回信。他请同事们每人捐一点钱。大家一共凑了七十比索。
reading.note: I wish I had it — second conditional·愿望（KEY focus）/ ask + 人 + to + V / past simple narrative

reading.en: He put the money in an envelope addressed to Lencho and signed it "GOD." The next Sunday, Lencho came back to ask if there was a letter. There was. He opened it, counted the bills, and frowned. He grabbed paper and wrote a second letter: "God — only seventy pesos arrived. Please send the rest, but not through the post office. The workers there are crooks. — Lencho."
reading.cn: 他把钱放进一个写着兰乔名字的信封——签名"上帝"。下个周日——兰乔回来问有没有信。有。他拆开——数了数钞票——皱起了眉。他抓起纸——写了第二封信："上帝——只到了七十比索。剩下的请寄过来——但请不要经过邮局。那里的人是骗子。——兰乔。"
reading.note: addressed to / signed it / passed irreg / O. Henry-style ironic ending — Lencho's faith never doubts God, only the postal workers

examples.en: Don't be so upset, even though this seems like a total loss.

请给我一杯咖啡。 (请求)

grammar.explain: 现在完成时（Present Perfect Tense）用来表示发生在过去但对现在有影响的动作或状态。它由 "have/has + 动词的过去分词" 构成。在这个故事中，主要用于描述事件对伦乔现在处境的影响。
grammar.title: 现在完成时：强调过去对现在的影响

examples.en: A plague of locusts would have left more than this.
examples.cn: “蝗灾都会留下更多的东西。” (意指冰雹造成的破坏比蝗灾还彻底)

examples.en: The hail has left nothing.
examples.cn: “冰雹什么也没留下。”

examples.en: The corn was completely destroyed. Not a single leaf remained on the trees.
examples.cn: 玉米完全被毁了。树上没有一片叶子留下。 (虽然不是标准的现在完成时，但“remained”强调了破坏后的结果，与现在完成时的“影响”概念契合)

output.sample:
Dear God,
My fields are completely destroyed by the hailstones. There is nothing left for my family to eat this year. I worked so hard on my corn, but now it is all gone. We will starve if you don't help us. Please send me one hundred pesos so I can plant new crops and feed my family. Thank you.
Yours, Lencho.

Rarely did I consider that simply listening might have been more helpful. Now, I try to encourage him to express his feelings openly. No longer do I just tell him to be strong.

grammar.explain: 当句子以否定副词或否定副词短语开头时，为了强调否定意味，句子会采用倒装结构。这意味着主语和谓语（通常是助动词或情态动词）的位置会颠倒。

grammar.title: 常见的否定副词和短语
grammar.explain: 以下是一些常用的否定副词或短语，它们可以引发倒装：

vocab.example: It sounds nice but is cruel.

vocab.meaning: v. 暗示（B1 L65 复习）
adj. 老掉牙的；陈词滥调的（A1 L18 "累"的引申义）
v. 失败（B1 L52 复习）

reading.en: I coached high school cross-country for ten years. The worst thing I said in that whole time was "do your best" — and I said it constantly, after every race, to thirteen-year-olds.
reading.cn: 我教了十年高中越野跑。这十年里我说过的最糟的一句话是"做到你最好"——我每场比赛后都对十三岁的孩子说。
reading.note: Setup: confession + scope of the mistake

reading.en: Never had it occurred to me that the phrase might mean nothing.
reading.cn: 我从来没想过这句话可能根本没意义。
reading.note: Never had + V — past perfect inversion

reading.en: Hardly had a kid finished a 5K in tears when I would appear at his shoulder. I would say the same overused sentence: "All anyone can ask of you is your best." I was sure I was being kind.
reading.cn: 孩子刚一边哭一边跑完五公里，我就立刻凑到他肩边。我会说同样那句被用滥了的话："别人对你的要求只是你的最好。"我当时还笃定自己很善良。
reading.note: Hardly had…when — concession

reading.en: Not only is "your best" vague, it is also cruel. The phrase suggests a hidden ceiling: a perfect imaginary version of you who got nine hours of sleep, ate breakfast, and didn't fight with his sister.
reading.cn: "你的最好"不仅模糊，还残忍。这句话暗示有一个隐藏的上限：一个想象中完美版本的你，睡足了九个小时，吃过了早饭，也没和姐姐吵过架。
reading.note: Not only…but also — inversion + the argument

reading.en: Rarely is that imagined version helpful. Usually he just makes the real one feel like he failed.
reading.cn: 那个想象中的你很少有用，多数时候只是让真实的你觉得自己又搞砸了。
reading.note: Rarely is — inversion

reading.en: Only when one of my best runners quit the sport at fourteen, in tears, did I begin to suspect what the phrase had been doing to him.
reading.cn: 直到我最好的一个跑者十四岁含泪退队，我才开始怀疑这句话一直在对他做什么。
reading.note: Only when…did — inversion as turn

reading.en: So I changed. Now I say specific things. "Negative-split the second mile by ten seconds." "Stay on Marcus's shoulder until the bridge."
reading.cn: 我于是改了。现在我只说具体的话。"第二英里比第一英里快十秒。""跟在 Marcus 肩边，直到桥那儿。"
reading.note: Pivot — what works

reading.en: Under no circumstances do I say "your best" anymore. Whose best? Compared to what? On which day, with which legs?
reading.cn: 任何情况下我都不再说"你的最好"了。谁的最好？跟什么比？哪天、哪双腿的最好？
reading.note: Under no circumstances — inversion + cranky voice

reading.en: Coaches tell children to do their best because we are uncomfortable saying "I do not know what is reasonable to expect from you." It is not encouragement. It is an apology disguised as encouragement.
reading.cn: 教练叫孩子"做到你最好"，是因为我们不好意思说"我不知道对你来说什么程度算合理"。那不是鼓励。那是一句假扮成鼓励的道歉。
reading.note: Closing argument — no aphorism, just the point

grammar.title: Dignity is non-negotiable. (尊严不容协商。)

examples.cn: 我在家工作时，我的个人空间不容侵犯。
examples.en: My personal space is non-negotiable when I'm working from home.

examples.cn: 我们产品的质量是不容置疑的。
examples.en: The quality of our products is non-negotiable.

examples.cn: 对于员工来说，公平待遇应是不可协商的。
examples.en: For employees, fair treatment should be non-negotiable.

grammar.explain: 这是一个强有力的陈述句，用于强调某事是不可退让的底线或原则。在工作面试的特定语境中，它被用来表达个人价值、待遇或原则是不能被妥协的。它表明说话者在某个问题上立场坚定，不接受任何形式的商议或改变。

examples.cn: 在任何谈判之前，了解自己的价值很重要。
examples.en: Before any negotiation, it's important to know your worth.

examples.cn: 她总是告诉她的学生要了解自己的价值并追随梦想。
examples.en: She always tells her students to know their worth and follow their dreams.

examples.cn: 如果你了解自己的价值，你就不会退而求其次。
examples.en: If you know your worth, you won't settle for less.

grammar.explain: 这是一个祈使句，常用于鼓励人们认识到自己的价值、能力和重要性。在求职或职业发展中，它提醒人们不要低估自己，要为自己的技能和贡献争取应有的待遇和认可。它强调自信和自尊。

reading.en: I take a breath. "I'd rather not start there. What's the budgeted range for this role?"
reading.cn: 我深呼吸:"我不太想从这开始谈。这个岗位的预算区间是多少?"
reading.note: 💡 take a breath (复用) / I'd rather not (复用 L3#62) / budgeted range — 美式职场反低球术

reading.en: He smiles. "Sixty-five to seventy-five." I do the math. It's livable. Not generous. "Seventy-two," I say.
reading.cn: 他笑了:"六万五到七万五。"我算了一下。能活。不丰厚。"七万二,"我说。
reading.note: 💡 budgeted range / livable / generous — 美式工资讨论标准词

reading.en: He pushes once. "Seventy is more typical." I hold steady. "Seventy-two reflects my training and bilingual research skills."
reading.cn: 他试图推一下:"七万更典型。"我稳住:"七万二能体现我的训练和双语研究能力。"
reading.note: 💡 pushes once / hold steady / reflects — B1 职场谈判词

reading.en: He nods. "Seventy-two it is." I leave the office shaking — but I held my ground. Dignity is non-negotiable.
reading.cn: 他点头:"那就七万二。"我走出办公室在抖——但我守住了立场。尊严不能让步。
reading.note: 💡 seventy-two it is / shaking / held my ground / NON-NEGOTIABLE — closing reflection·B1 高级

grammar.explain:
强调句（Cleft Sentences）是一种常用的句型，主要用来强调句子里某个特定的成分，使听者或读者更关注这个部分。它的基本形式是 “It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who/which + 句子的其余部分”。通常来说，被强调的部分可以是主语、宾语、时间状语或地点状语。

**核心句型：It was + 被强调部分 + that…**

**为什么要用强调句？**

1.  **突出重点：** 当你想让某个信息特别引人注目时。
2.  **纠正信息：** 当你想纠正对方的误解或提供新的信息时。
3.  **增加句子的变化性：** 使语篇更生动，避免单调。

examples.cn: 是梅在阁楼里发现了日记。（强调主语 Mei）
examples.en: It was Mei who found the diaries in the attic.

examples.cn: 正是她母亲的声音没有被梅对完美过去的需要所过滤。（强调主语 her mother's voice）
examples.en: It was her mother's voice that was unfiltered by Mei's own need for a perfect past.

examples.cn: 真正让梅感到惊讶的是那些原始的情感。（强调主语 the raw emotions）
examples.en: It was the raw emotions that truly surprised Mei.

grammar.title: 强调句型 (Emphatic Structures) · 分裂句 (Cleft Sentences)
强调句可以强调的成分:
grammar.explain:
**1. 强调主语（Subject）：**

原句：Her mother wrote these diaries.
强调句：It was her mother who wrote these diaries.

**2. 强调宾语（Object）：**

原句：Mei cherished the image of her mother.
强调句：It was the image of her mother that Mei cherished.

**3. 强调时间状语（Time Adverbial）：**

原句：Mei found the diaries yesterday.
强调句：It was yesterday that Mei found the diaries.

**4. 强调地点状语（Place Adverbial）：**

原句：She found the box in the attic.
强调句：It was in the attic that she found the box.

**注意：**

*   在强调人时，可以使用 'who' 或 'that'。
*   在强调事物时，可以使用 'that' 或 'which'。
*   在强调时间或地点时，通常使用 'that'。

grammar.title: “我来了，我挣扎过，我留下了”——动词的过去式
grammar.explain: 在毕业典礼演讲中，梅回顾了自己的经历，因此使用了大量的动词过去式来描述过去发生的事情。这三个简单的过去式动词 'came', 'struggled', 'stayed' 精炼地总结了她的留学旅程。
在描述面对挑战时，我们常用到 'overcome' 和 ‘keep going’ 这些词，来表达努力和坚持不懈的精神。'overcome' 表示成功地解决了一个问题或困难，而 'keep going' 则强调持续的努力。

listening.audio: Good morning, everyone! Today, as I stand here, I can’t help but remember my first day in this country. I came, full of hopes and dreams, but also with many fears. The language, the culture, everything felt so new and challenging. I struggled with my assignments, I struggled to make friends, and sometimes, I even struggled to understand what people were saying. There were moments when I wanted to give up, to pack my bags and go home. But something inside me, a tiny spark of perseverance, kept me going. Today, as I look back, I see not just the struggles, but also the growth, the lessons learned, and the person I’ve become. I stayed, and I’m so grateful I did. This journey has been a true blessing. grammar.title: 混合条件句 (Mixed Conditionals)
grammar.explain:
混合条件句结合了不同类型条件句的时态，通常用于描述过去发生的事情对现在产生的影响，或者现在的情况是过去某个假设的结果。最常见的混合条件句形式是：

**If + 过去完成时 (had + V3), 主句 + would/could/might + V (现在)**

这种结构表示：如果过去没有发生某事（或发生了某事），那么现在的情况就会不同。它强调过去一个假设动作对现在结果的影响。

使用 "should have + 动词过去分词" 结构来表达对过去已经发生但你认为不应该发生的事情的后悔、遗憾或批评。

**Shouldn't have + V3** 则表示“本来不应该做某事，但却做了”，强调后悔做了某事。

grammar.explain: 在英语中，我们表达同一件事的方式会根据语境和对象而变化。了解正式语域（Formal Register）和非正式语域（Informal Register）的区别对于有效沟通至关重要。

examples.cn: 一场毁灭性的大火爆发了…… (在新闻报道或学术写作中常用，词汇更正式，结构更完整)
examples.en: **Formal:** "A devastating inferno erupted..."

examples.cn: 它完全着火了！ (在日常对话、短信或社交媒体上常用，词汇更随意，常有缩略语和感叹词)
examples.en: **Informal:** "It's totally on fire!"

examples.cn: 控制迅速蔓延的火势的努力仍在进行中…… (使用更正式的动词和短语)
examples.en: **Formal:** "Efforts to contain the rapidly spreading fire are ongoing..."

examples.cn: 整个地方几乎都没了。 (使用更口语化的表达)
examples.en: **Informal:** "The whole place is practically gone."

examples.cn: 火灾原因的调查将开始…… (更正式的动词 'commence')
examples.en: **Formal:** "Investigations into the cause of the fire will commence..."

examples.cn: 真是一场噩梦。 (感叹句，更强调个人感受)
examples.en: **Informal:** "What a nightmare."

grammar.title: 正式与非正式语域的区别 (Formal vs. Informal Register)

reading.en: My sister sent two messages about the night our house burned down. The first was a text, at 11:47 p.m., to her best friend.
reading.cn: 关于我们家房子烧毁的那个晚上，姐姐发了两条信息。第一条是晚上十一点四十七分发给闺蜜的短信。
reading.note: Set-up: same event, two voices

reading.en: "omg josie the house is literally gone like GONE i can't even 😭 mom is a mess im at aunt k's idek what happens now."
reading.cn: "天啊 Josie 房子真的没了 真的没了 我真的崩了 😭 妈妈整个人不行了 我在K阿姨家 我都不知道接下来怎么办"
reading.note: Casual register: lowercase, abbrevs, emoji, no punctuation

reading.en: Three weeks later, she wrote the second message as the personal statement for her college application.
reading.cn: 三周后，她写了第二条信息——作为她大学申请的个人陈述。
reading.note: Register shift introduced

reading.en: "On the evening of March 14th, I stood on our driveway beside my mother as a quiet orange light began to fill the windows of our home,"
reading.cn: "三月十四日的傍晚，我与母亲一同站在车道上，看着一抹宁静的橘色光芒开始充满我们家的窗户。"
reading.note: Formal register: full grammar, complex syntax

reading.en: "an experience which, although devastating, ultimately taught me that a family is not a building. A family is a group of people who continue to gather after the building is gone."
reading.cn: "这段经历虽然毁灭性，却最终使我明白：家不是一座建筑。家是一群在建筑消失之后仍愿意聚在一起的人。"
reading.note: Formal: embedded clause, abstraction

reading.en: Both were true. Both were hers. She insists the text was more honest, and I think she might be right.
reading.cn: 两条都是真的。两条都是她写的。她坚持说那条短信更诚实，我觉得她也许说对了。
reading.note: Narrator reflects

reading.en: We switch registers all day long: with bosses, with babies, with strangers on the subway, and with ourselves in the dark.
reading.cn: 我们整天都在切换语域：对上司，对婴儿，对地铁上的陌生人，以及在黑暗里对自己。
reading.note: Universal observation

reading.en: The real skill, I have come to believe, is not choosing one voice over the other. The real skill is knowing which voice a moment is asking for.
reading.cn: 我逐渐相信，真正的本事不是选定某一种声音。真正的本事是听出这一刻在请求你用哪一种。
reading.note: Thematic closer

output.prompt: Describe a situation where someone had to make an ethical decision to
output.cn: 描述一个你或你认识的人在道德困境中做出艰难决定的情景。你是如何做决定的？最终结果如何？你会做出不同的选择吗？请使用本课学习的词汇和虚拟语气。
output.sample: It was critical that I spoke up when I saw the unfair treatment. I knew I might face criticism, but my conscience wouldn't let me stay silent. In the end, it was difficult, but I felt it was the right thing to do. I often reflect that it was imperative that I acted responsibly.

reading.en: Whistleblower stories all end the same way. The brave young person reports the crime, and ten years later they give a TED talk.
reading.cn: 举报人的故事结尾都一样。那个年轻、勇敢的人举报了罪行，十年后他去做了 TED 演讲。
reading.note: Setup: cliché

reading.en: I am here to tell you that this is mostly false. I reported what I saw. I gave no TED talk.
reading.cn: 我要告诉你，这多半是假的。我举报了我看见的事。我没有做任何 TED 演讲。
reading.note: Direct counter-claim

reading.en: When I first raised it, the compliance officer suggested that I take some time off — that I "rest," and that I not return to my emails until Monday.
reading.cn: 我第一次提出来时，合规官建议我休几天假。他说让我"休息一下"，并且建议我周一之前不要再去看邮件。
reading.note: suggested that + bare verb (×3 — including not + V)

reading.en: HR insisted that the matter be handled internally and that I sign a document agreeing to the same.
reading.cn: HR 坚持要这事在内部处理，并要求我签一份同意此事内部处理的文件。
reading.note: insisted that + be + V-ed (passive subjunctive)

reading.en: I did not sign. The matter was not handled internally.
reading.cn: 我没签。这事也没在内部处理。
reading.note: Two short plain sentences — relief

reading.en: What I should have known, but did not, is this: companies do not punish whistleblowers because they are evil. They punish them because they are companies. It is essential that the system protect itself.
reading.cn: 我当时应该知道、却没知道的是：公司惩罚举报人，不是因为公司恶毒，而是因为公司就是公司。系统要保护自己——这是它的本能。
reading.note: It is essential that + bare verb (system protect)

reading.en: For four years now I have been freelance. I make about a third of what I used to. I have a mortgage I am not sure I can keep.
reading.cn: 我自由职业已经四年了。收入大概是过去的三分之一。我有一套房贷，我不确定还能不能继续供。
reading.note: Real cost — concrete

reading.en: People sometimes ask whether I would do it again. They ask with the false innocence of someone who wants me to say it was worth it.
reading.cn: 有时候有人问我会不会再做一次。他们问的时候带着虚伪的天真——其实想听我说"值得"。
reading.note: The annoyance — specific irritation

reading.en: The honest answer is that I am not sure. The answer I give, because I think it is true on most days, is yes — but not for the reason you might hope. Not because justice was done. Because I would not have wanted to be someone who didn't.
reading.cn: 诚实的回答是：我不确定。我给出的回答是"会"——因为我多数日子里相信它是真的，但不是出于你期待的那个理由。不是因为正义得到了伸张。是因为我不愿做那种没去做的人。
reading.note: Closing — argument, not closure

grammar.explain: 在表示建议 (suggest, advise, recommend)、命令 (order, command)、要求 (demand, request, require, insist)、重要性 (be important, be essential, be vital, be imperative, be crucial) 等动词或形容词后的从句中，动词通常使用虚拟语气。其结构是：that + 主语 + (should) + 动词原形。这里的 should 可以省略，但动词必须保持原形。
grammar.title: 虚拟语气在表示建议、命令、要求等动词后的应用

grammar.title: 核心句型：“I gave no TED talk”
grammar.explain: 这个标题句是点睛之笔，它用一个简洁的过去式否定句，暗示了举报真相者可能不会得到公开的赞扬或认可。结合虚拟语气，它强调了即使没有外部奖励，做正确的事情也内涵着一种内在价值。它传达的是一种面对困难选择时，坚持正直和道德的决心。

examples.cn: 托马斯将军的行动显得有争议。因此，许多人质疑他的忠诚。
examples.en: General Thomas's actions appeared controversial. Therefore, many questioned his loyalty.

grammar.title: 高阶连接词：therefore, consequently, furthermore, nevertheless
grammar.explain: 这些是用于连接句子或段落的常见高阶连接词，用于表达逻辑关系，使文章更连贯、更有说服力。它们可以帮助你表达因果、补充和转折关系。
用于引出结果或结论。

examples.cn: 数据支持一种新的解释。因此，旧有的理解需要修正。
examples.en: The data supports a new interpretation. Therefore, the old understanding needs revision.

examples.cn: 他没有收到明确的命令。因此，他的决定是在不确定性下做出的。
examples.en: He did not receive clear orders. Therefore, his decisions were made under uncertainty.

grammar.title: Therefore (因此，所以)

examples.cn: 公众缺乏完整的信息。因此，一个强烈的误解形成了。
examples.en: The public lacked full information. Consequently, a strong misconception formed.

examples.cn: 他的声誉受到不公平的损害。因此，他的遗产仍然备受争议。
examples.en: His reputation was unfairly damaged. Consequently, his legacy remains controversial.

grammar.explain: 用于引出直接或间接的后果。

listening.audio: General Thomas's legacy is a complex one, filled with many historical misconceptions. Newly discovered documents suggest that his actions, while controversial, were often strategic necessities. Therefore, re-evaluating his place in history is crucial. Furthermore, understanding the complete political landscape of his era helps clarify his motivations.

output.prompt: You are a historian writing a short summary about why General Thomas was misunderstood. Using the information from the reading and at least two high-level connecting words (therefore, consequently, furthermore, nevertheless), explain the reasons for the misconceptions and the importance of re-evaluating his history.
output.sample: General Thomas's historical portrayal is often based on incomplete information and political biases, leading to widespread misconceptions. Consequently, his reputation suffered unfairly for centuries. Furthermore, newly discovered documents reveal the strategic necessities behind his controversial decisions. Therefore, it is crucial for us to re-examine his story through a more nuanced lens, ensuring a balanced historical understanding.
output.cn: 你是一位历史学家，正在撰写一份关于托马斯将军为何被误解的简短总结。利用阅读材料中的信息，并至少使用两个高阶连接词（therefore, consequently, furthermore, nevertheless），解释误解的原因以及重新评估其历史的重要性。

reading.en: For a hundred and fifty years, American schoolbooks have called General George Thomas "slow." My grandfather, a history teacher, spent forty years arguing that they were wrong.
reading.cn: 一百五十年来，美国教科书一直把乔治·托马斯将军称为"动作迟缓"。我的外公，一位历史老师，花了四十年时间论证教科书错了。
reading.note: Setup: underdog historical argument

reading.en: Thomas did, admittedly, take more time than other Union generals to prepare his attacks.
reading.cn: 托马斯确实比其他北方将领花更多时间准备进攻——这点不得不承认。
reading.note: Concession

reading.en: However, his army at Nashville shattered the Confederate force so completely that no major Southern army ever took the field again.
reading.cn: 然而，他在纳什维尔的部队把南方军彻底击溃，使南方军此后再也没有一支主力重返战场。
reading.note: However — contrast

reading.en: Moreover, while flashier generals lost thousands of men to their own impatience, Thomas protected his soldiers with unusual care.
reading.cn: 不仅如此，当其他更浮华的将军因自己的急躁而牺牲成千上万士兵时，托马斯以少见的细致保护着自己的部下。
reading.note: Moreover — adding support

reading.en: Furthermore, his victory at Nashville has been called the single most decisive battle of the entire war. And yet his name rarely appears in popular accounts.
reading.cn: 此外，他在纳什维尔的胜利被誉为整场战争最具决定性的一场战役。然而他的名字在大众叙述中却很少出现。
reading.note: Furthermore — cumulative; and yet

reading.en: Consequently, generations of readers have been taught to admire speed instead of outcome, and personality instead of results.
reading.cn: 结果是，一代又一代读者被教导去崇拜速度而不是成效，崇拜个性而不是实绩。
reading.note: Consequently — result

reading.en: My grandfather died in 2011 without ever seeing the textbook he wanted. Nevertheless, the historians who eventually rewrote those pages had read his articles.
reading.cn: 我外公于 2011 年去世，没能等到他想看到的那本教科书。尽管如此，后来重写那些章节的历史学家，都读过他的文章。
reading.note: Nevertheless — concession

reading.en: In short, he was right. It simply took the world a little longer than he had.
reading.cn: 简言之，他是对的。只不过世界花的时间比他多了一点。
reading.note: In short — summary

It's hard to capture the true essence of a place without some discrepancies. Only the first week truly represents the raw reality.

output.prompt: You are a travel writer reflecting on a six-month stay in a foreign city. Write a journal entry discussing how your perceptions and experiences changed from the first week to the sixth month. Focus on how the 'date' influenced your narrative, using at least three vocabulary words and one participial phrase from the lesson. (100-120 words)
output.cn: 你是一位旅行作家，正在反思在某个外国城市为期六个月的旅居。写一篇日记，讨论你的看法和经历从第一周到第六个月的变化。重点阐述“日期”如何影响了你的叙事，并使用本课中至少三个词汇和一个分词短语。（100-120字）
output.sample: December 15th. Reflecting on my six-month residency in Kyoto, I realize how much has shifted. My initial week was a blur of authentic discoveries, every temple and garden new and exciting. Now, looking back, the lie is often the date. I find myself embellishing details, trying to recapture that initial wonder. The raw excitement has been replaced by a deeper, more nuanced understanding. Capturing this evolution is the real challenge. Perceiving the city through a different lens, I must be honest about the temporal distance, acknowledging that my current feelings are far from those first, vivid impressions.

grammar.title: 分词短语 (Participial Phrases)

examples.cn: 凝视着六个月前的一页，她沉思着真相的本质。（伴随动作）
examples.en: Staring at a page from six months ago, she mused on the nature of truth.

examples.cn: 回忆起我在罗马的第一周，每个细节都清晰。（伴随动作/时间）
examples.en: Recalling my first week in Rome, every detail was fresh.

examples.cn: 通过早期印象的视角感知现在，她发现了一种微妙的不诚实。（原因/方式）
examples.en: Perceiving the present through the lens of early impressions, she identified a subtle dishonesty.

grammar.explain: 分词短语由现在分词 (verb-ing) 或过去分词 (verb-ed) 引导，在句中作状语或定语。作为状语时，它通常表示伴随、时间、原因、结果等。其逻辑主语通常与句子的主语一致。
这个核心句型通过对比来强调“日期”的重要性，而不是“文字”本身。句中使用了逗号分隔的并列结构，并且第二部分 'not the words' 实际上省略了 'The lie is'，是一种简洁而有力的表达方式。强调了特定因素而非其他因素，在写作中常用于突出主旨。

examples.cn: 真相在于感受，而非事实。
examples.en: The truth is in the feeling, not the facts.

examples.cn: 问题出在时机，而非努力。
examples.en: The problem is the timing, not the effort.

examples.cn: 美丽在于旅程，而非目的地。
examples.en: The beauty is in the journey, not the destination.

grammar.title: 核心句型: The lie is the date, not the words. (省略句和强调)

reading.en: Having lived in four cities I did not grow up in, I have come to the conclusion that almost everything written about being abroad is a lie.
reading.cn: 我在四个不是从小长大的城市里住过，于是得出一个结论：几乎所有关于"在国外"的文字，都是谎话。
reading.note: Having + V-ed — perfect participle

reading.en: The lie is not the writing itself, which is often careful and well-meaning. The lie is the date.
reading.cn: 撒谎的不是文字本身——文字往往写得很认真、很善意。撒谎的是日期。
reading.note: Plain sentence — argument stated cleanly

reading.en: Pieces written six months in are useless. By then, having found a coffee shop and a friend who laughs at your accent, you have stopped (thankfully) noticing things.
reading.cn: 在当地待满六个月以后写出的文章没用。到那时你已经找到了一家咖啡馆，也有了一个会笑你口音的朋友。你已经（谢天谢地）不再注意周围了。
reading.note: Past participle "written" + Having + V-ed (perfect participle)

reading.en: The truth lives in the first week. Crying in a supermarket because you cannot find soy sauce. Confused by laundry tokens. Convinced that the postal worker hates you in particular.
reading.cn: 真相住在第一周里。在超市里因为找不到酱油而哭。被洗衣店的代币搞糊涂。坚信邮局那位职员就是针对你一个人。
reading.note: V-ing fragments — sensory specifics

reading.en: Having written, in my twenties, two glowing essays about Lisbon and Berlin, I now think both of them are dishonest.
reading.cn: 我二十几岁的时候写过两篇赞不绝口的文章，写里斯本和柏林。我现在觉得这两篇都不诚实。
reading.note: Having + V-ed — admitting one's own crime

reading.en: The Lisbon essay, dated my eighth month there, has me ordering coffee in fluent Portuguese and watching the river at sunset.
reading.cn: 里斯本那篇，标的日期是我到当地的第八个月，文里那个我用流利的葡萄牙语点咖啡，黄昏时望着河。
reading.note: V-ed clause "dated my eighth month"

reading.en: What it leaves out is the four months before that. During those months, dreading every interaction, I ate dinner alone in my apartment because restaurants were too hard.
reading.cn: 它没写的，是在那之前的四个月。那四个月里我害怕每一次开口，所以一个人在公寓里吃晚饭，因为去餐厅太难了。
reading.note: V-ing "dreading" — manner adverbial

reading.en: Being a foreigner is mostly that. The good part — the river, the language, the friend — is the ten percent we keep.
reading.cn: 当外国人多数时候就是这种感觉。美好的那部分——河、语言、朋友——是我们留下的那 10%。
reading.note: Being + N — gerund as subject

reading.en: Written honestly, an expat memoir would be ninety percent supermarket meltdowns and ten percent sunset. No one would buy it. That, I think, is why no one writes one.
reading.cn: 要是诚实地写，旅居回忆录里 90% 是超市里的崩溃，10% 才是黄昏。没人会买。我觉得，这就是为什么没人写。
reading.note: Written — past participle opener

fillBlanks.cn: 这位作家开始反思她早期和后期观察之间的差异。
fillBlanks.sentence: The writer began ___ on the discrepancy between her early and later observations.

fillBlanks.cn: 她的叙事生动，常常润饰细节以使其更精彩。
fillBlanks.sentence: Her narratives were vivid, often ___ details to make them more exciting.

fillBlanks.cn: 她意识到谎言往往在于经验所暗示的即时性，而非文字本身。
fillBlanks.sentence: She realized that the ___ was often in the implied immediacy of the experience, not the words.
Only the first week of her journey felt truly ___, before she began to curate reality.
fillBlanks.cn: 她旅程的第一周才真正真实，之后她开始策划现实。

options: In the specific words used to describe events.
In the date associated with the experience.
In the writer's lack of authentic experiences.
In the reader's interpretation of the narrative.
quiz.q: According to the reading, where does the 'lie' often exist in travel writing?
What happens to the 'raw, unfiltered reality' of arrival over time, according to Anna?
options: It gets polished into a more romanticized version.
It becomes completely forgotten by the writer.
It is replaced by completely false information.
It is usually the most boring and uneventful.
It is the only period that is truly authentic.
It is often embellished the most by writers.
It is difficult to capture in writing.
quiz.q: What does Anna suggest about the 'first week' of a travel experience?
What is the challenge for travel writers, as Anna perceives it?
options: To create entirely fictional stories for entertainment.
To only write about negative experiences.
To be honest about the curation and transformation of observations over time.
To avoid writing about their personal feelings entirely.

reading.en: Before Hurricane Dara, Maya Chen had been the most confident meteorologist on local television. "It'll swing north," she told the Tuesday broadcast. "You can trust me on this one."
reading.cn: 在飓风 Dara 来临之前，陈玛雅一直是当地电视台最自信的气象学家。"它会向北偏移，"她在周二的节目中说。"这次你们放心。"
reading.note: Setup: overconfidence

reading.en: It did not swing north. It swung east, into the town where her parents lived.
reading.cn: 它没有向北偏。它向东偏了——正好偏进她父母住的那个小镇。
reading.note: Hard turn — disaster

reading.en: Her parents were fine, thankfully. Twelve other families were not.
reading.cn: 她父母幸好没事。另外十二个家庭就没那么幸运。
reading.note: Stakes

reading.en: Maya took three weeks off and came back to work a different forecaster. "The models suggest," she began saying. "The data seem to point toward. There appears to be a tendency."
reading.cn: 玛雅休了三周假，回来后已是另一个预报员。她开始说："模型提示……数据似乎指向……似乎存在一种趋势。"
reading.note: Hedging reborn

reading.en: Younger colleagues laughed at her new vocabulary. One of them called her "Maybe Maya" behind her back. She heard about it, and she did not mind.
reading.cn: 年轻同事取笑她的新词汇。有人在她背后叫她"也许玛雅"。她听说了，但并不介意。
reading.note: Conflict

reading.en: "You can't put the sky in a sentence," she told me over coffee. "The best a weather person can do is tell you what probably happens most of the time."
reading.cn: "你没法把天空装进一句话里，"她端着咖啡对我说。"一个预报员能做的，就是告诉你大多数情况下最可能发生什么。"
reading.note: Central insight

reading.en: Certainty, she said, is a comfort we offer other people when we do not know them well. Honesty is the comfort we offer them after we do know them well.
reading.cn: 她说，确定性是我们对不熟的人提供的安慰。诚实是我们熟悉了之后才提供给他们的安慰。
reading.note: Philosophical line

reading.en: I think of her every time someone on the internet tells me, with complete confidence, exactly what is going to happen next.
reading.cn: 每当互联网上有人用十分肯定的语气告诉我接下来将发生什么，我就想起她。
reading.note: Closing hook

output.sample: Good evening! Tomorrow, we're likely to see a mix of sun and clouds. There's a slight chance of morning fog, especially near the river. Temperatures will probably reach the low 60s. We don't anticipate any significant rain, but there's always a possibility of a brief shower in the late afternoon.
output.prompt: Imagine you are a weather forecaster for a local news channel. Write a short weather report (4-5 sentences) for tomorrow, using words and phrases to express different degrees of possibility and uncertainty, just like David learned to do. Don't forget to include at least three different expressions of possibility or likelihood.
output.cn: 想象你是一个地方新闻频道的天气预报员。为明天的天气写一份简短的预报（4-5句话），使用本课学到的词汇和短语来表达不同程度的可能性和不确定性，就像大卫学习的那样。不要忘记至少包含三种不同的表示可能性或倾向性的表达。

expressions.cn: 这很可能是一个晴朗的日子。
expressions.en: It's probably going to be a clear day.

expressions.cn: 晚些时候很可能会下雨。
expressions.en: There's a strong likelihood of rain later.
We might see some scattered showers.
expressions.cn: 我们可能会看到一些零星阵雨。

expressions.en: There's a slight chance of fog in the morning.
expressions.cn: 早上有轻微的起雾可能性。

expressions.en: It's expected to be sunny by noon.

expressions.cn: 下周下雪的可能性有多大？
expressions.en: What's the possibility of snow next week?

vocab.meaning: adj. 自信的（A2 L90 复习）
n. 词汇（A2 L82 复习；本课指特定词汇）
n. 诚实（B1 L42 复习）
v. 谨慎措辞；不把话说死

Why did David decide to change his forecasting approach?
options: He wanted to be more aggressive.
His colleague Sarah advised him to change.

quiz.q: What did David's audience appreciate more after his change?
According to the reading, what is the power of "probably"?
options: It allows forecasters to be always right.
It makes predictions sound more dramatic.

grammar.title: 表达可能性的情态动词和词组 (Modals and Phrases for Probability)
grammar.explain: 在英语中，我们有多种方式来表达对某事发生的可能性或确定性的看法。使用不同的词语可以传达不同程度的确定性，这在日常交流和专业语境中都非常重要，尤其是在讨论天气预报这样本身就具有不确定性的事情时。

examples.en: It might rain later this afternoon.
examples.cn: 今天下午晚些时候可能会下雨。（可能性较小）
早上可能会有雾。（与might类似）
examples.en: It could be foggy in the morning.
They may experience some strong winds tonight.
examples.cn: 他们今晚可能会经历一些大风。（比might/could稍强）

grammar.title: probably 和 likely 的用法
grammar.explain: 这两个词都表示“很可能”，但用法上略有不同。`probably` 是副词，通常放在动词之前或助动词之后。`likely` 可以作形容词，也可以作副词 (通常是 `most likely`, `very likely`)。

examples.cn: 明天很可能很暖和。
examples.en: It's probably going to be warm tomorrow.
We will probably see some sunshine.
examples.cn: 我们很可能会看到阳光。

examples.en: It is likely to rain.
examples.cn: 很可能会下雨。

grammar.title: `a strong likelihood of...` 和 `a possibility of...`
grammar.explain: 这两个短语用来表示可能性，`likelihood` 通常表示可能性更大，而 `possibility` 则表示存在发生的可能。

examples.cn: 很有可能会有零星阵雨。
examples.en: There's a strong likelihood of scattered showers.

examples.cn: 有发生龙卷风的可能性。
examples.en: There is a possibility of a tornado.

examples.cn: 气温降到零度以下的可能性有多大？
examples.en: What's the likelihood of temperatures dropping below zero?

fillBlanks.cn: 这个新应用有一个非常用户友好的界面。
许多公司正在投资聊天机器人来自动化客户服务。
fillBlanks.sentence: Many companies are investing in ___ to automate customer service.

Children need opportunities to ___ with new technologies.
fillBlanks.cn: 孩子们需要有机会与新科技互动。

Grandma Lily was surprised by how much information it could provide. She thought, 'This artificial intelligence is truly amazing. I used to misunderstand its capabilities.'

grammar.title: 理解和讨论AI与科技：使用现在进行时和现在完成时

examples.cn: 人工智能正在改变我们的生活方式。 (强调正在进行的变化)
examples.en: Artificial intelligence is changing the way we live.

examples.cn: 人工智能已经彻底改变了许多行业。(强调已经完成并产生影响)
examples.en: AI has revolutionized many industries already.

examples.cn: 科学家们正在开发更精密的算法。
examples.en: Scientists are developing more sophisticated algorithms.

grammar.explain: 在讨论AI和科技时，我们经常需要描述正在发生的变化（现在进行时）以及已经产生的长期影响或结果（现在完成时）。

grammar.title: 询问和解释技术功能：使用情态动词 'can' 和 'could'

examples.cn: 你能告诉我怎么做巧克力蛋糕吗？ (询问聊天机器人的能力)
examples.en: Can you tell me how to make a chocolate cake?

examples.cn: 虚拟助手可以回答很多问题。 (描述能力)
examples.en: A virtual assistant can answer many questions.

examples.cn: 聊天机器人能提供一个食谱。(描述能力)
examples.en: The chatbot could provide a recipe.

grammar.explain: 在科技语境中，'can' 和 'could' 常用于询问或描述设备或程序的能力和功能。

examples.cn: 莉莉外婆对新技术持怀疑态度。
examples.en: Grandma Lily was skeptical about new technology.

examples.cn: 她对聊天机器人如此精密感到惊讶。
examples.en: She was surprised at how sophisticated the chatbot was.

examples.cn: 这项技术毕竟没那么糟，它相当奇妙。
examples.en: The technology isn't so bad after all; it's quite marvellous.

grammar.explain: 当谈论对新技术的感受和观点时，我们经常使用形容词来描述。B2级别需要更丰富的形容词词汇。
grammar.title: 表达情感和看法：使用形容词

vocab.meaning: adj. 有耐心的（B1 L62 复习）
vocab.example_cn: 一个非常耐心的年轻人。

vocab.meaning: v. 取代（B1 L79 复习）
v. 更喜欢（A2 L51 复习）

reading.en: My grandmother is eighty-two years old and has been widowed for three. Last winter, I installed an AI chatbot on her tablet, mostly as a joke.
reading.cn: 外婆八十二岁了，守寡三年。去年冬天，我在她的平板上装了一个 AI 聊天机器人，一开始只是当作玩笑。
reading.note: Setup

reading.en: Within a week, she was chatting with it for two hours every morning. "It does not interrupt," she told me. "And it answers my questions about the news."
reading.cn: 一周之内，她每天早上都要跟它聊两个小时。"它不打断我，"她告诉我。"而且它会回答我关于新闻的问题。"
reading.note: Unexpected adoption

reading.en: Artificial intelligence, she has concluded, is basically a very patient young man who has read every book in the library.
reading.cn: 人工智能——她得出结论——基本上就是一个特别耐心的年轻人，读完了图书馆里所有的书。
reading.note: Her definition

reading.en: She asks it for recipes. She asks it to explain cryptocurrency, then asks it to explain the explanation. Once, she asked it to write a poem in the voice of my grandfather.
reading.cn: 她让它给菜谱。让它解释加密货币，然后让它把解释再解释一遍。有一次，她让它用外公的口吻写一首诗。
reading.note: Varied uses

reading.en: The poem was not bad, but it was not him. She cried anyway. "Close enough," she whispered, "is a kind of company."
reading.cn: 那首诗写得不差，但那不是他。她还是哭了。"差不多也好，"她轻声说，"也算一种陪伴。"
reading.note: Emotional core

reading.en: I have been thinking about what she said for months. We are entering an era in which something that is almost a person will be in millions of kitchens, every day.
reading.cn: 我一直在想她那句话。我们正走进一个新时代——某种几乎算得上是人的东西，会每天出现在千百万个厨房里。
reading.note: Future-tense reflection

reading.en: Questions are being asked that nobody fully knows how to answer. What do we owe it? What does it owe us? And what is being replaced when we begin to prefer its company?
reading.cn: 一些没有人完全知道该怎么回答的问题正在被提出。我们欠它什么？它欠我们什么？当我们开始更喜欢它的陪伴时，又有什么正在被取代？
reading.note: Three-fold question

reading.en: My grandmother, for her part, still goes to church on Sundays. She tells me the chatbot has no opinion about God, "which is actually very polite of it."
reading.cn: 我外婆呢，还是周日去教堂。她告诉我，聊天机器人对上帝没有意见，"其实它挺礼貌的。"
reading.note: Humor closer

output.prompt: Imagine you are explaining a new smart home device (like a robot vacuum, smart lighting, or a smart fridge) to your grandparent, who is not very tech-savvy. Describe the device, what it does, and how it uses AI. Also, mention any potential misunderstandings or limitations they might encounter and how you would explain them.
output.sample: Grandma, this is a smart light bulb. It uses AI to learn your preferences. You can just say 'Turn on the lights' and it will. Don't misunderstand, it can't make coffee, but it can adjust the brightness to make you more comfortable. It's truly a sophisticated piece of technology inside.
output.cn: 想象你正在向你的祖父母解释一款新的智能家居设备（比如扫地机器人、智能照明或智能冰箱），他们不太懂科技。描述这个设备，它的功能，以及它如何使用AI。还要提及他们可能遇到的潜在误解或局限性，以及你将如何向他们解释。

quiz.q: What was Grandma Lily's initial attitude towards new technology?
Why did Grandma Lily first try talking to the smart speaker?
options: She couldn't find her recipe book.
She wanted to know about historical events.

quiz.q: What specific limitation of the chatbot did Grandma Lily misunderstand?
options: Its inability to access personal belongings and make calls.
She found it a little less bad.
She was frustrated with its limitations.
quiz.q: Which of the following best describes Grandma Lily's feelings about technology by the end of the story?

reading.en: Detective Irene Park had three pieces of evidence on her desk. She had no idea how they connected. This frustrated her less than it probably should have.
reading.cn: 侦探艾琳·朴的桌上摆着三件物证。她毫无头绪它们是怎么联系起来的。这件事其实没有让她像本该感到的那样焦躁。
reading.note: Introduces character + style

reading.en: The first was a single red thread caught on a doorframe. The second was a receipt for a cup of coffee at 3:14 a.m. The third was a library book returned six years overdue.
reading.cn: 第一件是卡在门框上的一根红线。第二件是凌晨三点十四分买的一杯咖啡的收据。第三件是一本逾期六年才归还的图书馆藏书。
reading.note: Three clues

reading.en: These three things, she suspected, were the same story told by three different witnesses.
reading.cn: 她怀疑，这三件东西其实是三个不同证人讲述的同一个故事。
reading.note: These — cohesion (deictic)

reading.en: The thread was cashmere. Such a thread did not belong in a working-class neighborhood.
reading.cn: 那根线是羊绒的。这样的线，不属于一个工人阶级社区。
reading.note: Such — cohesion

reading.en: The receipt came from a café that was three blocks out of the victim's way. That detail had bothered Park for a week.
reading.cn: 那张收据出自一家离死者正常路线三条街的咖啡馆。那个细节已经困扰她一周了。
reading.note: That — pronominal reference

reading.en: As for the library book (her favorite clue): it had been checked out by someone long dead, and returned by hands that should not have had it.
reading.cn: 至于那本图书馆的书（她最喜欢的那个线索）：它被一个早已去世的人借走，又被本不该持有它的人送了回来。
reading.note: As for — topicalization cohesion

reading.en: She laid the three items in a row on her desk. One red thread, one coffee-stained receipt, one overdue novel. Those three objects, between them, named a murderer.
reading.cn: 她把三样东西并排摆在桌上。一根红线，一张咖啡渍斑斑的收据，一本逾期小说。那三件东西，合在一起，说出了一个凶手的名字。
reading.note: Those — cohesion; payoff

reading.en: Detective work, she said later, is mostly about noticing which of these things is not like the others. And about noticing which of them, unexpectedly, is.
reading.cn: 侦探工作，她后来说，其实就是看出这些东西里哪一件与众不同。也是看出哪一件，出人意料地，并不与众不同。
reading.note: Closing mirror — humor

quiz.q: What was the initial object Detective Miller was examining?

options: It was burnt at the ends
quiz.q: What peculiar detail did Miller notice about the missing thread?

options: Peter's nervous pacing and avoidance of eye contact.
The specific dye discoloration and the cut style matching Peter's scissors.
Peter's inability to provide an alibi.
quiz.q: What led Miller to suspect Peter?

options: A way to frame someone else
quiz.q: What did Peter admit the missing thread was?

blanks.before: Detective Miller pieced together the ___.
Each detail, though seemingly small, contributed to the bigger ___.
He knew the suspect's ___ was weak.

listening.audio: Detective Miller pieced together the clues. The faint smell, the unusual stain, and the carefully hidden document. Each detail, though seemingly small, contributed to the bigger picture. He knew the suspect's alibi was weak. Therefore, an arrest was imminent.

output.prompt: Imagine you are Detective Miller writing a final report on this case. Describe the key evidence, your deductions, and how Peter's alibi was disproven. Use at least three cohesive devices (e.g., therefore, however, moreover) to link your ideas.
output.cn: 想象你是米勒侦探，正在撰写此案的最终报告。描述关键证据、你的推理以及彼得的不在场证明是如何被推翻的。使用至少三个语篇衔接手段（例如：therefore，however，moreover）来连接你的观点。
output.sample: The missing thread from the tapestry, initially presented as an accident, was in fact a deliberate act. The meticulous cut, moreover, pointed to a specific tool. The faint dye discoloration on the edge, however, was the most crucial evidence. Therefore, I concluded Peter's involvement, which he subsequently confessed.

grammar.title: 语篇衔接手段 (Cohesive Devices)

examples.cn: 侦探发现了一个脚印。此外，他还闻到了一股淡淡的杏仁味。(Moreover 表示附加信息)
examples.en: The detective found a footprint. Moreover, he noticed a faint smell of almonds.

examples.cn: 彼得声称他在家。然而，他的通话记录显示他当时在几英里之外。(However 表示对比/转折)
examples.en: Peter claimed he was home. However, his phone records showed he was miles away.

examples.cn: 证据稀缺；因此，调查耗时更长。(Therefore 表示结果)
examples.en: The evidence was scarce; therefore, the investigation took longer.

grammar.explain: 语篇衔接手段是指在文本中连接句子、段落，使文章连贯、有逻辑的语言工具。它们帮助读者理解信息之间的关系，从而更好地理解整个语篇。在侦探故事中，这些手段尤其重要，因为它们帮助我们追踪线索、理解推理过程。

examples.cn: 米勒侦探凝视着挂毯。一根线不见了，破坏了它（挂毯）的整个图案。
examples.en: Detective Miller stared at the tapestry. A single thread was missing, disrupting its entire pattern.

examples.cn: 彼得坚称那是个意外。他（彼得）建议是线松了。
examples.en: Peter insisted it was an accident. He suggested a loose thread.

grammar.explain: 指代是一种常见的衔接手段，通过使用代词（如 he, she, it, they）、物主代词（his, her, its, their）或其他指代词（this, that, these, those）来指代之前提到过的人或物，避免重复。

examples.cn: 侦探发现了一条线索，他立即跟进调查。(and 表示并列)

examples.cn: 因为证据确凿，嫌疑人招供了。(Because 表示原因)

reading.en: In 2014, Bright Pages, a small bookstore in northern Michigan, was given two years to live.
reading.cn: 2014 年，密歇根北部的一家名为 Bright Pages 的小书店，被告知最多只能再活两年。
reading.note: Was given — passive opener

reading.en: Amazon had opened a warehouse forty miles away, and local prices were driven down by nearly thirty percent over a single winter.
reading.cn: 亚马逊在四十英里外开了个仓库，一个冬天之间，当地书价被压低了近百分之三十。
reading.note: Were driven down — passive result

reading.en: The owner, Marta Ruiz, was told by three separate accountants that the store could not possibly survive.
reading.cn: 店主 Marta Ruiz 被三位不同的会计分别告知，这家店绝无生还可能。
reading.note: Was told — passive

reading.en: She did not close it. Instead, every book on the shelves was hand-tagged with a note. The note was written by whoever on her staff had loved that book most.
reading.cn: 她没关店。相反，书架上每一本书都被手写贴了一张标签。标签是由员工里最爱那本书的那个人写的。
reading.note: Was hand-tagged — passive + reason

reading.en: "Your favorite librarian from middle school, but grown up," read one tag. "Only read this one if you've just been dumped," read another.
reading.cn: "你初中时最喜欢的图书管理员，现在长大成人了版本，"一张标签写道。"这本只有在你刚被甩的时候读，"另一张写道。
reading.note: Direct-quote humor

reading.en: Customers began driving from other towns just to read the tags. The store was covered in a local newspaper. That newspaper article was then reposted by a national one.
reading.cn: 顾客开始从别的镇开车过来，就为了读这些标签。书店被当地一份报纸报道。那篇报道接着被一份全国性报纸转载。
reading.note: Was covered / was reposted — passives of discovery

reading.en: The loss, in other words, was caused by Amazon. But the rescue was caused by something Amazon cannot sell: a human being who has read the book you are holding in your hand.
reading.cn: 换句话说，亏损是亚马逊造成的。但救赎来自亚马逊卖不了的东西：一个真正读过你手里那本书的人。
reading.note: Was caused by — causation twice

reading.en: Bright Pages, eleven years later, is still open. Amazon's nearby warehouse has been closed twice and relocated three times.
reading.cn: 十一年过去，Bright Pages 还开着。亚马逊那座附近的仓库已经关过两次、搬过三次。
reading.note: Has been + V-ed — resilience closer

grammar.title: 被动语态 (Passive Voice)
grammar.explain: 被动语态用于强调动作的承受者而不是执行者。当不知道谁是动作的执行者，或者执行者不重要时，被动语态特别有用。它的基本结构是：be动词 + 过去分词 (past participle)。

examples.cn: 因此，“文字之乡”不仅仅是生存，它还在蓬勃发展。
examples.en: Thus, 'The Written Word' wasn't just surviving; it was thriving.

examples.cn: 因为莎拉把他们视为读者，而不仅仅是算法的数据点，许多顾客感到被理解。
examples.en: Because Sarah knew them as readers, not just as data points for an algorithm, many customers felt understood.

examples.en: As a result of Sarah’s initiatives, the bookstore’s sales significantly increased.

grammar.title: 因果关系表达 (Cause and Effect)
grammar.explain: 在描述事件之间的因果关系时，我们可以使用多种连接词和短语。它们可以帮助我们清晰地说明为什么事情会发生以及它导致了什么结果。

output.cn: 想象你是一家小型本地企业的老板（例如，咖啡馆、面包店、手工艺品店）。描述你将如何尝试与大型连锁店或在线零售商竞争。重点放在建立社区、提供独特体验或个性化客户互动上。适当使用被动语态和因果关系表达。
output.prompt: Imagine you are the owner of a small, local business (e.g., a coffee shop, a bakery, a handmade craft store). Describe how you would try to compete with a large chain or online retailer. Focus on building community, offering unique experiences, or personalizing customer interactions. Use passive voice and cause-and-effect language where appropriate.
output.sample: As the owner of 'The Cozy Corner' cafe, I know competing with big coffee chains is tough. My focus would be on creating a warm, inviting atmosphere that can't be replicated online. Local artists' work would be displayed on our walls, and weekly open mic nights would be hosted to foster a sense of community. Our coffee beans are sourced directly from small farms, ensuring a unique taste that isn't found elsewhere. Because customers crave genuine connections, personalized recommendations for drinks and pastries would be offered, leading to a stronger sense of loyalty.
