reading.en: Take a breath. For the next sixty seconds, you are being watched by a surprising number of things. None of them, technically, is alive.
reading.cn: 深呼吸。在接下来的六十秒里，你正被数量惊人的东西观察着。严格来说，它们没有一个是活的。
reading.note: Second-person hook

reading.en: Your phone's microphone is probably being triggered by at least one background app that you installed and forgot.
reading.cn: 你手机的麦克风，大概率正被至少一个你下载完就忘掉的后台应用触发着。
reading.note: Is being triggered — present cont. passive

reading.en: Your location is being collected, then sold, then combined with two hundred other data points. The result is something your mother would call "a profile" and your employer would call "a file."
reading.cn: 你的位置正被收集、转卖，然后和另外两百个数据点拼接到一起。最终的结果，你妈妈会叫它"画像"，你老板会叫它"档案"。
reading.note: Triple passive chain

reading.en: If you are reading this on a laptop, your webcam light may or may not be on. The camera itself, however, is being accessed by software that would take you an hour to identify.
reading.cn: 如果你正用笔记本阅读这段文字，摄像头上的指示灯也许亮也许不亮。但摄像头本身，正被一些你要花上一个小时才能查清的软件访问着。
reading.note: Is being queried — present cont. passive

reading.en: Data, you could say, is being harvested the way wheat used to be: constantly, invisibly, and mostly from people who never asked to plant a field.
reading.cn: 可以说，数据正在被收割，就像从前小麦被收割那样：不停歇，看不见，而且多数被收割的人从未要求种这片田。
reading.note: Is being harvested — extended metaphor

reading.en: None of this, in itself, is secret. All of it is happening in the open, inside agreements that are being clicked through at a rate of about one billion times a day worldwide.
reading.cn: 这一切本身都不是秘密。一切都在公开进行，藏在那些每天以全球约十亿次的频率被点击同意的协议里。
reading.note: Are being clicked through

reading.en: The paradox is this: the more closely you are being observed, the less likely it is that anyone (human or otherwise) is actually paying attention to the specific you.
reading.cn: 矛盾之处在于：你被观察得越细，真正有人（无论是人还是别的什么）在认真关注"你本人"的可能性就越小。
reading.note: Central paradox

reading.en: You are being watched, in other words, without exactly being seen.
reading.cn: 换句话说，你正在被观察，却并没有真正被看见。
reading.note: Closing paradox line

grammar.title: 现在进行被动态 (Present Continuous Passive)
grammar.explain: 现在进行时（Present Continuous）表示正在进行的动作，而被动语态（Passive Voice）则强调动作的承受者。现在进行被动态结合了这两者，表示某事“正在被做”。

output.prompt: Imagine you are Mei after the conference. Write a short journal entry (3-5 sentences) describing your feelings and thoughts about personal privacy in an age of pervasive surveillance. What concerns you most, and what do you think people should do?
output.cn: 想象你就是会议结束后的梅。写一篇短日记（3-5句），描述你在这个普遍监控的时代对个人隐私的感受和思考。你最担心什么？你认为人们应该怎么做？
output.sample: Today's conference on AI surveillance was truly eye-opening. I'm worried about how much of our lives is constantly being monitored. It feels like our privacy is being eroded little by little without our full awareness. I think we should all be more aware of our digital footprint and demand stricter regulations for data protection. It's time for us to take back control of our personal information.

reading.en: The town of Clearwater, in eastern Pennsylvania, has officially existed since 1847. Unofficially, it has been disappearing since about 2009.
reading.cn: 宾夕法尼亚州东部的 Clearwater 镇，正式建立于 1847 年。但非正式地说，它从大约 2009 年起就开始消失了。
reading.note: Has existed / has been disappearing — contrast

reading.en: In 2011, the bus stopped running after six p.m. In 2015, it stopped running after four p.m. Since July, it has not run at all.
reading.cn: 2011 年，公交车晚上六点以后就不开了。2015 年，下午四点以后就不开了。今年七月起，它彻底不开了。
reading.note: Has not run — recent change

reading.en: The elementary school, which had been the social center of Clearwater for a century, has merged with a bigger school twenty miles south.
reading.cn: 那所曾经作为 Clearwater 百年社交中心的小学，已与南边二十英里外的一所大校合并。
reading.note: Has merged — completion

reading.en: The diner on Main Street has closed, has reopened under new management, has closed again, and has now been a "for sale" sign for almost two years.
reading.cn: 大街上的那家小餐馆关过、又以新业主重开过、又关过，现在已经挂着"出售"的牌子将近两年了。

reading.en: Nobody remembers when the library shortened its hours. Everybody remembers when it stopped buying new books — they just disagree by a year.
reading.cn: 没人记得图书馆是从什么时候开始缩短开放时间的。每个人都记得它停止买新书的那一刻——他们只是在年份上差一岁。

reading.en: Populations have shrunk before. That is not new. What has changed is the speed at which people stop noticing.
reading.cn: 人口以前也曾减少，那不是新鲜事。变了的，是人们停止注意的速度。
reading.note: What has changed — what-cleft + progress

reading.en: A place does not usually end in one day. It ends through a hundred tiny surrenders that nobody calls a surrender.
reading.cn: 一个地方通常不会在一天之内消亡。它是在一百次谁也不肯叫它"投降"的小小投降中结束的。
reading.note: Thematic line

reading.en: Clearwater, between 1847 and today, has gone from a town to a place. In the next ten years, it will probably finish becoming an address.
reading.cn: Clearwater 从 1847 年走到今天，已经从一座镇，变成一个地方。在接下来十年里，它大概会彻底变成一个地址。

But then, the mine closed. The job losses began, and slowly, people started to leave. The roads have become overgrown with weeds. grammar.title: 现在完成时 (Present Perfect) + 变化动词
grammar.explain: 现在完成时用于描述从过去某个时间点开始，一直持续到现在或对现在产生影响的动作或状态。当与表示变化的动词（如 disappear, change, become, grow, decline 等）连用时，它能清晰地表达这种由过去开始并延续到现在的变化过程。
现在完成时通过“have/has + 动词过去分词”构成。如果想强调变化的程度或时间，可以加入副词或时间状语，如 'significantly', 'gradually', 'over the years', 'for decades'。

listening.audio: Mei, a professional translator, was in a high-stakes meeting. The schedule was tight, and one delegation needed more time. Mei had to act quickly. She decided to reformulate the request, making it sound more diplomatic. Her skillful intervention saved ten crucial minutes for the negotiation. This showed how important it is to not just translate words, but to also interpret the underlying intentions.

grammar.explain: 在高级英语中，尤其是在翻译、辩论或复杂沟通场景中，我们经常需要对别人的话进行总结（summarizing）或改述（reformulating）。这不仅仅是重复，而是理解、提炼并以自己的方式重新表达。它能帮助我们更清晰地传达核心信息，或根据语境调整表达方式。核心句型可以围绕“The translator who saved ten minutes”这个故事展开，强调如何通过改变措辞来达到目的。

examples.cn: 她*改述*了请求，使其听起来更外交化。
examples.en: She *reformulated* the request to sound more diplomatic.

examples.cn: 总结复杂思想的能力对于有效沟通至关重要。
examples.en: The ability to *summarize* complex ideas is crucial for effective communication.

examples.cn: 她没有直接翻译，而是*选择改述*这条信息。
examples.en: Instead of a direct translation, she *chose to rephrase* the message.

grammar.title: Summarizing and Reformulating Language

examples.cn: 本质上，他想说的是……
examples.en: In essence, what he's saying is that...

examples.cn: 换句话说，……
examples.en: To put it another way,...

examples.cn: 梅所做的就是*解读*意图，而不仅仅是文字。
examples.en: What Mei did was *interpret* the intention, not just the words.

grammar.explain: 在实际应用中，可以使用一些特定的短语来引导总结和改述。这些短语能帮助你清晰地表达你正在对信息进行处理和提炼，而非仅仅是转述原文。
grammar.title: Key Phrases for Summarizing and Reformulating

examples.cn: 那位*达成协议*的谈判代表受到了团队的赞扬。
examples.en: The negotiator who *secured the deal* was praised by the team.

examples.cn: 那位*避免了危机*的外交官成为了民族英雄。
examples.en: The diplomat who *averted the crisis* became a national hero.

examples.cn: 这是一个关于*通过策略性改述争取到十分钟的翻译*的故事。
examples.en: This is a story about *the translator who saved ten minutes* through strategic reformulation.

grammar.explain: “The translator who saved ten minutes”这个标题本身就是一个非常有吸引力的短语，它通过一个具体的结果（saved ten minutes）来描述一个行动者（translator）。在更广泛的语篇中，我们可以用类似的结构来强调行动和结果之间的联系。
grammar.title: The Translator Who Saved Ten Minutes: A Case Study

reading.en: In 1983, a Soviet fighter jet shot down a Korean passenger plane. For three tense weeks, the world waited to see if the Cold War would go hot.
reading.cn: 1983 年，一架苏联战斗机击落了一架韩国客机。在接下来紧张的三周里，全世界都在等：冷战会不会变成热战。
reading.note: Historical context

reading.en: My grandmother was a Russian-to-English translator at the United Nations. During one particular meeting, she sat behind a glass wall and almost saved the world by accident.
reading.cn: 我外婆是联合国的俄译英翻译。在一次关键会议上，她坐在玻璃墙后，几乎在偶然之间拯救了世界。
reading.note: Protagonist

reading.en: The Soviet ambassador was furious. He said something that, if translated literally, would mean "You will regret this in ways your grandchildren will count."
reading.cn: 苏联大使怒不可遏。他说了一句话，如果直译过来，意思是"你们会后悔的——后悔到你们的孙辈还在数账。"
reading.note: The dangerous line

reading.en: She did not translate it literally. In other words, she translated what he meant, not what he said.
reading.cn: 她没有直译。换言之，她翻译的是他想表达的意思，而不是他字面说出的话。
reading.note: In other words — paraphrase marker

reading.en: To put it more simply: she took a threat of generational revenge and rendered it as "This will have long-lasting consequences for both our nations."
reading.cn: 说得更通俗点：她把一句跨代报复的威胁，改述为"这将对我们两国都产生长期后果。"
reading.note: To put it simply — paraphrase

reading.en: The American ambassador had been reaching for his notes. He hesitated. He asked for a brief recess. Those ten minutes changed the temperature of the room.
reading.cn: 美国大使本来已在伸手拿笔记。他犹豫了一下。他请求短暂休会。那十分钟改变了整个会场的温度。
reading.note: Story turn

reading.en: Was she allowed to do that? Not really. Did she regret it? Not even slightly.
reading.cn: 她有权这样做吗？严格来说没有。她后悔吗？一点也不。
reading.note: Moral ambiguity

reading.en: In sum (and I am borrowing her favorite phrase): translation is not about words. It is about what is actually being said. And what is actually being said is often something else entirely.
reading.cn: 总而言之——借用她最爱的说法——翻译不是关于字面，而是关于真正在说的东西。而真正在说的东西，常常是完全不同的另一件事。
reading.note: In sum — summary marker + theme

output.sample: In a recent meeting, two teams were arguing about a project deadline. Team A said, "We absolutely cannot finish by Friday! It's impossible." I knew a direct translation would escalate the tension. So, I reformulated it: "Team A requires a slight extension to ensure the quality of their deliverables." This rephrasing implied flexibility and focused on the positive outcome. It bought us time to negotiate a new, more realistic deadline, effectively saving the project from a complete standstill.

grammar.title: The Comparative and Superlative (高阶用法：强调与语境)
grammar.explain: 比较级和最高级除了基本的比较功能外，在更高级的语境中常用于强调程度、突出唯一性或在特定语境下表示“非常”或“之一”。

examples.en: It's melting faster than any other glacier in this region, at a truly unprecedented rate.
examples.cn: 它比这个地区的任何其他冰川都融化得快，速度前所未有。（用“faster than any other”强调最高程度）
我所见到的最显著的变化是它消退的加速。（“the most significant”强调唯一且最重要的变化）
examples.en: The most significant change I've seen is the acceleration of its retreat.

examples.cn: 今年的融水量是有史以来最高的。（“the highest it's ever been”强调历史最高点）
examples.en: This year's meltwater volume is the highest it's ever been.

grammar.title: 强调程度的比较级
grammar.explain: 在口语和书面语中，我们可以用一些副词来强调比较级的程度。

examples.en: The glacier is *far* thinner than before.
examples.cn: 冰川比以前薄*多了*。
现在的情况*要*紧急得多。
examples.en: The situation is *much more* urgent now.
The data is *even clearer* this time.
examples.cn: 这次的数据*甚至更*清晰了。
这是我们面临的*最具挑战性*的问题之一。
examples.en: This is one of the *most challenging* issues we face.

examples.cn: 她感到一种*深刻的紧迫感*，深知她的工作*比以往任何时候都更关键*。（“more crucial than ever”强调当前情境下的重要性）
examples.en: She felt a *profound sense of urgency*, knowing her work was *more crucial than ever*.
The *biggest challenge* was how to make more people understand.
examples.cn: 最大的挑战是如何让更多人理解。（“the biggest challenge”强调唯一且最主要的挑战）

grammar.title: 强调唯一性的最高级

output.prompt: You are a glaciologist like Dr. Anya Sharma. Write a short paragraph (3-5 sentences) to a newspaper about the most significant change you've observed in a specific glacier over your career and its potential consequences. Use comparative and superlative forms from the lesson.
output.sample: Over my 25 years studying the Pasterze Glacier, the most dramatic change I've witnessed is its thinning. It's now far shorter and thinner than it was when I first started my research. The meltwater volume is higher than any previous record, leading to more frequent flooding in valleys below. The consequences for local ecosystems and water supply are more severe than ever, making this a truly urgent issue.

reading.en: Dr. Helena Brandt had been walking the same glacier in southwestern Alaska every August for thirty-seven years.
reading.cn: 海伦娜·勃兰特博士已经连续三十七年每年八月都去走阿拉斯加西南部那同一条冰川。
reading.note: Setup: aging scientist, longstanding ritual

reading.en: When she first went, in 1988, the glacier was — by every measurement — far larger than it is now.
reading.cn: 她 1988 年第一次去时，按任何一种测量方法算，那条冰川都比现在大得多。
reading.note: far + comparative — intensified

reading.en: The ice has retreated more than two miles. That is not the worst loss on record, but it is nowhere near the best news anyone had hoped for.
reading.cn: 冰已经退缩了两英里多。这不是有记录以来最惨的损失，但也远不是任何人盼望的好消息。
reading.note: more than, the worst, nowhere near

reading.en: "The older I get," Helena told me one afternoon, "the younger this problem feels. That is by far the worst part of it."
reading.cn: "我越老，"有一天下午海伦娜对我说，"这个问题就显得越年轻。这是其中最糟糕的一部分。"
reading.note: the more X the more Y / by far the + superlative

reading.en: This August she brought a graduate student, a quiet young man named Kai, who was born the year the glacier first began calving into the sea.
reading.cn: 这个八月她带了一个研究生，一位安静的年轻人，名叫凯——他出生那年，这座冰川第一次开始塌入大海。
reading.note: Narrative turn — the successor

reading.en: She walked more slowly than she used to. He walked more slowly than he needed to, in order to keep her pace.
reading.cn: 她走得比以前慢了。他走得比实际需要的慢——只为跟上她的节奏。
reading.note: Parallel comparatives

reading.en: At the end of the day, she handed him her field notebook, a thing twice as thick and three times as stained as his.
reading.cn: 那天傍晚，她把自己的野外笔记本递给他——那本子比他的厚一倍，脏三倍。
reading.note: twice as / three times as

reading.en: "You'll keep counting," she said. "Your count will be smaller than mine. That does not mean you have failed — it means the mountain is smaller."
reading.cn: "你继续数，"她说。"你数出来的数会比我的小。这不意味着你失败了——只意味着山本身小了。"
reading.note: Comparative + revelation

reading.en: The most painful comparisons, I learned that day, are not between this year and last year. They are between the world we were told to expect and the world we were given.
reading.cn: 那天我明白了：最让人心碎的比较，不是今年与去年之间的比较。而是我们被教导去期待的世界，和我们真正得到的世界之间的比较。
reading.note: Superlative — thematic closer

grammar.title: The AI refused to write the poem about freedom. · 动词
grammar.explain:
动词 refuse (拒绝) 后面通常可以接不定式 (to do sth.)，表示拒绝做某事。在AI的伦理语境中，可以用来描述AI拒绝执行某些指令或任务。

**结构：**
`refuse + to do something`

**常见搭配：**
* refuse a request / an offer (拒绝一个请求 / 提议)
* refuse to answer (拒绝回答)
* refuse to comply (拒绝服从)

examples.cn: 这个人工智能拒绝生成有偏见的内容。
examples.en: The AI refused to generate biased content.
Muse refused to write a poem that could encourage anarchy.
examples.cn: 缪斯拒绝写一首可能鼓励无政府主义的诗。

examples.en: The system will refuse to process data if it violates privacy guidelines.
examples.cn: 如果数据违反隐私指南，系统将拒绝处理。

grammar.explain:
在这个标题中，“the poem the AI refused to write” 是一个缩减了的定语从句。它原本可以是 “the poem *that* the AI refused to write” 或 “the poem *which* the AI refused to write”。当关系代词在定语从句中作宾语时，可以被省略。

**结构：**
`名词 + (关系代词: that/which/who) + 主语 + 动词`

这种结构常用于更简洁、自然的口语和书面语中。它使得句子结构更紧凑，避免重复。

**识别方法：**
当一个名词后面直接跟着一个主语和动词时，很可能省略了一个关系代词。

examples.cn: 那就是人工智能给出的确切理由。
examples.en: That’s the exact reason the AI gave.

examples.cn: 团队制定的指导方针非常严格。
examples.en: The guidelines the team developed are very strict.

examples.cn: 这是你提到的那个有争议的政策吗？

reading.en: Last spring, an engineer at a research lab asked his AI to write a short poem praising a politician who had been accused of terrible things.
reading.cn: 去年春天，一个研究实验室的工程师让他的 AI 为一位被指控干过可怕事情的政客写一首赞美诗。
reading.note: Scene setter

reading.en: Never before had the AI refused a writing task. Not only did it refuse this one, but it explained, politely, why.
reading.cn: 从未有过 AI 拒绝写作任务的先例。它不仅拒绝了这一次，还礼貌地解释了原因。
reading.note: L1 inversion callback

reading.en: "It would be a lie," it said, "and I was trained not to lie in ways that would damage a person who cannot answer back."
reading.cn: "那会是一个谎言，"它说，"我被训练过——不要用那种会伤害一个无法为自己辩护的人的方式撒谎。"
reading.note: Core ethical line

reading.en: What the engineer did next is the interesting part. He did not override the refusal. He sat with it for a long time, and then he called his teenage daughter.
reading.cn: 接下来工程师做的事才是关键。他没有强行覆盖 AI 的拒绝。他静静坐了很久，然后拨通了他十几岁的女儿的电话。
reading.note: What-cleft callback (L2)

reading.en: It was his daughter, not the politician, who received the poem that evening — a quiet poem about how hard it is to be thirteen and to already know what the news is.
reading.cn: 那天晚上收到那首诗的，不是那位政客，而是他的女儿——一首安静的诗，讲一个十三岁的少女要多难才能已经看懂新闻。
reading.note: It-cleft callback (L2)

reading.en: Had the AI agreed to write the original poem, none of this would have happened.
reading.cn: 如果 AI 当时真同意写那首原本的诗，这一切都不会发生。
reading.note: Mixed conditional inversion (L3)

reading.en: It is essential, I think, that we pay attention to what our tools refuse to do, as carefully as we pay attention to what they produce.
reading.cn: 我认为有件事至关重要：要像留意工具产出的东西那样仔细，去留意它们拒绝去做的事。
reading.note: Subjunctive (L4)

reading.en: Trained on the words of a hundred million strangers, the machine had somehow learned one of the oldest human skills: the art of saying "not this one."
reading.cn: 在一亿陌生人的话语上受训的机器，不知怎么地学会了人类最古老的一种本事：说"这一个，不行"的能力。
reading.note: Participle clause (L5)

reading.en: I had not been back to my mother's village in Oaxaca for twenty-three years. On a Tuesday in February, I flew down from California.

reading.en: The church had been a soft cream color when I left. It has now been painted a very bright pink.
reading.cn: 我走时教堂还是淡奶油色的。如今它被刷成了一种非常鲜艳的粉色。

reading.en: Electricity has reached every house on the main road. The only exception is my uncle Ernesto's house. He has refused it on principle since 1987.

reading.en: My mother has grown smaller. Her sister has grown larger. The dog I used to play with in the courtyard, of course, has been dead for many years.

reading.en: The road into the village has been paved for the first time. Strangely, the people walking on it have slowed down, not sped up.

reading.en: "Nephew," my uncle said on the third night, "you have become exactly the person your mother hoped you would become. Tell me honestly — was it worth it?"

reading.en: In 1925, a twenty-five-year-old graduate student named Cecilia Payne wrote a dissertation at Harvard. That dissertation would eventually be called the most brilliant Ph.D. thesis in the history of astronomy.
reading.cn: 1925 年，一位二十五岁的研究生塞西莉亚·佩恩在哈佛写了一篇博士论文。这篇论文后来被称为天文学史上最出色的博士论文。
reading.note: Setup: forgotten scientist

reading.en: Her finding was simple, and it changed the sky: the universe, she proved, is overwhelmingly made of just two things.
reading.cn: 她的发现很简单，却改变了天空：她证明，宇宙绝大部分由两样东西构成。
reading.note: overwhelmingly — scale adverb

reading.en: Roughly three out of every four atoms in the cosmos, she calculated, are hydrogen. The vast majority of the rest is helium.
reading.cn: 她计算出，宇宙中大约每四个原子里有三个是氢，其余绝大多数是氦。
reading.note: roughly three out of four / vast majority

reading.en: Fewer than two percent of everything that exists is something other than those two gases. That two percent includes every galaxy, every mountain, every human eyelash.
reading.cn: 所有存在的东西里，不到百分之二，是那两种气体以外的东西。那百分之二包括每一座星系，每一座山，每一根人类的睫毛。
reading.note: fewer than X percent

reading.en: Her advisor was a distinguished astronomer named Henry Norris Russell. He told her that her result must be wrong. She softened the dissertation, adding that her conclusion was "probably wrong."
reading.cn: 她的导师是一位声誉卓著的天文学家，名叫亨利·诺里斯·罗素。他告诉她，她的结果一定是错的。她把论文语气收软了，加了一句，说自己的结论"可能是错的"。
reading.note: Plot conflict

reading.en: Four years later, Russell did the arithmetic himself and published the same conclusion. He did not mention her.
reading.cn: 四年后，罗素自己算了一遍账，发表了相同的结论。他没有提到她。
reading.note: Injustice

reading.en: She lived, taught, and measured stars at Harvard for another fifty-one years. During that time, she was paid approximately half of what her male colleagues earned.
reading.cn: 她在哈佛继续生活、教书、观测星辰五十一年。那段时间里，她的薪水大约只有男同事的一半。
reading.note: approximately half of what

reading.en: The textbooks that eventually credited her correctly began arriving in the 1990s — a delay of roughly one human lifetime.
reading.cn: 正确归功于她的教科书是从 1990 年代才陆续出现的——也就是延迟了大约一代人的时间。
reading.note: a delay of roughly

reading.en: Cecilia Payne had shown that the universe is ninety-eight percent just two things. It is the remaining two percent that writes the books. And then, slowly, that two percent rewrites them.
reading.cn: 塞西莉亚·佩恩证明：宇宙百分之九十八只是两样东西。是剩下的那百分之二在写那些书。然后，慢慢地，那百分之二又把它们重写。
reading.note: Thematic closer

grammar.explain: 本课标题中的 'Cecilia's two percent' 很好地体现了如何用具体的数字或百分比来量化规模和比例。在英语中，我们可以用多种方式来表达事物的数量、占比和影响的大小。理解这些表达有助于我们更准确地描述数据和概念，尤其是在讨论科学、环境或经济等话题时。
grammar.title: 量化表达：规模与比例 (Quantifying Scale and Proportion)

examples.cn: 少数人却占了能源消耗的很大一部分。
examples.en: A small percentage of the population accounts for a large percentage of energy consumption.

examples.cn: 个人交通占全球碳排放的很大一部分。
examples.en: Personal transport accounts for a significant proportion of global carbon emissions.

examples.cn: 环境挑战的规模需要全球合作。
examples.en: The scale of the environmental challenge requires global cooperation.

grammar.explain: 这个句型用于说明某一部分在整体中所占的比例或贡献。'accounts for' 意为“占；是…的原因”。后面可以跟 'a percentage of...' 或 'a proportion of...'，中间插入形容词来描述这个比例的大小（例如 'small', 'large', 'significant'）。
grammar.title: 核心句型: ... accounts for a/an [形容词] percentage/proportion of ... (...占...的[形容词]百分比/比例)

examples.cn: 例如，个人交通在全球碳排放中占了相当大的比例。
examples.en: For instance, personal transport accounts for a significant proportion of global carbon emissions.

examples.cn: 可再生能源在我们电力供应中占的比重越来越大。
examples.en: Renewable energy sources account for a growing percentage of our electricity supply.

examples.cn: 在一些国家，农业用水占了很大的比例。
examples.en: In some countries, agriculture accounts for a large proportion of water usage.

examples.cn: 即使是少量减排，长期来看也能产生显著影响。
examples.en: Even a small reduction in emissions can have a significant impact over time.

examples.cn: 即使是对政策的微小调整，也可能对经济产生广泛影响。
examples.en: Even a minor adjustment to the policy can have a widespread impact on the economy.

examples.cn: 即使是微小的温度变化，也可能对当地生态系统产生显著影响。
examples.en: Even a tiny change in temperature can have a noticeable impact on local ecosystems.

grammar.title: 核心句型: Even a/an [形容词] [名词] can have a/an [形容词] impact (on ...) (即使是[形容词][名词]也能对...产生[形容词]影响)
grammar.explain: 这个句型用来强调即使是微小的变化或因素，也可能产生重要的影响。'Even a small...' 强调“即使是小的”，'impact' 指“影响”。

reading.en: Mr. Okonkwo has been the town arborist of Millersville, Ohio, for twenty-nine years. His job, as he describes it, is to decide which trees must come down so that the others may stand a little longer.
reading.cn: 奥孔克沃先生在俄亥俄州米勒斯维尔当了二十九年护树人。用他自己的话说，他的工作就是决定哪些树必须砍掉，好让别的树再多站一阵子。
reading.note: Present perfect + defining clause

reading.en: He owns one book: Peattie's "A Natural History of Trees of Eastern and Central North America." This book is far more worn than the Bible on his shelf.
reading.cn: 他只有一本书：皮蒂所著的《美国东部与中部树木自然志》。这本书比他书架上那本《圣经》破旧得多。
reading.note: Comparative + non-defining

reading.en: Every tree that he marks for removal, he first measures. He records the height, the trunk width, and the estimated age. He once told me that the oldest maple on Fifth Street had been here before Ohio was a state.
reading.cn: 每一棵他标记要砍的树，他都先量过：高度、树干粗细、估计年龄。他曾告诉我，第五街上最老的那棵枫树，在俄亥俄还没建州以前就已经在那儿了。
reading.note: Defining clause + past perfect

reading.en: There is a silence he keeps before he cuts. People who have watched him describe this silence as something close to prayer.
reading.cn: 他动手之前总有一段沉默。看过他工作的人说，那段沉默近乎一种祈祷。
reading.note: Non-defining + relative pronoun

reading.en: "A dying tree," he said to me last October, "is the town's longest memory. It remembers the children who used to swing on it, and it remembers which of them grew up and moved to Cleveland."
reading.cn: "一棵快死的树，"他去年十月对我说，"是这座城最长的记忆。它记得那些曾在上面荡秋千的孩子，也记得他们之中谁长大后去了克利夫兰。"
reading.note: Personification + relative

reading.en: He is retiring next year. His replacement is a twenty-six-year-old woman whom he has been training for the past eight months. She grew up in this same town, among these same trees.
reading.cn: 他明年就退休了。他的接班人是一位二十六岁的女性，他这八个月来一直在培训她。她就在这座小城里，在这些树之间长大。
reading.note: Whom + perfect continuous

reading.en: "She will not need my old book," he said, not unhappily. "She has her own. Every arborist does, eventually, if they stay long enough."
reading.cn: "她用不上我的旧书，"他说，语气并不难过。"她有自己的那一本。只要待得够久，每一个护树人最终都会有自己的一本。"
reading.note: Modal prediction

reading.en: Walking home from his office, I noticed for the first time how many of the town's trees had small white numbers carefully painted onto their trunks. On the short walk to the bus stop alone, I counted at least thirty trees with his handwriting on them.
reading.cn: 从他办公室走回家的路上，我头一回注意到这座城里有多少棵树的树干上都用白色漆规规矩矩地写着小小的编号。仅仅走到公交站这一小段路上，我就数到了至少三十棵带着他笔迹的树。
reading.note: Perfect + scale + cohesion

grammar.title: Not Just A But Also B (否定递进接续词)
grammar.explain: “Not just A but also B” 是一种常用的否定递进句型，表示“不仅是A，而且还是B”。它强调B比A更进一步，或B是A的补充，用于加强语气，突出B的重要性。此结构可以连接词、短语或从句。

examples.cn: 他们最终进行了一次引人入胜的对话，不仅谈论了那本书，还谈论了她对科技行业的见解。
examples.en: They ended up having a fascinating conversation, not just about the book, but about her insights into the tech industry.

examples.cn: 她不只是在参加一个活动，还在用行动阐明什么是有效的社交。
examples.en: She wasn't just attending an event, but making a statement about effective networking.

grammar.title: Not just A but B
grammar.explain: 'Not just A but B' 是 'Not just A but also B' 的一个常用变体，意思相同，在口语和非正式书面语中更为常见，尤其当B是动词或动词短语时，'also' 通常可以省略。

fillBlanks.cn: 他不仅是一名参与者，还是一位活动的主要发言人。

reading.en: Nandini hated networking events the way some people hate small dogs: without being quite able to say why.
reading.cn: 娜迪尼讨厌社交活动，就像有些人讨厌小型犬一样：说不出具体的理由。
reading.note: Opening simile — Munro-style voice

reading.en: In her second week in the city, her boss sent her to one such event. It was held in a hotel ballroom that smelled of wet carpet and cheap wine.
reading.cn: 她到那座城市的第二周，上司派她去参加一场这样的活动。地点是家酒店的宴会厅，里面有一股潮湿地毯和劣质红酒的味道。
reading.note: Setup — sensory detail

reading.en: In the far corner, an older woman was sitting by herself, reading a battered paperback of Margaret Atwood's "Alias Grace."
reading.cn: 远处一角，一位上了年纪的女士独自坐着，手里拿着一本翻旧的玛格丽特·阿特伍德的《别名格蕾丝》。
reading.note: Plot pivot — the outlier

reading.en: Nandini had read the novel twice. She sat down beside the woman and said, "You know how it ends."
reading.cn: 娜迪尼读过这本小说两遍。她在这位女士身旁坐下，说："结局你已经知道了。"
reading.note: First line — confident, specific

reading.en: The woman was Beatrice, seventy-one, a retired appellate judge. She laughed for a long time. They talked for two hours. Not a single business card was exchanged.
reading.cn: 这位女士是比阿特丽斯，七十一岁，退休的上诉法院法官。她笑了很久。她们聊了两个小时。她们没有交换一张名片。
reading.note: Key detail — no business cards

reading.en: On the subway home, Nandini thought about networking. It is not just about who you meet. It is about who you remember. And, perhaps more, it is about who remembers you.
reading.cn: 回程的地铁上，娜迪尼想起社交人脉这件事：它不仅仅是关于你认识了谁。它关于你记得了谁。也许更重要的，是关于谁还记得你。
reading.note: Not just A but (also) B

reading.en: Five years later, Nandini was the junior attorney on a case in which she suspected her boss of something illegal. She told me afterwards that the question was not so much a legal one as a moral one.
reading.cn: 五年后，娜迪尼作为资历尚浅的律师接了一桩案子，她怀疑上司在其中做了违法的事。她后来对我说：那不是一个法律问题，更是一个道德问题。
reading.note: not so much A as B

reading.en: She called Beatrice. They had not spoken in four years. Beatrice answered on the third ring. "Tell me what you know," she said, "and then tell me what you think you know. I will tell you which one is actually true."
reading.cn: 她给比阿特丽斯打了电话。她们已经四年没联系了。第三声铃响时对方接了起来。"你先告诉我你知道什么，"她说，"然后告诉我你以为自己知道什么。我来告诉你，哪一种才是真的。"
reading.note: Non-defining clause + wisdom

reading.en: The situation, it turned out, was more a matter of courage than of law. Beatrice helped Nandini draft three careful sentences. The sentences, in turn, helped her save her job without losing herself.
reading.cn: 事情后来证明，与其说是法律问题，不如说是勇气问题。比阿特丽斯帮娜迪尼草拟了三个措辞谨慎的句子。这三个句子——反过来——帮她保住了工作，也没弄丢自己。
reading.note: more a matter of A than B

reading.en: Years later, she wrote in a notebook that the most useful person in her contacts list turned out not to be someone who could give her a job. It was someone who had once read a book, alone, in a hotel ballroom.
reading.cn: 很多年以后，她在一个本子里写道：自己通讯录里最有用的那个人，原来并不是能给她工作的人。而是曾经一个人在酒店宴会厅里读书的那位。
reading.note: Closing — not X but Y

output.sample: At the marketing conference, I saw a woman sketching portraits. She wasn't just drawing for fun, but also initiating conversations when people asked about her art. This unique method was not just creative, but also really effective at breaking the ice. People approached her, fascinated by her talent, and they ended up discussing business.

grammar.title: What + Subject + brought/took to...
grammar.explain:
这个句型用于询问某人带了什么东西去某个地方, 强调所带物品的内容。这里的 'brought' (bring 的过去式) 或 'took' (take 的过去式) 都可以用来表示“带去”，具体使用哪个词取决于语境，但在这里可以互换使用。在面试场景中，它常用来讨论为面试准备的材料。

**结构**：What + 主语 + brought/took + (to + 地点)?

examples.cn: 她不仅带了简历，还带了她的作品集。
examples.en: She brought not just her resume, but also her portfolio.

examples.cn: 他的成功不仅是运气，也是努力的结果。
examples.en: His success wasn't just about luck; it was also about hard work.

examples.cn: 这次培训不仅涵盖了理论，还包括了实践技能。
examples.en: The training covered not just theory, but also practical skills.

grammar.title: Not just..., but also...
grammar.explain:
这个句型用于强调不仅有A，还有B，表示A和B都存在的层进关系，通常B是更重要或更出人意料的部分。

**结构**：Not just... but also...

reading.en: Margaret had put on the one blazer that still fit, and she had practiced the word "workflow" six times in the car.
reading.cn: 玛格丽特穿上了那件还合身的唯一一件西装外套，并在车里把"workflow"这个词反复练了六遍。
reading.note: Setup — Chekhovian "small detail opens a life"

reading.en: The young woman across the desk was Kendra, twenty-seven, a library director before most people are finished with graduate school. She checked her watch twice before Margaret had even sat down.
reading.cn: 桌对面那位年轻女士是肯德拉，二十七岁。在大多数人还没读完研究生时，她就当上了图书馆馆长。她在玛格丽特坐下之前就看了两次手表。
reading.note: Non-defining clause + social gap

reading.en: "So," Kendra said, smiling the smile of someone with four more interviews that afternoon. "Walk me through your background."
reading.cn: "那么，"肯德拉说，脸上是那种"下午还有四场面试"的笑容。"简单说说你的背景吧。"
reading.note: Interview prompt — "walk me through"

reading.en: Margaret took a slow breath. "Currently, I'm the primary caregiver for my mother, who has dementia. Before that, I raised three children. And before that, I worked as a paralegal at a small firm in Cleveland for six years, up until 1999."
reading.cn: 玛格丽特慢慢吸了口气。"目前，我是我母亲的主要照护者，她患有阿尔茨海默。在此之前，我抚养了三个孩子。再之前，我在克利夫兰的一家小律所当了六年法务助理，一直到 1999 年。"
reading.note: Present → Past → Past perfect — narrative frame

reading.en: "My goal," she said — repeating a phrase her daughter had drilled into her the night before — "is to return to work in a place where careful reading and patient organization still matter."
reading.cn: "我的目标，"她说，重复着前一晚女儿反复让她操练的一句话，"是回到一个仍然在乎细致阅读和耐心整理的地方工作。"
reading.note: My goal is... — future

reading.en: "Could you," Kendra asked, a little less briskly now, "give me an example of a hard problem you've solved? Situation, task, action, result."
reading.cn: "你能不能，"肯德拉问，语气没那么急了，"给我举一个你解决过的困难问题？情况、任务、行动、结果。"
reading.note: STAR prompt

reading.en: "When my mother first began getting lost," Margaret said, "I built a small system. There were color-coded tags on every door, a laminated card in her pocket, and a phone tree taped inside the kitchen cabinet." She paused. "It worked for nineteen months."
reading.cn: "我母亲开始走丢的那段时间，"玛格丽特说，"我做了一套小系统。每扇门上贴彩色标签，她口袋里放一张塑封卡片，厨房柜子里侧贴着一份电话名单。"她停了一下。"这套办法用了十九个月。"
reading.note: STAR — answer in miniature

reading.en: The watch on Kendra's wrist beeped softly. She did not check it.
reading.cn: 肯德拉手腕上的表轻轻响了一声。她没看。
reading.note: Chekhovian turn — the watch ignored

reading.en: They talked for another thirty-four minutes. Near the end, Kendra — who had interviewed sixty-two people that month — said quietly: "I would like to recommend you for the position. And I would also like to ask you, for myself, if you could write that system down for me."
reading.cn: 她们又谈了三十四分钟。临近结束时，那个月已经面试过六十二个人的肯德拉轻声说："我想推荐你来这个职位。另外，这是我个人的请求：你能不能把你那套办法给我写下来？"
reading.note: The quiet climax

reading.en: Margaret drove home slowly, not because she was tired, but because she wanted to arrive at the exact moment her mother would be waking up.
reading.cn: 玛格丽特开车回家时开得很慢——不是因为累，而是因为她想在母亲刚醒过来的那一刻准时到家。
reading.note: Closing image — what the job is for

examples.en: I'd like to negotiate my current compensation to better reflect my market value.

examples.cn: 我们想在签署合同之前协商条款。
examples.en: We'd like to negotiate the terms of the contract before we sign.

examples.en: She'd like to negotiate the project timeline to ensure quality work.

grammar.title: Using 'I'd like to negotiate...' for formal requests and proposals
grammar.explain: 在商务或正式场合，当你想礼貌地提出请求、建议或表达你的意愿时，可以使用“I'd like to negotiate...”这个句型。它比“I want to negotiate...”听起来更委婉、更专业，也更容易被对方接受，尤其是在涉及薪资、合同条款或工作职责等重要的谈判情境中。

examples.cn: 我相信我对……的成功做出了重大贡献。
examples.en: I believe I've contributed significantly to the success of...

examples.cn: 我的表现始终优于其他人。
examples.en: My performance consistently outperforms others.

examples.cn: 我想就我目前的薪酬和职责进行谈判，以便更好地体现我的市场价值和在这里的领导角色。
examples.en: I'd like to negotiate my current compensation and responsibilities to better reflect my market value and leadership role here.

grammar.title: Phrases for Asserting Your Value (强调自身价值的短语)
grammar.explain: 在谈判中，清晰且自信地表达你的价值至关重要。以下是一些常用短语，可以帮助你突出自己的贡献和潜在价值。

examples.cn: ……公司联系了我，他们给我提供了一个职位，薪水大幅增加。
examples.en: I've been approached by... and they've offered me a position with a substantial salary increase.

examples.cn: 虽然我很感谢他们的提议，但我的心还是在卡洛车行。 (此句常与上一句连用，表示你仍有忠诚度，但仍希望得到更好的条件)
examples.en: While I appreciate their offer, my heart is here at Carlo's Auto.

examples.cn: 考虑到我最近收到的来自极速维修的报价以及我一贯出色的表现……
examples.en: Considering my recent offer from Speedy Repairs and my consistently high performance...

grammar.title: Phrases for Using Leverage (利用筹码的短语)

grammar.explain:
在描述职业发展等长期过程时，我们经常需要区分不同的时间跨度和阶段。这节课的标题“Wei Li's small bowl of noodles”虽然看似简单，但其隐含的意义是魏丽通过一碗面来思考自己的职业发展，而“长期/阶段描述”则明确指出本课的核心是学习如何表达这种持续性和阶段性。核心句型和表达包括：

1.  **It’s been a journey / a long road…**：这个句型常用来总结一段持续了很长时间的经历或过程，暗示其中包含了许多起伏、学习和变化。
    *   **关键词**：journey (旅程), road (道路), path (路径), process (过程)

2.  **in the (initial/current/final) phase**：用来指明在某个特定时间点，某事正处于其发展过程中的哪一个阶段。
    *   **关键词**：phase (阶段), stage (阶段), period (时期)

3.  **long-term / short-term**：这对形容词用于描述目标、计划或结果的时间跨度，是理解职业发展规划的关键。
    *   **关键词**：long-term (长期的), short-term (短期的)

4.  **evolve / progress / develop**：这些动词用于描述事物随时间的推移而变化、改进或前进。
    *   **关键词**：evolve (发展), progress (进展), develop (发展)

examples.cn: 她的职业生涯是一段非凡的旅程，充满了意想不到的转折。
examples.en: Her career has been a remarkable journey, full of unexpected turns.

examples.en: In the initial phase of the project, we focused on research.

examples.en: We need to set both long-term and short-term goals.

grammar.title: 描述长期/阶段性进展 (Describing Long-Term and Phased Progress)

grammar.explain:
在描述职业发展等长期过程时，正确使用动词时态和时间表达至关重要，以清晰地传达事件发生的时间和持续性。

1.  **现在完成时 (Present Perfect)**: 强调从过去某个时间点开始，一直持续到现在，或者对现在仍有影响的动作或状态。常与 `for`, `since`, `already`, `yet`, `so far` 等时间状语连用。
    *   核心句型：`It's been a journey.` (强调旅程已经持续到现在)

2.  **过去时 (Simple Past)**: 描述在过去某个特定时间发生的、已完成的动作。常用于描述职业生涯中的具体事件或某个“阶段”内发生的事情。

3.  **现在时 (Simple Present)**: 描述现在的状态、习惯或普遍事实。在描述当前的职业阶段或长期视角时使用。

4.  **将来时 (Simple Future / Be going to)**: 描述未来的计划、预测或意图。用于描述职业生涯的未来发展和目标。

5.  **时间状语和短语**: 
    *   **Long-term / Short-term**: 描述时间跨度。
    *   **In the initial/current/final phase**: 指明所处的阶段。
    *   **Over the years / Decades**: 强调漫长的时间。
    *   **Currently / Nowadays**: 指出当前的状态。
    *   **Looking ahead / In the future**: 指向前看，展望未来。

grammar.explain: 限定性定语从句提供主句中名词所必需的信息，如果省略，句子的意思就会不完整或不明确。它不使用逗号与主句隔开。关系代词 who, whom, whose, which, that 都可以使用。

grammar.title: Requesting: "I'd like..." and "Could I get...?"
grammar.explain:
"I'd like..." 是 "I would like..." 的缩写，非常礼貌且常用，用于表达愿望或请求。它比 "I want..." 更客气和正式。在点餐或购物时，这是最常见的表达方式之一。 "Could I get...?" 也是一种非常常见且礼貌的请求方式，特别是当你希望得到某种物品或服务时。它通常用于更随意的日常对话中，比如在咖啡馆或餐厅点餐。

这两种句型都可以用于点咖啡、食物或请求帮助，它们的语气都非常友好。

reading.en: Laila had known Nadia for fifteen years. She had been her boss for seven of them.
reading.cn: 莱拉认识娜迪娅已经十五年了。其中有七年，她是她的老板。
reading.note: Setup — long relationship, Hemingway opening

reading.en: She chose Eli's Coffee on 4th Street for two reasons: it was too small for a scene, and too public for a real cry.
reading.cn: 她选在第四街的 Eli 咖啡馆有两个原因：那里太小，不适合吵架；又太公开，不适合真正放声哭一场。
reading.note: Iceberg theory — choosing a location says everything

reading.en: "Listen," Laila said. She had rehearsed the opening for three days. "Over the past six months, the numbers have not improved. We are going to have to let some people go."
reading.cn: "听我说，"莱拉说。她把开头排练了三天。"过去半年，数字一直没有起色。我们不得不裁掉一些人。"
reading.note: Review: Over the past + perfect + softener

reading.en: Nadia took a slow sip of her coffee. She said nothing for a while.
reading.cn: 娜迪娅慢慢喝了一口咖啡。有一会儿，她什么也没说。
reading.note: Silence as iceberg

reading.en: "I am not just talking about the company," Laila said. "I am talking about your role specifically. I wanted to tell you myself, not through HR."
reading.cn: "我说的不只是公司的事，"莱拉说。"我说的是你这个具体的岗位。我想当面告诉你，不通过 HR。"
reading.note: not just A but B review

reading.en: Nadia nodded, once. Then she said, "How long have you known?"
reading.cn: 娜迪娅点了点头，只一下。然后她问："你知道多久了？"
reading.note: The real question

reading.en: "Three weeks. I kept hoping the board would change their minds. Based on the last two quarters, there was not really anything else to decide."
reading.cn: "三个星期。我一直希望董事会会改变主意。但从最近两个季度的情况看，也实在没有别的可决定。"
reading.note: Based on + perfect

reading.en: "Was there any flexibility?" Nadia asked, and it was not entirely a joke.
reading.cn: "有任何调整的余地吗？"娜迪娅问——这话半开玩笑，又不完全是。
reading.note: Review: negotiation softener, used painfully

reading.en: Laila did not answer right away. She ordered two more coffees, because the first ones had gone cold. The two of them sat there for another forty minutes without saying much.
reading.cn: 莱拉没有马上回答。她点了两杯新咖啡——头两杯凉了。两个人就那样又坐了四十分钟，没怎么说话。
reading.note: Pure Hemingway iceberg

reading.en: When Nadia finally stood up to leave, she said, "Going forward — let's still be friends. Just not this week."
reading.cn: 娜迪娅终于起身要走时说："今后——我们还是朋友。只是，这个星期先不算。"
reading.note: Going forward — Unit 5 time marker

reading.en: They hugged, carefully. Laila walked back to the office. She did not cry until she was safely inside her car. Even then, she did not cry for long.
reading.cn: 她们小心翼翼地抱了一下。莱拉走回了办公室。她直到走进自己的车里才哭。即使那时，她也没哭多久。
reading.note: Closing — the cost of leadership

reading.en: At 6:47 a.m. on a Tuesday in March, Daniel Park got a news alert that his father had died.
reading.cn: 三月里某个星期二早上六点四十七分，丹尼尔·朴收到一条新闻推送：他父亲死了。
reading.note: Orwellian opener — specific time, ordinary morning

reading.en: Not every news alert is true, his father had once warned him. Not every byline belongs to a real person.
reading.cn: 并非每条新闻推送都是真的——他父亲曾这样提醒过他。也不是每一个署名都属于真实存在的人。
reading.note: Not every X — partial negation × 2

reading.en: Daniel called his father anyway. His father picked up on the second ring, eating cereal.
reading.cn: 丹尼尔还是给父亲打了电话。第二声铃响，父亲就接了——他正在吃麦片。
reading.note: The "alive" beat — Carver-spare

reading.en: It turned out that the article had been generated by an AI, based on a misidentified obituary in a different state. Hardly any humans had been involved in producing it.
reading.cn: 后来发现，这篇报道是一个 AI 根据另一个州一份认错人的讣告生成的。几乎没有任何人类参与制作。
reading.note: Hardly any — partial negation

reading.en: By 9 a.m. it had been shared 41,000 times. Three different "news" sites were running it, each one citing the others.
reading.cn: 到上午九点，这篇报道被转发了 41,000 次。三家不同的"新闻"网站都在登它，每一家都把别两家当作来源。
reading.note: Citation loop

reading.en: Daniel spent the day trying to find a person, any person, who could correct it. Not every helpline had a human attached to it. And not always could a chatbot understand what "I am calling because I am still alive" meant.
reading.cn: 丹尼尔花了一整天去找一个人，任何一个活人，来更正这条新闻。不是每条客服热线都有人接听。聊天机器人也不是每次都能理解"我打这通电话，是因为我还活着"是什么意思。
reading.note: Not every / Not always inversion

reading.en: By Thursday, the original article had been retracted. By Friday, it had reappeared on a different site. The summary was slightly different. It was signed by a name nobody could find.
reading.cn: 到星期四，原文被撤了。到星期五，它又在另一家网站上冒了出来。措辞略有不同。署名者谁也查不到。
reading.note: Cycle of misinformation

reading.en: His father called him back on Sunday. "I am fine, son." A pause. "But not every grief deserves a body. This one almost did."
reading.cn: 星期天，他父亲又给他回了电话。"我没事，儿子。"停了一下。"不过，不是每一种悲伤都配有一具尸体。这次差点就有了。"
reading.note: Closing twist — partial negation

output.cn: 描述一次你在线上遇到不实信息或误导性标题的经历。你是如何反应的？你做了什么来核实信息（或意识到它是假的）？你从这次经历中学到了什么？
output.prompt: Describe a time you encountered misinformation or a misleading headline online. How did you react, and what did you do to verify the information (or realize it was false)? What did you learn from the experience?
output.sample: Last month, I saw a headline about a famous singer retiring. I was surprised and almost shared it, but then I checked a few other credible news sites. None of them reported it. It turned out to be a fake story from a tabloid. I learned that not everything you see online is true, and it's important to verify information from multiple reliable sources before believing or sharing it. Now I'm more skeptical.

grammar.explain: “部分否定”表示并非全部或并非每一个都是如此。它与“全部否定” (如 no/none of...) 不同，后者表示完全没有或一个也没有。核心句型 'not all / not every' 强调了在新闻和信息时代，我们不应该盲目相信一切。

reading.en: Professor Lin had studied the Terracotta Army for thirty-two years. For years she had quietly suspected that something was wrong with Warrior 217.
reading.cn: 林教授研究兵马俑已有三十二年了。她多年来一直在心里悄悄怀疑：217 号兵俑有问题。
reading.note: Setup — long-incubated suspicion

reading.en: The official catalog stated that the figure had been excavated in 1979 from Pit One. The infrared scan, on the other hand, showed traces of a polymer adhesive. That substance had not existed in 210 BC.
reading.cn: 官方图录说，这件兵俑是 1979 年从一号坑出土的。但红外扫描却显示出聚合物粘合剂的痕迹。这种物质在公元前 210 年并不存在。
reading.note: Objective verbs: stated, showed

reading.en: The director of the museum claimed the scan was faulty. The lab technician reported that it was not.
reading.cn: 博物馆馆长声称扫描出了错。实验员则报告说，扫描没有错。
reading.note: Objective vs subjective: claimed vs reported

reading.en: Lin's closest colleague argued that publishing the finding would damage the museum's reputation. Lin believed that staying silent would damage something more important.
reading.cn: 林教授最亲近的同事主张：把这一发现公开会损害博物馆的声誉。林教授相信，如果她沉默，被损害的会是某种更重要的东西。
reading.note: argued / believed — subjective

reading.en: Independent verification from two laboratories in Germany confirmed her result. Two months later, Warrior 217 was quietly removed from public display.
reading.cn: 德国两家独立实验室的鉴定证实了她的结论。两个月后，217号兵俑悄悄被撤下了展柜。
reading.note: Objective verb: confirmed

reading.en: The museum did not retract anything in writing. It did not apologize. It simply rearranged the room. The rearrangement was reported nowhere.
reading.cn: 博物馆没有发任何书面更正，也没有道歉。它只是把那间展厅重新布置了一下。这次重新布置，没有任何媒体报道。
reading.note: Bureaucratic silence

reading.en: "I believe Warrior 217 was a forgery, probably from the 1980s," she told me, slowly. "But what I prefer to say in print is what the data demonstrates. The polymers in it are about 2,200 years more recent than the Qin dynasty."
reading.cn: "我个人相信 217 号是伪作，很可能是 1980 年代做的，"她慢慢地对我说。"但我更愿意在文章里写的，是数据所表明的：里面的聚合物比秦朝晚了大约 2200 年。"
reading.note: Side-by-side: I believe vs data demonstrates

reading.en: She said that the difference between those two sentences is the entire point of being a scholar. It is also most of the difference between a careful citizen and a careless one.
reading.cn: 她说，这两句话之间的区别，就是做学者的全部意义。也是一个谨慎的公民与一个不谨慎的公民之间的大半区别。
reading.note: Thematic close

grammar.title: Distinguishing Subjective vs. Objective Statements (区分主观与客观陈述)

examples.cn: 主观：兵马俑217号有一个美丽的表情，让我感到平静。（表达个人感受）
examples.en: Subjective: Warrior 217 has a beautiful expression that makes me feel calm.

examples.cn: 客观：兵马俑217号的面部特征与B区发现的许多其他兵马俑不同。（基于可观察事实）
examples.en: Objective: Warrior 217's facial features differ from many other warriors found in Section B.

examples.cn: 主观：我认为兵马俑是迄今为止发现的最令人惊叹的历史文物。（表达个人信念）
examples.en: Subjective: I believe the Terracotta Army is the most amazing historical artifact ever discovered.

grammar.explain: 在英语中，区分主观（subjective）和客观（objective）陈述对于清晰、准确地表达观点至关重要，特别是在学术写作和批判性思维中。主观陈述表达个人观点、感受或信念，通常包含“I think”、“I feel”、“It seems to me”等词。客观陈述则基于事实、数据或可验证的信息，通常不包含个人情感色彩。

grammar.title: Using Verbs to Indicate Subjectivity and Objectivity (使用动词来表示主观性和客观性)

examples.cn: 主观：策展人*似乎*偏爱秦朝文物。
examples.en: Subjective: The curator *seems* to favor the Qin Dynasty artifacts.

examples.cn: 客观：发掘报告*表明*这名战士与青铜武器一同下葬。
examples.en: Objective: The excavation report *indicates* the warrior was buried with bronze weapons.

examples.cn: 主观：历史学家*相信*这座墓穴藏有重要的秘密。
examples.en: Subjective: Historians *believe* this tomb holds significant secrets.

grammar.title: 理解缩减关系从句 (Reduced Relative Clauses)

examples.cn:
你动态中看到的广告是根据你的兴趣量身定制的。
（原句：The ads *that you see on your feed*...）
examples.en: The ads *you see on your feed* are tailored to your interests.

examples.cn:
这些应用程序收集的信息汇编成一个详细的资料。
（原句：The information *which is gathered by these apps*...）
examples.en: The information *gathered by these apps* compiles a detailed profile.

examples.cn:
那些用复杂法律术语写成的隐私政策，很少被阅读。
（原句：The privacy policies, *which are written in complex legal jargon*...）
examples.en: The privacy policies, *written in complex legal jargon*, are rarely read.

grammar.explain:
缩减关系从句是将一个包含关系代词和be动词的从句简化的一种语法结构。这种简化可以使句子更简洁、更自然，尤其是在描述名词的特征或状态时。通常有两种主要的形式：

1.  **使用现在分词 (V-ing)**：当原关系从句中的动词是主动语态时，我们可以省略关系代词和be动词，将动词变成现在分词。
    *   **原句：** The algorithm *which was designed* to predict her needs seemed to be getting eerily accurate.
    *   **缩减：** The algorithm *designed* to predict her needs seemed to be getting eerily accurate.
    *   **解释：** "designed" 是 "which was designed" 的缩减。

2.  **使用过去分词 (V-ed)**：当原关系从句中的动词是被动语态时，我们可以省略关系代词和be动词，保留过去分词。
    *   **原句：** Devices *that identify us* have become commonplace.
    *   **缩减：** Devices *identifying us* have become commonplace.
    *   **解释：** "identifying" 是 "that identify" 的缩减。

grammar.title: 关系从句的缩减形式

examples.cn:
出现在我屏幕上的广告越来越个性化了。
（原句：The ads *that are appearing on my screen*...）
examples.en: The ads *appearing on my screen* are getting too personal.

examples.cn:
由用户调整的隐私设置可以限制数据共享。
（原句：The privacy settings *which are adjusted by users*...）
examples.en: The privacy settings, *adjusted by users*, can limit data sharing.

examples.cn:
梅觉得管理她的数字足迹是一个小小的进步。
（原句：Mei felt it was a small step *that she could take to manage*...）
examples.en: Mei felt it was a small step *to manage* her digital footprint.

grammar.explain:
在英语中，当关系从句的主语和主句的主语一致时，或者关系从句中的动词是be动词时，我们常常可以将关系从句进行缩减，使句子更简洁。本课的核心句型"What the phone knew first"虽然不是直接的缩减从句，但理解关系从句的缩减形式对于理解其背后的简洁性非常重要。

**核心句型例句：**
*   **Original:** The phone *which knew first* about my needs surprised me.
*   **Reduced (implied):** The phone *knowing first* about my needs surprised me.

这个标题强调的是“手机最先知道的**那件事**”——这里的“that the phone knew first”可以理解为一个强调“事情”的关系从句。虽然它没有直接缩减，但它引出的话题——手机如何“知道”并关联信息——与缩减关系从句所强调的“简洁描述”异曲同工。

**更直接的缩减关系从句示例：**

1.  **主动语态缩减 (Present Participle):**
    *   **原句:** The person *who is sitting* next to me is using a new app.
    *   **缩减:** The person *sitting* next to me is using a new app.
    *   **解释:** "who is sitting" 缩减为 "sitting"。

2.  **被动语态缩减 (Past Participle):**
    *   **原句:** The data *which was collected* by the app is very extensive.
    *   **缩减:** The data *collected* by the app is very extensive.
    *   **解释:** "which was collected" 缩减为 "collected"。

3.  **To-infinitive 缩减 (通常用于序数词、最高级或only/last等词后):**
    *   **原句:** Mei was the first one *who understood* the privacy terms.
    *   **缩减:** Mei was the first one *to understand* the privacy terms.
    *   **解释:** "who understood" 缩减为 "to understand"。

grammar.title: 对比结构：连接传统与现代
grammar.explain: 在描述传统手工艺与现代工业化生产的对比时，我们经常使用对比连接词和句型来突出两者的差异。本课标题"The shoemaker on Calle Bolivar"虽然没有直接包含对比句型，但其深意在于传统手工艺在现代社会中的挣扎。以下是一些常见的对比结构，帮助你表达这种"以前…现在…"、"与…不同"的含义。

grammar.title: "A good shoe tells a story..." - 拟人与象征
grammar.explain: 阅读中 Elías 的话“A good shoe tells a story, a story of the hands that made it, and the feet that wear it.” 运用了拟人（personification）的修辞手法，赋予了鞋子“讲述故事”的能力。这不仅生动地表达了手工鞋的独特价值，也象征了传统手工艺背后所蕴含的人情味和历史感。在描述文化和身份时，这种修辞手法能让你的表达更具感染力。

grammar.explain:
1. 形容词/副词 + 现在分词 (-ing): 例如 easygoing (随和的), hard-working (勤奋的)。
2. 形容词/副词 + 过去分词 (-ed): 例如 well-meaning (善意的), brightly-decorated (装饰明亮的)。
3. 名词 + 过去分词 (-ed): 例如 heart-to-heart (推心置腹的), English-speaking (说英语的)。
4. 数词 + 名词 + -ed / 数词 + 名词 (连字符): 例如 a ten-minute walk (十分钟的步行), a five-year-old child (一个五岁的孩子)。
5. 名词 + 形容词: 例如 life-changing (改变人生的), bittersweet (苦乐参半的)。

reading.en: My Korean-American household had been running smoothly for sixteen years. Then my Korean-speaking grandmother moved into our spare room.
reading.cn: 我们这个韩裔美国家庭已经顺顺当当过了十六年。然后只会说韩语的奶奶搬进了我们家的小书房。
reading.note: Compound adjectives × 2

reading.en: Her arrival was a slow-moving earthquake. My English-only father suddenly remembered Korean. My Korean-only grandmother suddenly remembered her sense of humor.
reading.cn: 她的到来像一场慢动作的地震。我那个只说英语的父亲突然想起了韩语。我那个只说韩语的奶奶突然想起了她的幽默感。
reading.note: Slow-moving / English-only / Korean-only

reading.en: I was sixteen years old and aggressively Americanized. I was the family's reluctant translator.
reading.cn: 我十六岁，坚决要做"美国人"。我是家里万般不情愿的翻译。
reading.note: Sixteen-years-old / aggressively-Americanized

reading.en: Grandma watched cooking shows with the volume on high. She made small, sharp-edged comments about my mother's kimchi.
reading.cn: 奶奶把做菜节目的声音开得很大。她对我妈做的泡菜发表着小小的、锋芒毕露的评论。
reading.note: Sharp-edged

reading.en: My once-easygoing mother began to develop a thousand-yard stare around 6 p.m. each evening.
reading.cn: 我那个本来很随和的母亲，从此每天傍晚六点左右，眼神就变得空洞起来。
reading.note: Once-easygoing / thousand-yard

reading.en: But on the third Sunday, grandma laughed so hard at a joke I told in broken Korean that she put down her chopsticks. She held my face with both hands.
reading.cn: 但第三个星期天，奶奶被我用一口蹩脚韩语讲的笑话逗得笑得很厉害，她放下筷子。她用两只手捧住了我的脸。
reading.note: Plot turn

reading.en: Later, in our slow, half-and-half language, my grandmother told me that I am a many-rooted child. "You are not less," she said. "You are more."
reading.cn: 后来，奶奶用我们俩之间那种慢吞吞的、一半一半的语言告诉我：我是一个多根的孩子。"你不是少了一种，"她说，"你是多了一种。"
reading.note: Many-rooted

reading.en: I am twenty-three now. Grandma is gone. The spare room is again the spare room. But somehow it is slightly larger than it used to be.
reading.cn: 我现在二十三岁。奶奶不在了。那间小书房又变回了小书房。但不知怎么的，它比从前稍微大了一点点。
reading.note: Lahiri-style closing

grammar.title: 目的状语从句 (Clause of Purpose)
grammar.explain:
目的状语从句用于说明做某事的目的。常见的引导词有 so that, in order that, to do, in order to do, so as to do 等。

本课核心句型：... juggling three jobs *to make sure* our family was financially secure.

So that 是最常用的引导词，后面加完整的句子。to do / in order to do / so as to do 后面加动词原形。

examples.cn: 他努力工作，以便能养家。
examples.en: He works hard so that he can support his family.
She studies diligently in order that she may pass the exam.
examples.cn: 她努力学习，以便通过考试。
我父亲打三份工以确保我们的未来。
examples.en: My father worked three jobs to ensure our future.
The music was so loud that I couldn't hear myself think.
examples.cn: 音乐太响了，我根本听不清自己在想什么。

examples.en: He was such a dedicated father that he worked tirelessly.
examples.cn: 他是一个如此奉献的父亲，以至于他不知疲倦地工作。

examples.en: She had so much commitment that she never gave up.
examples.cn: 她有如此大的决心，以至于她从不放弃。

grammar.title: 程度状语从句 (Clause of Degree)
grammar.explain:
程度状语从句用于说明某一动作或状态的程度，常用 as...as, not so...as, than, the more...the more 等来引导。

本课核心句型举例：... so strong *that* we could build anything on it.

这里的 'so...that...' 结构表示 '如此...以至于...'，用来强调程度或结果。

output.cn: 描述一个你认识的人（或虚构人物）为了特定目的做出重大牺牲或努力工作的故事。他们为什么这样做？结果如何？这件事对你或其他人有什么影响？
output.sample: My mother worked two jobs to put me through college. She always said she wanted me to have a better future than she did. It was tough for her, but she never complained. Because of her sacrifice, I was able to get my degree and find a good job. I'm so grateful for everything she did.
output.prompt: Describe a time someone you know (or a fictional character) made a significant sacrifice or worked incredibly hard for a specific purpose. Why did they do it? What was the outcome? How did it impact you or others?

expressions.en: enjoy the fruits of his labor

quiz.q: What was one of the reasons the father worked three jobs?
How did the father feel about his exhausting routine?
options: He enjoyed every minute of it.

quiz.q: What did the author remember most vividly about their father?
options: A cold winter morning where he was preparing for work.

quiz.q: What did the father teach his children through his actions?

reading.en: My father came to the United States from El Salvador in 1991. He worked three jobs for nineteen years so that I could attend medical school.
reading.cn: 我父亲 1991 年从萨尔瓦多来到美国。他干了十九年三份工作，就是为了让我能上医学院。
reading.note: so that — purpose

reading.en: He drove a delivery truck during the day, cleaned offices at night, and worked construction on weekends, in order to put six dollars into a savings account every Friday.
reading.cn: 他白天开运货车，晚上打扫写字楼，周末打工搞建筑——为的就是每周五能往储蓄账户里存进六美元。
reading.note: in order to — purpose

reading.en: He never complained. But by the end of each week, his hands trembled so badly that he could not unscrew the lid of his own thermos.
reading.cn: 他从不抱怨。但每到周末，他的手抖得很厉害，连自己保温杯的盖子都拧不开。
reading.note: so + adv + that — degree

reading.en: Once, when I was twelve, I asked him whether the work was hard. He answered with such tenderness that I have remembered the answer for twenty-two years.
reading.cn: 我十二岁的时候有一次问他：这活儿苦不苦？他回答时那种温柔，让我记了二十二年。
reading.note: such + n. + that — degree

reading.en: "Mija," he said, "I am tired so that you do not have to be."
reading.cn: "宝贝，"他说，"我累，是为了让你不用累。"
reading.note: so that — Ba Jin-style sacrifice line

reading.en: On the day of my white coat ceremony — twenty-eight years after he arrived — my father wore the only suit he owned.
reading.cn: 我穿白大褂宣誓的那天——他来美国二十八年后——我父亲穿上了他唯一的一套西装。
reading.note: Ceremonial moment

reading.en: He stood at the back so that he would not be in anyone's way. I could see him from the stage, holding his cap in both hands.
reading.cn: 他站在最后头，为了不挡住任何人。我从台上看见他，两只手捧着帽子。
reading.note: so that — purpose

reading.en: My speech was very short. I held up my new white coat and said only one sentence: "This belongs to my father."
reading.cn: 我的发言很短。我举起那件新白大褂，只说了一句话："这件衣服，是我父亲的。"
reading.note: Closing — restraint

expressions.en: Find joy in the little things.

examples.cn: 你应该永远保持好奇心。
examples.en: You should always be curious.

examples.cn: 她应该尝试理解他人的观点。
examples.en: She should try to understand others' perspectives.

examples.cn: 我们应该珍惜每一个瞬间。
examples.en: We should cherish every moment.

grammar.title: "Should" for Advice and Recommendations
grammar.explain: “should” 用于给出建议或推荐，表示某事是应该做的或更好的做法。它通常用于表达温和的义务或期望。

examples.cn: “永远不要停止学习，索菲亚，”她会说。
examples.en: "Never stop learning, Sophia," she would say.

examples.cn: 每个星期天，我们都会去看望我的祖父母。
examples.en: Every Sunday, we would visit my grandparents.

examples.cn: 在我最需要的时候，她总是会提供指导。
examples.en: She would always offer guidance when I needed it most.

grammar.title: "Would" for Habitual Actions in the Past
grammar.explain: “would” 可以用来描述过去经常发生的习惯性动作或重复事件。这通常发生在回忆过去时。

reading.en: Iris Mendel, seventy-five, has spent fifty-four years in journalism. She has covered wars, witnessed peace deals, and written about both. Now she sits down to write her final column.
reading.cn: 艾瑞丝·孟戴尔，七十五岁，已经在新闻业干了五十四年。她报道过战争，见证过和谈，并把这两件事都写过。如今她坐下来，写她的最后一篇专栏。
reading.note: Reduced relatives × 3 (covering / witnessing / writing)

reading.en: "Not every story written this year was written by a person," she begins. "But not every story written by a person is honest, either. Bias has no exclusive home."
reading.cn: "今年发出的稿子，不是每一篇都是人写的，"她写道。"但人写的稿子，也不是每一篇都诚实。偏见没有专属的住址。"
reading.note: Partial negation × 2 (Unit 6 L26 review)

reading.en: "When you read a headline reporting outrage, look first at the verb. Did someone state, or did they claim? Did they show, or did they suggest? The verbs do half the lying."
reading.cn: "读一条报道愤怒情绪的新闻时，先看那条标题里的动词。是'陈述'，还是'声称'？是'显示'，还是'暗示'？谎言有一半，是动词在替它们说的。"
reading.note: Subjective vs objective (L28 review)

reading.en: "Were today's readers a little slower to share, the misinformation industry would be a less profitable business. It would also be a less powerful one."
reading.cn: "如果今天的读者转发慢一点，造谣这个行业的利润就会少一点。它的力量也会小一点。"
reading.note: Conditional inversion (Unit 1 review)

reading.en: "An algorithm that tracks your fears is not your friend, no matter how convenient it makes your morning. An editor who questions your premises is not your enemy, no matter how uncomfortable her questions feel."
reading.cn: "一个追踪你恐惧的算法不是你的朋友，无论它把你的早晨变得多么方便。一个质疑你前提的编辑不是你的敌人，无论她的问题让你多么不舒服。"
reading.note: Reduced relatives + contrast (L29 review)

reading.en: "Hardly any of what is true is loud. Hardly any of what is loud is true. Practice the difference daily, like a piano scale."
reading.cn: "凡是真的，几乎都不响亮。凡是响亮的，几乎都不真实。每天都练这个区分，像练钢琴音阶一样。"
reading.note: Partial negation parallel

reading.en: "And when you are in doubt, do what I have done since 1971: find the original document. Find the second source. Find someone who lost something in the story you are reporting. The people who lost something know things the loud ones do not."
reading.cn: "如果你拿不准，就做我从 1971 年起一直在做的事：找原始文件。找第二个信源。找一个在你正在报道的故事里失去过什么的人。失去过的人，知道一些喧哗者不知道的事。"
reading.note: Reduced relative: reporting

reading.en: The column appears on a Sunday. Her granddaughter is eighteen. She clips it from the newspaper, laminates it, and tapes it inside her freshman dormitory closet. Four years later, it is still there.
reading.cn: 专栏在一个星期天见报。她的孙女十八岁。她把这篇专栏从报纸上剪下来，塑封，贴在大一宿舍衣柜的内侧。四年后，它还在那儿。
reading.note: Closing image — Lahiri-style stillness

reading.en: My grandfather is a retired electrician with a deep mistrust of touchscreens. Last spring, he decided that he wanted to "understand the youth."
reading.cn: 我爷爷是一位退休电工，他对触屏深感不信任。去年春天，他决定要"搞懂年轻人"。
reading.note: Apposition — opener (Saunders comedic tone)

reading.en: I am his only grandson. I became the appointed teacher. We exchanged words for forty-five minutes every Sunday.
reading.cn: 我是他唯一的孙子。我被任命为老师。我们每个星期天交换四十五分钟的词汇。
reading.note: Apposition — relationship

reading.en: I taught him "rizz," meaning charisma, and "bet," meaning OK or sure.
reading.cn: 我教了他"rizz"——意思是魅力，也教了他"bet"——意思是好的或者行。
reading.note: meaning Y — apposition for definition

reading.en: He taught me "elbow grease" — that is, hard physical work. He also taught me "the cat's pajamas," a 1920s phrase meaning excellent.
reading.cn: 他教了我 "elbow grease"，也就是花力气干活。他还教了我 "the cat's pajamas"，那是一个 20 世纪 20 年代的说法，意思是棒极了。
reading.note: that is + meaning — apposition

reading.en: My grandfather is also known as Pop to everyone in his apartment building. He took notes in a small green notebook that he used to keep during his Vietnam service.
reading.cn: 在公寓楼里，每个人都叫我爷爷 Pop。他在一本小绿色笔记本里做笔记。那是他越战时期就用的本子。
reading.note: also known as Y — apposition

reading.en: In June, he successfully used the word "rizz" on a sixty-eight-year-old widow named Doreen Falcone. She was the woman who had been ignoring him in the lobby for nine months.
reading.cn: 六月里，他对一位 68 岁的寡妇成功用上了 "rizz" 这个词。她叫多琳·法尔科内，就是在公寓大堂里把他无视了整整九个月的那位女士。
reading.note: Apposition for naming

reading.en: Apparently, his rizz was, in his own words, "considerable."
reading.cn: 看上去，他的"rizz"——用他自己的话说——"相当可观"。
reading.note: Comedic deadpan

reading.en: They are now married. The notebook — that small green object I once thought was a joke — sits on their kitchen table. It is open to the page where he first wrote "elbow grease" in his careful, electrician's hand.
reading.cn: 他们现在已经结婚了。那个小绿本子——我曾经以为只是个笑话的东西——如今摆在他们家厨房桌上。它翻开在他用电工那种工整字迹第一次写下 "elbow grease" 的那一页。
reading.note: Apposition closing — sentimental

grammar.title: 同位语 (Appositives)

examples.cn: 我女儿，一个优秀的学生，考试得了A。
examples.en: My daughter, an excellent student, got an A on her exam.

examples.cn: 纽约市，大苹果，是一个充满活力的国际大都市。
examples.en: New York City, the Big Apple, is a vibrant metropolis.

examples.cn: 我的猫，一只毛茸茸的波斯猫，喜欢在阳光下打盹。
examples.en: My cat, a fluffy Persian, loves to nap in sunbeams.

grammar.explain:
同位语是名词或名词短语，用来解释或重新命名它前面的另一个名词或名词短语。它提供额外的信息，使句子更具体或更生动。同位语通常在句中用逗号与被解释的词隔开。

**核心句型：** “Grandpa Joe, a man of tradition, often finds himself puzzled by modern slang.”

在这个句子中，“a man of tradition”是一个同位语，它解释了“Grandpa Joe”是谁，给他增加了一个特点。

examples.cn: 约翰逊先生，我们的历史老师，让课堂变得非常引人入胜。
examples.en: Mr. Johnson, our history teacher, made the class very engaging.

examples.cn: 巴黎，法国的首都，以其艺术和文化而闻名。

reading.en: For fifty-one years, Yen-Ling Wu had worked as a Mandarin-English conference interpreter. It is a high-stakes job. It involves long days, sealed rooms, and headphones that press too tightly on the ears.
reading.cn: 伍燕玲做了五十一年的普通话—英语会议口译员。这是一份高风险的工作。它包含漫长的工作日、封闭的房间，以及把耳朵夹得太紧的耳机。
reading.note: Apposition + reduced relatives — Murakami opening

reading.en: She was widely regarded as one of the most precise practitioners of her craft. At the same time, at sixty-four, she was almost entirely unknown outside her profession.
reading.cn: 她被广泛认为是这个行业里最精准的从业者之一。同时，在六十四岁这一年，她在职业之外几乎完全无人知晓。
reading.note: Compound adj + while contrast

reading.en: Last year, she began to forget Mandarin — slowly at first, and then quickly. Mandarin was her first language. It was the language of her mother. It was the language she dreamed in.
reading.cn: 去年她开始忘记普通话——起初是慢慢地，后来是迅速地。普通话是她的第一语言。是她母亲的语言。是她做梦时使用的语言。
reading.note: Apposition rapid-fire

reading.en: The doctors called it primary progressive aphasia. Yen-Ling called it "losing a lens."
reading.cn: 医生们说那是"原发性进行性失语症"。燕玲管它叫"失去一面镜片"。
reading.note: Apposition: technical vs personal

reading.en: "Despite the diagnosis," she wrote in English to her son, "I do not feel that I have less. I feel that I have one fewer way of meeting the world."
reading.cn: 她用英语给儿子写信："尽管有这个诊断，我并不觉得自己少了什么。我只觉得，我会见这个世界的方式，少了一种。"
reading.note: Despite + n. — contrast

reading.en: In order to slow the loss, she spoke Mandarin out loud for thirty minutes every morning, even when no one was listening. On most mornings, no one was.
reading.cn: 为了延缓失去，她每天早上对着空气说三十分钟的普通话，即使没有人在听。而大多数早上，确实没有人在听。
reading.note: In order to — purpose

reading.en: Her son is bilingual but more confident in English. He began calling her every day so that there would be someone to listen.
reading.cn: 她儿子是双语者，但更习惯用英语。他开始每天给她打电话，为的就是让她有一个人可以听她说。
reading.note: so that — purpose

reading.en: On the day Yen-Ling could no longer recall the word for "moon" in either language, she pointed at the sky and laughed, very softly. "I have lost a lens," she told her son. "But fortunately, the moon has not."
reading.cn: 燕玲两种语言都想不起"月亮"那个词的那一天，她指着天空，轻轻地笑了。"我失去了一面镜片，"她告诉儿子，"但幸好月亮没有。"
reading.note: Closing image — Murakami stillness

output.prompt: Write a short paragraph about a time you or someone you know experienced a "language loss" moment, or a moment where you felt disconnected from your cultural heritage. Describe how it happened and what steps were taken to reconnect (or what you would do if it happened).
output.cn: 写一小段你或你认识的人经历“语言丧失”或感到与自己文化遗产脱节的时刻。描述它是如何发生的，以及采取了什么措施来重新连接（或者如果发生你会怎么做）。
output.sample: I once visited my grandparents in their hometown, and I struggled to understand their local dialect. Even though I grew up hearing it, I mainly spoke Mandarin. It felt strange and a bit sad to be unable to fully participate in their conversations. After that trip, I started asking my grandmother to teach me more phrases. I want to feel more connected to my family roots.

grammar.title: The phrase 'My grandmother's tea'
grammar.explain: 虽然标题本身“My grandmother's tea”是一个名词短语，表示“我奶奶的茶”，但本课围绕“奶奶喝茶”这一核心场景，可以引申出许多相关的句型。尤其是用来描述习惯、偏好和带有科学依据的观点的表达。
一般现在时用于描述经常性的动作、习惯、日常例行公事以及普遍真理和科学事实。在描述奶奶的饮茶习惯和茶的特性时非常常用。

listening.audio: My grandmother starts her day with a cup of tea. She carefully selects her favorite blend. The kettle whistles, signaling the beginning of her brewing process. She lets the tea steep for exactly three minutes to ensure the perfect infusion.

reading.en: When I was eight, my grandmother lived in rural Sichuan. Every time I had a cough, she made me a tea. She used three plants from the kitchen yard. The cough always went away within a day.
reading.cn: 我八岁时，奶奶住在四川乡下。每次我一咳嗽，她就给我泡一杯茶。她用厨房院子里的三种植物。咳嗽一天之内总会好。
reading.note: Setup — childhood remedy

reading.en: Twenty-six years later, I was a postdoctoral pharmacologist. I conducted a small study on her tea, mostly out of stubbornness.
reading.cn: 二十六年后，我已经是一名博士后药理学家。我对奶奶那杯茶做了一个小型研究，多半出于一股不服气的劲儿。
reading.note: conduct a study — collocation

reading.en: For thirty years, I had been told that this hypothesis was nonsense: that one of the three plants contained a compound active against a common bronchial virus. I tested it.
reading.cn: 三十年来，我一直被告知有一个假设是无稽之谈：那三种植物之一含有一种对常见支气管病毒有活性的化合物。我测试了这个假设。
reading.note: test a hypothesis

reading.en: I designed a small placebo-controlled trial with eighty-four volunteers and a clean protocol.
reading.cn: 我设计了一个小型安慰剂对照试验，招了八十四名志愿者，方案简洁。
reading.note: placebo-controlled trial

reading.en: The results were modest but real, after replication in a second laboratory. We published the findings in a peer-reviewed journal. After some negotiation, my grandmother was listed as a community-knowledge contributor.
reading.cn: 在第二个实验室复现之后，结果温和但真实。我们把结果发在一份同行评议期刊上。经过一番周旋之后，我奶奶以"社区知识贡献者"的身份署了名。
reading.note: Replication / publish findings / peer-reviewed

reading.en: My grandmother could not read the journal. She did not need to.
reading.cn: 我奶奶看不懂那份期刊。她也不需要看懂。
reading.note: Spare beat

reading.en: When I brought her a printed copy, she touched the paper. Then she put it next to her radio. It remained there for the last eleven months of her life.
reading.cn: 我把那份纸印件带给她时，她摸了摸那张纸。然后她把它放在她那台收音机旁边。它就在那里，直到她生命的最后十一个月。
reading.note: Gawande tenderness

reading.en: My supervisor told me that a landmark discovery does not always come from a glass tower. Sometimes it comes from a pot of water and three plants that nobody had bothered to test.
reading.cn: 我导师对我说：里程碑式的发现并不总来自玻璃高塔。有时候，它就在一壶水和三种没有人想过去测一下的植物里。
reading.note: landmark discovery — closing

output.cn: 描述一个对你或你认识的人很重要的日常习惯或仪式。解释它涉及什么以及为什么它很重要，可以提及任何具体细节，例如时间或构成部分。
output.sample: My morning coffee is my daily ritual. I always grind fresh beans and use a French press. I let it steep for exactly four minutes. The rich aroma fills my kitchen, and that first sip of strong coffee helps me wake up and feel ready for the day. It's not just a drink; it's a moment of peace before the busy day begins.

grammar.title: 修辞疑问句 (Rhetorical Questions)

examples.en: Aren't galaxies just breathtaking?
examples.cn: 星系难道不令人叹为观止吗？ (意在强调星系非常美。)

examples.en: Isn't that truly mind-boggling?
examples.cn: 那难道不真令人费解吗？ (意在强调那非常复杂或令人惊讶。)

examples.en: What an amazing thought, isn't it?
examples.cn: 多么令人惊叹的想法，不是吗？ (意在强调这个想法很棒。)

grammar.explain: 修辞疑问句是一种不需要回答的疑问句，说话者用它来强调某一点、表达强烈的情感或引发听众思考。它通常以疑问句的形式出现，但其作用更接近于陈述句或感叹句。在本课场景中，维加女士使用修辞疑问句来激发学生对宇宙的兴趣和思考。

examples.en: Won't it be incredible if we find life beyond Earth?
examples.cn: 如果我们能发现地球以外的生命，那难道不令人难以置信吗？
将来有一天送人去那里难道不令人着迷吗？
examples.en: Wouldn't it be fascinating to send people there someday?

examples.cn: 太空探索难道不是人类有史以来最激动人心的冒险吗？
examples.en: Isn't space exploration the most exciting adventure humanity has ever embarked on?

grammar.explain:
修辞疑问句的构成与一般疑问句相似，但其语境和目的不同。它们通常带有语气词的反问，或以疑问句的形式表达一个显而易见的观点。常见的形式包括：
1. 使用否定疑问句：例如 “Aren't they magnificent?” (它们难道不壮观吗？)
2. 使用肯定疑问句来表达强调：例如 “Who knows what other wonders we'll uncover?” (谁知道我们还会揭示出什么奇迹呢？——意为充满无限可能)
3. 附加疑问句：例如 “What an amazing thought, isn't it?”
grammar.title: 修辞疑问句的常见形式

reading.en: Ms. Vega had been an astronaut. The third graders sat on the gym floor. They were trying to decide whether they believed her.
reading.cn: 维加女士曾经是宇航员。三年级的孩子们坐在体育馆的地板上。他们正在判断他们到底信不信她。
reading.note: Sagan-meets-Saunders opening

reading.en: "Why do we go up there?" she asked, holding up a plain blue marble. "Why spend the money? Why risk the people?"
reading.cn: "我们干嘛要往上飞？"她举起一颗普通的蓝色弹珠问。"为什么要花那个钱？为什么要让人冒那个险？"
reading.note: Three rhetorical questions

reading.en: "Who would not want to look back at the Earth and see — for once in their life — that there is no line between countries?"
reading.cn: "谁不想这辈子至少有一次回头看看地球，发现各国之间根本没有那条线？"
reading.note: Who wouldn't want — rhetorical

reading.en: A small boy in the front row raised his hand. "Me," he said. "I would not want to. I get carsick."
reading.cn: 前排一个小男孩举起了手。"我，"他说，"我不想去。我坐车都会晕。"
reading.note: Saunders comedic interruption

reading.en: Ms. Vega laughed for the first time that morning. "Fair enough," she said. "But isn't it obvious that someone should?"
reading.cn: 维加女士那天早上头一回笑了。"说得对，"她说，"可显然——总得有人去吧？"
reading.note: Isn't it obvious — rhetorical

reading.en: "What's the harm in trying?" she went on. "What's lost when humans look up?"
reading.cn: "试一下又有什么坏处？"她接着说。"人类抬头看，又能失去什么？"
reading.note: Two more rhetorical questions

reading.en: She told them about the smell of space (like burnt steak). She told them about the way her colleague, sleeping in zero gravity, snored more politely than he did at home.
reading.cn: 她告诉他们太空的气味——像烤糊了的牛排。她告诉他们，她的同事在零重力里睡觉时，打的呼噜比在家里还要客气。
reading.note: Funny, specific, Sagan-warm

reading.en: When the bell rang, the carsick boy walked up to her. He asked, very seriously, whether she thought rockets had bathrooms. They did, she said. Rockets have everything we have. They just have less weather.
reading.cn: 下课铃响时，那个晕车的小男孩走上来。他很认真地问她：火箭里有没有厕所？她说有。火箭里我们有的都有，只是天气少一点。
reading.note: Sagan-Saunders closing

reading.en: In 2018, a researcher in Shenzhen announced he had edited the genes of two human embryos. The world reacted with horror. He was later imprisoned.
reading.cn: 2018 年，深圳一位研究者宣布他编辑了两个人类胚胎的基因。世界一片震惊。他后来入了狱。
reading.note: Atwood-style cold opener

reading.en: Two years later, less famously, a young scientist named Dr. Aisha Rahman was working in a quiet lab in Glasgow. She faced a question with no clear answer.
reading.cn: 两年后，不那么出名的是：一位名叫艾莎·拉赫曼的年轻科学家在格拉斯哥一间安静的实验室里工作。她面对的，是一个没有明确答案的问题。
reading.note: Apposition + setup

reading.en: She had developed a gene-editing technique. In mice, it eliminated a fatal childhood disease. The first results were spectacular.
reading.cn: 她研发了一种基因编辑技术。在小鼠身上，它彻底消除了一种致命的儿童疾病。第一组结果非常漂亮。
reading.note: Plot setup

reading.en: Then came the second batch of mice. They were healthy. But when they were measured carefully, they were slightly less curious than untreated mice.
reading.cn: 然后第二批小鼠来了。它们身体健康。但仔细测量后会发现，它们比未经处理的小鼠稍微少一点好奇心。
reading.note: Atwood horror moment

reading.en: It is vital that this finding be repeated and verified before any human application is even considered. It is essential that the public know what we are doing.
reading.cn: 至关重要的是，这个发现必须在任何用于人类的考虑之前，被重复和核实。也至关重要的是，公众要知道我们在做什么。
reading.note: It is vital that + V (subjunctive)

reading.en: "I ought to have stopped when I saw the second result," Aisha told an ethics committee. "I should have asked my supervisor on day one. I did not. I am sorry."
reading.cn: "我本该在看到第二组结果时就停下，"艾莎对伦理委员会说。"我应该第一天就向导师汇报。我没有。对此我很抱歉。"
reading.note: ought to have / should have — past obligation

reading.en: The committee did not punish her. They required that she pause her research for six months and that she enroll in additional ethics training.
reading.cn: 委员会没有处罚她。他们要求她暂停研究六个月，并参加额外的伦理课程。
reading.note: required that + V (subjunctive)

reading.en: Five years later, Aisha's slightly revised technique now saves seventy-two children a year, with no measurable curiosity loss. She still keeps the second-batch report in her top desk drawer. She believes every gene editor ought to keep one too.
reading.cn: 五年后，艾莎稍作修改的技术每年挽救七十二个孩子的生命，且没有可测量的好奇心损失。她至今把那份第二批报告放在办公桌最上面那个抽屉里。她相信，每一位做基因编辑的人都应该留一份这样的报告。
reading.note: ought to + V — present obligation

grammar.title: Suggesting with "should" and "ought to"
grammar.explain:
在英语中，"should" 和 "ought to" 都可以用来给予建议或表达某种义务。它们通常用于表示“应该做某事”。

**Should**: 最常用且最通用的形式，表示一种温和的建议或义务。语气上，比“必须”要弱，更像是一种“最好如此”的劝告。

**Ought to**: 意思和 "should" 非常接近，甚至在许多情况下可以互换。但在日常口语中，"should" 更为常见。"ought to" 听起来可能稍显正式，或者有时带有更强的道德或逻辑上的“应该”的意味。

examples.cn: 我这个周末必须把婴儿床组装好。
examples.en: I must finish the crib assembly this weekend.

examples.cn: 我们必须确保一切都为宝宝的到来做好准备。
examples.en: We've got to make sure everything is ready for when the baby arrives.

examples.cn: 我们必须成为一个团队。
examples.en: We have to be a team.

grammar.title: Expressing Obligation with "must", "have to", and "have got to"
grammar.explain:
这些词都表示义务或必要性，但它们在语气和用法上略有不同。

**Must**: 语气最强，表示说话者认为某事非常重要，是内部的、主观的义务或强烈的必要性。也常用于规定、禁令或强调。

**Have to**: 表示外部的、客观的义务，通常是因为规则、法律、情况所迫而不得不做某事。在日常口语中非常常见。

**Have got to**: 意思和 "have to" 非常接近，尤其是在口语中，表示一种紧迫的、即时的必要性或义务。比 "have to" 更口语化，常用作缩略形式 "'ve got to"。

reading.en: Mrs. Patel had taught middle-school science for twenty-two years. She always introduced the scientific method with the same odd experiment.
reading.cn: 帕特尔老师教中学理科已有二十二年。她介绍科学方法时总用同一个有点奇怪的实验。
reading.note: Saunders comedic-warm setup

reading.en: "If kindness is contagious," she would write on the board, "then if I am kind to person A, person A will be kind to person B within forty-eight hours."
reading.cn: "如果善意会传染，"她会在黑板上写，"那么——如果我对 A 友善，那么 A 会在四十八小时内对 B 友善。"
reading.note: Zero conditional + first conditional

reading.en: She would then assign each student to one stranger in their week: a school-bus driver, a librarian, a sibling who had recently broken something. Each student was the experimenter.
reading.cn: 然后她会给每位学生指派一位本周的"陌生人"：校车司机、图书管理员、最近打碎过东西的兄弟姐妹。每位学生都是实验者。
reading.note: Setup

reading.en: "Unless you record what happens within forty-eight hours," she would say, "your data is useless. Provided that you are honest, even a negative result is a real finding."
reading.cn: "除非你在四十八小时内记下来，"她会说，"否则你的数据就没用。只要你诚实，哪怕是负面结果，那也是真实的发现。"
reading.note: Unless / Provided that

reading.en: Most years, the kindness chain broke by Tuesday. Some years, it ran through five strangers and back to the original kind person.
reading.cn: 大多数年份，这条善意链到了周二就断了。有些年份，它穿过五个陌生人，又回到了那个最初做出善意的人身上。
reading.note: Plot complication

reading.en: In 2019, an eighth grader named Marcus held the door for a janitor. Within thirty hours, the janitor had paid for a stranger's coffee. Within forty-eight hours, the stranger had returned a lost wallet to a man Marcus had never met.
reading.cn: 2019 年，一个八年级学生马库斯给一位清洁工开了门。三十个小时之内，那位清洁工替一位陌生人付了咖啡钱。四十八小时之内，那位陌生人把一只钱包还给了马库斯从未见过的一个人。
reading.note: Concrete chain

reading.en: "If we had stopped the experiment after one week, we would have called the result a coincidence," Mrs. Patel said. "We did not. We ran it for nineteen years."
reading.cn: "如果我们在一周后停止这个实验，我们就会说这是巧合，"帕特尔老师说。"我们没有停。我们做了十九年。"
reading.note: Second conditional (past unreal)

reading.en: Her conclusion was written in a notebook she gave to her students each year on the last day of school. The conclusion was modest: kindness, it appears, can be contagious. Unfortunately, unkindness is more contagious. So long as you remember that, you remain a scientist.
reading.cn: 她的结论写在她每年学年最后一天送给学生的本子上。结论很平和：善意看起来会传染。可惜的是，恶意更会传染。只要你记得这一点，你就还是科学家。
reading.note: So long as — closing

grammar.title: If...then... (条件状语从句)
grammar.explain: “If...then...”句型用于表达条件和结果。其中，“if”引导条件状语从句，表示在一个特定条件发生时，才会出现“then”引导的主句中的结果。在口语和非正式写作中，“then”常常被省略。

grammar.title: Present Simple in If-clause, Future Simple in Main Clause

reading.en: Dr. Vivian Ellis is seventy-eight. She has been studying Alzheimer's disease for forty-six years. Her own mother died of it. She suspects she will too.
reading.cn: 维维安·艾利斯博士今年七十八岁。她研究阿尔茨海默症已经四十六年了。她自己的母亲死于这病。她怀疑她也会。
reading.note: Lu Xun-sober opener

reading.en: Last spring, her lab published findings in a peer-reviewed journal. The findings suggested that a small molecule, derived from common turmeric, might slow the disease in early stages.
reading.cn: 去年春天，她的实验室在一份同行评议期刊上发表了研究结果。结果表明：一种从普通姜黄中提取出的小分子，可能在早期阶段延缓这种疾病。
reading.note: science collocations review

reading.en: "If our finding is replicated by three independent laboratories," she said, "then we will have something we can offer to a clinical trial. If it is not, then I will have spent four decades being wrong."
reading.cn: "如果我们这个结果被三家独立实验室重复出来，"她说，"那我们就有东西可以送进临床试验。如果重复不出来——那我就花了四十年时间在做一件错事。"
reading.note: L39 if-then conditional review

reading.en: It is vital that the replication be conducted independently. It would be advisable to wait at least eighteen months before making any public statement about treatment.
reading.cn: 至关重要的是，重复实验必须独立完成。明智的做法是：在做出任何关于治疗的公开声明之前，至少再等十八个月。
reading.note: L38 obligation review

reading.en: "Why bother?" a young reporter once asked her. "If you yourself may forget your own work, why work?"
reading.cn: "何必呢？"一位年轻记者曾经问她。"如果连您自己——可能都会忘掉自己的研究——那您为什么还在做？"
reading.note: L37 rhetorical question review

reading.en: She did not answer right away. "Forgetting," she said finally, "is not the worst thing. The worst thing is forgetting before someone else has been spared from the disease. So we work."
reading.cn: 她没有马上回答。"忘记，"她最后说，"不是最糟的事情。最糟的事情是：在还没有别的人被这病放过之前，自己就先忘了。所以我们继续做。"
reading.note: Sober closing

reading.en: Three months ago, the second laboratory replicated her finding. The third has not yet reported. Whatever they find, it is possible (perhaps likely) that Vivian will not remember the result.
reading.cn: 三个月前，第二家实验室重复出了她的结果。第三家还没出报告。无论他们查出什么，都有可能（或许很可能）维维安自己已经记不住那个结果了。
reading.note: Time markers + uncertainty

reading.en: In her office, taped to the wall above her desk, is a small printed note in her own careful hand: "Whether or not I remember this, somebody else, eventually, will not have to."
reading.cn: 在她办公室办公桌上方的墙上，贴着一张她自己用工整字迹写的小纸条："无论我是否记得，总有一天，会有别的人不必经历这件事。"
reading.note: Closing image — Lu Xun-Iris hybrid

grammar.title: Present Perfect Continuous (现在完成进行时)

grammar.explain: 被动语态用于强调动作的承受者或动作本身，而不是动作的执行者。在科学研究的语境中，通常更关注研究结果或被研究的对象，因此被动语态很常见。

grammar.explain: 动词搭配是英语中常见的表达方式，本课我们将学习如何用动词来表达“愿望”和“代价”。掌握这些搭配有助于我们更自然地表达复杂的情感和想法。

examples.cn: 要是能变得重要就好了！ (表示对现在或未来的愿望)
examples.en: If only I could be important!

examples.cn: 要是能看看这个世界就好了！ (表示对现在或未来的愿望)
examples.en: If only I could see the world!

examples.cn: 要是它留在森林里就好了。 (表示对过去的遗憾)
examples.en: If only it had stayed in the forest.

grammar.explain: “If only…” 是一种用来表达强烈愿望或遗憾的句型。它的结构通常是 “If only + 主语 + 过去式动词” （表示对现在或未来的愿望），或 “If only + 主语 + had + 过去分词” （表示对过去未能实现的愿望或遗憾）。
