reading.en: In a great forest, a small fir tree grew impatient with its life. It longed for height, for importance, for somewhere to go.
reading.cn: 一片大森林里，一棵小冷杉对自己当下的生活越来越不耐烦。它渴望长高、变得重要、去到某个地方。
reading.note: "longed for" + abstract noun (key B2 collocation)

reading.en: Every spring, men with axes came and chose the tallest trees. The fir tree watched them go and wondered where they were taken.
reading.cn: 每年春天，拿着斧头的人会来挑最高的树。小冷杉望着它们被带走，琢磨着它们被运去了哪里。
reading.note: Past habit — "every spring + would-style action"

reading.en: "They are taken to the sea, to become masts on great ships," said the storks. "Be glad you are still young and free." But the fir tree only wished it were chosen.
reading.cn: "它们被运到海边，做大船的桅杆，"鹳鸟说。"你还年轻自由，应该高兴。"可小冷杉只希望自己也被选中。
reading.note: "wished it were" — past subjunctive for unreal wish

reading.en: One December, the men returned. They cut the fir tree down without warning and carried it away. Its first thought was triumph.
reading.cn: 十二月的某一天，那些人又来了。他们没打招呼就把小冷杉砍倒、抬走。它的第一个念头是胜利。
reading.note: Sequence verbs: returned → cut → carried → was

reading.en: In a fine house, it was set up in the parlor and decorated with candles, golden apples, and silver stars. Children danced around it and laughed.
reading.cn: 在一栋讲究的房子里，它被立在客厅里，挂上蜡烛、金苹果、银星。孩子们围着它跳舞、欢笑。
reading.note: Passive chain: was set up + decorated with

reading.en: For one evening, it stood in glory. "This," the fir tree thought, "is what I was waiting for all my life."
reading.cn: 那一晚，它在荣光里站着。"这，"小冷杉想，"就是我这辈子等的东西。"
reading.note: "was waiting for" — past continuous of long anticipation

reading.en: The next morning, the candles were gone. Servants dragged the tree into a dark attic and forgot it among old chests and dust.
reading.cn: 第二天早晨，蜡烛不见了。仆人们把它拖进一间昏暗的阁楼，扔在旧箱子和灰尘里，再没人记得它。
reading.note: "dragged into" + "forgot among" — verbs of disregard

reading.en: Mice came for a few evenings to listen to its forest stories, then they too went away. The tree began to understand what it had given up.
reading.cn: 几个晚上有老鼠来听它讲森林里的故事，然后老鼠也走了。这棵树开始明白自己究竟放弃了什么。
reading.note: "give up" + abstract object — perfect for cost/loss

reading.en: In spring it was dragged outside, broken into kindling, and burned. As it burned, it remembered the green moss and the slow summer rain. "I should have been content," it thought. "I traded a whole life for one evening."
reading.cn: 春天时它被拖到院子里，劈成柴，烧了。火焰里它想起绿色的苔藓和夏天里慢慢落下的雨。"我本该知足的，"它想。"我用一辈子，换了一个晚上。"
reading.note: Closing: "should have + V-ed" + "trade X for Y" — both core B2 collocations

output.sample: I once longed for a prestigious job in a big city. I worked incredibly hard to get it, and my wish eventually came true. However, it came with the sacrifice of leaving my family and friends behind. I sometimes regret missing out on small, happy moments. I learned that what truly matters is not just achieving your dreams, but also cherishing the relationships you have.

In the quiet attic, as it began to wither, the fir tree started to regret its youthful longing for change, understanding the true value of its simple life in the forest.

output.prompt: Imagine you are Pahom's wife. Write a short journal entry (3-5 sentences) reflecting on his desire for more land and the outcome. Use at least one indirect question and one vocabulary word from the lesson.
output.sample: Oh, Pahom. I always asked him why we needed so much land. He never listened. I often wondered how much satisfaction he truly expected to find. His endless desire to acquire more ultimately sealed his fate. Now, what will happen to us?
output.cn: 想象你是帕霍姆的妻子。写一篇简短的日记（3-5句），反思他对更多土地的渴望和结果。使用至少一个间接疑问句和本课的一个词汇。

grammar.title: 间接疑问句 (Indirect Questions)

examples.en: Direct: "How much land does a man need?"
examples.cn: 直接疑问句：“一个人需要多少土地？”
间接疑问句：他经常想一个人需要多少土地。
examples.en: Indirect: He often wondered how much land a man needed.

examples.cn: 直接疑问句：“我到底能走多少地？”
examples.en: Direct: "How much land can I really cover?"

grammar.explain: 间接疑问句是将疑问句并入陈述句中的一种句型。当疑问句作为另一个句子的宾语时，它就变成了间接疑问句。主要的区别在于语序，间接疑问旬的语序与陈述句相同：主语 + 谓语，不再使用疑问句的倒装语序。

grammar.title: 间接疑问句的构成

examples.cn: 间接疑问句：他不停地问自己到底能走多少地。
examples.en: Indirect: He kept asking himself how much land he could really cover.
Direct: "What had his wife said?"
examples.cn: 直接疑问句：“他妻子说了什么？”

examples.en: Indirect: He thought about what his wife had said.
examples.cn: 间接疑问句：他想起了他妻子说过的话。

grammar.explain: 当直接疑问句是特殊疑问句时 (即以 `what`, `where`, `when`, `why`, `how` 开头)，间接疑问句通常以这些疑问词引导，后面接陈述句语序。如果直接疑问句是一般疑问句 (即用助动词引导回答 yes/no 的问题)，则间接疑问句通常用 whether 或 if 引导。

listening.audio: Pahom was a peasant who always wanted more land. He wondered how much land he needed to be happy. He heard about a deal and decided to acquire as much as possible. His greed pushed him to walk far, ignoring the warnings. He never found true satisfaction, only exhaustion.

vocab.meaning: phrase 琢磨；自问是否（间接疑问核心）
vocab.example: He often wondered whether he would ever own enough.
vocab.example_cn: 他常常自问是否能拥有足够多。

reading.en: Pahom owned a small farm. He often wondered whether he would ever own enough.
reading.cn: 帕霍姆有一座小农场。他常常在心里想：自己有没有可能拥有足够多。
reading.note: "wondered whether" — classic indirect question

reading.en: A traveler from the steppes told him about the Bashkirs. They would sell as much land as a man could walk around in a single day, for one thousand rubles.
reading.cn: 一个从草原过来的旅人告诉他巴什基尔人的事——他们卖地的方式是：一个人一天能走完一圈的范围都归他，价格一千卢布。
reading.note: "as much X as Y could V" — quantifier comparison

reading.en: Pahom asked whether the offer was genuine. The traveler said it was — and that the land was rich, black, and unbroken.
reading.cn: 帕霍姆问这事是不是真的。旅人说是真的——而且那片地肥沃、黝黑、没人开垦过。
reading.note: "asked whether" — reported question

reading.en: Pahom traveled for many days. He brought one thousand rubles in a leather bag. He did not yet know how far he could walk in one day.
reading.cn: 帕霍姆走了好多天。他带着一只皮袋装着一千卢布。他还不知道自己一天能走多远。
reading.note: "did not know how far" — embedded wh-question

reading.en: At sunrise, the Bashkir chief told him: "Walk where you wish. Mark your route. Return here by sunset, or your money is forfeit."
reading.cn: 日出时，巴什基尔的酋长对他说："你想往哪儿走就往哪儿走。沿路做标记。日落之前回到这里，否则钱就没了。"
reading.note: Direct quote — sets the contract clearly

reading.en: Pahom set out fast. By noon he had marked a great square. He kept asking himself if a little more might be possible.
reading.cn: 帕霍姆开始走得很快。到了中午，他已经画出了一个很大的方形。他不停地问自己：是不是再多一点也行？
reading.note: "asking himself if" — internal indirect question

reading.en: The sun began to fall. He realized, suddenly, that he had walked too far. He did not know whether he could still make it back. He started running.
reading.cn: 太阳开始往下落。他突然意识到自己走得太远了。他不知道自己能不能走得回去。他开始跑。
reading.note: "did not know whether" — uncertainty in past

reading.en: He ran the last miles with his lungs on fire, his head pounding. As the sun touched the horizon, he reached the starting point. He had not failed.
reading.cn: 最后几英里他跑得肺像着火、太阳穴狂跳。太阳碰到地平线的那一刻，他到了起点。他没有输。
reading.note: "had not failed" — past perfect of completion

reading.en: But Pahom fell at the the feet of the chief, dead. His servant buried him there, in a grave six feet long. Six feet of land was all the land he needed.
reading.cn: 可帕霍姆扑倒在酋长脚下，死了。他的仆人就地把他埋了，墓穴六英尺长。六英尺的地，就是他真正需要的全部土地。
reading.note: Closing irony — Tolstoy answers his own title

reading.en: Old Jacob Marley had been dead for seven years. On Christmas Eve, his ghost appeared in Scrooge's room, dragging a heavy chain made of money boxes, keys, padlocks, and ledgers.
reading.cn: 雅各布·马利去世已经七年了。圣诞夜，他的鬼魂出现在斯克鲁奇的房间里，身后拖着一条沉重的锁链——由钱箱、钥匙、挂锁和账簿打成。
reading.note: Past perfect (had been) + reduced relative (made of...)

reading.en: "You are fettered," said Scrooge, trembling. "Tell me why."
reading.cn: "你被锁住了，"斯克鲁奇颤抖着说。"告诉我为什么。"
reading.note: Direct speech setup

reading.en: "I wear the chain I forged in life," replied the ghost. "I made it link by link, and yard by yard. I girded it on of my own free will, and of my own free will I wore it."
reading.cn: "我戴着我生前自己打造的锁链，"鬼魂回答。"我一节一节、一码一码把它打出来。我自愿戴上它，自愿穿着它。"
reading.note: Parallel structure: link by link, yard by yard

reading.en: Scrooge looked down. He could not see his own chain, but he sensed it had grown long during his lifetime.
reading.cn: 斯克鲁奇低下头。他看不见自己的锁链，但他感觉到这条锁链在自己一生中已经变得很长。
reading.note: Modal could not see + past perfect (had grown)

reading.en: "I should have walked among my fellow-men," Marley moaned. "I should have looked outside my counting-house. I might have known kindness while there was time. But I did not."
reading.cn: "我本该走到同胞中间去，"马利呻吟道。"我本该从我的账房往外看一眼。我本可以在还有时间的时候认识善意。但我没有。"
reading.note: should/might have V-ed — modal perfects of regret (KEY focus)

reading.en: "You were always a good man of business, Jacob," Scrooge said weakly.
reading.cn: "雅各布，你一直是个精明的生意人，"斯克鲁奇虚弱地说。
reading.note: Past simple + emotive adverb

reading.en: "Business!" cried the ghost. "Mankind was my business. The common welfare was my business. Charity, mercy, forbearance — these were all my business. I could have helped. I would have helped, had I understood."
reading.cn: "生意？"鬼魂喊道。"人类，才是我的生意。大众的福祉，才是我的生意。慈悲、宽厚——这一切才是我的生意。我本可以帮的。如果我当年明白，我就会帮的。"
reading.note: could/would have V-ed + inverted conditional (had I understood)

reading.en: Three spirits would visit Scrooge, the ghost said, before the night was done. Without their help, Scrooge would walk Marley's path. With them, he might still choose differently.
reading.cn: 鬼魂说，今夜结束前会有三个幽灵来拜访斯克鲁奇。没有他们帮忙，斯克鲁奇就会走上马利那条路。有他们在，他也许还能选另一条。
reading.note: would V (future-in-past) + might still choose

reading.en: After the ghost left, Scrooge sat for a long time. He had been wealthy for forty years. He had not been kind for any of them. He understood, finally, what Marley should have understood — what he himself still might.
reading.cn: 鬼魂走后，斯克鲁奇坐了很久。他富有了四十年。这四十年里他没有一刻是善良的。他终于明白了——马利本该明白的事，他自己仍然来得及明白。
reading.note: Closing: modal perfects converging (should have / still might)

grammar.title: 情态完成式: Should/Could/Would have V-ed
grammar.explain: 情态完成时用于表达对过去发生的事情的假设、遗憾、推测或责备。它们都表示“本应该……”、“本可能……”、“本来会……”但实际情况并非如此。

examples.cn: 马利本应该用他的财富去帮助别人。（但他没有这样做，现在很后悔）
examples.en: Marley should have used his wealth to help others.

examples.cn: 如果斯克鲁奇早点改变，他本可以避免这个命运。（但他不是，所以陷入困境）
examples.en: Scrooge could have avoided this fate if he had changed earlier.

examples.cn: 如果他没有那么贪婪，他本就不会打造出如此沉重的锁链。（但他很贪婪，所以打造了）
examples.en: If he hadn't been so greedy, he wouldn't have forged such a heavy chain.

grammar.title: Should have V-ed
grammar.explain: 表示对过去应该做但没有做的事情感到后悔或提出建议/批评。

examples.cn: 我年轻时本应该多存点钱。（现在后悔）
examples.en: I should have saved more money when I was younger.
He should have invested in that company; it became very successful.
examples.cn: 他当时就应该投资那家公司，它现在非常成功。（现在觉得可惜）

examples.en: We could have finished the project on time if we had started earlier.
examples.cn: 如果我们早点开始，我们本可以按时完成项目。（但我们没有）

examples.en: She could have become a famous artist, but she chose a different path.
examples.cn: 她本可以成为一位著名艺术家，但她选择了不同的道路。（她有这个潜力但没实现）

grammar.title: Could have V-ed
grammar.explain: 表示过去有能力或有机会做某事，但没有做。也可以表示对过去的推测。

examples.en: If I had known about the opportunity, I would have taken it.
examples.cn: 如果我当时知道这个机会，我本会抓住它。（但我不知道，所以没抓住）
如果你当时求助，他本会帮助你的。（但你没求助）
examples.en: He would have helped you if you had asked.

grammar.title: Would have V-ed
grammar.explain: 常用于虚拟语气，表示过去在某种条件下“本会”发生的事情（但条件不满足，所以没发生）。

vocab.meaning: adj. 被锁链束缚的（文学用法）

vocab.example: I wear the chain I forged in life.
vocab.example_cn: 我戴着我生前自己打造的锁链。

vocab.example: I made it link by link.
vocab.example_cn: 我一节一节地把它打出来。

vocab.example: His chain had grown long during his lifetime.
vocab.example_cn: 他的锁链在他一生中已经变得很长。

vocab.meaning: n. 账房（旧时商人办公处）
vocab.example: I should have looked outside my counting-house.
vocab.example_cn: 我本该从我的账房往外看一眼。

vocab.example: The common welfare was my business.
vocab.example_cn: 大众的福祉才是我的生意。

vocab.example: Charity, mercy, forbearance — these were all my business.
vocab.example_cn: 慈悲、宽厚——这一切才是我的生意。
斯克鲁奇颤抖着说出口。
会有三个幽灵来拜访他。

output.sample: Oh, Scrooge, if I could turn back time! I should have cherished human connection over accumulating gold. I deeply regret not having used my vast wealth to alleviate the suffering of others. Instead, I built this terrible chain, link by link. I would have lived a life of joy, rather than one of loneliness, if only I had understood the true value of generosity.
output.prompt: Imagine you are Marley’s ghost. Write a short paragraph expressing your deepest regrets about your past actions and what you should have done differently with your life and wealth. Use at least two modal perfect sentences (should/could/would have V-ed).
output.cn: 想象你是马利的幽灵。写一小段话表达你对过去行为最深的懊悔，以及你本应该如何不同地度过你的人生和使用你的财富。至少使用两个情态完成式句型 (should/could/would have V-ed)。

options: A chain of cash-boxes, keys, and ledgers
quiz.q: What kind of chain was Marley bound by?
Why was Marley’s spirit condemned to wander the world?
options: Because of his greed and lack of empathy
Because he lost all his money

quiz.q: What did Marley regret not doing when he was alive?
options: Not using his wealth to help others
Not spending enough time with Scrooge
He should go on a long journey.

expressions.cn: 他生前一环一环地打造了他自己的锁链。
expressions.en: He forged his own chain in life, link by link.
His spirit was condemned to wander the world.
expressions.cn: 他的灵魂注定要在这个世界上游荡。

expressions.en: He deeply regretted not having used his wealth to help others.
expressions.cn: 他深深后悔没有用自己的财富去帮助别人。
你注定要背负更沉重的锁链。
expressions.en: You're doomed to carry an even heavier chain.
It's a heavy burden to bear.

He regretted not having used his ___ to help others.
Marley warned Scrooge that he should ___ his ways, or he would face a similar, perhaps even heavier, fate.

Marley warned Scrooge that he should change his ways, or he would face a similar, perhaps even heavier, fate. Scrooge was frightened by the consequences of a life spent in greed.

output.cn: 你最近考虑做一项投资或一次大额购买。描述你的考虑事项、潜在风险和预期价值。使用本课至少3个词汇或表达。
output.sample: I'm thinking about buying a vintage car. It's a big investment, and I know it's always a risk because repairs can be expensive. However, I think its value will increase over time, so it could be a smart move in the long run. I hope it pays off!
output.prompt: You recently thought about making an investment or a big purchase. Describe your considerations, potential risks, and expected value. Use at least 3 vocabulary words or expressions from this lesson.

expressions.scene: 形容努力或投资有成效

vocab.example: He chose solitary confinement over death.
vocab.example_cn: 他选择了单独监禁而不是死。

vocab.example: The lawyer lived in a garden lodge.
vocab.example_cn: 律师住在花园里的小屋。
糟糕的投资让银行家破产。

vocab.example: He lost it all to gambling.
I have come to despise wealth.
He did not weep that night.
He locked the letter in his safe.

examples.cn: 他打赌他的队伍会赢得冠军。
examples.en: He made a bet that his team would win the championship.

examples.cn: 我绝不会用我的积蓄在这种不稳定的股票上冒险。
examples.en: I would never take a risk with my savings on such a volatile stock.

examples.cn: 他们就新产品是否会成功打了个赌。
examples.en: They made a bet on whether the new product would succeed.

examples.cn: 为了这么好的机会，值得冒一下险。
examples.en: It's worth taking a risk for such a great opportunity.

grammar.title: Making a Bet / Taking a Risk
grammar.explain: 在英语中，"make a bet" 表示“打赌”，通常指在某事的结果上下赌注。而 "take a risk" 则表示“冒险”，指承担可能带来负面结果的风险。两者都常用于讨论不确定性或潜在回报的语境中。

grammar.title: Worth / Value / Investment / Profit & Loss
grammar.explain:
这些词汇都与“钱与价值”的主题紧密相关：
*   **Worth**: 主要指物品的“价值”或“值得”。
*   **Value**: 可以指具象的“价值”也可以指抽象的“价值观”，或动词“估价”。
*   **Investment**: “投资”，指投入资金以期获得回报。
*   **Profit**: “利润”，指收益减去成本后的盈余。
*   **Loss**: “损失，亏损”，指亏损的金额。

examples.cn: 这辆古董车价值连城。
examples.en: The antique car is worth a fortune.

examples.cn: 你房子的市场价值是多少？
examples.en: What is the market value of your house?

examples.cn: 他对房地产的投资获得了回报。
examples.en: His investment in real estate paid off.

examples.cn: 公司目标是实现10%的利润率。
examples.en: The company aims for a 10% profit margin.

examples.cn: 她以巨大的损失卖掉了那些股票。
examples.en: She sold the stocks at a significant loss.

quiz.q: What was Liam's experience with making a bet on a startup company?
options: He lost a lot of money.
He got lucky and it was a sure thing.

quiz.q: According to Mei, what did her friend do that turned out to be a smart investment?
options: She made a bet on the stock market.
She bought an old house and renovated it.
She found a bargain on a vintage watch.
She invested in a new startup company.

quiz.q: What did Liam recently find a fantastic bargain on?
What is the main topic Mei and Liam are discussing?

reading.en: On a dark autumn evening, an old banker remembered a party he had thrown fifteen years before.
reading.cn: 一个昏暗的秋夜，一位老银行家回想起十五年前他举办过的那场宴会。
reading.note: Past perfect (had thrown) — long-prior backstory

reading.en: At the party, the guests had argued about the death penalty. A young lawyer had said something unforgettable: 'I would choose to live, even in solitary confinement, rather than die.'
reading.cn: 宴会上，宾客们争论过死刑。一位年轻的律师说了一句令人难忘的话：'我宁愿活，哪怕被单独监禁，也不愿死。'
reading.note: Subjunctive 'would choose' + 'rather than' (preference, L41 review)

reading.en: The banker, then rich and confident, made a bet. 'Stay alone in my garden lodge for fifteen years,' he said, 'and I will give you two million rubles.' The lawyer, only twenty-five, accepted.
reading.cn: 当时的银行家又富有又自信，提出了一场赌注。'在我花园的小屋里独自住十五年，'他说，'我就给你两百万卢布。'那位律师当时只有二十五岁，他答应了。
reading.note: Direct speech + first conditional (will give)

reading.en: The lawyer, who had been free, was now locked in a single small lodge. Books were sent in by request. No human voice was allowed.
reading.cn: 曾经自由的律师如今被锁在一栋小屋里。书是按要求送进去的。任何人的声音都不被允许。
reading.note: Reduced relative (who had been free) + passive chain

reading.en: Year after year, the lawyer's reading habits changed. At first, novels and music. Then theology, philosophy, language. By the fifteenth year, he had read in seventeen languages — and seemed to want nothing.
reading.cn: 一年又一年，律师的阅读习惯在变。最开始是小说和音乐。然后是神学、哲学、语言学。到了第十五年，他已经能用十七种语言阅读——而且似乎什么也不想要了。
reading.note: Trend description (L42 review): 'at first... then... by the fifteenth year'

reading.en: Meanwhile, the banker had lost everything. Bad investments, gambling, a war. On the morning of the deadline, he wondered whether he could pay the two million.
reading.cn: 与此同时，银行家失去了一切。糟糕的投资、赌博、一场战争。约定到期那天清晨，他在想自己究竟还付不付得起那两百万。
reading.note: Indirect question (L43 review): 'wondered whether he could pay'

reading.en: He could not. So that night he crept toward the lodge, planning to kill the lawyer in his sleep. On the desk, he found a letter.
reading.cn: 他付不起。于是那一夜他悄悄走向小屋，打算在律师熟睡时杀了他。在书桌上，他发现了一封信。
reading.note: Modal could not + sequence verbs

reading.en: "I have come to despise everything you offered me," the letter read. "Books, freedom, money — even life. I should have refused this bet from the start. I will leave five hours before the deadline. I forfeit the two million."
reading.cn: "我已经鄙视你所给我的一切，"信上写道。"书本、自由、金钱——甚至生命。我从一开始就应该拒绝这场赌注。我会在到期前五个小时离开。我放弃这两百万。"
reading.note: Modal perfect (L44 review): 'should have refused'

reading.en: Five hours before the deadline, the lawyer climbed out of the window and walked away. The banker locked the letter in his safe. He did not weep that night, but he never told anyone what he had read.
reading.cn: 在约定到期前五个小时，律师爬出窗外，走了。银行家把那封信锁进保险柜。那一夜他没有哭，但他从此再没把读到的话告诉过任何人。
reading.note: Past perfect (had read) + closing aphorism

It was a tough lesson about taking too much

fillBlanks.sentence: I made a ___ on the result of the football game.

fillBlanks.sentence: Buying shares in that tech company turned out to be a good ___.
fillBlanks.cn: 购买那家科技公司的股票结果是一项很好的投资。

fillBlanks.sentence: She got a real ___ on that designer bag during the sale.
fillBlanks.cn: 她在打折时买那个名牌包真是捡到便宜了。
这个新项目预计将为公司带来可观的利润。
fillBlanks.sentence: The new project is expected to generate a significant ___ for the company.
The king wanted to find answers to his three important ___ about life and governance.
fillBlanks.cn: 国王想找到关于生命和治理的三个重要问题的答案。

fillBlanks.sentence: Many people came to the palace, but their answers ___ greatly.
fillBlanks.cn: 许多人来到宫殿，但他们的答案大相径庭。

fillBlanks.sentence: He decided to seek the ___ of a wise hermit.
fillBlanks.cn: 他决定寻求一位智者隐士的智慧。

fillBlanks.sentence: The hermit only saw ___ folk, so the king dressed simply.
fillBlanks.cn: 隐士只接见普通人，所以国王穿得很朴素。

fillBlanks.sentence: The king found the old man ___ a garden in front of his hut.
fillBlanks.cn: 国王发现老人在他的小屋前挖花园。

output.sample: Your Majesty, it would be a good idea to always consider the well-being of your people. My advice would be to listen carefully to their needs and concerns. Perhaps you could spend more time among the common folk to truly understand their lives. Focusing on acts of kindness and justice should always be your priority.
output.cn: 假设你是国王的顾问之一。他问你：“最重要的事情是什么？”写一个3-5句的短段落，向国王提出你的建议。使用本课中学到的建议或劝告表达。
output.prompt: Imagine you are one of the advisors to the king. He asks you, "What is the most important thing to do?" Write a short paragraph of 3-5 sentences giving your advice to the king. Use expressions of suggestion or advice from the lesson.

reading.en: A king once decided that if he could only learn three things, he would never make a wrong decision again.
reading.cn: 一位国王曾决定：只要他能学到三件事，他就再也不会做出错误的决定。
reading.note: Mixed conditional (if + could ... would)

reading.en: His three questions were: "When is the right time to do anything? Who are the people I most need to listen to? And what is the most important thing to do?"
reading.cn: 他的三个问题是："做任何事，什么时候是对的时候？我最需要听取谁的意见？最重要的事是什么？"
reading.note: Wh-questions in formal advice-seeking form

reading.en: Many wise men gave answers, but no two answers agreed. So the king disguised himself as a peasant and went to find an old hermit who lived alone in the woods.
reading.cn: 很多智者都给出了答案，但没有两个答案是一致的。于是国王扮成农民，去山里找那位独自隐居的老隐士。
reading.note: Reduced relative (who lived alone)

reading.en: When the king asked his questions, the hermit said nothing. He continued digging his small garden. "Let me dig for you," the king said. "You ought to rest." The hermit accepted.
reading.cn: 国王问出他的问题时，隐士什么也没说。他继续挖他那一小块菜地。"让我替你挖吧，"国王说。"你应该歇歇。"隐士同意了。
reading.note: ought to + V — formal advice (L46 KEY focus)

reading.en: After hours of digging, a wounded man stumbled out of the forest. The king bound the man's wound with his own shirt. The man recovered. Only then did he speak.
reading.cn: 挖了几个小时之后，一个受伤的人踉跄着从林子里走出来。国王用自己的衬衣给那人包扎伤口。那人恢复了，这时才开口说话。
reading.note: Inversion 'only then did he speak' (review L1 inversion)

reading.en: "I came to kill you," the wounded man confessed. "You executed my brother. I should have struck you on the road. But you saved me. From now on, I had better serve you for the rest of my life."
reading.cn: "我本来是来杀你的，"那受伤的人坦白。"你曾经处决了我的哥哥。我本该在路上就动手。但你救了我。从此以后，我最好为你效劳一辈子。"
reading.note: should have V-ed (regret) + had better V (strong resolve)

reading.en: The king was astonished. He turned to the hermit. "I still need my answers," he said. "What ought I to know?"
reading.cn: 国王十分惊讶。他转向隐士。"我还需要我的答案，"他说。"我应当知道什么？"
reading.note: Formal modal inversion: 'What ought I to know?'

reading.en: "You already have them," the hermit replied. "The right time was now, when you stopped to dig. The most important person was the one before you, the wounded man. The most important thing to do was to do good for him. There is no other time, no other person, no other purpose."
reading.cn: "你已经有了答案，"隐士回答。"对的时候，就是你停下来挖地的此刻。最重要的人，就是眼前这个，那位伤者。最重要的事，就是对他做善事。没有别的时间，没有别的人，没有别的目的。"
reading.note: Parallel structure ('the most important... was...') for emphasis

reading.en: The king walked back to the city changed. He had asked the wrong questions for years. What mattered most was not three answers — it was the man in front of him, now.
reading.cn: 国王走回城里，已是另一个人。他多年来问错了问题。最重要的不是三个答案——而是眼前这个人，此刻。
reading.note: What-cleft (review L2) + closing aphorism

examples.cn: 你应该专注于当下。
examples.en: You should focus on the present moment.

examples.cn: 他应该更经常地听取顾问的意见。
examples.en: He ought to listen to his advisors more often.

examples.cn: 也许你可以咨询一位智者隐士。
examples.en: Perhaps you could consult a wise hermit.

examples.cn: 考虑所有观点会是个好主意。
examples.en: It would be a good idea to consider all perspectives.

examples.cn: 我的建议是帮助那些有需要的人。
examples.en: My advice would be to help those in need.

grammar.explain: 在英语中，我们有多种方式来表达建议或劝告。这节课我们将重点学习几种常见的句型，它们可以帮助你在不同语境下提出建议或给出忠告。
grammar.title: 建议与劝告语气 (Suggesting and Advising)

examples.cn: 国王应该听取他的人民的意见。
examples.en: The king should listen to his people.

examples.cn: 你理应优先考虑真正重要的事情。
examples.en: You ought to prioritize what is truly important.

grammar.explain: 这两个词都表示“应该”，用于给出建议、劝告或表达义务。它们的语气略有不同，“ought to”有时听起来更正式或更强调道德上的责任。
grammar.title: “Should” / “Ought to” (应该)
"Perhaps you could..." (也许你可以...)

examples.cn: 也许你可以考虑一下普通民众的需求。
examples.en: Perhaps you could consider the needs of the common folk.

examples.cn: 也许你可以从帮助身边的人开始。
examples.en: Perhaps you could start by helping those around you.

grammar.explain: 这是一个更委婉、更礼貌的建议方式，通常用于提出一个可能性或选项。

examples.cn: 友善对待每一个人会是个好主意。
examples.en: It would be a good idea to act kindly towards everyone.

examples.cn: 专注于当下会是个好主意。
examples.en: It would be a good idea to focus on the present.

grammar.explain: 这个句型用于强调某个行动是一个明智的选择或一个好的建议。
grammar.title: "It would be a good idea to..." (会是个好主意)
"My advice would be..." (我的建议是...)

examples.cn: 隐士的建议是活在当下。
examples.en: The hermit's advice would be to live in the present.

examples.cn: 我的建议是永远友善地对待他人。
examples.en: My advice would be to always treat others with kindness.

grammar.explain: 这是一个直接提供个人建议的句型，语气比较直接但依然礼貌。

listening.audio: The king was confused by the many different answers. He thought, "Perhaps I should seek advice from someone known for his wisdom, rather than just my council." So, he decided to visit a wise hermit who lived alone in the forest. The hermit was known to be very sagacious and only met with common people. The king dressed simply, hoping the hermit would share his deep insights.

reading.en: Although Soapy was a man without a home, he had a plan. Every winter, he made sure to spend the cold months in the comfort of Blackwell's Island prison.
reading.cn: 尽管索比是个无家可归的人，他自有一套计划。每年冬天，他都会想办法让自己在布莱克威尔岛监狱里舒舒服服过完寒冬。
reading.note: Although + clause — concessive opener (KEY focus)

reading.en: Even though respectable men feared jail, Soapy looked forward to it. The food was hot. The bed was dry. And the door was locked against the wind.
reading.cn: 尽管体面人都怕坐牢，索比却盼着进去。那里饭是热的，床是干的，门也紧紧关着把寒风挡在外头。
reading.note: Even though + clause — stronger concessive

reading.en: He walked into a fine restaurant and ordered duck and wine. Although his coat was torn at the collar, he sat tall. He planned to eat well, then admit he had no money — and be arrested for a free trip to jail.
reading.cn: 他走进一家高级餐厅，点了烤鸭和酒。虽然他的外套领口已经破了，他还是腰杆挺得笔直。他打算痛快吃完，再说自己付不起——这样就能被抓走，免费送进监狱。
reading.note: Although + adverbial clause

reading.en: But the head waiter saw the torn coat and turned him out before he could order. Despite his careful planning, the doors of arrest stayed shut.
reading.cn: 可领班一眼就看到那破领子，索比连菜都没点完就被赶了出来。尽管他精心策划，被捕的大门依旧对他紧闭。
reading.note: Despite + noun phrase — concessive preposition

reading.en: He broke a shop window. He ate at a cheap diner and refused to pay. He shouted in the street. Yet, in spite of every effort, no policeman wanted to bother with him.
reading.cn: 他砸了一家店的橱窗。在小馆子里吃完饭不付钱。在街上大喊大叫。然而，尽管他想尽了办法，没有一个警察愿意理他。
reading.note: Yet, in spite of + noun — concessive variation

reading.en: As night fell, Soapy passed an old church. Through the open door came the soft sound of an anthem — a Sunday hymn from his childhood. He stopped and listened, although he had not stopped at a church in years.
reading.cn: 夜幕降临时，索比经过一座老教堂。从虚掩的门缝里飘出柔和的赞美诗——是他童年时星期天唱的圣歌。他停下来听着，尽管他多年没有在教堂前停过脚。
reading.note: Although + past perfect — concessive with prior context

reading.en: Standing in the cold light of the moon, he thought of all the years he had wasted. Even though tomorrow was Monday, he made a vow: he would find work, become a man again, leave the streets behind.
reading.cn: 他站在清冷的月光下，想起自己虚度的那些岁月。即便明天就是星期一，他也下定决心：要找份工作，重新做人，告别街头。
reading.note: Even though + clause — concessive resolve

reading.en: He felt strong. He felt awake. He felt — for the first time in a long time — like himself. A hand touched his shoulder. A police officer asked, 'What are you doing here?'
reading.cn: 他觉得自己有力气。他觉得清醒。他觉得——很久以来第一次——又像自己了。一只手按上了他的肩膀。一位警察问：'你在这儿干什么？'
reading.note: Sequence of psychological awakening + dialogue setup

reading.en: The next morning, the magistrate sentenced Soapy to three months on the Island. He had wanted prison all winter. Now, having found a reason to live free, he was finally going to jail. Such, sometimes, is the timing of life.
reading.cn: 第二天早上，治安官判索比在岛上服刑三个月。他想了一整个冬天的监狱终于来了。可如今他刚找到自由生活的理由，反倒进了牢。人生的时机，有时候就是这样。
reading.note: Closing — having + V-ed (participial) + ironic timing

grammar.title: 让步状语从句 (Adverbial Clauses of Concession)
grammar.explain: 让步状语从句表达与主句相反或者出乎意料的情况。它们通常由以下词引导：though, although, even though, while, whereas, as, however, no matter what/who/how, in spite of, despite 等。

examples.cn: 尽管他尽了最大的努力，警察似乎都对他视而不见。
examples.en: Despite his best efforts, the police seemed to ignore him.

examples.cn: 尽管天冷，他还是在公园长椅上过夜。
examples.en: In spite of the cold, he spent the night on a park bench.

listening.audio: Soapy, a homeless man, desperately sought a warm shelter for the winter. He tried many times to get arrested, even though he didn't want to hurt anyone. However, the police seemed to ignore his attempts regardless of what he did. One day, he heard a beautiful anthem from a church and had a change of heart. He decided to find a job and escape his misery. But just then, a police officer approached him and arrested him for loitering.

reading.en: After I submit, I FaceTime my parents. It's morning in Beijing.

reading.en: Mom is quiet at first. Then she says, "Whoever you become, we are proud."

reading.en: Dad adds, "Whatever happens, you are still our daughter. Whatever the result, we'll be there."

reading.en: Wei walks past with a thumbs up. I almost cry — for the third time this week.

reading.en: I don't know which school will say yes. But I know who will catch me if no one does.

vocab.example: It was a kind of stillness she had never seen.
vocab.example_cn: 那是一种她从未见过的安静。

vocab.example: Her realization came like cold water.

vocab.example: His confession needed no further explanation.

vocab.example: Some confessions need no further explanation.
vocab.example_cn: 有些坦白不需要再多做解释。

vocab.example: Their two sacrifices had cancelled each other out.
vocab.example_cn: 他们两人的牺牲，正好相互抵消。

vocab.example: This is the wisdom of the Magi.

reading.en: Della had exactly one dollar and eighty-seven cents. The arrival of Christmas was less than twenty-four hours away.
reading.cn: 黛拉手里只有一块八毛七。圣诞节的到来，已经只剩不到二十四个小时。
reading.note: Nominalization (arrival)

reading.en: For weeks, her preparation for this day had been a single goal: a gift worthy of her husband Jim. Their poverty was real, but her devotion was greater.
reading.cn: 几个星期以来，她为这天做的所有准备只有一件事：找一份配得上丈夫吉姆的礼物。他们的贫穷是真实的，但她对他的爱意，比贫穷更深。
reading.note: Nominalization × 3 (preparation, poverty, devotion)

reading.en: In all their possessions, two things were of great value. Jim's gold watch had been his father's, and his grandfather's. Della's brown hair fell below her knees, with the soft shine of a brown waterfall.
reading.cn: 他们家里所有的东西里，只有两样真正贵重。吉姆的金表，是父亲、爷爷传下来的。黛拉的栗色长发垂到膝下，闪着像褐色瀑布一样柔和的光。
reading.note: Nominalization (possessions)

reading.en: Her decision came without hesitation. She stopped at a shop whose sign read "Madame Sofronie. Hair Goods of All Kinds." Twenty dollars later, she walked out — her head cold and her purse full.
reading.cn: 她做这个决定时几乎没有犹豫。她在一家招牌写着「索弗朗夫人 · 各种发制品」的店门口停下，走了进去。二十块钱之后，她走出来——头顶发凉，钱包却满了。
reading.note: Nominalization × 2 (decision, hesitation)

reading.en: With the money, she bought a platinum watch chain for Jim. The chain's simplicity and quietness were exactly right. Like Jim, it had value without showiness.
reading.cn: 她用这笔钱给吉姆买了一条铂金表链。这条链子的简洁与低调正合适。像吉姆这个人——它有价值，但不张扬。
reading.note: Nominalization × 4 (simplicity, quietness, value, showiness)

reading.en: When Jim came home that evening, his reaction was strange. It was not anger, nor disappointment, nor displeasure. It was a kind of stillness Della had never seen on his face before.
reading.cn: 傍晚吉姆回家时，他的反应很奇怪。不是生气，不是失望，也不是不悦。那是一种黛拉从未在他脸上见过的安静。
reading.note: Nominalization × 5 (reaction, anger, disappointment, displeasure, stillness)

reading.en: Slowly, he placed a small package on the table. Inside were the combs Della had been admiring in a shop window for months — beautiful tortoise-shell combs, perfect for her long hair. Her realization came like cold water.
reading.cn: 他慢慢把一个小包放在桌上。里面是几把黛拉对着橱窗看了几个月的发梳——漂亮的玳瑁发梳，正适合她的长发。她明白过来的那一刻，像被冷水浇了一身。
reading.note: Nominalization (realization)

reading.en: "I sold the watch," Jim said, "to buy your combs." His confession needed no further explanation. Their two sacrifices — made out of love — had cancelled each other out exactly.
reading.cn: 「我把表卖了，」吉姆说，「为了给你买梳子。」他的坦白不需要再多解释什么。他们出于爱做的两个牺牲，正好相互抵消。
reading.note: Nominalization × 3 (confession, explanation, sacrifices)

reading.en: This is the wisdom of the Magi: of all the gifts in the world, those that look the most foolish are sometimes the wisest. The exchange of useless treasures, given in devotion, is itself the gift.
reading.cn: 这就是麦琪的智慧：在世上所有礼物中，那些看起来最傻的，有时候恰恰是最有智慧的。两件没用的宝物在彼此间交换——只因为爱——这件事本身，就是真正的礼物。
reading.note: Closing aphorism — nominalization-rich (wisdom, exchange, devotion)

vocab.meaning: v. 借入；借（borrow X from Y）
vocab.example: She borrowed a necklace from her friend.
vocab.example_cn: 她从朋友那里借了一串项链。
她富有的朋友福雷斯蒂耶夫人。

vocab.meaning: phrasal 升到；上升至（描述趋势核心动词）
vocab.example: Her status rose to the level she had imagined.
vocab.example_cn: 她的地位升到了她想象的高度。
他们找遍衣帽间——一无所获。

vocab.example: Her husband borrowed at terrible interest.

vocab.meaning: adj. 一模一样的；完全相同的
vocab.example_cn: 他们买了一串一模一样的项链。

vocab.example: Their poverty deepened year by year.
vocab.example_cn: 他们的贫穷一年比一年深。

vocab.meaning: v. 加深；变深（趋势动词）
n. 债务（注意 b 不发音）

vocab.example: The necklace I lent you was paste.
vocab.example_cn: 我借给你的那串是仿的。

vocab.example: It was worth at most five hundred francs.

reading.en: Mathilde was beautiful, but she had been born poor. She had married a clerk because she had no other choice.
reading.cn: 马蒂尔德很美，但生在一个穷家。她嫁给了一名小职员，因为她别无选择。
reading.note: Past perfect setup — "had been born / had married"

reading.en: She borrowed a diamond necklace from her wealthy friend Madame Forestier for one evening at the grand ball at the Ministry.
reading.cn: 部长舞会那一晚，她从富有的朋友福雷斯蒂耶夫人那里借了一串钻石项链。
reading.note: "borrowed X from Y" — common B2 verb pattern

reading.en: At the ball, she danced through the night. For one evening, her social standing rose to the level she had always imagined.
reading.cn: 舞会上她跳了一整夜。那一晚，她的社会地位升到了她一直幻想的高度。
reading.note: "rose to" — trend verb · key for describing change

reading.en: Walking home at dawn, she discovered the necklace was gone. They searched the streets, the carriage, the cloakroom — nothing.
reading.cn: 天蒙蒙亮往家走时，她发现项链不见了。他们找遍街道、马车、衣帽间——一无所获。
reading.note: Discovery point — narrative pivot

reading.en: Her husband borrowed at terrible interest. Together they bought an identical necklace for thirty-six thousand francs and returned it without a word.
reading.cn: 她丈夫以高得吓人的利息四处借钱。他们花了三万六千法郎，买了一串一模一样的项链，一句话不说就还了回去。
reading.note: "at + interest rate" — financial collocation

reading.en: Their poverty deepened year by year. They moved to a smaller apartment. Mathilde scrubbed floors, washed her own laundry, and grew thin and rough.
reading.cn: 他们的贫穷一年比一年深。他们搬进一间更小的公寓。马蒂尔德擦地板、自己洗衣，人变瘦、变粗糙。
reading.note: "deepened year by year" — gradual trend phrase

reading.en: After ten years, every franc had been repaid. Mathilde looked older than her age — but the debt had been settled to the last sou.
reading.cn: 十年之后，每一个法郎都还清了。马蒂尔德看上去比实际年纪老——但债务已经还到最后一个铜板。
reading.note: "every franc had been repaid" — passive completion

reading.en: One Sunday on the Champs-Élysées she saw Madame Forestier, still young and elegant. After ten years, she went up to her and told her the truth.
reading.cn: 一个星期天在香榭丽舍大街上，她看见了福雷斯蒂耶夫人——依旧年轻、依旧优雅。隔了十年，她走过去，把真相告诉了她。
reading.note: "After ten years" — time anchor for closing

reading.en: "But, my poor Mathilde," her friend said softly, "the necklace I lent you was paste. It was worth at most five hundred francs."
reading.cn: "可是，我可怜的马蒂尔德，"朋友轻轻说，"我借给你的那串是仿的。它最多值五百法郎。"
reading.note: Closing reversal — the signature ironic ending

vocab.example_cn: 我应该把那场大悲剧告诉你。

vocab.meaning: adj./n. 流浪的；贱民（古印度）

vocab.example: Romance at short notice was her specialty.
vocab.example_cn: 临时编故事是她的拿手好戏。

reading.en: Framton Nuttel was a man whose nerves needed rest. His sister had given him letters of introduction to several country families.
reading.cn: 弗兰顿·纳特尔是个神经紧张、需要静养的人。他姐姐给了他几封介绍信，让他去拜访几户乡下人家。
reading.note: Reduced relative + past perfect

reading.en: In a country house, he was met by Mrs. Sappleton's fifteen-year-old niece, Vera. "My aunt will be down in fifteen minutes," she said. "Until then, I must do my best to entertain you."
reading.cn: 在一栋乡下房子里，他被萨普尔顿太太那位十五岁的侄女维拉接待。"我姑姑十五分钟之内就下来，"她说。"在那之前，我得尽量让你不无聊。"
reading.note: Direct speech opener

reading.en: Vera asked whether Framton knew her aunt at all. Framton replied that he knew almost nothing about her — just her name and address.
reading.cn: 维拉问弗兰顿对她姑姑究竟了解多少。弗兰顿回答说，他几乎什么也不知道——只知道她的名字和地址。
reading.note: Reported speech: asked whether / replied that (L47 KEY focus)

reading.en: "Then I should tell you the great tragedy," Vera said softly. She pointed to the open French window. "Three years ago, my aunt's husband and her two younger brothers went out that window to hunt. They never returned. They drowned in a bog."
reading.cn: "那我应该把那场大悲剧告诉你，"维拉轻声说。她指着那扇开着的落地窗。"三年前，我姑姑的丈夫和她两个弟弟从那扇窗户出去打猎。他们再也没回来。他们都陷进沼泽淹死了。"
reading.note: Past simple narrative + 'never returned' (emphatic)

reading.en: Vera said her aunt still expected them to walk back through the window any minute. "That is why," Vera whispered, "the window is kept open until dusk every evening — even now."
reading.cn: 维拉说，姑姑仍然以为他们随时会从那扇窗户走回来。"所以，"维拉低声说，"每天傍晚天黑之前，那扇窗都开着——一直到现在。"
reading.note: Reported speech: said her aunt expected... (backshift)

reading.en: Mrs. Sappleton came in and apologized for being late. She told Framton that her husband and brothers would be home from hunting any moment. "They always come in through that window," she said cheerfully.
reading.cn: 萨普尔顿太太进来，为自己来晚了道歉。她告诉弗兰顿，她丈夫和弟弟随时可能打完猎回家。"他们总是从那扇窗户进来，"她快活地说。
reading.note: Reported speech: told Framton that + would (future-in-past)

reading.en: Framton listened in horror. He believed Mrs. Sappleton was suffering from a delusion — believing the dead would walk in. Then, through the open window, three figures appeared, carrying guns.
reading.cn: 弗兰顿越听越恐惧。他以为萨普尔顿太太得了妄想症——以为死人会走回来。这时，三个身影从那扇开着的窗户走了进来，肩上扛着猎枪。
reading.note: Believed + that-clause (reported belief) + sequence

reading.en: Framton ran. He did not stop running until he reached the road. Mrs. Sappleton's husband was puzzled. "What a strange man," he said. "He bolted as if he had seen a ghost."
reading.cn: 弗兰顿跑了。他一口气跑到马路上才停下。萨普尔顿先生很困惑。"这人真奇怪，"他说。"跑得跟见了鬼一样。"
reading.note: did not + V until + reached + 'as if + had seen' (subjunctive simile)

reading.en: Vera explained, with a face of innocent regret, that Framton had a horror of dogs — once, in India, he had been chased into a graveyard by a pack of pariah dogs. Romance at short notice was her specialty.
reading.cn: 维拉一脸天真的惋惜，解释说弗兰顿见不得狗——有一次在印度，他被一群野狗追进了一座墓地。"临时即兴编故事"是她的拿手好戏。
reading.note: Closing aphorism — Saki's famous line

vocab.example: He could not reach the lowest branch.
The Giant grieved for the boy.
Who has dared to wound you?

vocab.meaning: v. 杀；屠戮（slew, slain — 文学）

reading.en: When the Giant returned home, he found the children playing in his garden. He had been away visiting his Cornish friend for seven years. By the time he came back, his garden had become the children's favorite place.
reading.cn: 巨人回家时，发现孩子们正在他的花园里玩。他离家走访康沃尔的朋友已有七年。等他回来时，他的花园已经成了孩子们最喜欢的地方。
reading.note: had been away + V-ing (duration to past) + by the time + past perfect

reading.en: "My own garden is my own garden," the Giant roared. "I will allow nobody to play in it but myself." He built a high wall around it and put up a sign: TRESPASSERS WILL BE PROSECUTED.
reading.cn: "我的花园是我的花园，"巨人怒吼。"除了我自己，谁都不许在里面玩。"他在花园四周筑起高墙，立了块牌子：闯入者必究。
reading.note: Direct speech + future passive (will be prosecuted)

reading.en: Once the wall had been built, Spring no longer came to that garden. Snow covered the grass. The North Wind moved in. Hail came every day. Only Winter remained — for the Giant had refused everyone else.
reading.cn: 墙一建好，春天就不再光顾那座花园了。雪铺满草地。北风搬了进来。冰雹每天都来。只有冬天留了下来——因为巨人把别人都拒之门外了。
reading.note: Once + past perfect passive (had been built) + 'for' (= because)

reading.en: One morning, the Giant heard music. A linnet was singing outside his window. He had not heard birdsong for so long that he thought spring had returned to the world. Through a small hole in the wall, the children had crept back in. Their laughter had brought spring with them.
reading.cn: 一天早晨，巨人听到了音乐。一只朱顶雀在窗外唱歌。他已经太久没听到鸟鸣，以为春天回到了人间。原来孩子们从墙上一个小洞钻了回来。他们的笑声把春天也带回来了。
reading.note: Multiple past perfects: had not heard / had returned / had crept / had brought (KEY focus)

reading.en: Every tree had blossomed except one — in the corner stood a small child who could not reach the lowest branch. The Giant lifted him gently. The tree burst into flower at once. The boy threw his arms around the Giant's neck and kissed him.
reading.cn: 除了角落里那一棵，每棵树都开了花。角落里有个小男孩，够不到最低的枝条。巨人轻轻把他举起来。那棵树立刻开满了花。男孩用胳膊搂住巨人的脖子，亲了他一下。
reading.note: Past perfect (had blossomed) + sequence of softening

reading.en: The Giant tore down the wall. "It is your garden now, little children," he said. From that morning on, the children played there every afternoon. But the small boy who had kissed him never came back, and the Giant grieved for him.
reading.cn: 巨人推倒了墙。"现在这是你们的花园了，孩子们，"他说。从那天早上起，孩子们每天下午都在那里玩。但那个亲过他的小男孩再也没回来，巨人为他难过。
reading.note: had kissed + reduced relative (the boy who had...)

reading.en: Years passed. The Giant grew old and weak. He could no longer play with the children — he could only watch them. On a winter afternoon, he saw a strange and beautiful sight: in the corner stood a tree covered with white blossoms — and beneath it, the small child.
reading.cn: 年复一年。巨人变老变弱了。他不能再和孩子们一起玩——只能看着他们。一个冬天的下午，他看见一幅奇异而美丽的景象：角落里站着一棵开满白花的树——树下，是那个小男孩。
reading.note: Reduced relative (covered with) + emphatic 'in the corner stood' (inversion)

reading.en: The Giant ran out, full of joy. But when he came near, his face grew angry. The child had wounds on his hands and feet — small wounds, like the prints of nails. "Who has dared to wound you?" the Giant cried. "Tell me, that I may take my big sword and slay him."
reading.cn: 巨人满怀喜悦冲了出去。可走近时，他的脸阴了下来。男孩的手上、脚上有伤——小小的伤口，像钉子的钉痕。"谁敢伤害你？"巨人喊。"告诉我，我好拿起我的大刀去杀他。"
reading.note: Has dared (present perfect) + 'that I may + V' = old-fashioned purpose clause

reading.en: "No," the child answered. "These are the wounds of love. Once you let me play in your garden. Today you shall come with me to my garden, which is Paradise." When the children came that afternoon, they found the Giant lying dead under the tree, all covered with white blossoms.
reading.cn: "不，"男孩答。"这是爱的伤痕。从前你让我在你的花园里玩。今天，你要随我到我的花园里去——那是天堂。"那天下午孩子们来时，发现巨人躺在树下，已经死了，身上全是白色的花。
reading.note: Closing — 'shall' (literary future-imperative) + Christ allegory

vocab.example: The seed of hope had been planted.
She began to imagine a country house.
vocab.example_cn: 她开始想象一栋乡下房子。

vocab.example: Two strangers in their own house.
vocab.example_cn: 在自己家里成了陌生人。

vocab.example: The house, the marriage, the silence.
What they had each, briefly, wished for.
vocab.example_cn: 他们短短一瞬里各自渴望过的东西。

reading.en: Ivan and his wife Masha had been living quietly for years. They were not rich, but they were not poor either — although they had often dreamed of being either.
reading.cn: 伊万和他妻子玛莎多年来过着安静的日子。他们不富，也不算穷——尽管他们时常幻想成为其中一种。
reading.note: Past perfect (had been living, had dreamed) + concessive (although) — L48 + L49 review

reading.en: One evening, Ivan was reading the newspaper. "What was the lottery number Masha bought?" he asked himself. He looked. The first three digits matched. He told her that the prize might be theirs.
reading.cn: 一天傍晚，伊万正在读报纸。"玛莎买的那张彩票是几号来着？"他自言自语。他看了一眼。前三位数字对上了。他告诉她，奖也许就是他们的。
reading.note: Reported speech (asked himself / told her that) — L47 review

reading.en: Masha said it was probably nothing. "But you ought to check the rest," she said. Ivan laughed nervously. "If we won, what would we do?" he asked. "I had better not even hope."
reading.cn: 玛莎说大概没什么戏。"不过你应该把剩下几位也对一对，"她说。伊万紧张地笑了。"要是真中了，我们会做什么？"他问。"我最好别抱什么希望。"
reading.note: ought to / had better — L46 review (advice & counsel)

reading.en: But once the seed of hope had been planted, neither of them could stop. Masha began to imagine a country house, a garden, summers by the sea. Ivan, sitting silently, began to imagine — quite differently.
reading.cn: 可一旦希望的种子被埋下了，两人就再也停不下来。玛莎开始想象一栋乡下房子、一个花园、海边的夏天。伊万静静坐着，想的——完全是另一回事。
reading.note: Once + past perfect passive (had been planted) — L48 review

reading.en: He thought about how he had never traveled, how she had always wanted everything, how — even though they had been married for years — he had begun to find her tiresome. He told himself that with money, he would be free.
reading.cn: 他想到自己从未旅行过，想到她总是什么都想要，想到——尽管他们结婚多年了——他已经开始觉得她让人厌烦。他告诉自己，有了钱，他就自由了。
reading.note: Reported speech (told himself that) + even though clause + past perfect chain — REVIEW

reading.en: Masha, watching his face, asked whether he was hiding something. He answered that he was tired. But she had seen the look — and her own thoughts darkened too. She wondered whether he had ever truly loved her.
reading.cn: 玛莎看着他的脸，问他是不是有事瞒着。他答说只是累了。可她已经看到了那个表情——她自己的心思也阴了下来。她在想，他到底有没有真正爱过她。
reading.note: asked whether / answered that / wondered whether — L47 review

reading.en: For an hour they sat in silence, two strangers in their own house. Each of them thought, almost at the same moment: "I should have lived alone."
reading.cn: 两人沉默地坐了一个小时，仿佛在自己家里成了陌生人。几乎在同一刻，他们各自想：'我本该一个人过的。'
reading.note: should have V-ed — modal perfect of regret (L44 cumulative review)

reading.en: Then Ivan picked up the ticket and looked again, more carefully. The fourth digit did not match. The ticket was worthless. They had won nothing.
reading.cn: 这时伊万拿起彩票，更仔细地又看了一遍。第四位数字不对。彩票一文不值。他们什么也没中。
reading.note: Past perfect (had won) + simple statement of fact — emotional pivot

reading.en: Neither said a word. Masha went into the kitchen. Ivan stayed at the table. Although nothing had changed, everything had. The house, the marriage, the silence — all of it now had a new sound: the sound of what they had each, briefly, wished for.
reading.cn: 两人都没说话。玛莎走进厨房。伊万留在桌前。尽管什么也没变，一切又都变了。屋子、婚姻、沉默——这一切现在都有了一种新的声响：那是两人短短一瞬里各自渴望过的东西的回响。
reading.note: Closing — concessive (although) + past perfect + closing aphorism

vocab.example: A nightingale heard the boy crying.
Stain it with your heart's blood.
By dawn, the rose had turned crimson.
vocab.example_cn: 到天亮时，玫瑰已变深红。

vocab.example: It will not match my dress.

reading.en: Standing at his window, the young Student wept. The girl he loved had said she would dance with him only if he brought her a red rose. Looking around the garden, he saw no red rose anywhere.
reading.cn: 年轻的学生站在窗前哭泣。他爱的那个姑娘说，除非他给她带一朵红玫瑰，否则不会和他跳舞。他环顾整个花园，一朵红玫瑰也没看到。
reading.note: Standing... + Looking around... — present participial openers (KEY focus)

reading.en: In a tree above him, a nightingale heard the boy crying. Watching the boy with quiet pity, she said softly: "Here at last is a true lover."
reading.cn: 他头顶的一棵树上，一只夜莺听到了男孩的哭声。她静静地、怜悯地看着他，轻声说：'这总算是个真正的恋人了。'
reading.note: Watching... — participial adverbial introducing action

reading.en: The nightingale flew through the garden, asking each rose-tree for a red rose. Each tree said no. One tree, however, having pity for her, told her the secret.
reading.cn: 夜莺飞遍了花园，向每一棵玫瑰树要一朵红玫瑰。每棵都说没有。然而有一棵，怜悯她，把秘密告诉了她。
reading.note: asking each rose-tree — participial adverbial / having pity — perfect participle

reading.en: "If you want a red rose," the tree said, "you must build it out of music by moonlight, and stain it with your own heart's blood. Singing all night with your breast against a thorn — that is the only way."
reading.cn: "想要红玫瑰，"那棵树说，"你必须在月光下用歌声把它织出来，并用你心里的血染红它。把胸口顶在一根刺上整夜歌唱——那是唯一的办法。"
reading.note: Singing all night... — participial as topic-setting

reading.en: Believing the price was worth paying, the nightingale flew back to find the Student. He was lying in the grass, half asleep. She did not tell him what she would do.
reading.cn: 夜莺相信这代价值得，便飞回去找那位学生。他躺在草地上，半睡半醒。她没告诉他自己将要做什么。
reading.note: Believing... — participial expressing reason / half asleep — modifier

reading.en: When the moon rose, the nightingale pressed her breast against the thorn and began to sing. Singing of love that does not die, she pressed harder. The thorn went deeper, and a single rose began to grow on the bush, white at first.
reading.cn: 月亮升起时，夜莺把胸口顶在那根刺上，开始唱歌。她唱着不会死去的爱情，越唱越用力。那根刺扎得更深，一朵玫瑰开始在树上长出来，最初是白色的。
reading.note: Singing of love... — participial with content / Pressed harder — sequence

reading.en: Crying out in pain, she sang on. By dawn, the rose had turned crimson. The nightingale, having given everything, fell from the branch — dead among the grass.
reading.cn: 她痛得叫出声来，依然唱着。到天亮时，玫瑰已经变成深红。夜莺把一切都给了出去，从枝头跌下来——死在草丛中。
reading.note: Crying out... — present participle / having given... — perfect participle

reading.en: The Student woke and saw the red rose. Running to the girl's house, he held it out. But she only laughed. "It will not match my dress," she said. "And the Chamberlain's nephew has sent me real jewels — and jewels cost more than flowers."
reading.cn: 学生醒来，看见了那朵红玫瑰。他跑到姑娘家，把花递过去。可她只是笑。"和我的裙子不搭，"她说。"再说，宫廷大臣的侄子给我送了真正的珠宝——珠宝可比花值钱。"
reading.note: Running... — participial showing manner of arrival

reading.en: Throwing the rose into the street, the Student walked home. "Love is a foolish thing," he muttered, picking up a heavy book. "I will go back to philosophy." A cart wheel passed over the rose, crushing it into the mud.
reading.cn: 学生把玫瑰扔到街上，走回家去。"爱情是件蠢事，"他咕哝着，拿起一本厚书。"我还是回去读哲学吧。"一辆马车碾过那朵玫瑰，把它压进了泥里。
reading.note: Throwing... + picking up... + crushing — chain of participials

vocab.example: A small studio in Greenwich Village.
vocab.example_cn: 格林威治村的一间小画室。

vocab.example: An old ivy vine clung there.
vocab.example_cn: 一株老常春藤攀在那里。

vocab.example: The masterpiece he would one day paint.
He was admitted to the hospital.
By lantern in the freezing rain.
vocab.example_cn: 在结冰的雨里借着灯笼的光。

reading.en: In a small studio in Greenwich Village lived two young painters: Sue and Johnsy. It was Johnsy who fell ill that November — pneumonia, the doctor said. Never had a winter felt so heavy.
reading.cn: 格林威治村一间小画室里，住着两位年轻画家：苏和琼西。那年十一月生病的是琼西——肺炎，医生说。冬天从未让人觉得这般沉重。
reading.note: It was Johnsy who... — cleft sentence (KEY focus) / Never had... — negative inversion

reading.en: Lying in bed, Johnsy stared at the brick wall outside. An old ivy vine clung there. "When the last leaf falls," she whispered, "I will go too." It was this strange belief that frightened Sue most of all.
reading.cn: 琼西躺在床上，盯着窗外的砖墙。一株老常春藤攀在墙上。"等最后一片叶子掉了，"她小声说，"我也就走了。"让苏最害怕的，正是这个奇怪的念头。
reading.note: It was this strange belief that... — cleft for emphasis

reading.en: Behind their building lived old Behrman, a failed painter who, for forty years, had been talking about the masterpiece he would one day paint. Not once had he begun it.
reading.cn: 他们楼后住着老贝尔曼，一个失败的画家，四十年来一直说着自己有一天要画的那幅杰作。可他一次都没动笔。
reading.note: Not once had he begun it — negative inversion (KEY focus)

reading.en: When Sue told him about Johnsy, Behrman cursed loudly. "Why do you let her have such fool ideas?" he said. But it was clear, even then, that he had been moved.
reading.cn: 苏把琼西的事告诉他，贝尔曼大声咒骂。"你怎么由她生这种傻念头？"他说。可即便那时，谁都看得出，他已经动了心。
reading.note: It was clear that... — cleft for confirmation

reading.en: That night, the storm came. Rain hammered the window. Wind tore at the wall. By morning, only one leaf remained on the vine — and Johnsy lay watching it. "When it falls," she said, "so will I."
reading.cn: 那一夜，暴风雨来了。雨敲打着窗户。风撕扯着墙。到早晨，藤上只剩一片叶子——琼西躺着看着它。"它一落，"她说，"我也就走了。"
reading.note: Rain hammered... + so will I — emphatic structures

reading.en: But the leaf did not fall that day. Nor did it fall the next. Each morning, Johnsy looked, and there it still was — green, hanging on. Slowly, her will to live returned.
reading.cn: 可那片叶子那天没掉。第二天也没掉。每天早上，琼西看出去，它还在那儿——绿色的，还挂着。慢慢地，她活下去的意志回来了。
reading.note: Nor did it fall... — negative inversion ('nor + auxiliary + subject')

reading.en: On the third day, the doctor said she would live. "Now I must go to see Behrman," he added. "Yesterday, the old man was admitted to the hospital with pneumonia. Out he had gone the night of the storm — God knows where."
reading.cn: 到第三天，医生说她能挺过来了。"现在我得去看贝尔曼，"他又说，"昨天，那位老先生因为肺炎被送进了医院。暴风雨那夜他出了门——天晓得去了哪里。"
reading.note: Out he had gone... — fronted adverbial for emphasis

reading.en: Two days later, Sue came to Johnsy. "There is something I must show you," she said. They went to the window. Sue pointed at the leaf. "Look closely. It has not moved in the wind. Not once has it shaken since the storm."
reading.cn: 两天后，苏来到琼西身边。"有件事我必须给你看，"她说。她们走到窗前。苏指着那片叶子。"仔细看。它在风里一动也没动过。从那夜暴风雨以来，它一次都没颤过。"
reading.note: Not once has it shaken — negative inversion in present perfect

reading.en: It was Behrman, Sue explained, who had painted the leaf on the wall the night of the storm. Yellow and green and brown, leaf-veins drawn fine — done in the freezing rain, by lantern. "That," Sue said quietly, "was his masterpiece."
reading.cn: 苏解释说，是贝尔曼在暴风雨那一夜把那片叶子画在墙上的。黄、绿、棕，叶脉描得细致——在结冰的雨里画出来，借着一盏灯笼的光。"那，"苏轻声说，"是他的杰作。"
reading.note: Closing — It was Behrman who... — cleft + 'That was his masterpiece' = emphatic

vocab.example_cn: 他们把艾克尔斯拖回去。

vocab.example: No one remembered voting for him.
Stuck to the sole was a butterfly.

reading.en: In the year 2055, Eckels paid ten thousand dollars for a hunting trip. Time Safari Inc. would send him 65 million years into the past — to shoot a Tyrannosaurus rex. If anything went wrong, the guide warned, the future could change forever.
reading.cn: 公元2055年，艾克尔斯付了一万美元参加一次狩猎之旅。时间狩猎公司会把他送到六千五百万年前——去猎杀一头霸王龙。要是出了任何差池，向导警告说，未来都可能永远改变。
reading.note: Future-in-past + first conditional with 'could change' (KEY chain begins)

reading.en: "Stay on the metal Path," the guide said. "If you step off, you might crush an insect. If you crushed an insect, the food chain would shift. Were that to happen, history itself could be different."
reading.cn: "待在金属路面上，"向导说。"要是踩下去，你可能会踩死一只虫。要是踩死了一只虫，食物链就会改变。如果真发生了那种事，历史本身都可能不同。"
reading.note: Mixed conditional ladder + 'Were that to happen' = inverted second conditional (KEY focus)

reading.en: When the dinosaur appeared, Eckels froze. Unless he could pull the trigger, the others would die. He could not. He stumbled — off the Path — into the soft jungle floor.
reading.cn: 霸王龙出现时，艾克尔斯僵住了。除非他能扣动扳机，其他人就要死。他扣不下去。他跌跌撞撞——下了那条路——踩进柔软的丛林地面。
reading.note: unless + clause + 'were' subjunctive / off the Path — fronted adverbial

reading.en: The others shot the dinosaur. They dragged Eckels back to the time machine. Had they checked his boots more carefully, they would have noticed something — but they did not.
reading.cn: 其他人击毙了霸王龙。他们把艾克尔斯拖回时间机器。如果他们更仔细地检查他的靴子，就会注意到一些东西——但他们没有。
reading.note: Had they checked... — inverted third conditional (KEY focus)

reading.en: Back in 2055, the air smelled different. The signs in the office had different lettering. The election results, posted on the wall, named a man no one in the room remembered voting for.
reading.cn: 回到2055年，空气闻起来不一样了。办公室里的招牌字体也不同。墙上贴的选举结果，是个所有人都不记得投过票的人当选。
reading.note: Atmospheric shift — implicit consequence of the past change

reading.en: Eckels looked down at his boots. Stuck to the sole was a butterfly. He had killed it. "If I had not stepped off the Path," he whispered, "this would not have happened. Were I able to go back, I would do anything."
reading.cn: 艾克尔斯低头看自己的靴子。鞋底上粘着一只蝴蝶。他踩死了它。"要是我没下那条路，"他低声说，"这一切就不会发生。如果我能回去，我会愿意付出一切。"
reading.note: Third conditional + Were I able to... = inverted second conditional

reading.en: But the past was past. Time, having branched, would not re-merge. He looked at the guide. "Unless you can take me back," he said, "send me back this very moment, my life is over."
reading.cn: 可过去就是过去。时间一旦分叉，便不会再合拢。他望向向导。"除非你能把我送回去，"他说，"现在就送我回去，否则我就完了。"
reading.note: having branched — perfect participle / unless + can — first conditional

reading.en: The guide raised his rifle. "Were the company to find out you stepped off the Path," he said quietly, "they would charge you the full penalty. But if you had stayed on the Path, you would have ruined nothing. Now everything is ruined. Including you."
reading.cn: 向导举起步枪。"要是公司发现你下了那条路，"他平静地说，"他们会让你赔到底。可要是你当初待在路上，就什么也不会毁掉。现在一切都毁了。也包括你。"
reading.note: Were the company to find out... + if you had stayed... — inverted 2nd + 3rd conditional

reading.en: Eckels closed his eyes. Behind him, there was a sound of thunder.
reading.cn: 艾克尔斯闭上了眼睛。在他身后，响起了一声雷霆。
reading.note: Closing — minimal sentence, maximum impact (Bradbury's signature)

vocab.example: Mrs. Mallard had a weak heart.
There had been a railroad accident.
A woman struck by sudden grief.
vocab.example_cn: 一个被突然悲痛击中的女人。

vocab.meaning: adj. 微妙的；难以察觉的

vocab.example: Her bosom rose and fell tumultuously.

vocab.meaning: adj. 无能为力的；无力的
vocab.example: Her will was as powerless as her two thin hands.
vocab.example_cn: 她的意志和她那两只瘦小的手一样无力。

vocab.example: The strongest impulse of her being.
vocab.example_cn: 她生命里最强烈的本能。

vocab.example: There had been a railway accident.

reading.en: Knowing that Mrs. Mallard had a weak heart, her sister Josephine broke the news as gently as she could. There had been a railroad accident. Brently Mallard's name was on the list of those killed.
reading.cn: 约瑟芬知道马拉德太太心脏不好，便尽量温和地把消息告诉她。发生了一场铁路事故。布伦特利·马拉德的名字在遇难者名单上。
reading.note: Knowing that... — present participial opener (review L51)

reading.en: Mrs. Mallard wept at once, in the wild way of a woman struck by sudden grief. Then, alone in her room, she sank into a chair facing the open window. A new spring had come outside. She did not yet know it had come for her, too.
reading.cn: 马拉德太太当即痛哭起来，那是被巨大悲痛击中的女人才有的狂烈方式。然后，她独自回到房间，瘫坐进面对敞开窗户的椅子里。窗外，新的春天已经到来。她还不知道，春天也是为她而来的。
reading.note: Free indirect — final sentence presents her not-yet-realized thought

reading.en: There was something coming to her. She did not know what it was — too subtle to name. But she felt it, creeping out of the sky, reaching toward her through the sounds, the scents, the color in the air. She began to wait for it.
reading.cn: 有什么东西正向她而来。她不知道是什么——太微妙，叫不出名字。但她感觉到它，从天空里悄悄出来，透过各种声响、气味、空气里的颜色，朝她伸过手来。她开始等它。
reading.note: 'Too subtle to name' is HER thought presented as narration (KEY focus)

reading.en: Now her bosom rose and fell tumultuously. She was beginning to recognize this thing that was approaching to possess her. She tried to beat it back with her will — but her will was as powerless as her two thin hands.
reading.cn: 她的胸膛起伏激烈。她开始认出这个正逼近、要占据她的东西。她试图用意志推开它——可她的意志，和她那两只瘦小的手一样无力。
reading.note: Free indirect — the metaphor 'as powerless as her two thin hands' is HER self-image

reading.en: When at last she allowed it, a little whispered word escaped her parted lips. She said it again and again. "Free, free, free!" She no longer saw a corpse on the railway. She saw years to come — years that would belong to her, and her alone.
reading.cn: 她终于让那东西进来了，一句轻轻的低语从她微张的唇间溜出。她一遍一遍地说。"自由了，自由了，自由了！"她不再看到铁路上的尸体了。她看到的是即将到来的岁月——属于她、只属于她的岁月。
reading.note: Direct speech ('Free, free, free!') + free indirect (the years she would see)

reading.en: She had loved him — sometimes. Often, she had not. What did it matter? Love, the unsolved mystery, counted for nothing now beside this thing she suddenly recognized as the strongest impulse of her being: the right to be herself.
reading.cn: 她爱过他——有时候。但更多时候，她没有爱过。这又算什么呢？爱，那个永远解不开的谜，在她突然认出的这个东西面前根本算不了什么——这东西是她生命里最强烈的本能：做自己的权利。
reading.note: 'What did it matter?' is HER thought, NOT the narrator's question (KEY focus)

reading.en: Josephine was kneeling outside the locked door. "Louise, open the door! You will make yourself ill!" Mrs. Mallard answered, "Go away. I am not making myself ill." She was, in truth, drinking in a very elixir of life through the open window.
reading.cn: 约瑟芬跪在那扇锁着的门外。"路易丝，开门！你会把自己折腾出病来的！"马拉德太太答道："走开。我没有把自己折腾出病。"实际上，她正透过那扇敞开的窗户，畅饮着生命的甘露。
reading.note: Direct speech contrast + 'very elixir of life' — narrator's metaphor blending with her POV

reading.en: She rose at last and opened the door. Her sister was looking up at her, frightened. The two of them descended the stairs together. Richards, her husband's friend, stood waiting at the bottom — and the front door opened.
reading.cn: 她终于站起身，打开了门。妹妹仰头看着她，神情惊恐。两人一同下了楼。她丈夫的朋友理查兹在楼下等着——这时，前门开了。
reading.note: Sequence of action — narrative tension

reading.en: It was Brently Mallard who entered, a little travel-stained, a suitcase in hand. He had not been near the accident. He did not even know about it. Josephine cried out. Richards moved to shield him. But Mrs. Mallard saw him first — and fell. The doctors said she had died of heart disease — of the joy that kills.
reading.cn: 走进来的，正是布伦特利·马拉德——风尘仆仆，手里提着一只箱子。他根本没去过事故现场附近。他甚至都不知道有这事。约瑟芬叫出声来。理查兹动作要挡住他。可马拉德太太先看到他——倒下了。医生们说，她是心脏病发作而死——是被喜悦杀死的。
reading.note: Closing — cleft 'It was Brently who...' (review L52) + ironic final line

vocab.example_cn: 靠在落满灰尘的窗帘上。

vocab.example: If she could only find the courage.
vocab.example_cn: 只要她能找到那点勇气。

vocab.example: She had been keeping that promise.
The same tune was being played.
Frank was waiting beyond the gate.
vocab.example_cn: 弗兰克在闸门那边等着。

vocab.example: It was paralysis that had won.

reading.en: Sitting at the window, Eveline watched the evening invade the avenue. Her head leaned against the dusty curtains. She was tired. Frank was coming to take her away — if she could only find the courage.
reading.cn: 伊芙琳坐在窗前，看着傍晚一寸寸侵进街道。她的头靠在落满灰尘的窗帘上。她很累。弗兰克要来带她离开——只要她能找到那点勇气。
reading.note: Sitting at... — participial opener (L51 review)

reading.en: It was Buenos Aires that Frank had spoken of, a city across the sea. Were she to leave with him, she would have a new home, a husband, a life. Were she to stay, she would have her father's drinking and her mother's promise.
reading.cn: 弗兰克说起的是布宜诺斯艾利斯，一座海那边的城。要是她跟他走，她就有新家、丈夫、人生。要是她留下，就只剩父亲的酗酒和母亲的承诺。
reading.note: It was Buenos Aires that... — cleft (L52) / Were she to... — inverted 2nd conditional (L53)

reading.en: Her mother had made her promise — there in the dim room, the light fading — to keep the home together as long as she could. Eveline had promised. She had been keeping that promise for seven years.
reading.cn: 她母亲曾让她发誓——在那间昏暗的屋里，光线一点点暗下去——只要她还撑得住，就把这个家撑住。伊芙琳答应了。这誓言她已经守了七年。
reading.note: had made + had been keeping — past perfect chain (L48 review)

reading.en: Now she heard a street organ playing. The same tune was being played the night her mother died. "Damn the Italian wretches who came over here!" her father had shouted, throwing them a coin. Tonight she heard it again — the same melancholy air.
reading.cn: 现在她听到一阵街头风琴的声音。母亲去世那夜，弹的也是这一支曲子。"该死的从国外跑来的意大利人！"她父亲那时喊着，扔给了他们一枚硬币。今夜她又听见了——同一支忧伤的调子。
reading.note: Past continuous passive (was being played) + reported speech direct

reading.en: If she stayed, she thought, she would die in this house, like her mother had done — slowly, of life turned inward. The years she could see, all of them dim. The years she might have abroad — those, she could not picture clearly.
reading.cn: 她想，要是留下，她就会死在这屋子里，像母亲那样——慢慢地，因生活向内塌陷而死。她看得见的那些岁月，都很黯淡。她在海外可能拥有的岁月——那些，她想象不清楚。
reading.note: If she stayed, she thought, she would die... — mixed conditional + free indirect (L53 + L54 review)

reading.en: She rose. Holding her ticket in one hand, her bag in the other, she walked toward the dock. Frank was waiting beyond the gate. "Come!" he called, his face bright. "Come!"
reading.cn: 她站起来。一手拿着船票，一手提着包，走向码头。弗兰克在闸门那边等着。"过来！"他喊，脸上发亮。"过来！"
reading.note: Holding... — participial absolute (L51 review)

reading.en: Standing at the gate, she gripped the iron railing. Never had her hands felt so cold. Not once did her feet move forward. Bells rang. The ship was about to leave.
reading.cn: 她站在闸门前，紧紧攥住铁栏杆。她的手从未这么凉过。她的脚一下也没朝前迈。钟声响起。船就要开了。
reading.note: Standing... — participial / Never had... + Not once did... — negative inversion (L51 + L52 review)

reading.en: "Eveline! Evvy!" Frank cried, again and again. He was pulled toward the gate by the moving crowd. Were she to follow, even now, she might still make it.
reading.cn: "伊芙琳！伊芙！"弗兰克一遍遍喊。他被涌动的人潮推向闸门。如果她现在跟上去，也许还赶得上。
reading.note: Were she to follow... — inverted 2nd conditional (L53 review)

reading.en: But she gave him no sign — no wave, no word. Her white face stared back at him as if at a stranger. He passed beyond. The ship sailed. She stood there, motionless, neither saving herself nor saying goodbye. It was paralysis that had won.
reading.cn: 可她没给他任何表示——没挥手，没说话。她苍白的脸望着他，像望一个陌生人。他过去了。船开了。她站在那里，一动不动，既没救自己，也没告别。胜的是瘫痪。
reading.note: Closing — It was X that... — cleft (L52 review)

vocab.example: Why will you say that I am mad?
Observe how calmly I can tell you.
vocab.example_cn: 看我能多平静地讲给你听。
念头一出，便日夜缠着我。

vocab.example: It haunted me day and night.
His eye resembled that of a vulture.
I fancied a ringing in my ears.
With what dissimulation I went to work!
I shone a ray of lantern-light upon his eye.
vocab.example_cn: 我把灯笼光打在他眼上。

reading.en: True! nervous, very, very dreadfully nervous I had been and am. But why will you say that I am mad? Listen — observe how calmly, how healthily I can tell you the whole story.
reading.cn: 没错！我紧张，非常、非常可怕地紧张过，现在仍然紧张。可你为什么偏说我疯了？听着——你看我能多平静、多正常地把整件事讲给你听。
reading.note: True! — emphatic interjection / 'very, very dreadfully' — repetition for emphasis (KEY focus)

reading.en: It is impossible to say how the idea first entered my brain — but, once conceived, it haunted me day and night. I loved the old man. He had never wronged me. He had never given me insult. But there was his eye — yes, it was his eye!
reading.cn: 我说不清这念头是怎么钻进我脑子里的——但一旦冒出来，便日夜缠着我。我爱那位老人。他从没害过我。从没冒犯过我。但他有那只眼睛——对，就是那只眼睛！
reading.note: Past perfect (had wronged) + emphatic repetition ('his eye — yes, it was his eye!')

reading.en: One of his eyes resembled that of a vulture — a pale blue eye, with a film over it. Whenever it fell upon me, my blood ran cold. Slowly, very slowly — I made up my mind to take the life of the old man, and rid myself of the eye for ever.
reading.cn: 他的一只眼睛像秃鹫的——苍蓝色，覆着一层翳。每当那只眼落在我身上，我的血就发凉。慢慢地，非常慢——我下定决心要取那位老人的性命，永远摆脱那只眼。
reading.note: Slowly, very slowly — adverb repetition for pacing (KEY focus)

reading.en: Now this is the point — you fancy me mad. Madmen know nothing. But you should have seen me. You should have seen how wisely I proceeded — with what caution, with what foresight, with what dissimulation I went to work!
reading.cn: 听好——你以为我疯了。疯子什么都不懂。可你真该看看我。真该看看我是多么聪明地动手——多么谨慎、多么有远见、多么会掩饰！
reading.note: should have seen — modal perfect (L44 review) + 'with what... with what... with what...' — anaphora (KEY focus)

reading.en: For seven nights I opened the old man's door — slowly, slowly, just enough to put my head in. And every night I shone a single ray of lantern-light upon his eye. Every night the eye was closed. The eye was the offense, not the man.
reading.cn: 整整七夜，我都打开那位老人的房门——慢慢地、慢慢地，刚好够把头探进去。每一夜，我都把一束灯笼光打在他的眼上。每一夜，那只眼都是闭着的。冒犯我的是那只眼，不是那个人。
reading.note: Past simple narrative + repetition ('every night... every night...')

reading.en: On the eighth night, the eye was open — open and looking at me. Fury seized me. I rushed in. I dragged him to the floor. In an instant, it was done. The old man was dead.
reading.cn: 第八夜，那只眼睁开了——睁开着，看着我。狂怒攫住了我。我冲了进去。把他拽倒在地。一瞬间，事情就完了。老人死了。
reading.note: Sequence of short sentences — Poe's escalation technique

reading.en: I dismembered the body. I hid it under the floorboards. So cleverly had I done my work that no human eye — not even his — could have detected anything wrong. At four o'clock, the police came. I led them through the house, calm as a stone.
reading.cn: 我把尸体处理了。我藏在地板下。我做得如此巧妙，连人的眼睛——甚至他的——也察觉不出任何不对。凌晨四点，警察来了。我领他们走过整间屋子，镇定得像块石头。
reading.note: So cleverly had I done... — so + adverb inversion (L52 review)

reading.en: We sat. They chatted. But after a while, my head began to ache, and I fancied a ringing in my ears. It was a low, dull, quick sound — much like a watch makes when wrapped in cotton. I knew that sound. It grew louder — louder — louder. Why would they not be gone?
reading.cn: 我们坐下。他们闲聊。可没多久，我的头开始痛，我觉得耳朵里有一阵嗡鸣。那是一种低沉、闷哑、急促的声响——很像怀表用棉花裹住时的声音。我认得这声音。它越响越大——越响越大——越响越大。他们怎么还不走？
reading.note: Repetition 'louder — louder — louder' (KEY focus) + free indirect (Why would they not be gone?)

reading.en: "Villains!" I shrieked. "Dissemble no more! I admit the deed! Tear up the planks! — here, here! — it is the beating of his hideous heart!" — and I had betrayed myself by the tell-tale heart that was, all along, my own.
reading.cn: "恶棍！"我尖叫。"别再装了！我承认！撬开地板！——这里，这里！——是他那颗可憎的心还在跳！"——我被那颗告密的心出卖了，而那颗心，从头到尾，是我自己的。
reading.note: Closing — repetition ('here, here!') + final irony

vocab.example: An unlit cigar in his mouth.
vocab.example_cn: 嘴里叼着一支没点燃的雪茄。

vocab.example: A slow, plain sort of fellow.
vocab.example_cn: 一个慢吞吞、不起眼的家伙。

vocab.example: Be the one to amount to something.

reading.en: The policeman walked his beat as midnight approached. The wind was cold, the streets nearly empty. While most citizens were home asleep, he was still on duty.
reading.cn: 午夜将近，警察走着他的巡逻线。风很冷，街上几乎没人。当大多数市民都在家睡觉时，他还在值勤。
reading.note: While + clause — contrast of simultaneous states (KEY focus)

reading.en: In a darkened doorway stood a man, an unlit cigar in his mouth. As the policeman approached, the man spoke quickly. "It's all right, officer — I'm waiting for a friend. Twenty years ago tonight, I had dinner here with my best friend, Jimmy."
reading.cn: 一个昏暗的门洞里站着一个人，嘴里叼着一支没点燃的雪茄。警察走近时，那人迅速开口。"没事，警官——我在等一个朋友。二十年前的今晚，我和我最好的朋友吉米在这里吃过饭。"
reading.note: In a darkened doorway stood... — fronted adverbial inversion (L52 review)

reading.en: "We made a pact," Bob continued, striking a match. "No matter where life took us, we would meet right here, twenty years to the night. Jimmy stayed in New York. I went West."
reading.cn: "我们立了个誓，"鲍勃接着说，划亮一根火柴。"不管人生把我们带到哪里，二十年后的这一晚，我们都要回到这儿见面。吉米留在了纽约。我去了西部。"
reading.note: striking a match — present participle (L51 review)

reading.en: By the light of the match, the policeman saw a face — a man with sharp, pale eyes and a small white scar near the right eyebrow. While Bob talked happily of his Western fortune, the officer's expression had changed. But Bob, glowing with anticipation, did not notice.
reading.cn: 火柴的光照在那人的脸上——一双锐利的、苍白的眼睛，右眉边一道细细的白色伤疤。当鲍勃兴致勃勃地讲他在西部发家的事时，警察的神情已经变了。可鲍勃满怀期待，没注意到。
reading.note: While Bob talked... — contrast clause / glowing with anticipation — participial (L51 review)

reading.en: "I made it big in the West," Bob said. "Money, business, everything. Jimmy was a slow, plain sort of fellow — by comparison, I always thought I'd be the one to amount to something."
reading.cn: "我在西部干出了大名堂，"鲍勃说。"钱、生意，什么都有。吉米是个慢吞吞、不起眼的家伙——比起来，我一直觉得能有出息的会是我。"
reading.note: By comparison... — contrast preposition (KEY focus)

reading.en: The policeman wished Bob luck and walked on. Twenty minutes later, another man approached the doorway, in a long overcoat, collar turned up. "Bob, is that you?" he asked. "Jimmy!" Bob cried. They shook hands warmly.
reading.cn: 警察祝鲍勃好运，便走开了。二十分钟后，另一个人走近门洞，穿着长大衣，领子翻起来。"鲍勃，是你吗？"他问。"吉米！"鲍勃喊。两人热情地握了手。
reading.note: Sequence of action — narrative continuity

reading.en: Walking arm in arm, the two men crossed the street, talking of old times. Whereas Bob spoke loudly and laughed often, the other man was quiet, glancing sideways from time to time.
reading.cn: 两人挽着胳膊穿过街，聊着过去的事。鲍勃声音洪亮、时不时大笑，而另一人却很安静，时不时朝侧面瞥一眼。
reading.note: Whereas + clause — formal contrast (KEY focus)

reading.en: Beneath a streetlamp, Bob looked closely at the man for the first time. He stopped walking. "You're not Jimmy," he said slowly. "Jimmy had a Roman nose. Yours is a pug nose. In contrast to him, you're —" He froze.
reading.cn: 在一盏路灯下，鲍勃第一次仔细看了那人一眼。他停下脚步。"你不是吉米，"他慢慢说。"吉米是罗马鼻。你的是塌鼻子。和他比起来，你——"他僵住了。
reading.note: In contrast to him... — contrast preposition (KEY focus)

reading.en: The man pulled out a badge. "You're under arrest, Bob. Chicago wired us. Jimmy Wells was the policeman you spoke with twenty minutes ago. He recognized you when you struck the match. Unlike a stranger, he could not arrest you himself. He left a note." The note read: "Bob, I was at the appointed place on time. — Jimmy."
reading.cn: 那人掏出警徽。"你被捕了，鲍勃。芝加哥发了电报。吉米·韦尔斯就是二十分钟前和你说话的那个警察。你划火柴时他认出了你。和一个陌生人不同的是，他没法亲自逮捕你。他留下了一张纸条。"纸条上写着："鲍勃，我准时到了约定的地方。——吉米。"
reading.note: Unlike a stranger... — contrast preposition (KEY focus) + closing aphorism

vocab.example_cn: 我和许多亲戚住在一起。
我们会做三十个水果蛋糕。
我们一整年都在攒硬币。

vocab.example: Coins from cutting flowers for funerals.
He had once tipped his hat to her.
vocab.example_cn: 他有一次冲她抬过帽子。

vocab.example: They sent the news in a telegram.
vocab.example_cn: 他们用电报送来了消息。

reading.en: When I was seven, I lived in a country house in Alabama with many cousins. But the only cousin who really knew me was a sixty-year-old woman who used to tell me her name was 'my friend.' She was small and round, with sun-bleached white hair and bright eyes.
reading.cn: 我七岁那年，住在阿拉巴马一栋乡下房子里，亲戚很多。但唯一真正懂我的，是一位六十多岁的老妇人，她以前总告诉我她的名字就叫'我的朋友'。她个头小、圆圆的，头发被太阳晒得发白，眼睛却很亮。
reading.note: used to + V — habitual past for ENDED state (KEY focus)

reading.en: Every November, she would announce to me: 'It's fruitcake weather.' That meant we would make thirty fruitcakes — for strangers. We had not met most of them. We never would.
reading.cn: 每年十一月，她都会对我宣布：'是水果蛋糕的天气了。'那意味着我们要做三十个水果蛋糕——为陌生人做。我们大多数人都没见过。我们也永远不会见到。
reading.note: would + V — habitual past for REPEATED action (KEY focus)

reading.en: We would save coins all year — coins from selling jellies, coins from cutting flowers for funerals, coins from mowing yards. By November, our savings, in a box under her bed, would always be just enough for the candied fruit, the flour, the whiskey.
reading.cn: 我们一整年都在攒硬币——卖果酱攒下的硬币，给葬礼剪花得的硬币，替人剪草坪挣的硬币。到十一月，藏在她床下盒子里的存款，总是刚好够买蜜饯、面粉、威士忌。
reading.note: would save + would always be — habitual past chain

reading.en: Each year we would walk to Mr. Haha's bar to buy the whiskey. We were both afraid of him. But every year he would not charge us. "Children," he would say to her, "pay me with one of those cakes."
reading.cn: 每年我们都会走到哈哈先生的酒馆买威士忌。我们两个都怕他。可每年他都不收我们的钱。"孩子们，"他会对她说，"用一个蛋糕抵我吧。"
reading.note: would walk + would not charge + would say — habitual past dialogue framing

reading.en: Once the cakes were finished, we would post them off to people we had only read about: President Roosevelt, the missionary in Borneo, a bus driver who had once tipped his hat to her.
reading.cn: 蛋糕做好后，我们就把它们寄给那些我们只在新闻里读到过的人：罗斯福总统、婆罗洲的传教士、有一次冲她抬过帽子的公交车司机。
reading.note: would post — habitual past for the annual ritual

reading.en: Once a year, also, we would cut down our own Christmas tree from the woods. She used to drag it home herself, while I, only seven, helped pull. We used to hang on it the same things every year — silver paper, pine cones, things made by hand.
reading.cn: 每年也有一次，我们会自己到林子里砍圣诞树。她以前总是亲自把树拖回家，我才七岁，帮着拉。我们以前每年都挂同样的东西——银纸、松果、手做的小玩意儿。
reading.note: would cut + used to drag + used to hang — combined habitual past

reading.en: And we would dance — she and I — around the tree, with her old gramophone playing. She did not know any modern songs. She used to sing the ones she had learned as a girl.
reading.cn: 我们会跳舞——她和我——围着树跳，她那台老留声机响着。她不会唱新歌。她过去一直唱她小时候学过的那些。
reading.note: would dance + used to sing — emotional habitual

reading.en: Then they sent me away to military school. I would write to her. She would write back, in long, slow letters, in her childish hand. Each letter would tell me what the weather was, what Queenie the dog was doing, when the fruitcake season had begun.
reading.cn: 后来他们把我送到了军事学校。我会给她写信。她也会回信，长长的、慢慢的信，是她那像小孩子一样的笔迹。每封信都告诉我天气怎么样，狗 Queenie 在干什么，水果蛋糕的季节什么时候开始了。
reading.note: would write + would write back + would tell — habitual letter exchange

reading.en: She died one November morning. I was at school. They sent the news in a telegram. I have never gone home for Christmas since. But every November — even now — when the air turns cold, I still expect a telegram from her: 'It's fruitcake weather.'
reading.cn: 她在一个十一月的早晨去世了。我在学校。他们用电报送来了消息。从那以后我再没回家过圣诞节。可每年十一月——即使现在——空气一变冷，我仍然在等她的一封电报：'是水果蛋糕的天气了。'
reading.note: Closing — narrator's adult voice, present perfect ('have never gone') + present (still expect)

vocab.example_cn: 一根绳子套在他脖子上。
安排看起来算是利落的。

vocab.example: The soldier kicked the plank away.
He stepped forward to embrace her.
A blinding light blazed about him.
vocab.example_cn: 刺目的光在他四周炸开。

reading.en: A man stood upon a railroad bridge in northern Alabama, looking down into the swift water below. His hands were tied behind him. A rope closely encircled his neck. He appeared to be about thirty-five years old.
reading.cn: 一个男人站在阿拉巴马北部一座铁路桥上，朝下看着桥下的急流。他的双手被反绑在身后。一根绳子紧紧套在他的脖子上。他看上去三十五岁左右。
reading.note: appeared to be — hedging for observed but uncertain age (KEY focus)

reading.en: He was, it seemed, a planter — a man of the kind that one might call a gentleman of the South. The arrangements for the hanging seemed efficient, though not, perhaps, kind.
reading.cn: 他似乎是个种植园主——也许可以说，是南方人称作的那种绅士。绞刑的安排看起来算是利落的——尽管，或许说不上仁慈。
reading.note: it seemed / one might call / seemed... though, perhaps — multiple hedges (KEY focus)

reading.en: Below, the swift water tended to throw foam against the wooden piles. As the soldier kicked the plank away, the planter dropped — and seemed, at that very moment, to feel the rope snap.
reading.cn: 下方，急流不断把泡沫拍向木桩。当士兵把木板踢开时，那位种植园主跌了下去——而就在那一刻，他似乎感觉到绳子断了。
reading.note: tended to + V — habitual probability / seemed to + V — sensory hedge

reading.en: Free, it seemed, of the rope, he plunged into the water below. He could feel the icy cold around him. Bullets whistled past, but they appeared to slow as they approached him — as though the air itself were thicker.
reading.cn: 看起来挣脱了绳子，他扑进下面的水里。他能感觉到周围冰冷的水。子弹嗖嗖飞过，可它们靠近他时似乎慢了下来——仿佛空气本身都变厚了。
reading.note: appeared to slow / as though + past subjunctive — strong hedging

reading.en: It is likely that, in such moments, perception itself becomes strange. The planter felt that hours had passed when, perhaps, only seconds had. He would later recall the colors of stones at the river bottom — although, of course, no one ever does.
reading.cn: 在这样的时刻，知觉本身大概会变得奇怪。这位种植园主觉得已经过去了好几个小时，可也许只过了几秒。他后来回忆起河底石头的颜色——尽管，当然了，没人真的能做到这个。
reading.note: It is likely that... / perhaps / would later recall — heavy academic hedging

reading.en: He seemed to swim ashore. He seemed to walk through a forest, all night. By dawn he could see, far away, the white face of his own house. His wife, it appeared, was waiting at the gate. She held out her arms.
reading.cn: 他似乎游上了岸。他似乎在林子里走了整整一夜。天亮时，他远远地看见了自家的白色房屋。他的妻子，看起来正在门口等他。她伸出手臂。
reading.note: seemed to + V chain — sustained hedging that something is wrong

reading.en: He stepped forward to embrace her. At that very instant, however, he seemed to feel a stunning blow upon the back of the neck. A blinding white light blazed all about him, with a sound like the shock of a cannon.
reading.cn: 他迈步上前要拥抱她。然而就在那一刻，他似乎感觉到后颈被狠狠击了一下。一道刺目的白光在他四周炸开，像炮声一样。
reading.note: however — discourse marker (preview L61) + seemed to + V — final hedge before reveal
