reading.en: The planter was dead. His body, with a broken neck, swung gently from side to side beneath the timbers of the Owl Creek bridge. Everything between the kicking of the plank and this moment had, in all likelihood, taken less than a single second.
reading.cn: 那位种植园主死了。他的身体颈骨已断，在猫头鹰溪桥的木梁下轻轻地左右摆动。从木板被踢开到这一刻之间发生的一切——很可能不过是一秒钟以内的事。
reading.note: in all likelihood — strong probability hedge / final reveal

reading.en: It seems that the human mind, when faced with sudden death, may invent an entire life. Whether such an experience would feel real to the dying — that is something we cannot, perhaps, ever fully know.
reading.cn: 看来，人在面对突如其来的死亡时，心灵也许会编造出一整段人生。这样的体验对濒死者是否会显得真实——这或许是我们永远无法完全知晓的事。
reading.note: Closing — It seems that... / Whether... — academic hedging cluster

vocab.example: Mrs. White would knit by the lamp.
vocab.example_cn: 怀特太太会在灯下织毛衣。
看上去是个平常的夜晚。

vocab.example: He put a spell on it.
He snatched it out of the fire.

vocab.example_cn: 他半开玩笑地举起猴爪。

vocab.example: The paw twisted in his hand.
Humming a tune, he went off.

vocab.meaning: v. 摸索；笨手笨脚地找

reading.en: On a cold, wet night, the White family used to sit by the fire after supper. Mr. White would play chess with his son Herbert. Mrs. White would knit by the lamp. It seemed an ordinary evening — like a hundred others.
reading.cn: 在一个寒冷潮湿的夜晚，怀特一家以前总是吃完晚饭后坐在炉火旁。怀特先生会和儿子赫伯特下棋。怀特太太会在灯下织毛衣。这看上去和平常无异——和过去一百个夜晚一样。
reading.note: used to + would — habitual past (L58 review) / It seemed — hedge (L59 review)

reading.en: There came a knock at the door. Sergeant-Major Morris, just back from India, came in. Whereas Mr. White had stayed in this quiet village all his life, his old friend had traveled the world.
reading.cn: 门口响起敲门声。刚从印度回来的莫里斯军士长走了进来。怀特先生一辈子待在这个安静的村子里，而他的老友走过了大半个世界。
reading.note: Whereas — formal contrast (L57 review)

reading.en: After dinner, Morris pulled from his pocket a small dried paw. "It is a monkey's paw," he said. "An old fakir put a spell on it — three men, three wishes. The first man's last wish was for death. By comparison, my own three wishes left me wishing I had never made them."
reading.cn: 饭后，莫里斯从口袋里掏出一只小小的干瘪猴爪。"这是一只猴爪，"他说。"一个老法基尔在上面下了咒——三个人，三个愿望。第一个人的最后一个愿是想死。比起来，我自己许的三个愿，让我希望从来没许过。"
reading.note: By comparison — contrast (L57) + I had never made them — past perfect counterfactual

reading.en: Morris threw the paw into the fire. Mr. White, however, snatched it out. "Don't!" cried Morris. "If you must wish, wish for something sensible." But Mr. White, laughing, would not let it go.
reading.cn: 莫里斯把猴爪扔进火里。可怀特先生却把它抢了出来。"别！"莫里斯喊。"要是你非要许愿，就许个明智点的吧。"可怀特先生笑着，怎么也不肯放下。
reading.note: however — discourse marker (preview L61) + would not — habitual refusal (L58)

reading.en: After Morris left, Herbert suggested: "Wish for two hundred pounds, Father — just enough to clear the house." Mr. White, half-mocking, raised the paw. "I wish for two hundred pounds," he said. The paw — slowly, very slowly — twisted in his hand. He cried out and dropped it.
reading.cn: 莫里斯走后，赫伯特提议："许个两百英镑吧，爸——刚好够把房子的债还清。"怀特先生半开玩笑地举起猴爪。"我希望得到两百英镑，"他说。猴爪——慢慢地、非常慢地——在他手里扭动了一下。他叫了一声，把它扔了。
reading.note: slowly, very slowly — adverb repetition (L56 review)

reading.en: Nothing happened that night. The next morning, Herbert went off to work — humming a tune, never to return. By afternoon, a stranger stood at their gate. Whereas they had hoped for normal news, the man's face told them otherwise.
reading.cn: 那一夜什么也没发生。第二天早上，赫伯特哼着小曲去上班了——再没回来。下午，一个陌生人站在他们家门口。他们盼着是平常的消息，可那人的脸告诉他们并非如此。
reading.note: never to return — purpose/result infinitive / Whereas — contrast (L57)

reading.en: "There has been an accident at the factory," he said. "Your son was caught in the machinery." It seemed, the stranger added, the company was prepared to offer compensation. The compensation was two hundred pounds.
reading.cn: "工厂里出了事故，"他说。"您儿子被卷进了机器里。"看起来，他补充道，公司愿意支付一笔赔偿。赔偿金是两百英镑。
reading.note: It seemed — hedging (L59) + ironic 200 pounds reveal

reading.en: After the funeral, Mrs. White could not stop crying. One night, days later, she rose suddenly. 'The paw!' she cried. 'Wish him alive again!' Mr. White begged her not to. But she would not be reasoned with. He used the second wish.
reading.cn: 葬礼之后，怀特太太一直哭。几天后的一个夜里，她突然坐了起来。'猴爪！'她喊。'许愿让他活过来！'怀特先生求她别这么做。可她怎么也劝不动。他许下了第二个愿望。
reading.note: would not be reasoned with — habitual refusal passive

reading.en: Slowly — slowly — slowly — there came a knock at the door. Mrs. White ran to open it. Mr. White, however, fumbled for the paw and made the third, final wish. The knocking stopped. When she opened the door, the road was empty. Quite empty.
reading.cn: 慢慢——慢慢——慢慢地——门口响起了敲门声。怀特太太跑去开门。可怀特先生摸索着抓起猴爪，许下了第三个、也是最后一个愿望。敲门声停了。她打开门时，路上空空如也。空荡荡的。
reading.note: Closing — slowly slowly slowly — repetition (L56 review) + however — contrast

vocab.example: A staff that resembled a serpent.
A figure stood at the altar.
No hopeful verse upon his stone.
vocab.example_cn: 墓碑上没有充满希望的铭文。
他临终的那一刻只剩阴郁。

reading.en: Young Goodman Brown set out at sunset on an errand into the forest. His wife, whose name was Faith, begged him to stay. Nevertheless, he kissed her goodbye and stepped onto the dark path.
reading.cn: 年轻的古德曼·布朗在日落时出发，去林子里办一件事。他的妻子名叫菲斯（Faith），求他留下。然而，他还是吻别了她，踏上了那条幽暗的小路。
reading.note: Nevertheless — formal concession adverb (KEY focus)

reading.en: In the forest he met a traveler — a man who looked, oddly, very much like himself, only older. "You are late, Goodman Brown," the man said. "I have been waiting." Brown answered that his wife, Faith, had kept him. The traveler, however, only smiled.
reading.cn: 林子里他遇到一位行路人——奇怪的是，那人长得很像他自己，只是年长一些。"古德曼·布朗，你来晚了，"那人说。"我等了一阵了。"布朗答说，他的妻子菲斯耽搁了他。那行路人，然而，只是笑了笑。
reading.note: however — discourse marker mid-clause (KEY focus)

reading.en: They walked deeper into the woods. The traveler showed Brown a staff that resembled a black serpent. Furthermore, he claimed to have known Brown's father and grandfather — both, he said, had walked this path before. "It cannot be true," said Brown. "My ancestors were holy men."
reading.cn: 他们朝林子深处走去。行路人给布朗看一根酷似黑蛇的手杖。此外，他声称认识布朗的父亲和祖父——他说，两人都走过这条路。"这不可能，"布朗说。"我的先辈都是虔诚的人。"
reading.note: Furthermore — addition connector (KEY focus)

reading.en: They came to a clearing where, on every side, the figures of the village pressed close: deacons, ministers, his old catechism teacher. Indeed, the very people Brown thought most pious were gathered there. Moreover, he saw his wife Faith's pink ribbon caught on a branch — and his heart, accordingly, broke.
reading.cn: 他们走到一片林间空地。空地四周，村里的人挤了过来：执事、牧师、他从前的教义老师。实际上，那些他以为最虔诚的人，全聚在了这里。更糟的是，他看见妻子菲斯的粉色丝带挂在一根枝头——他的心，于是碎了。
reading.note: Indeed / Moreover / accordingly — three cohesion devices in close succession (KEY focus)

reading.en: "My Faith is gone!" he cried. "There is no good on earth — therefore, sin is all there is!" He laughed wildly and rushed forward into the heart of the gathering. The forest, in turn, seemed to laugh with him.
reading.cn: "菲斯走了！"他喊。"人间没有善——因此，罪就是一切！"他狂笑着冲进集会的中心。林子，反过来，也仿佛在跟他大笑。
reading.note: therefore — causal connector / in turn — sequencing connector

reading.en: A figure stood at the altar. The figure spoke. Whether what the figure said was real, Brown could not tell. Consequently, when he woke at dawn — alone in the cold forest — he could not say whether the night had been a dream or not.
reading.cn: 一个身影站在祭坛前。那身影开口了。它说的是不是真的，布朗辨不清。因此，当他在黎明独自醒来——在冷清的林子里——他无法判断那一夜究竟是不是一场梦。
reading.note: Consequently — formal cause-result connector (KEY focus)

reading.en: He returned to the village. Faith ran to greet him. He, nonetheless, drew back. The minister he passed in the street seemed, to him, no longer holy. Even the children's hymns sounded false. Thus the night had marked him.
reading.cn: 他回到村里。菲斯跑过来迎他。他，然而，退后了一步。他在街上经过的牧师，在他眼里，已不再神圣。连孩子们的圣歌听起来都是假的。这一夜，于是改变了他。
reading.note: nonetheless — formal concession (KEY focus) / Thus — formal result

reading.en: For the rest of his life, Brown walked among his neighbors as a stranger. He went to church; however, he heard no comfort there. He prayed; however, he expected no answer. Furthermore, when his wife smiled at him at table, he saw, instead of love, the face he had glimpsed in the forest.
reading.cn: 余生之中，布朗都像陌生人一样生活在邻里之间。他去教堂；可在那里听不到任何慰藉。他祷告；可不再期待回应。此外，当妻子在餐桌上对他微笑，他看见的不再是爱，而是那夜在林子里瞥见的脸。
reading.note: however / Furthermore — sustained discourse marker chain

reading.en: When at last Goodman Brown died, an old man, his neighbors carved no hopeful verse upon his stone. For his dying hour was gloom. Hence, the lesson: a single night of suspicion can poison a whole life — whether the night was real or not.
reading.cn: 古德曼·布朗最后老去并离世时，邻居没有在他的墓碑上刻上任何充满希望的铭文。因为他临终的那一刻只剩阴郁。由此可见，这则故事的寓意：一夜的猜疑，可以毒死一生——不管那一夜是不是真的。
reading.note: Closing — Hence — formal causal connector / final aphorism

vocab.example: Take that basket down to the woman.
vocab.example_cn: 把篮子送到那个女人那儿。

reading.en: And after all the weather was ideal. They could not have had a more perfect day for a garden-party. Windless, warm, the sky covered with golden haze — the kind of morning written about in poems.
reading.cn: 毕竟天气真是再好不过了。他们再也找不到比这更完美的一天来办花园派对。无风、温暖、天空覆着一层金色的薄雾——是诗里写的那种早晨。
reading.note: covered with — reduced from 'which was covered with' (KEY focus) / written about — reduced from 'which is written about'

reading.en: Workmen carrying poles and rolls of canvas appeared on the lawn, ready to put up the marquee. Laura, sent out by her mother to direct them, hurried across the grass holding a piece of bread and butter.
reading.cn: 几个扛着杆子和帆布卷的工人出现在草坪上，准备搭起遮阳棚。劳拉是被妈妈派出来安排他们的，她攥着一块涂了黄油的面包匆匆穿过草地。
reading.note: carrying poles... — reduced from 'who were carrying poles' / sent out by... — reduced from 'who had been sent out by'

reading.en: The man chosen to lead the workers had a friendly smile. The marquee, set up in the corner of the lawn, would face the garden's most splendid view: the karaka trees, heavy with their orange fruit.
reading.cn: 那个被选出来带队的工人，笑容很和气。那个搭在草坪一角的遮阳棚，正对着花园里最壮观的景：那几棵 karaka 树，挂满了橙红色的果实。
reading.note: chosen to lead... / set up in... / heavy with... — three reduced relatives (KEY focus)

reading.en: Just as Laura was finishing the arrangements, a woman, breathless and shaking, came running into the garden. The cottages just outside their gate, where the poorest workmen lived, had been the scene of a sudden death. A man, a carter known to everyone in the village, had been thrown from his horse that morning.
reading.cn: 劳拉刚把布置安排妥当，一个女人喘着气、发着抖跑进了花园。门外那一排住着最穷工人的小屋，刚刚发生了一桩突然的死亡。一个名叫卡特、村里人人都认识的赶车人，那天早上从马上摔了下来。
reading.note: breathless and shaking — reduced participial / known to everyone — reduced from 'who was known to'

reading.en: Laura, deeply shaken, ran to her mother. "We must stop the party," she said. "There is a man dead just down the road." Her mother, sitting at her dressing-table, only smiled. "Don't be absurd, my dear. People killed in such accidents are not part of our world."
reading.cn: 劳拉深受震动，跑去找母亲。"我们得停办派对，"她说。"路那头有人死了。"母亲，坐在梳妆台前，只是笑了笑。"别傻了，亲爱的。在那种事故里死掉的人，不属于我们的世界。"
reading.note: deeply shaken / sitting at her dressing-table / killed in such accidents — three reduced relatives

reading.en: The party went on. Guests arriving in white dresses and dark suits filled the lawn. The band, hired for the day, played from the veranda. Laura, given a new hat by her mother, was told she looked charming. She tried to forget the news brought from the cottage.
reading.cn: 派对继续。穿白裙、深色西装的客人陆续到来，挤满了草坪。当天雇来的乐队在游廊上演奏。母亲给劳拉戴了一顶新帽子，对她说她看起来真迷人。她努力想忘掉刚从那间小屋传来的消息。
reading.note: arriving in white dresses / hired for the day / given a new hat / brought from the cottage — chain of reductions

reading.en: When the party was over and the leftover food was being packed, Laura's mother had a sudden idea. 'Take that basket, full of sandwiches and cakes, down to the poor woman. It will comfort her.'
reading.cn: 派对结束、剩下的食物正被装起来时，劳拉的母亲忽然想到一个主意。"把那只装满三明治和蛋糕的篮子，送到那位可怜的女人家里去。会给她一些安慰。"
reading.note: full of sandwiches and cakes — reduced from 'which is full of'

reading.en: Laura, embarrassed and uncertain, walked down the lane. The cottage, dimmer than she had imagined, was full of people speaking in low voices. A woman, weeping silently, took her into a small room. There lay the dead man, his face turned to the pillow.
reading.cn: 劳拉又尴尬又不确定，走下那条小路。那间小屋比她想象的更昏暗，屋里挤满了低声说话的人。一个无声哭泣的女人把她引进一间小屋。死去的男人就躺在那里，脸朝向枕头。
reading.note: dimmer than she had imagined / speaking in low voices / weeping silently / turned to the pillow — multiple reductions

reading.en: Laura looked at the face. He seemed peaceful, far from her world. She wanted to say something — anything — but only one word came. "Forgive my hat." Walking home through the dusk, she met her brother. "Was it awful?" he asked. She tried to answer. "Isn't life — " she began. But she could not finish. He understood.
reading.cn: 劳拉看着那张脸。他看起来很安详，与她的世界相去甚远。她想说点什么——任何话都行——却只挤出一句。"原谅我这顶帽子。"她走在暮色里回家，路上碰见了哥哥。"很可怕吧？"他问。她想回答。"人生不是——"她开口。可她说不下去。他懂了。
reading.note: Closing — Walking home through the dusk — reduced participial / final ellipsis (preview L63)

vocab.example: The accused subject was on trial.

reading.en: Long ago there ruled a king who was, in his way, both progressive and barbaric. He had built an arena where, when an accused subject was on trial, justice was decided by chance. The king required that the accused stand alone before two doors.
reading.cn: 很久以前，有一位国王，他自有他那一套，既开明又野蛮。他建了一座竞技场，凡有臣民被控告，审判就靠机缘。这位国王要求被告独自站在两扇门前。
reading.note: It is required that + 主语 + V (原形) — formal subjunctive (KEY focus)

reading.en: Behind one door, it was insisted, there must always be a hungry tiger; behind the other, a beautiful lady. If the accused man chose the tiger door, he would be torn to pieces, his guilt thus proven. If he chose the lady, he would marry her on the spot — innocent, however unwilling.
reading.cn: 据说，一扇门后必定永远关着一只饿虎；另一扇门后则是位美女。要是被告挑了关老虎的门，他会被撕成碎片，罪名因此被证实。要是他挑了女子那扇门，他就当场和她成婚——清白，但也许并不情愿。
reading.note: It was insisted (that) + must always be — formal mandative subjunctive

reading.en: Now this king had a daughter, beloved beyond measure. She loved a young courtier — a man of low birth, far below her station. The king demanded that no such match be allowed. He commanded that the courtier be tried at once in the arena.
reading.cn: 这位国王有一个女儿，他爱她爱到极致。公主爱上了一位年轻廷臣——出身低微，远配不上她。国王要求绝不许这般婚事；他命令那廷臣立刻在竞技场受审。
reading.note: demanded that + V (原形) / commanded that + V (原形) — mandative subjunctive (KEY focus)

reading.en: On the appointed day, the courtier walked into the arena. Were he to choose the lady, his life would be saved — but he would belong to another. Were he to choose the tiger, he would die — but at least his princess would not have to watch him love a rival.
reading.cn: 约定的那天，廷臣走进了竞技场。如果他挑女子那扇门，他的命就保住了——但他会属于别人。如果他挑老虎那扇门，他会死——但至少公主不必看着他爱上情敌。
reading.note: Were he to choose... — inverted second conditional (L53 review)

reading.en: It was essential that the courtier know which door hid which fate. He looked up at the princess. Through her own secret efforts, she had learned what was behind each door. She made — at terrible cost — a small motion of her right hand.
reading.cn: 至关重要的是，那廷臣得知道哪扇门后藏着哪种命运。他抬头看公主。她凭着自己暗中查问，已经知道每扇门后是什么。她——付出了极大的代价——用右手微微做了一个动作。
reading.note: It was essential that + 主语 + V (原形) — mandative subjunctive (KEY focus)

reading.en: Now: which door did she signal? Consider what she knew. The lady behind the right-hand door was beautiful and known to her. The princess had often seen her, and had begun to suspect that the lady, too, was in love with the courtier.
reading.cn: 好——她示意了哪扇门？想想她知道什么。右边那扇门后的女子貌美，公主认得她。公主常常见到她，并开始怀疑那位女子也爱着廷臣。
reading.note: Consider what she knew — imperative + embedded question / had begun to suspect — past perfect (L48 review)

reading.en: If she had pointed to the lady, the courtier would have lived — but the princess would have watched her beloved married to a rival, perhaps loved by him in turn. If she had pointed to the tiger, the courtier would have died — but at least no one else would have him.
reading.cn: 如果她指了女子那扇门，廷臣便能活——但公主就要看着她心爱的人和情敌结婚，甚至可能反过来爱上对方。如果她指了老虎那扇门，廷臣便会死——但至少没有别的女人能拥有他。
reading.note: If she had + V-ed... would have V-ed — third conditional pair (L53 review)

reading.en: Were her love stronger than her jealousy, she would save him. Were her jealousy stronger than her love, she would not. The author insists that we, the readers, decide. He requires that each of us look into our own hearts and choose.
reading.cn: 假如她的爱比她的妒强，她就救他。假如她的妒比她的爱强，她就不救。作者坚持：让我们——读者——来定。他要求我们每一个人都向自己的心里看一眼，自行选择。
reading.note: Were her love stronger... — inverted second conditional / insists that... requires that... — mandative subjunctive cluster

reading.en: Which came out of the door — the lady, or the tiger? The answer depends on the reader. And so this story has no ending — only a question, asked of every heart that ever read it.
reading.cn: 门里出来的——是那位美女，还是那只老虎？答案取决于读者。所以这个故事没有结局——只有一个问题，问向每一个曾读过它的心。
reading.note: Closing — direct question + 'depends on the reader' — Stockton's famous open ending

vocab.example: He pressed his face to the window.

vocab.meaning: adj. 异国情调的；奇异的

vocab.example: He came home late and drunk.
Most of the stalls had closed.

vocab.example_cn: 一只被虚荣驱赶的造物。

reading.en: North Richmond Street was quiet in the long winter evenings. Behind one of the houses lived a boy who, every morning, would press his face to the window and watch his friend Mangan's older sister come out to call her brother in.
reading.cn: 在漫长的冬夜里，北里士满街很安静。一栋房子里住着一个男孩，他每天早上都把脸贴在窗上，看着他朋友曼根的姐姐出来叫弟弟回家。
reading.note: would press — habitual past (L58 review)

reading.en: He did not know her well — he had only spoken with her a few times. Yet her image accompanied him even in places most hostile to romance. I wish I could speak to her, he often thought. If only I had something to say.
reading.cn: 他并不了解她——他只和她说过几次话。可她的形象，却跟着他进入最不浪漫的场合。'我多想和她说说话，'他常常这样想。'要是我能找到话说就好了。'
reading.note: I wish I could + V — wish for present ability (KEY focus) / If only + past — present regret (KEY focus)

reading.en: One evening, at last, she spoke to him. "Are you going to Araby?" she asked. Araby was the name of a Saturday-night bazaar — exotic, far away. He said yes, although he had not planned to. "I wish I could go," she said softly. "But I cannot."
reading.cn: 终于，有一天傍晚，她对他开了口。"你要去阿拉比吗？"她问。阿拉比是一家周六夜里的市集——异国情调，遥远。他说要去，其实他根本没打算。"我多想去，"她轻声说。"可是我去不了。"
reading.note: I wish I could + V — wish about a present situation she can't change

reading.en: The boy promised — almost without thinking — to bring her something. From that night, the bazaar became the center of his life. Days passed. He waited. The whole house felt thin and empty. If only Saturday would come, he thought. I wish my uncle would come home with the money he had promised.
reading.cn: 男孩——几乎不假思索——答应给她带点东西回来。从那一夜起，那个市集成了他生活的中心。日子一天天过去。他等着。整栋房子都显得稀薄而空荡。'要是星期六能来就好了，'他想。'真希望叔叔能带着他答应的钱回家。'
reading.note: If only + would — wish for future change (KEY focus) / I wish ... would — wish for someone else's future action

reading.en: Saturday came. His uncle, however, came home late and drunk. The boy waited in the dark hall. "What are you sitting there for?" his aunt asked. "I forgot," his uncle muttered. "Take this — go." The boy took the money. By the time the train reached Araby, it was almost ten.
reading.cn: 星期六到了。然而叔叔回来晚了，又喝醉了。男孩在漆黑的厅里等。"你坐在这儿干嘛？"姑姑问。"我忘了，"叔叔嘟哝着。"拿着——去吧。"男孩拿了钱。火车开到阿拉比时，已经快十点。
reading.note: By the time + past simple, past simple — review L48 (past perfect)

reading.en: He walked through the great dim hall. Most of the stalls had closed. He had pictured a bazaar of light and music — instead, he found two men counting money on a tray and a young lady, English-accented, flirting with a customer.
reading.cn: 他穿过那座空旷昏暗的大厅。大多数摊位已经关了。他原本以为这里会是一个充满灯光与音乐的市集——可他看到的是两个男人在托盘上数钱，一个带英国口音的姑娘正在和一个顾客调情。
reading.note: had pictured / had closed — past perfect (L48 review) / instead — discourse marker (L61 review)

reading.en: He stood at one stall, looking at vases. The young lady asked, without much interest, whether he wanted to buy. He said no, almost without breath. He turned. Walking back through the empty hall, he thought: I wish I had not come. If only I had not made the promise. I would rather have stayed at home.
reading.cn: 他站在一个摊位前，看着花瓶。那位姑娘没什么兴致地问他要不要买。他几乎喘不过气地说不要。他转身。穿过那个空荡的厅走回去时，他想："真希望我没来。要是我没许下那个承诺就好了。我宁愿留在家里。"
reading.note: I wish + past perfect — wish about past (KEY focus) / If only + past perfect — past regret / I would rather have V-ed — preferred past (KEY focus)

reading.en: He looked up into the darkness. He saw himself as a creature driven and derided by vanity — and his eyes burned with anguish and anger. The girl, the bazaar, the gift — he wished, now, that none of it had ever mattered to him.
reading.cn: 他抬头望进黑暗。他看见自己是一个被虚荣驱赶、又被虚荣讥嘲的小动物——他的眼里燃着愤怒和羞愧。那个姑娘、那个市集、那件礼物——此刻他多么希望，这些从来都没在他心里有过分量。
reading.note: Free indirect (L54 review) + I wished that + past perfect — wish about past

reading.en: He wished he were older. He wished he had not given the girl the place she held in his mind. He wished, most of all, that he had been wiser sooner. But the lights were going off above him. He stood alone in the darkening hall, ashamed of his own hopes.
reading.cn: 他多希望自己再大一些。他多希望从未给过那个姑娘她在自己心里占据的位置。他最希望的是——自己能早一点懂事。可是头顶的灯一盏接一盏地熄了。他独自站在渐渐暗下来的厅里，为自己曾有过的希望而羞愧。
reading.note: Closing — three wish + past perfect / wish + past — devastating regret cluster

vocab.meaning: adj. 废弃的；不再使用的

vocab.example_cn: 一只爱得没道理的母鸡。

vocab.example: A polecat-ferret hidden in a hutch.

reading.en: Conradin was ten years old, and the doctor had pronounced that the boy would not live another five years. His cousin and guardian, Mrs. De Ropp, was, in his eyes, the embodiment of every annoyance. Furthermore, she required that he sit indoors most of the day.
reading.cn: 康拉丁十岁了，医生宣告这孩子活不过五年。他的表姐兼监护人德·罗普太太，在他眼里是一切讨厌之物的化身。更糟的是，她要求他每天大半时间都待在屋里。
reading.note: Furthermore — cohesion (L61 review) / required that he sit — mandative subjunctive (L63 review)

reading.en: In the back garden stood a disused tool-shed, almost forgotten. There, Conradin kept two creatures: a hen, beloved beyond reason, and a polecat-ferret, hidden in a hutch covered with old sacking. The polecat, fed in secret, was the focus of his entire life.
reading.cn: 后花园里立着一间荒废的工具棚，几乎被人忘了。康拉丁在那儿藏着两只动物：一只老母鸡，他爱得没道理；还有一只箭貂——藏在用旧麻袋盖着的笼子里。这只箭貂是他整个生命的中心，被他暗中喂养。
reading.note: disused / almost forgotten / beloved beyond reason / hidden / covered / fed in secret — chain of reduced relatives (L62 review)

reading.en: He gave the polecat a name — Sredni Vashtar — and worshipped it as a god. Every Thursday, in silence, he performed a small rite in the shed. He wished, with all the strength of his thin chest, that Sredni Vashtar would do something terrible to Mrs. De Ropp.
reading.cn: 他给这只箭貂起了个名字——斯雷德尼·瓦什塔——并把它当作神来供奉。每个星期四，他都在棚子里默默举行一场小小的仪式。他用瘦弱胸膛里全部的力气祈愿：愿斯雷德尼·瓦什塔降下可怕的事在德·罗普太太身上。
reading.note: He wished + that + would — wish for future action (L64 review)

reading.en: It was inevitable that, sooner or later, Mrs. De Ropp would notice his frequent visits to the shed. One morning, she announced that she would investigate. She demanded that the door be opened. Conradin said nothing.
reading.cn: 迟早，德·罗普太太会注意到他频繁出入工具棚。这是免不了的。一天早晨，她宣布她要去查个究竟。她命令把门打开。康拉丁什么也没说。
reading.note: It was inevitable that... — formal subjunctive trigger / demanded that the door be opened — passive subjunctive (L63 review)

reading.en: Indeed, he sensed the moment had come. From the dining-room window, he watched her cross the garden, her keys jingling. The polecat-ferret, sleeping in its hutch, did not stir. She bent over the hutch.
reading.cn: 实际上，他感到时刻到了。他在餐厅窗口望着她穿过花园，钥匙叮当作响。睡在笼子里的箭貂没有动。她俯身看那只笼子。
reading.note: Indeed — cohesion (L61 review) / sleeping in its hutch — reduced relative (L62 review)

reading.en: Conradin stayed at the window. He whispered, again and again, the same chant. "Sredni Vashtar went forth. His enemies called for peace, but he brought them death."
reading.cn: 康拉丁站在窗前没动。他一遍又一遍地低声念着同一段祷词。"斯雷德尼·瓦什塔出去了。他的敌人求和，他给了他们死亡。"
reading.note: Repetition for emphasis (L56 review)

reading.en: Furthermore, he sang — softly, but in his thin treble voice — a song he had made up himself. The maid, hearing him, looked into the dining-room. He was eating toast. He had buttered it himself.
reading.cn: 此外，他还轻声唱起一首歌——用他细弱的童声——一首他自己编的歌。女仆听见，往餐厅里看了一眼。他正在吃涂了黄油的吐司。黄油是他自己抹的。
reading.note: Furthermore — cohesion (L61 review) / hearing him — reduced relative (L62 review)

reading.en: After a long time, the maid screamed. People came running. Voices in the hall called for someone — anyone. "Wherever is the mistress?" they asked. "She must, surely, have come back by now."
reading.cn: 过了很长一段时间，女仆尖叫起来。人们跑了进来。门厅里传来叫喊声，叫着某个人——谁都行。"夫人究竟在哪里？"他们问。"她，到这时候，一定该回来了。"
reading.note: Wherever / surely — emphatic markers / She must, surely, have come back — modal perfect (L44 review)

reading.en: Conradin took another piece of toast. From the shed, slowly, the polecat-ferret had emerged — its small dark mouth and throat stained red. Conradin, looking out the window, wished the moment would last. If only, he thought, every Thursday could be like this.
reading.cn: 康拉丁又拿了一块吐司。慢慢地，箭貂从工具棚里出来——小小的嘴和喉咙染成了红色。康拉丁望着窗外，希望这一刻永远持续下去。'要是每个星期四都能这样就好了，'他想。
reading.note: Closing — looking out the window — reduced (L62) / wished + would + If only + could — wish cluster (L64 review)

vocab.example_cn: 著名律师丹尼尔·韦伯斯特。
韦伯斯特请求公平审判。

reading.en: Jabez Stone, a New Hampshire farmer, claimed that nothing he tried ever worked. His crops failed. His cattle died. One day he announced he would sell his soul to the Devil for ten years of luck.
reading.cn: 贾贝兹·斯通是新罕布什尔州的一个农民，他声称自己干什么都不行。庄稼歉收。牛死了。有一天，他宣告愿意把灵魂卖给魔鬼，换十年好运。
reading.note: claimed that — neutral assertion (KEY focus) / announced he would — reported speech (L47 review)

reading.en: Sure enough, a stranger came that night. Stone signed the paper. For the next ten years, his fortune climbed. He insisted to his neighbors that he was simply lucky. He denied that anything strange had ever happened.
reading.cn: 果然，那夜来了个陌生人。斯通在纸上签了字。接下来的十年里，他的家业蒸蒸日上。他向邻居坚称自己只是运气好。他否认发生过任何奇怪的事。
reading.note: insisted that — strong claim (KEY focus) / denied that — refusal to admit (KEY focus)

reading.en: When the ten years were nearly up, Stone admitted to himself that he was terrified. He confessed his secret to Daniel Webster, the famous lawyer. "Save me," he begged. Webster, after a long pause, conceded that the case would be hard — but he said he would defend Stone.
reading.cn: 十年眼看到期，斯通对自己承认他害怕极了。他把秘密告诉了著名的律师丹尼尔·韦伯斯特。"救我，"他恳求。韦伯斯特沉默了好一会儿，承认这案子会很难——但他说他会为斯通辩护。
reading.note: admitted to himself that — concession to oneself (KEY focus) / conceded that — admit a difficulty (KEY focus)

reading.en: The Devil arrived at midnight. Stone protested that the contract was unfair. The Devil maintained that all conditions had been clearly written. He argued that Stone had received exactly what he asked for. He even claimed that the Constitution itself protected the rights of slave-holders — and that a soul, once sold, was property.
reading.cn: 午夜，魔鬼到了。斯通抗议这合约不公平。魔鬼主张所有条件都白纸黑字写明了。他争辩说斯通得到了他要的一切。他甚至声称，连宪法本身都保护奴隶主的权利——一个灵魂一旦出卖，就是财产。
reading.note: protested that / maintained that / argued that / claimed that — four reporting verbs in cluster (KEY focus)

reading.en: Webster requested a fair trial. The Devil agreed — but suggested that the jury be chosen from his own collection of damned American villains. Webster did not flinch. He countered that he would rather face such a jury than admit defeat.
reading.cn: 韦伯斯特请求一场公平审判。魔鬼同意了——但建议陪审团由他自己手里那些堕落的美国恶徒组成。韦伯斯特毫不退让。他反驳说：他宁愿面对这样的陪审团，也不肯认输。
reading.note: requested + suggested that + V (subjunctive L63) / countered that — refute (KEY focus)

reading.en: The jury was assembled — twelve faces from American history, all guilty of treason or murder. Webster rose to speak. He acknowledged that Stone had broken his word. He admitted that the contract was real. But he reminded the jury that they, too, had once been Americans.
reading.cn: 陪审团组好了——十二张来自美国历史的脸，都犯过叛国或谋杀的罪。韦伯斯特站起身发言。他承认斯通确实毁了承诺。他承认合约是真的。但他提醒陪审团，他们自己也曾经是美国人。
reading.note: acknowledged that — formal admission / admitted that — concede a fact / reminded the jury that — assert prior fact

reading.en: Webster spoke of liberty, of the land, of the everyday courage of farmers like Stone. He insisted that no man — not even one who had signed away his soul — should be denied the chance to begin again. The jury, listening, began to weep.
reading.cn: 韦伯斯特讲到自由、讲到这片土地、讲到斯通这样的农民身上日复一日的勇气。他坚称没有任何一个人——哪怕是签字卖灵的人——应当被剥夺重新开始的机会。陪审团听着听着，开始流泪。
reading.note: insisted that... should — strong moral claim with subjunctive (L63 review)

reading.en: The foreman stood. "We find for the defendant," he announced. The Devil howled. He demanded the verdict be overturned. Webster reminded him that all proceedings had been according to the Devil's own terms. The Devil, defeated, conceded that the case was lost.
reading.cn: 陪审长站起来。"我们裁决被告胜诉，"他宣布。魔鬼嚎叫起来。他要求推翻判决。韦伯斯特提醒他：整个审判程序都是按魔鬼自己定的规矩走的。魔鬼一败涂地，承认这案子输了。
reading.note: announced — formal declaration / demanded that be overturned — subjunctive / conceded that — admit defeat

reading.en: Stone went home a free man. He never made another bargain. And in New Hampshire, even now, lawyers tell their students: when in trouble, argue from American principle, and never concede the spirit of your case — even if the facts admit you are guilty.
reading.cn: 斯通自由地回了家。他再没和任何人做过那种交易。直到现在，新罕布什尔的律师还会告诉学生：碰到麻烦，要从美国精神立论；永远不要在精神上让步——哪怕事实上你已认罪。
reading.note: Closing — argue from / concede the spirit / admit you are guilty — reporting verbs in legal context

vocab.example_cn: 它确实代表了某种古老的东西。

reading.en: On a clear and sunny morning of June 27th, the people of the village began to gather in the square. The lottery, like the square dances and the Halloween program, did take place every year. The villagers did believe in tradition.
reading.cn: 六月二十七日是个晴朗明亮的早晨，村民们在广场上聚集起来。这场抽签和方块舞、万圣节活动一样，每年都办。村民们确实相信传统。
reading.note: did take place / did believe — auxiliary emphasis (KEY focus)

reading.en: Children, just out of school for the summer, began to gather first. Bobby Martin had already filled his pockets with stones, and the other boys, following his example, did the same. Boys do collect stones, after all.
reading.cn: 刚刚开始放暑假的孩子们最先聚拢来。鲍比·马丁已经把口袋装满了石头，其他男孩照着他的样子也这么做。男孩子，毕竟，是会捡石头的。
reading.note: Boys do collect stones — generic statement with auxiliary do (KEY focus)

reading.en: Mr. Summers, who arranged the lottery, came carrying a black wooden box. The original box had been lost. The current one did show signs of long use — splintered, faded, stained — but the villagers did not want a new one. The box did represent something old, and that meant something to them.
reading.cn: 举办抽签的萨默斯先生抱着一只黑色的木盒走来。最早的盒子早就丢了。现在这只显得用了很久——开裂、褪色、有污渍——但村民们不想换新的。这只盒子代表了某种古老的东西，而那对他们意味着什么。
reading.note: did show / did not want / did represent — emphasis chain

reading.en: Tessie Hutchinson came hurrying in late. "Clean forgot what day it was," she said. Her husband Bill called out cheerfully: "You did get here in time, Tessie." The villagers laughed. Tessie did laugh too, although her eyes flickered around the square.
reading.cn: 泰西·哈钦森匆匆赶到，迟了。"我把日子忘得一干二净，"她说。她丈夫比尔高声喊："泰西，你确实来得及。"大家笑了。泰西也笑了——尽管她的眼神在广场上扫来扫去。
reading.note: You did get here in time — emphasis on success (KEY focus) / did laugh — emphasis on outward action

reading.en: Mr. Summers cleared his throat. "Now, I'll read the names — heads of families first." Some villagers, watching him, whispered that other towns nearby had already given up the lottery. Old Man Warner, however, snorted. "Pack of crazy fools," he muttered. "There's always been a lottery. Used to be a saying — 'Lottery in June, corn be heavy soon.' What I do know is, it works."
reading.cn: 萨默斯先生清了清嗓子。"现在我念名字——先念家长。"有几个村民边看边小声说，附近别的镇早就不办这玩意了。可瓦纳老头哼了一声。"一堆疯子，"他嘟哝。"抽签一直都有。以前还有句话——'六月抽签，玉米早肥。'我所知道的是，它管用。"
reading.note: What I do know is — emphatic cleft (KEY focus) / Used to be — habitual past (L58 review)

reading.en: When the family of Hutchinson was drawn, Tessie cried out. "It wasn't fair! Bill didn't have time to take the paper he wanted!" Her neighbors did not look at her. The next round began — within the family. Five slips of paper, one black-marked, were prepared.
reading.cn: 当哈钦森一家被抽中时，泰西嚷起来。"不公平！比尔根本没时间挑他想要的那张！"邻居们没有看她。下一轮开始了——这一回是在家庭内部。五张纸条准备好了，其中一张做了黑色记号。
reading.note: didn't have time — past simple negative + did not look — emphasis through negation

reading.en: Bill, the husband, drew first. Then the children. Then Tessie. Each held a slip of paper. The villagers stood very still. "Show your papers," Mr. Summers said. The slips were turned over one by one. Bill's was blank. The children's were blank. Tessie's did have the black spot.
reading.cn: 丈夫比尔先抽。然后是孩子们。然后是泰西。每人手里都捏着一张纸条。村民们一动也不动。"把纸条翻过来看，"萨默斯先生说。一张张翻开。比尔的是白纸。孩子们的也是白纸。泰西的——上面果然有那个黑点。
reading.note: Tessie's did have the black spot — emphasis on the dreaded outcome (KEY focus)

reading.en: Tessie held her hands out. "It isn't fair, it isn't right!" she screamed. The villagers, however, were already moving toward her. Mrs. Delacroix, her best friend, picked up a stone. "Come on, hurry up," she called to the others. The children — those small boys — did indeed have stones ready.
reading.cn: 泰西伸出双手。"这不公平！这不对！"她尖叫。可村民们已经向她靠拢。她最好的朋友德拉克鲁瓦太太捡起一块石头。"快，快点，"她朝其他人喊。那些孩子——刚才那些小男孩——的确，手里早就攥着石头了。
reading.note: did indeed have — double emphasis (do + indeed) (KEY focus)

reading.en: And then they did what every village in this story has always done. They were on her in a moment. "It isn't fair, it isn't right," she cried again — and the stones did fall. Tradition does require that the lottery be held every year. And every year, the village does keep its tradition.
reading.cn: 然后他们做了这个故事里每个村庄一直在做的事。一瞬间他们都扑了过去。"这不公平！这不对！"她再喊一声——石头开始落下。传统要求每年举行抽签。每年，村子都履行着它的传统。
reading.note: Closing — did fall / does require + that + V (subjunctive) / does keep — emphasis cluster

vocab.example: He made a landfall on the island.
Given supplies and a head start.

reading.en: Sanger Rainsford, a famous hunter, was sailing toward the Amazon when he fell overboard one black night. He swam toward a distant shore — and after a long struggle, made a landfall on Ship-Trap Island, a place that drew superstition and dread from every sailor in the Caribbean.
reading.cn: 著名猎人桑格·兰斯福德正乘船开往亚马逊，一个漆黑的夜里他从船上跌了下去。他朝远处的岸游去——经过艰难的挣扎，终于在'船陷岛'登岸——一个让加勒比海所有船员都心生迷信和恐惧的地方。
reading.note: drew superstition and dread — verb + abstract noun (KEY focus)

reading.en: He took shelter in a great house at the island's center. The owner, General Zaroff, welcomed him with extraordinary courtesy. Zaroff offered hospitality, took an interest in Rainsford's reputation, and over dinner, raised an unusual question.
reading.cn: 他在岛中央一栋大宅里寻得了庇护。主人扎罗夫将军以非凡的礼数欢迎他。扎罗夫提供款待，对兰斯福德的名声很感兴趣——晚餐时，提出了一个不寻常的问题。
reading.note: took shelter / welcomed with courtesy / offered hospitality / took an interest / raised a question — five collocations (KEY focus)

reading.en: "Hunting," Zaroff said, "ceased to give me satisfaction many years ago. Lions, tigers — too predictable. So I bred a new sport. I hunt the most cunning, the most dangerous game on earth — one that gives me genuine pleasure." Rainsford asked what he meant. Zaroff bowed. "Man," he said simply.
reading.cn: "打猎，"扎罗夫说，"很多年前就不能让我获得乐趣了。狮子、老虎——太好猜了。所以我培养出一种新的运动。我猎捕地球上最狡猾、最危险的猎物——能给我带来真正快乐的那种。"兰斯福德问他什么意思。扎罗夫鞠了一躬。"人，"他简单地说。
reading.note: ceased to give satisfaction / bred a new sport / hunt game / give pleasure — verb-noun collocations

reading.en: Rainsford expressed shock. He drew a sharp distinction between hunting beasts and hunting men. Zaroff dismissed the objection. He claimed the chase still met civilized standards: the prey was given supplies, a head start, three days of freedom. If the prey survived, he was let go.
reading.cn: 兰斯福德表达了震惊。他在猎兽与猎人之间划下了一道鲜明的界限。扎罗夫不以为然。他声称这种追猎依然合乎文明标准：猎物有补给、有先机、有三天的自由。要是猎物撑下来了，就放了他。
reading.note: expressed shock / drew a distinction / dismissed the objection / met civilized standards / met a head start — collocations

reading.en: "I refuse to take part," Rainsford said. Zaroff smiled. "Then you yourself shall be the next prey. Tomorrow at sunrise, you will be given a knife and three hours' start. If you survive until midnight on the third day, you may take the boat."
reading.cn: "我不参加，"兰斯福德说。扎罗夫笑了。"那你自己就是下一个猎物。明早日出，会给你一把刀和三个小时的先机。要是你能撑到第三天午夜，就可以驾船离开。"
reading.note: refuse to take part / take the boat — modal collocations

reading.en: At dawn, Rainsford set off into the jungle. He drew on every skill he had ever acquired. He laid traps. He left false trails. He spent a sleepless night in a tree, listening for footsteps. Several times he caught sight of Zaroff — and several times Zaroff lost the trail.
reading.cn: 黎明时分，兰斯福德出发进入丛林。他动用了自己学过的每一项本领。他设陷阱。留假踪迹。在树上度过一个无眠的夜晚，留心听脚步声。他好几次瞥见扎罗夫——扎罗夫也几次跟丢了。
reading.note: set off / drew on a skill / laid traps / left trails / spent a night / caught sight / lost the trail — chain of action collocations

reading.en: By the third day, Rainsford was exhausted, bleeding from a leg wound. The dogs were closing in. He had run out of options. Drawing a deep breath, he reached the cliff above the sea — and threw himself off.
reading.cn: 到第三天，兰斯福德筋疲力尽，腿上的伤还在流血。猎犬越逼越近。他已经没什么选择。他深吸一口气，跑到海上方的悬崖——纵身跳下。
reading.note: run out of options / draw a deep breath / throw oneself off — collocations

reading.en: Zaroff returned to his house at dusk, having lost his prey at the cliff. He took a hot bath. He poured a glass of brandy. He gave the matter no further thought — until, opening his bedroom door, he found Rainsford waiting in the shadows.
reading.cn: 扎罗夫黄昏时回到屋里，他在悬崖那儿失去了猎物。他洗了个热水澡。倒了一杯白兰地。他没把这事再放在心上——直到他打开卧室门，发现兰斯福德正在阴影里等着他。
reading.note: took a bath / poured a glass / gave the matter no thought — chain of routine collocations contrasting with the surprise

reading.en: "You have won the game, Rainsford," Zaroff conceded — but his voice betrayed no surprise. "Now we test which of us is the better animal." He drew a sword. They circled each other once. Years later, Rainsford would say only: "I have never slept in a better bed than the General's." Beyond that, he never spoke of it.
reading.cn: "兰斯福德，你赢了，"扎罗夫承认——但语气里没有惊讶。"现在我们看一看，我们俩谁是更厉害的那只野兽。"他抽出一把剑。两人对视绕行了一圈。多年以后，兰斯福德只会说："我从没睡过比将军那张更好的床。"再多的话，他不会说。
reading.note: Closing — won the game / betrayed no surprise / drew a sword / circled each other / spoke of it — collocations

vocab.example: The deliberate steadiness of her gaze.
She snatched it from my hand.
Tears of rage in her eyes.

reading.en: When I arrived at the Olsons' apartment, the parents looked anxious. What they wanted was simple: for me to examine their daughter Mathilda. She had a high fever, and three children at her school had already died of diphtheria.
reading.cn: 我到奥尔森家公寓时，父母两人面带焦虑。他们要的其实很简单：让我给女儿玛蒂尔达做检查。她在发高烧，她学校已经有三个孩子死于白喉了。
reading.note: What they wanted was... — wh-cleft for emphasis (KEY focus)

reading.en: The girl, about three years old, sat on her father's lap. She was very pretty — her eyes calm, her hair like gold. What struck me first was that she had been told nothing. "She doesn't know what we think it might be," her mother whispered.
reading.cn: 女孩大概三岁，坐在父亲膝盖上。她长得很美——眼神平静，头发金色。让我一开始就注意到的，是没人告诉她任何事。"她不知道我们怀疑她得了什么病，"母亲低声说。
reading.note: What struck me first was... — wh-cleft introducing observation (KEY focus)

reading.en: "All I need to do is look at your throat," I said gently. The girl did not move. What surprised me was the deliberate steadiness of her gaze. She was not afraid — she was prepared.
reading.cn: "我只需要看一下你的喉咙，"我温和地说。女孩一动不动。让我吃惊的是她目光那种刻意的镇定。她不是害怕——她是准备好了。
reading.note: All I need to do is... — wh-cleft + zero infinitive (KEY focus) / What surprised me was... — wh-cleft

reading.en: I asked again. She said nothing. I tried a wooden tongue depressor. With a sudden movement, she snatched it from my hand and threw it across the room. What followed was a struggle.
reading.cn: 我又问了一次。她什么也没说。我试着用木质压舌板。她突然一把从我手里夺走，扔到了房间另一头。接下来发生的，是一场拉锯。
reading.note: What followed was... — wh-cleft for sequence

reading.en: Her father, embarrassed, tried to hold her arms. She fought silently — kicking, twisting. The mother kept saying, "Be a good girl. The doctor won't hurt you." What angered me was that her parents kept apologizing — to her, and to me.
reading.cn: 父亲尴尬地想抓住她的手臂。她无声地反抗——踢、扭。母亲一直说："乖一点。医生不会伤你的。"让我恼火的是，父母一直在道歉——既向她，也向我。
reading.note: What angered me was that... — wh-cleft + that-clause (KEY focus)

reading.en: The truth is, the longer she resisted, the more I wanted to win. What I felt was not just professional duty. It was something less honorable — the urge to break a stubborn child. I knew it was wrong. I knew it; and I went on.
reading.cn: 事实是，她抵抗得越久，我就越想赢。我心里涌出的，不只是职业责任。还有一种没那么光彩的东西——一种想压服一个倔强孩子的冲动。我知道这不对。我知道——可我没有停。
reading.note: What I felt was not... It was... — wh-cleft + denial-affirmation pair

reading.en: Finally, with the metal spoon between her teeth, I forced her mouth open. What I saw confirmed my fear: tonsils covered with white membrane. She had been hiding her sore throat from her parents for days.
reading.cn: 最后，我用一把金属勺子塞在她牙齿之间，强行撑开她的嘴。看到的画面证实了我的担心：扁桃体上覆着一层白膜。她已经把喉咙痛瞒了父母好几天。
reading.note: What I saw confirmed my fear — wh-cleft + result clause

reading.en: The girl, defeated, was now beyond fury. With tears of rage in her eyes, she tried to attack me again. What she could not forgive was not the pain. It was the failure — being seen, being known.
reading.cn: 女孩输了，怒火已经超过了所有的边界。她眼里含着愤怒的泪，又想扑上来打我。她不能原谅的，不是疼。是输——是被看穿、被看清。
reading.note: What she could not forgive was not... It was... — wh-cleft + denial-affirmation

reading.en: Walking back to my car in the cold air, I thought about her. All I had wanted was to do my job. All she had wanted was to be left alone. What lay between us was not just diphtheria — it was the use of force, and the strange satisfaction it had given me. That was what I would not forget.
reading.cn: 在冷空气里走回车上时，我一直在想她。我所要的，不过是做我的工作。她所要的，不过是被留下不打扰。我们之间隔着的，不仅是白喉——是那种动用武力的事实，以及它带给我的、让我不安的某种满足。那才是我不会忘记的事。
reading.note: Closing — three wh-cleft structures stacked (All I had wanted... / All she had wanted... / What lay between us was...)

vocab.example: The regular rhythm of the office.

vocab.example_cn: 办公室八卦是他不屑的。
她给他倒了一杯苏格兰威士忌。

reading.en: Mr. Martin had worked at F & S for twenty-two years. He was the head of the filing department. What he valued most was order, silence, and the regular rhythm of the office. He did not smoke; he did not drink. He had never even raised his voice.
reading.cn: 马丁先生在 F&S 公司干了二十二年。他是档案部主管。他最看重的，是秩序、安静，以及办公室每天规律的节奏。他不抽烟；不喝酒。他甚至从没提高过嗓门。
reading.note: What he valued most was... — wh-cleft (L69 review) / did not smoke / had never raised — emphasis (L67 review)

reading.en: Then, a year ago, Mr. Fitweiler hired Mrs. Ulgine Barrows as his "special advisor." From that day on, what had been a calm office became a place of constant disruption. Mrs. Barrows shouted across the hall. She used baseball metaphors at every meeting. "Are you tearing up the pea patch?" she would ask. "Are you sitting in the catbird seat?"
reading.cn: 一年前，菲特韦勒先生请来了乌尔金·巴罗斯太太当他的"特别顾问"。从那天起，原本安静的办公室变成了一个不断被搅扰的地方。巴罗斯太太隔着大厅大声说话。她在每次会议上都用棒球比喻。"你是把豌豆地翻个底朝天？"她常问。"你是坐在占上风的位子上？"
reading.note: From that day on — discourse marker / what had been... became... — wh-cleft (L69 review)

reading.en: Mr. Martin endured her without comment. He claimed to others that her noise did not bother him. He insisted that office gossip was beneath him. But when she suggested to Mr. Fitweiler that the filing department be reorganized, Martin knew his time had come. He drew up a plan. He would, quite simply, kill her.
reading.cn: 马丁先生默默忍着她。他对别人说她的噪音对他没影响。他坚称办公室八卦是他不屑参与的。但当她向菲特韦勒先生建议重组档案部时，马丁知道他的时刻到了。他制定了一个方案。他要——简简单单——杀了她。
reading.note: claimed / insisted / suggested that the filing department be reorganized — reporting verbs + subjunctive (L66+L63 review)

reading.en: Tuesday, after work, he walked to her apartment. He had checked the layout, drawn up the route, and chosen the time with care. What he had not done was rehearse what to say if anything went wrong.
reading.cn: 周二下班后，他走去她的公寓。他事先查过布局，画出路线，仔细选定了时间。他唯独没有做的，是排练万一出错时该说什么。
reading.note: had checked / had drawn up / had chosen — past perfect chain (L48 review) / What he had not done was... — wh-cleft (L69)

reading.en: Mrs. Barrows, surprised but pleased, let him in. She poured him a Scotch. "Pour yourself one," she said. He did. He drank it down. Then he asked for another. She, herself surprised, did pour another.
reading.cn: 巴罗斯太太既惊讶又高兴，让他进了门。她给他倒了一杯苏格兰威士忌。"你自己再倒一杯吧，"她说。他倒了。一口喝下。然后他要了第二杯。她，自己也吃惊，也确实又倒了一杯。
reading.note: did pour another — do/did emphasis (L67 review)

reading.en: Then Mr. Martin, who had never smoked, took out a cigarette. He, the man who never drank, took a third whiskey. "I do enjoy a good Scotch," he said. "And I do find that — when one is planning to bump off the boss — a heroin shot first is what really steadies the nerves."
reading.cn: 然后马丁先生——一个从没抽过烟的人——拿出一支烟。他，那个从不喝酒的人，喝下了第三杯威士忌。"我确实享受好的苏格兰威士忌，"他说。"我也确实发现——一个人要是打算干掉老板——先打一针海洛因，才真正能让神经稳下来。"
reading.note: do enjoy / do find — do-emphasis (L67 review) / what really steadies the nerves — wh-cleft (L69 review)

reading.en: Mrs. Barrows stared. He went on, casually, to claim that he often did such things. He maintained that Fitweiler had cheated him. He admitted that he had been planning the murder for weeks. Then he stood, walked out, and said good night.
reading.cn: 巴罗斯太太盯着他。他若无其事地接着说，他常做这种事。他主张菲特韦勒骗过他。他承认这场谋杀他已策划数周。然后他站起身，走了出去，道了晚安。
reading.note: claim / maintain / admit — reporting verbs (L66 review)

reading.en: The next morning, Mrs. Barrows burst into Mr. Fitweiler's office. She insisted that Martin was a heroin addict. She claimed that he had threatened to kill the boss. She demanded that he be fired immediately.
reading.cn: 第二天早上，巴罗斯太太冲进菲特韦勒先生的办公室。她坚称马丁是海洛因瘾君子。她声称他威胁要杀老板。她要求把他立刻解雇。
reading.note: insisted / claimed / demanded that he be fired — reporting verbs + subjunctive (L66+L63 review)

reading.en: Mr. Fitweiler, who had known Martin for twenty-two years, drew Mrs. Barrows aside. He admitted, gently, that her work had been excellent — but that she had clearly been overworking, perhaps to the point of nervous breakdown. The next day, what arrived on Mrs. Barrows's desk was a polite letter of dismissal. Mr. Martin, sitting at his old desk, did not look up. He went on filing.
reading.cn: 菲特韦勒先生，在二十二年里都认识马丁，把巴罗斯太太拉到一边。他温和地承认，她的工作一直出色——但她显然劳累过度，也许已经到了精神崩溃的边缘。第二天，落到巴罗斯太太桌上的，是一封措辞客气的解雇信。马丁先生坐在他原来的位子上，没有抬头。他继续整理档案。
reading.note: Closing — admitted / drew aside (collocation L68) / what arrived on her desk was... — wh-cleft (L69 review)

vocab.example_cn: 她们第一次罗马社交季。

vocab.meaning: adj. 尽责的；循规蹈矩的

vocab.example: Went to the Colosseum after dark.
The color had drained from her face.

reading.en: On a sunny terrace in Rome, two American widows sat together looking down at the Forum. Mrs. Slade and Mrs. Ansley were old friends — friends with whom each had shared girlhood, marriage, motherhood, and now widowhood. The waiter, to whom they had given their order long ago, did not return.
reading.cn: 罗马一块阳光下的露台上，两位美国寡妇坐在一起，俯瞰着古罗马广场。斯莱德太太和安斯利太太是老朋友——是彼此一起经历过少女时代、婚姻、做母亲、如今又一起守寡的朋友。她们早早点过菜的那位侍者，没有再回来。
reading.note: friends with whom each had shared... / waiter to whom they had given... — prepositional relatives (KEY focus)

reading.en: Below them stretched the city in which both women had spent the most decisive year of their lives. It was the year of which they rarely spoke — the year of their first Roman season, when both had loved the same man.
reading.cn: 她们脚下铺展着的，是这两位女士度过她们人生中最决定性那一年的城市。那是她们极少提起的一年——她们第一次罗马社交季的那一年，那一年里，两人爱上了同一个男人。
reading.note: the city in which / the year of which — prepositional relatives (KEY focus)

reading.en: Mrs. Slade had married him. The man for whom both had cared, Delphin Slade, had been hers for twenty-five years before he died. Her daughter Jenny, by now downstairs, was dutiful and quiet — the kind of girl about whom no one would ever speak with fire.
reading.cn: 斯莱德太太嫁给了他。两人都为之倾心的那个人——德尔芬·斯莱德——曾属于她整整二十五年，直到他去世。她的女儿珍妮，此刻就在楼下，循规蹈矩、不爱说话——是那种没人会带着热情议论的姑娘。
reading.note: the man for whom both had cared / a girl about whom no one would speak — prepositional relatives

reading.en: Mrs. Ansley's daughter Barbara, on the other hand, was the kind of girl on whose presence young men instantly fixed their attention. The vivid daughter, the quiet daughter — and at this moment they were both out together with two Italian gentlemen of whose families nothing was certainly known.
reading.cn: 另一方面，安斯利太太的女儿芭芭拉，是那种年轻男人一进门就把注意力锁住的姑娘。活泼的女儿、安静的女儿——这一刻她们俩都和两位意大利绅士一起出门了——而那两位绅士的家世，没有人确切清楚。
reading.note: a girl on whose presence... / Italian gentlemen of whose families... — possessive prepositional relatives

reading.en: Mrs. Slade, watching the sky over the Forum darken, finally spoke. "Do you remember," she said, "the night, twenty-five years ago, on which you went to the Colosseum after dark to meet — well, who?"
reading.cn: 斯莱德太太望着古罗马广场上方的天空慢慢暗下来，终于开了口。"你记不记得，"她说，"二十五年前的一个晚上，你天黑以后去斗兽场——你去见谁来着？"
reading.note: the night on which you went... — prepositional relative (KEY focus)

reading.en: Mrs. Ansley grew pale. "I had a letter," she said quietly. Mrs. Slade paused. "The letter," she said, "of which you have always thought he was the writer — was written, in fact, by me."
reading.cn: 安斯利太太脸色变白。"当时我收到了一封信，"她平静地说。斯莱德太太顿了顿。"那封信，"她说，"——你一直以为是他写的——其实是我写的。"
reading.note: The letter of which you have thought... — prepositional relative + reported thought

reading.en: Mrs. Ansley sat very still. "I went," she said. "And he was there." Mrs. Slade looked up sharply. "He could not have been," she said. "I forged the letter — to send you out into the cold and catch Roman fever."
reading.cn: 安斯利太太坐着没动。"我去了，"她说。"他在那儿。"斯莱德太太猛地抬头。"他不可能在的，"她说。"那封信是我伪造的——为了把你赶到冷风里，染上'罗马热'。"
reading.note: He could not have been — modal speculation about past (preview L73)

reading.en: "He was there," Mrs. Ansley repeated. "He answered my letter. I had written first, you see — telling him to come, the night on which I knew I would receive his reply."
reading.cn: "他真的在，"安斯利太太重复。"他回了我的信。我先写的——告诉他来，就是我知道自己会收到他回信的那一夜。"
reading.note: the night on which I knew... — prepositional relative

reading.en: Mrs. Slade stared. "Well — I had Delphin," she said at last, with effort. "All those years." Mrs. Ansley rose. "Yes," she said. "Yes, you had him. But I — I had Barbara." And the woman from whose face the color had drained walked slowly toward the stairs, leaving Mrs. Slade alone on the terrace.
reading.cn: 斯莱德太太瞪着她。"——可我有过德尔芬，"她终于挤出一句。"那么多年。"安斯利太太站起身。"是啊，"她说。"你有他。可我——我有过芭芭拉。"——然后那个脸上血色已退尽的女人，慢慢朝楼梯走去，把斯莱德太太一个人留在了露台上。
reading.note: Closing — the woman from whose face the color had drained — possessive prepositional relative

vocab.example_cn: 一位庄重而美丽的女人。

vocab.example: An exam he could not afford to fail.
May determine the next ten years.

vocab.example_cn: 一个很深的建筑工地坑。

vocab.example: A wooden hoarding stood at the back.
vocab.example_cn: 临街那面立着一块木栏。

reading.en: Lionel Wallace was a successful man — a Cabinet minister, the kind of man whose career rose as if guided by a steady hand. One evening, dining with an old school-friend, he told a story he had told no one else. It began when he was five.
reading.cn: 莱昂内尔·华莱士是成功人士——一位内阁大臣，那种事业像被一只稳定的手牵着上升的人。一个傍晚，他和一位老校友共进晚餐，讲了一段他从未告诉任何人的故事。一切始于他五岁那年。
reading.note: as if guided by a steady hand — as if + past participle (KEY focus)

reading.en: Walking alone down a dim street in West Kensington, he had come upon a long white wall and, in it, a green door. He felt drawn to the door, as though it had been calling him for as long as he could remember.
reading.cn: 他独自走在西肯辛顿一条幽暗的街上，遇到了一堵长长的白墙，墙上有一扇绿色的门。他觉得自己被吸引——仿佛这扇门从他记得起就一直在叫他。
reading.note: as though it had been calling him — as though + past perfect continuous (KEY focus)

reading.en: He pushed it open and stepped through. Beyond was a garden — wider, brighter, and stranger than any place he had seen. Two great panthers played on a smooth lawn as if they were kittens. The air felt as though it had been waiting just for him.
reading.cn: 他推开门，走了进去。门后是一座花园——比他见过的任何地方都更广阔、更明亮、更奇异。两只巨大的黑豹在平整的草坪上玩耍，仿佛它们是小猫。空气仿佛专为他而等了很久。
reading.note: as if they were kittens — as if + past simple (KEY focus) / as though it had been waiting — as though + past perfect continuous

reading.en: A grave, beautiful woman walked toward him. She greeted him as if he had always lived there. She showed him a book, and in the book he saw — to his shock — every moment of his life, written and pictured. The pages turned by themselves, slowly, gently, as if a wind he could not feel were turning them.
reading.cn: 一位庄重而美丽的女人朝他走来。她问候他的样子，仿佛他一直就住在这里。她给他看一本书，他在书里看到——令他震惊地——他生命中每一刻，都被写下来、画下来。书页自己慢慢地、轻柔地翻着，仿佛被一阵他感觉不到的风翻动。
reading.note: as if he had always lived there — as if + past perfect / as if a wind ... were turning — as if + past subjunctive (KEY focus)

reading.en: When she came to the page that showed him at the green door, the woman closed the book. He found himself, suddenly, on the cold West Kensington street again. He cried — as a child cries when he has lost something for which he cannot name the value.
reading.cn: 当她翻到他站在绿门前的那一页时，她合上了书。他突然发现自己又回到了寒冷的西肯辛顿街上。他哭了——像一个孩子失去了他自己也说不出价值的东西时那样哭。
reading.note: as a child cries when he has lost — comparison clause / for which he cannot name — relative (L71 review)

reading.en: Years later, hurrying to school, he saw the green door again. He paused — but he was already late, and his teacher would not understand. He passed it by. He felt, for the rest of that day, as if a part of himself had been left on the other side.
reading.cn: 几年后，他急着去上学，又看见了那扇绿门。他停下来——可他已经迟到了，老师会不容他迟到。他走过去了。那一整天他都觉得，自己的一部分仿佛被留在了门的另一边。
reading.note: as if a part of himself had been left — as if + past perfect

reading.en: Twice more, in his life, the door appeared. Once on the night of an examination he could not afford to fail. Once on the way to a Cabinet meeting at which his career would be decided. Both times, he passed it by. Both times, he felt afterwards as though he had betrayed a friend.
reading.cn: 在他的一生中，那扇门又出现过两次。一次是在一场他输不起的考试当晚。一次是在赴一场决定他仕途的内阁会议途中。两次他都走过去了。两次之后他都觉得，仿佛自己背叛了一位朋友。
reading.note: as though he had betrayed a friend — as though + past perfect (regret tone)

reading.en: Now, telling the story over dinner, he looked at his friend with strange eyes. "I see it almost weekly now," he said. "Tomorrow I have a meeting that may determine the next ten years of my life. If I see the door tomorrow — I think, this time, I will go through. I have lived as if doing so meant losing everything. Now I think it would mean gaining it back."
reading.cn: 此刻，餐桌上讲完故事的他，目光怪异。"现在我几乎每周都看见它，"他说。"明天有一场会议，可能决定我未来十年。要是明天我看见那扇门——我想，这一次，我会走过去。一直以来我都活得仿佛走过去意味着失去一切。现在我觉得——那意味着把那一切要回来。"
reading.note: as if doing so meant losing — as if + past simple (subjunctive)

reading.en: Three days later, his body was found in a deep construction pit. A wooden hoarding stood at the back, with a small white door set into it. The door, locked but unbolted from the inside, opened onto twenty feet of empty air. He had stepped through, his friend imagined, as if the wall had melted before him — as if the garden had, at long last, opened to receive him home.
reading.cn: 三天后，人们在一个很深的建筑工地坑里发现了他的尸体。坑里临街那一面立着一块木栏，上面安着一扇小小的白门。那扇门锁着，但从里面没有插销——门外是二十英尺的虚空。朋友想象，他踏过去的样子，仿佛那堵墙在他面前融化了——仿佛那座花园终于打开，要把他迎接回家。
reading.note: Closing — as if the wall had melted / as if the garden had opened — as if + past perfect (counterfactual close)

vocab.example_cn: 她的继父罗伊罗特医生。

vocab.meaning: adj. 暴力的；性情暴烈的
vocab.example_cn: 性情暴烈的罗伊罗特医生。

vocab.example: The bed was bolted to the floor.
vocab.example_cn: 床被螺栓固定在地板上。

reading.en: On a cold April morning, Helen Stoner came to Sherlock Holmes in Baker Street. She was pale, trembling, and very young. She told him that her twin sister had died two years before. The death had been ruled natural — but Helen no longer believed it could have been.
reading.cn: 四月里一个寒冷的早晨，海伦·斯通纳来贝克街找夏洛克·福尔摩斯。她脸色苍白，颤抖着，非常年轻。她告诉他，她的孪生姐姐两年前去世了。当时被判定为自然死亡——但海伦如今不再相信那真的可能是自然原因。
reading.note: could have been — modal speculation about the past (KEY focus)

reading.en: Her sister, just before dying, had cried out a strange phrase: "the speckled band!" Helen had heard the words clearly. She had also heard, in the seconds before, a low whistle and a metallic clang. "It must have come from the next room," she said. "But the door was locked — locked from the inside."
reading.cn: 她姐姐临终前喊出了一句奇怪的话："那条斑点带！"海伦清清楚楚地听见。在那之前几秒，她还听见了一声低低的口哨和金属相碰的声响。"那一定是从隔壁屋来的，"她说。"可那间屋的门是锁着的——而且是从里面锁的。"
reading.note: It must have come from... — modal speculation (must + have + V-ed) (KEY focus)

reading.en: Now, two years later, Helen herself was about to be married. Her stepfather, the violent Dr. Roylott, had recently moved her to her sister's old room. "He cannot have done so without a reason," she whispered. Holmes leaned forward. "We must hear everything. Tell us, please, of his finances."
reading.cn: 如今，两年后，海伦自己即将结婚。她那性情暴烈的继父罗伊罗特医生，最近把她搬到了姐姐当年的房间。"他这么做不可能没有原因，"她低声说。福尔摩斯前倾。"我们必须听全部事实。请告诉我们，他的财务状况。"
reading.note: He cannot have done so — modal speculation: cannot + have + V-ed (KEY focus)

reading.en: Helen explained that, by her late mother's will, the family income would be greatly reduced if either daughter married. "He might have wanted my sister's death — for the same financial reason that he must now want mine."
reading.cn: 海伦解释说，按照她已故母亲的遗嘱，要是任何一个女儿结婚，家里的收入将大幅减少。"他可能想要姐姐的死——出于同一种经济原因，他现在一定也希望我死。"
reading.note: He might have wanted... — modal speculation: might + have + V-ed (KEY focus) / he must now want — present must

reading.en: Holmes traveled to Stoke Moran that afternoon. He examined the bedroom carefully. The bed was bolted to the floor — strangely, it could not be moved. A bell-rope hung beside the bed but, when Holmes pulled it, no bell rang. Above the bed, in the wall, was a small ventilator opening into Roylott's adjoining room.
reading.cn: 当天下午，福尔摩斯去了斯托克莫兰庄园。他仔细检查了卧室。床被螺栓固定在地板上——奇怪——根本动不了。床边垂着一条铃绳，但福尔摩斯拉了一下，没有铃响。床头墙上有一个通风口，开向罗伊罗特相邻的房间。
reading.note: Sequence of past simple — Holmes's observations (basis for inference)

reading.en: "The bed must have been fixed there for a reason," Holmes said. "And the bell-rope cannot have been built to ring — it must have been built for something else. Whatever passes through the ventilator must descend along the rope, onto the pillow."
reading.cn: "床被钉死在那里一定有原因，"福尔摩斯说。"那条铃绳不可能是用来响铃的——它一定是用来做别的事的。任何穿过通风口的东西，必然顺着这条绳子下来，落在枕头上。"
reading.note: must have been fixed / cannot have been built / must have been built — three modal speculations (KEY focus)

reading.en: That night, Holmes and Watson hid in the bedroom. The candle was out; only a thin shaft of light passed under the door. Around three in the morning, they heard a soft hiss. "It must be coming through now," Holmes whispered. He struck a match — and lashed at the bell-rope with his cane.
reading.cn: 那夜，福尔摩斯和华生藏在卧室里。蜡烛熄了，只有一道薄薄的光从门下透进来。凌晨三点左右，他们听到一阵柔软的嘶声。"它一定是现在过来了，"福尔摩斯低声说。他点燃一根火柴——抽出手杖朝铃绳猛打。
reading.note: It must be coming — present modal speculation / lashed — past action

reading.en: From the next room came a terrible cry. Holmes and Watson rushed in. Dr. Roylott sat dead in his chair, a band of yellow-and-brown spots wound about his head. It was a swamp adder — the most deadly snake in India. The doctor must have trained it to come and go through the ventilator. Tonight, finding the rope blocked, it had returned and bitten him.
reading.cn: 隔壁屋里传出一声惨叫。福尔摩斯和华生冲进去。罗伊罗特医生死在椅子上，头上盘着一条黄棕斑点的带子。那是一条沼泽蛇——印度最毒的蛇。这位医生一定训练过它穿过通风口往返。今晚，发现绳子那边被挡住，它顺原路回来，咬了他自己。
reading.note: must have trained — modal speculation (KEY focus) / Finding the rope blocked — participial reason (L51 review)

reading.en: Walking back to London at dawn, Watson asked how Holmes had reasoned it through. "The fixed bed could only have been placed there to put the sleeper directly under the rope," Holmes said. "The rope that could not ring must have been a path. The whistle she heard must have been the doctor calling the snake home. As for the metallic clang — he must have shut the safe in which he kept it."
reading.cn: 黎明时回伦敦的路上，华生问他是怎么推理出来的。"固定的床只可能是为了让睡着的人正好躺在绳子下方，"福尔摩斯说。"那条不会响的绳子一定是条通路。她听到的口哨声，一定是那位医生召蛇回去。至于那声金属——他一定是关上了装它的保险柜。"
reading.note: Closing — could only have been placed / must have been a path / must have been the doctor calling — full modal speculation cluster

vocab.example_cn: 只有一个男人来追求她。

vocab.example: She refused to pay her taxes.
What had once been a nightshirt.
A long strand of iron-gray hair.

reading.en: Miss Emily Grierson was, by far, the strangest figure in our small Mississippi town. The older she grew, the more closed her house became. The longer she stayed inside, the wilder the rumors grew about what she might be hiding.
reading.cn: 艾米丽·格里尔森小姐是我们这座密西西比小镇里最古怪的人物，远远超过镇上其他人。她年纪越大，那栋房子就关得越严。她待在里面越久，关于她在藏什么的传言就越离奇。
reading.note: by far the strangest — emphatic comparative (KEY focus) / The older... the more... — parallel comparative (KEY focus)

reading.en: When her father died, she was thirty. He had refused all suitors — none of them had been good enough, by his account. Yet no woman, our mothers said, was less prepared for life alone than Emily.
reading.cn: 她父亲去世时，她三十岁。他拒绝过所有追求者——按他的说法，没有一个配得上她。然而，我们的母亲们都说，没有一个女人比艾米丽更不会一个人生活。
reading.note: no woman was less prepared than Emily — comparative with 'no...less than' (KEY focus)

reading.en: After his death, only one man came courting — Homer Barron, a Northerner, a road-foreman, far less dignified than the men her father had turned away. The town disapproved no less strongly than her father would have.
reading.cn: 父亲死后，只有一个男人来追求她——荷马·巴伦，北方人，修路工头，远没有她父亲赶走过的那些人体面。镇上对此的反对，丝毫不亚于她父亲生前会有的反对。
reading.note: far less dignified than — comparative with 'far less' (KEY focus) / no less strongly than — emphatic equality

reading.en: Emily, however, walked with Homer through the streets. The more the town gossiped, the more she seemed to enjoy his company. The older women said: "She has forgotten herself." The younger women said: "Better any husband than none at all."
reading.cn: 艾米丽却照旧和荷马在街上散步。镇上议论越多，她似乎越享受他的陪伴。年长的妇人说："她忘记自己是谁了。"年轻的妇人说："有个丈夫总比没有强。"
reading.note: The more... the more — parallel comparative / Better X than Y — comparative idiom

reading.en: Then Homer disappeared. Some said he had gone north for work; others, that Emily had driven him away. None of these guesses, as it turned out, was anywhere near the truth. Emily lived on, alone, far longer than anyone expected — for nearly forty more years.
reading.cn: 后来荷马消失了。有人说他北上找工作；有人说艾米丽把他赶走了。事后看，这些猜测没有一个接近真相。艾米丽继续活着，独自一人，比所有人预期的都久得多——又过了将近四十年。
reading.note: far longer than expected — comparative with intensifier 'far'

reading.en: She refused to pay her taxes. She refused to allow numbers on her mailbox. She did not appear in public except on rare Sundays, looking smaller and grayer each year. The longer she lived, the less she seemed to belong to our century.
reading.cn: 她拒绝交税。她不让在自己邮箱上挂门牌号。除了偶尔的星期天露面，她不在公开场合出现——每出现一次都显得更小、更灰。她活得越久，就越不像属于我们这个世纪的人。
reading.note: The longer... the less... — parallel comparative

reading.en: When at last Emily died, the town gathered for the funeral. Old men in Confederate uniforms came; women came in their best black. After the burial, our curiosity grew greater than our manners. We climbed the stairs of her house — into a room no living person had entered for forty years.
reading.cn: 艾米丽终于去世时，全镇都来参加葬礼。穿着南军军服的老人来了；女人们穿着她们最好的黑衣前来。下葬之后，我们的好奇心压过了礼数。我们爬上她家的楼梯——走进一个四十年里没有任何活人进过的房间。
reading.note: greater than our manners — comparative with abstract noun

reading.en: Behind a thick layer of dust, on the bed, lay the body of a man — what was left of him — in what had once been a nightshirt. Beside him, on the second pillow, the print of a head. And caught in the fold of the pillow — a long strand of iron-gray hair.
reading.cn: 厚厚一层灰尘底下，床上躺着一个男人的尸体——剩下的部分——身上还穿着曾经是睡衣的东西。在他身边，第二个枕头上有头压过的痕迹。枕头的褶皱里——一缕长长的铁灰色头发。
reading.note: what was left of him — what-clause (review L69)

reading.en: We stood in silence. Emily had not been merely strange. She had been, in the most terrible sense, faithful — more faithful, perhaps, than any of us would dare to be. The longer we looked, the less we understood. Some loves, it seemed, do not end with death — and some houses keep their secrets longer than we can keep ours.
reading.cn: 我们沉默地站着。艾米丽不只是古怪。她以最可怕的方式忠诚——也许比我们任何人敢做到的都更忠诚。我们看得越久，懂得越少。看来有些爱情不会因死亡而结束——有些房子能比我们更久地守着秘密。
reading.note: Closing — more faithful... than any of us would dare / longer than we can keep — comparative cluster

vocab.meaning: n. 鸽子（白鸽常作和平象征）

vocab.example: The Jewish quota was one in twenty.
vocab.example_cn: 犹太人配额是二十取一。

vocab.example: Walking corridors I had never seen.
vocab.example_cn: 走在我从未见过的走廊里。

vocab.example: As if he had been crowned.

vocab.meaning: n. 种族迫害（特指对犹太人）
n. 残疾人（旧；今天用 disabled 替代）

reading.en: When I was nine, I wanted, more than anything, a dovecot of my own — a small wooden house in which I could keep two pairs of doves. My father, a man for whom education was the highest goal, said: 'If you pass into the gymnasium with the highest mark, the dovecot will be yours.'
reading.cn: 我九岁时，最想要的就是一座属于自己的鸽舍——一间小小的木屋，可以养两对鸽子。我父亲，一个把教育当作至高目标的人，说："你只要以最高分考进文科中学，鸽舍就是你的。"
reading.note: in which I could keep — prepositional relative (L71 review) / for whom education was — prepositional relative (L71 review)

reading.en: I was, by far, the youngest applicant in the city that year. The Jewish quota was one in twenty. The harder I studied, the more terrified I became. The night before the exam, I dreamed I was already inside the school, walking corridors I had never seen — as though I had always belonged there.
reading.cn: 那一年我是全市报考的孩子中最小的，远远最小。犹太人录取名额是二十取一。我学得越用功，就越害怕。考试前一夜，我梦见自己已经进了那所学校，走在我从未见过的走廊里——仿佛我一直就属于那里。
reading.note: by far the youngest — superlative emphasis (L74) / The harder... the more — double comparative (L74) / as though I had always belonged — as though + past perfect (L72)

reading.en: I passed. I passed with the highest mark. My father, on the day of the news, walked through the streets as if he had been crowned. I myself only wanted my dovecot — a thing he had promised, and a thing of which I now constantly dreamed.
reading.cn: 我考上了。我以最高分考上了。消息传来的那天，父亲走在街上——仿佛他登基了。而我只想要那座鸽舍——一件他答应过、我如今时时梦到的东西。
reading.note: as if he had been crowned — as if + past perfect (L72) / a thing of which I dreamed — prepositional relative (L71)

reading.en: On the morning of the new term, I went to buy the doves. The hunchback Ivan, from whom I always bought, was kindest of all the dealers. "Today is your day," he said, smiling. He gave me four doves — two pigeons of pure white, two of mottled brown — for which I had saved a whole summer.
reading.cn: 新学期开学那天清晨，我去买鸽子。驼背伊万——我一直从他那儿买——是所有鸽贩里最和气的。"今天是你的日子，"他笑着说。他给了我四只鸽子——两只纯白的，两只褐色斑点的——我为这些鸽子存了整整一个夏天的钱。
reading.note: from whom I always bought / for which I had saved — prepositional relatives (L71 review) / kindest of all — superlative

reading.en: Coming home through the market square, I held the basket of doves to my chest. The streets, on which I had walked all my life, looked unfamiliar that morning. Crowds had gathered. Faces I had known since I was a baby looked at me as though they had never seen me before.
reading.cn: 我穿过集市广场往家走，把装鸽子的篮子抱在胸口。我从小走过的那些街道，那个早晨看上去陌生。人群聚了起来。我从襁褓里就认识的那些面孔，看着我——仿佛从未见过我一般。
reading.note: on which I had walked all my life — prepositional relative (L71) / as though they had never seen — as though + past perfect (L72)

reading.en: Something must have happened. The pogrom must have started while I was at the market. Glass had been broken. Smoke was rising over the Jewish quarter. As I ran toward home, an old woman — a stranger — caught me by the arm. 'Boy,' she whispered, 'today is not a day for doves.'
reading.cn: 一定是出事了。我去集市那会儿，迫害一定已经开始了。玻璃被砸碎。烟从犹太区那边升起来。我朝家跑去时，一位老妇人——一个陌生人——一把抓住我的手臂。'孩子，'她低声说，'今天不是适合鸽子的日子。'
reading.note: Something must have happened / The pogrom must have started — modal speculation (L73 review)

reading.en: I did not understand. I kept running. At the corner of Pushkin Street, an old man, the cripple Makarenko, sat on his cart. He had always sold cigarettes; today, his face was as red as if it had been painted. He saw the basket I was carrying. He could not have done worse, perhaps, than what he did next.
reading.cn: 我没听懂。我继续跑。在普希金街角，瘸腿的马卡连科老人坐在他的车上。他从前一直卖烟；今天他的脸通红——仿佛被涂了颜料。他看见我抱着的篮子。他大概再也做不出比接下来的事更坏的事了。
reading.note: as red as if it had been painted — as if + past perfect (L72) / He could not have done worse — modal speculation (L73)

reading.en: He took one of my doves — the one I cared for most — and crushed it in his hand against my temple. The wet feathers, the still-warm body, struck against my eye. "There," he said. "There is your school."
reading.cn: 他从篮子里抓起一只鸽子——我最疼爱的那只——在我太阳穴上把它捏碎了。湿羽毛、还温的小身体，砸在我眼睛上。"瞧，"他说。"那就是你的学校。"
reading.note: the one I cared for most — relative + superlative

reading.en: I walked home with feathers in my hair and the dead bird against my cheek. Inside, my father was packing what little we still had. He looked at me. He said nothing. The dovecot, by far the most beautiful thing of which I had ever dreamed, was never built. The school I had entered with the highest mark, I never returned to. Some doors, once you have seen what stands behind them, you cannot walk through again.
reading.cn: 我头发里粘着羽毛，脸上贴着那只死掉的鸽子，走回家。屋里，父亲正在收拾我们仅剩的东西。他看着我。一句话也没说。那座鸽舍——远远是我梦想过的最美的东西——再没有建起来。我以最高分考进的那所学校，我再也没回去过。有些门——你看到过门后面的东西之后——就再也走不进去了。
reading.note: Closing — by far the most beautiful... of which I had ever dreamed — superlative + prep relative (L74+L71) / Some doors... you cannot walk through — discourse closure

vocab.meaning: phr. 内战（特指美国南北战争）

reading.en: On a stormy September evening, John Openshaw came to Baker Street. Holmes was reading; Watson was, too. The young man's face was pale, and so were his hands.
reading.cn: 九月一个风雨大作的晚上，约翰·奥彭肖来到贝克街。福尔摩斯在看书；华生也在看。这位年轻人脸色苍白，他的手也是。
reading.note: was, too — substitute auxiliary (KEY focus) / so were his hands — so + auxiliary inversion (KEY focus)

reading.en: "My uncle received a letter from India eight years ago," Openshaw began. "Inside were five orange pips and a note: K.K.K. He went pale, just as my father did six months later, and just as I do now." Holmes nodded, as did Watson.
reading.cn: "我叔叔八年前收到了一封从印度寄来的信，"奥彭肖开口。"信里是五颗橘核和一张字条：K.K.K. 他脸色变白了——六个月后我父亲也一样，现在我也一样。"福尔摩斯点点头，华生也点头。
reading.note: just as my father did / just as I do now — do as substitute (KEY focus) / as did Watson — as + did + subject (KEY focus)

reading.en: "My uncle had returned from America after the Civil War," Openshaw continued. "Some did well there; he did not. He had business in Florida, where many former Confederates also did. He came back rich, but bitter. Within seven weeks of the letter, he was found dead. The police called it an accident; we did not."
reading.cn: "我叔叔在内战之后从美国回来，"奥彭肖接着说。"有人在那儿混得好；他没有。他在佛罗里达做生意，许多前邦联人也在那儿。他回来时富有，但满腹怨气。收到那封信七周内，他就被发现死了。警察说是意外；我们不那么认为。"
reading.note: Some did well; he did not — do contrast (KEY focus) / many former Confederates also did — also did substitute / we did not — negative substitute

reading.en: Holmes asked to see the letter. Openshaw did not have it; neither did he have his uncle's diary. "Both were burned," he said. "By whom?" Holmes asked. "By my uncle himself, I think — or so I was told."
reading.cn: 福尔摩斯要看那封信。奥彭肖没有；他叔叔的日记也没有。"两样都被烧了，"他说。"被谁烧的？"福尔摩斯问。"我想是我叔叔自己烧的——至少别人是这么告诉我的。"
reading.note: neither did he have — neither + auxiliary + subject (KEY focus) / Both were burned — pronoun substitute

reading.en: Holmes leaned forward. "And your father — when his letter came — what did he do?" "Nothing," Openshaw said quietly. "He should have gone to the police. He did not. Three weeks later, he, too, was dead. Now my letter has come. The pips arrived this morning. I came to you, hoping you can do what neither of them could."
reading.cn: 福尔摩斯前倾。"那你父亲——他收到信时——做了什么？""什么也没做，"奥彭肖轻声说。"他本该去报警。他没去。三周后，他也死了。现在轮到我了。橘核今天早上到的。我来找你，希望你能做到他们俩都没能做到的事。"
reading.note: did not — negative substitute (L67 review) / he, too, was dead — too substitute / what neither of them could — neither + modal

reading.en: Holmes leaned back. "Mr. Openshaw, the letter was sent from a ship. The Lone Star, an American sailing-vessel, must have arrived at Pondicherry around the date your uncle's letter was posted. The ship is even now in the English Channel. So is your enemy."
reading.cn: 福尔摩斯往后一靠。"奥彭肖先生，这封信是从船上寄来的。「孤星号」，一艘美国帆船，一定在你叔叔信寄出的时候停在过本地治里。那艘船此刻就在英吉利海峡。你的敌人也在。"
reading.note: So is your enemy — so + auxiliary + subject (KEY focus)

reading.en: "Go home now," Holmes said urgently. "Lock everything. Tomorrow we shall act." Openshaw thanked him and left. Watson, watching the rain, murmured: "I do not like to let him walk alone." "Nor do I," said Holmes, frowning.
reading.cn: "现在就回家，"福尔摩斯急促地说。"把一切都锁好。明天我们就行动。"奥彭肖谢过他，离开了。华生看着外面的雨，喃喃道："我不想让他一个人走。""我也不想，"福尔摩斯皱着眉说。
reading.note: Nor do I — nor + auxiliary + subject (KEY focus) — agreement with negative

reading.en: In the morning, the news came: a young man had been found drowned in the Thames near Waterloo Bridge. There were no marks of struggle. There were no witnesses, either. Holmes set down the paper. "We were too late," he said. "I was. So was Watson. So was Scotland Yard. The Lone Star sailed at midnight."
reading.cn: 早上，消息传来：滑铁卢桥附近的泰晤士河里发现一个淹死的年轻人。没有打斗痕迹。也没有目击者。福尔摩斯把报纸放下。"我们晚了，"他说。"我晚了。华生晚了。苏格兰场也晚了。「孤星号」已在午夜启航。"
reading.note: There were no witnesses, either — either + negative agreement / I was. So was Watson. So was Scotland Yard. — chained 'so was' substitution

reading.en: Three months later, Holmes received a single newspaper clipping. A bark named the Lone Star had been lost in an Atlantic gale; only a fragment of the stern, on which the ship's name was painted, was ever found. "The sea has done what we could not," Holmes said quietly. "And so, in its own way, has justice."
reading.cn: 三个月后，福尔摩斯收到一张报纸剪报。一艘名为"孤星号"的帆船在大西洋的一场风暴中失踪了；只找到一块刻着船名的船尾残片。"大海做到了我们没能做到的事，"福尔摩斯平静地说。"以它自己的方式——正义也做到了。"
reading.note: Closing — has done what we could not / And so... has justice — substitute auxiliary chain

vocab.meaning: n. 心理学家；心理医生

vocab.example: Guilty of giving them too much.

reading.en: In the Hadley family's automated house of the future, every wall could project any place on earth. The children, Wendy and Peter, were obsessed with using the nursery — a room capable of producing a fully simulated environment.
reading.cn: 在哈德利家未来式的自动化房子里，每一面墙都能投射出地球上任何地方。两个孩子——温迪和彼得——着迷于用那间育儿室——一个能完整模拟任何环境的房间。
reading.note: obsessed with using — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus) / capable of producing — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus)

reading.en: For weeks, the nursery had been showing the same scene: an African veldt, hot and dry, with vultures circling and lions feeding on something the parents could not quite see. George Hadley grew tired of asking his children to choose another setting. They were, he admitted, very good at ignoring him.
reading.cn: 几个星期以来，育儿室一直在显示同一个场景：非洲草原，炎热干燥，秃鹫在头顶盘旋，几只狮子在吃什么——做父母的看不太清。乔治·哈德利对让孩子换个布景这件事感到厌烦。他承认，他们非常擅长不理睬他。
reading.note: tired of asking — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus) / good at ignoring — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus)

reading.en: His wife, Lydia, was worried about leaving the children alone in the room. She was not interested in arguing with George; she was just afraid. "I think there is something wrong with this house," she said. "Or with the children."
reading.cn: 他妻子莉迪亚担心把孩子单独留在那间屋子里。她并不想和乔治争论；她只是害怕。"我觉得这栋房子有点不对，"她说。"要么就是孩子有点不对。"
reading.note: worried about leaving / interested in arguing — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus)

reading.en: George went into the nursery alone. He was not used to feeling the temperature change so drastically when he stepped inside. The lions, on seeing him, lifted their heads. He was surprised at being recognized — they fixed on him, and on him only.
reading.cn: 乔治独自走进育儿室。他不习惯一进去温度就变化得这么剧烈。狮子看见他，抬起了头。他被它们认出，让他吃了一惊——它们盯着他，只盯着他。
reading.note: used to feeling — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus) / on seeing him — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus) / surprised at being recognized — preposition + V-ing (passive)

reading.en: When he tried to change the setting, the room refused. The children had locked the program. George was capable of overriding it — but he was not certain about doing so. Doing so would mean punishing his children, something he had little experience of.
reading.cn: 他想换布景时，房间不响应了。孩子们锁住了程序。乔治本可以越权解锁——但他不确定该不该这么做。这么做意味着惩罚孩子——而他在惩罚孩子这件事上几乎没有经验。
reading.note: capable of overriding / certain about doing / experience of punishing — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus)

reading.en: That evening, George called a child psychologist. The doctor, after walking through the house, was firm. "You are guilty of giving them too much. The room obeys their wishes — including their wishes about you. You must close the nursery before the situation becomes worse."
reading.cn: 那天傍晚，乔治叫来了一位儿童心理医生。医生在屋里走了一圈，态度很坚决。"你犯了给他们太多的错。这间屋子顺从他们的愿望——包括他们对你的愿望。在事情变得更糟之前，你必须把育儿室关掉。"
reading.note: guilty of giving / before becoming worse — preposition + V-ing

reading.en: George closed the nursery. The children began crying. They begged him to reconsider. They accused him of not loving them. By midnight, they were calmer. They asked, sweetly, for one last hour in the room — "before saying goodbye to it forever." George, exhausted from arguing, agreed.
reading.cn: 乔治把育儿室关了。孩子们哭起来。他们求他再考虑。指责他不爱他们。到了午夜，他们冷静下来。他们甜甜地请求——再让他们在那间屋里待最后一个小时——"算是和它告别"。乔治从争吵里筋疲力尽，同意了。
reading.note: accused him of not loving — preposition + V-ing (negative) / before saying goodbye — preposition + V-ing / exhausted from arguing — preposition + V-ing

reading.en: When George and Lydia entered the nursery to fetch the children, the door slammed behind them. The walls were the African veldt. The lions, only ten feet away, advanced. The children, somewhere outside the room, must have been listening to the screams. George had time only for understanding what had happened — and for regretting it.
reading.cn: 乔治和莉迪亚进屋去叫孩子时，门在他们身后砰地关上。墙变成了非洲草原。狮子，离他们只有十英尺，正在逼近。孩子们一定在屋外某处听着惨叫声。乔治只来得及——明白发生了什么——以及为之后悔。
reading.note: for understanding / for regretting — preposition + V-ing (KEY focus) / time only for + V-ing (collocation)

reading.en: When the psychologist came back the next morning, the children were sitting calmly in the nursery, eating sandwiches. They were no longer interested in arguing. The vultures had finished. "We were almost too late in stopping this," the doctor said. "Or perhaps we still are."
reading.cn: 第二天早上心理医生回来时，孩子们正安静地坐在育儿室里吃三明治。他们不再有兴趣争论了。秃鹫已经吃完。"我们差点来不及阻止这一切，"医生说。"或许，我们还是来不及。"
reading.note: Closing — interested in arguing / late in stopping — preposition + V-ing

vocab.example: A fine, then a day in jail.

reading.en: In Babylon, every citizen took part in the lottery. Admittedly, this was, at first, the kind of innocent lottery known anywhere — small prizes drawn weekly, a few coins lost or won. Granted, no one took it very seriously.
reading.cn: 在巴比伦，每个公民都参加彩票。诚然，这一开始是各地常见的那种无害彩票——每周开奖、奖金不多，输赢都是几个硬币的事。诚然，没人把它当回事。
reading.note: Admittedly — concessive adverb opener (KEY focus) / Granted — concessive adverb (KEY focus)

reading.en: In time, the merchants who ran the lottery introduced "negative prizes" — small punishments for losers. A fine, then a day in jail. Arguably, this was a small change. That said, it was the first move toward a far darker game.
reading.cn: 后来，主办彩票的商人引入了"负奖品"——给输家的小惩罚。先是一笔罚金，再是一天牢狱。可以说，这只是个小改动。话虽如此，它却是迈向远更黑暗游戏的第一步。
reading.note: Arguably — concessive (qualified) adverb (KEY focus) / That said — concessive marker (KEY focus)

reading.en: In every generation, the lottery grew bolder. Winners now received palaces and slaves; losers were exiled, blinded, or worse. Mind you, the games remained legal — and, indeed, mandatory. By law, every citizen drew at least once a year.
reading.cn: 一代又一代，彩票越变越大胆。赢家现在能拿到宫殿和奴隶；输家被流放、被弄瞎，或更糟。话说回来，这些游戏依然合法——并且，事实上，是强制的。按法律规定，每个公民至少每年抽一次。
reading.note: Mind you — concessive marker (KEY focus) / and, indeed — emphatic concession
