reading.en: Outsiders, hearing of the system, were appalled. To them, the cruelty seemed obvious. To us Babylonians, however, the lottery had become indistinguishable from life itself. Granted, this is hard to explain. Then again, every people has its own absurdities — ours simply have a name.
reading.cn: 外人听说这套制度，都感到震惊。对他们而言，残忍是明显的。然而对我们巴比伦人来说，彩票已经和生活本身不可分割了。诚然，这很难解释。话说回来，每个民族都有自己的荒诞——我们的只是有个名字而已。
reading.note: Granted / Then again — concessive adverbs (KEY focus)

reading.en: The Company — for so it came to be called — gradually took over even small private decisions. If a man fell in love, the Company decreed by lottery whether he could marry. Admittedly, the lots were sometimes kind. Often, however, they were cruel without reason.
reading.cn: "公司"——后来人们这么称呼它——逐渐连小小的私人决定也接管了。一个男人爱上一个人，公司就用抽签决定他能不能结婚。诚然，抽出的签有时很仁慈。然而更多时候，它毫无理由地残忍。
reading.note: Admittedly / however — concessive structures

reading.en: By my generation, no event in Babylon could be said, with certainty, not to have been the result of the lottery. The man who saved you from drowning, the woman who stole from you, the law that taxed you — arguably, all of it the lottery's work. That said, none of it could be proven.
reading.cn: 到我这代，巴比伦没有一件事可以确定地说不是抽签的结果。救你命的人、偷你东西的人、向你征税的法律——可以说，全是彩票之手。话虽如此，谁也证明不了。
reading.note: arguably — concessive (KEY focus) / That said — concessive (KEY focus)

reading.en: Some say the Company no longer exists — that it has dissolved into the air, into chance, into the secret ordering of the world. Others — and admittedly I am one — believe it has only become more total: that everything we call "fate" or "fortune" is, in truth, a draw.
reading.cn: 有人说公司已经不存在了——它已经溶化在空气里、在偶然里、在世界秘密的运作里。也有人——诚然我是其中之一——相信它只是变得更彻底：我们所谓的"命运"或"运气"，其实就是一次抽签。
reading.note: and admittedly I am one — concessive (KEY focus) / parenthetical concession

reading.en: Foreign visitors sometimes ask: "Are you not afraid?" To which I answer, with a shrug: "Granted, the lottery has taken much from me. Then again, what could be taken that was not, originally, given by the same hand?"
reading.cn: 外国来访者有时问："你不害怕吗？"对此我耸耸肩答道："诚然，彩票从我这里拿走了很多。话说回来，能被拿走的，原本不也是同一只手给的吗？"
reading.note: To which I answer — preposition relative (L71 review) / Granted / Then again — concessive cluster

reading.en: A clever European once said to me: "If your lottery is everything, it is nothing." Admittedly, this was elegant. That said, it missed the point: in Babylon, we have stopped trying to tell the lottery apart from anything else. We have, you might say, simply learned to live inside the draw.
reading.cn: 一个聪明的欧洲人曾对我说："如果你们的彩票就是一切，那它就什么都不是。"诚然，这话说得漂亮。话虽如此，他没说到点子上：在巴比伦，我们已经不再尝试把彩票从别的东西里分出来。可以说，我们只是学会了——活在那场抽签里。
reading.note: Closing — Admittedly... That said... — full concessive structure / you might say — qualifying

vocab.example: Left to peel from the wall.
This notebook has not been found.
I was creeping along the wall.

reading.en: It is rarely that ordinary people like John and myself are given a strange old house for the summer. Yet that, I am told, is exactly what has happened. The house was once owned by a wealthy family. It is now being rented to us at a very low price.
reading.cn: 像约翰和我这样普通的人，很少能在夏天得到一栋古怪的老房子住。可是，我被告知，眼下正是这种情况。这栋房子从前属于一个有钱人家。如今它正被以很低的价钱租给我们。
reading.note: are given / I am told / was once owned / is now being rented — passive constructions chain (KEY focus)

reading.en: John is a doctor. Perhaps — though I would never say so to any living soul — that is one reason why I am not getting better. You see, I am told I am suffering only from a slight nervous depression. I am to do nothing but rest. I am forbidden to write a single word.
reading.cn: 约翰是医生。也许——尽管这话我绝不会对任何活人说——这正是我没有好起来的原因之一。你知道，他们告诉我，我只是患了轻微的神经性抑郁。我除了休息什么也不该做。我被禁止写下任何一个字。
reading.note: I am told / I am to do / I am forbidden — passive + obligation passives (KEY focus)

reading.en: I have been put in the upstairs room — formerly, I think, a nursery. The wallpaper is the most horrid yellow I have ever seen. It is torn off in patches; in others, it has been left to peel from the wall.
reading.cn: 我被安置在楼上那间屋——我猜，从前是间育儿室。墙纸是我见过的最丑的黄色。有的地方被一块块撕掉了；另一些地方，则任其从墙上脱落。
reading.note: I have been put / It is torn off / has been left to peel — present perfect passive variations (KEY focus)

reading.en: John is to be away every weekend. I am not to leave the room. I am to be looked after by his sister, Jennie, who is, I am assured, a perfect housekeeper. Jennie, however, is being watched by me as carefully as I am being watched by her.
reading.cn: 约翰每个周末都要外出。我不许离开这间屋。我会由他妹妹詹妮照顾——他们再三向我保证，她是个完美的管家。然而，詹妮被我像她监视我一样仔细地监视着。
reading.note: is to be / I am to be looked after / is being watched / am being watched — passive infinitive + continuous passive

reading.en: Days are passed in this room. Nothing is permitted but lying down and looking at the paper. The pattern, I have begun to see, is being moved by something — by someone — behind it.
reading.cn: 日子一天天在这间屋里过去。除了躺着看墙纸，别的什么都不被允许。我开始看出来：墙纸上的图案，正被某种东西——某个人——在它后面推动着。
reading.note: Days are passed / Nothing is permitted / is being moved — passive constructions

reading.en: By moonlight, the figure is clearer. A woman — I am sure of it — is being held inside the pattern. She moves slightly when no one is watching. She has, I now believe, been imprisoned there for a long time.
reading.cn: 借着月光，那个身影更清晰了。一个女人——我确信——正被困在那个图案里。当没人看时，她会微微动一下。我现在相信——她已经被困在那里很久了。
reading.note: is being held / has been imprisoned — present continuous passive + present perfect passive

reading.en: I am no longer to write — that is what I have been told, repeatedly, since the first day. But this notebook has not been found. I keep it hidden where the paper has been cut away from a corner. The paper, I notice, has been cut away in several places. Someone before me, perhaps, was trying to free her too.
reading.cn: 我不被允许再写——这话是我从第一天起就被反复告知的。但这本笔记本还没被发现。我把它藏在墙纸被撕掉的一角里。我注意到，墙纸有好几处被撕掉了。也许在我之前，有人也在试着把她放出来。
reading.note: I am no longer to / I have been told / has not been found / has been cut away — multiple passives (KEY focus)

reading.en: Tonight is the last night. We are to leave tomorrow. Everything has been packed. The room has been stripped — except the wallpaper, which cannot be removed. Tonight, while John is away, the woman and I are going to be free at last. The paper has been peeled, in long strips, all around the room. The woman is being released, by me, from the pattern.
reading.cn: 今晚是最后一夜。我们明天就要离开。一切都被打包了。屋子被搬空了——只剩墙纸——它撕不下来。今夜，趁约翰不在，那个女人和我终于要自由了。墙纸已经被撕成长长的条，绕屋一圈。那个女人——正被我——从图案里放出来。
reading.note: are to leave / has been packed / has been stripped / cannot be removed / is being released — passive cluster

reading.en: When John returned the next morning, the door had been locked from inside. He called out; he was not answered. He broke it down. The room had been stripped to the floor — long yellow paper, torn off in strips. I was creeping along the wall. "I have got out at last," I told him, "in spite of you and Jane! And I have pulled off most of the paper, so you can't put me back!" He fainted. I had to creep over him every time.
reading.cn: 第二天早上约翰回来时，门已经从里面被锁上了。他喊我；没被回应。他把门撞开。屋子已经被剥得只剩地板——长长的黄色墙纸，一条条被撕掉。我正沿着墙根爬。"我终于出来了，"我告诉他，"不管你和简怎么阻止！我把大半墙纸都撕下来了，你再也没法把我塞回去！"他晕倒了。我每次都必须从他身上爬过去。
reading.note: Closing — had been locked / was not answered / had been stripped / torn off — past perfect passives

vocab.example_cn: 一个关于大教堂的节目。

vocab.example: I was being instructed by him.
His fingers riding with the pen.

reading.en: This blind man, an old friend of my wife's, was on his way to spend the night. His wife had just died. Admittedly, I was not looking forward to his visit. Granted, I had no real reason for that. I just was.
reading.cn: 这位盲人，是我妻子的一个老朋友，要来过夜。他妻子刚去世。诚然，我不期待他的拜访。诚然，我没有真正的理由。我就是不想。
reading.note: Admittedly / Granted — concessive adverbs (L78 review) / I just was — substitution (L76 review)

reading.en: I was bothered by his being blind. My wife had been writing to him for ten years; I had not. She was looking forward to seeing him; I was not. She was excited about cooking dinner; so was she about everything that night.
reading.cn: 他眼盲这件事让我心里别扭。我妻子和他通信已经十年了；我没有。她盼着见他；我不盼。她兴奋着做晚饭；那一夜她对一切都兴奋。
reading.note: bothered by his being blind — preposition + V-ing (L77 review) / I had not / I was not — ellipsis (L76 review) / so was she — substitute (L76)

reading.en: When the man arrived, I was surprised at finding him bigger than I had expected. He had been driven from the train station by a friend. He was wearing dark glasses, but they had been pushed up onto his forehead. "I haven't been blind all my life," he said.
reading.cn: 那人来到时，我惊讶地发现他比我想的高大。他是被一位朋友从火车站送来的。他戴着墨镜——但已被推到了额头上。"我不是一辈子都瞎，"他说。
reading.note: surprised at finding — preposition + V-ing (L77) / had been driven / had been pushed — past perfect passive (L79)

reading.en: After dinner, my wife went to bed early. The blind man and I were left alone, both of us tired of pretending. We were not interested in talking — neither of us was. So we just watched television. Or, rather, I watched, and he listened.
reading.cn: 晚饭后，我妻子早早上床睡了。盲人和我被留下，我们俩都厌倦了假装。我们都不想说话——两人都不想。所以我们就看电视。或者说，我看，他听。
reading.note: tired of pretending — preposition + V-ing (L77) / interested in talking — preposition + V-ing / neither of us was — neither + auxiliary (L76)

reading.en: A program about cathedrals came on. Admittedly, I was not paying much attention. But the blind man, having only sound to go by, was. "Do you know what a cathedral looks like?" he asked. "I have heard about them. They were built to last forever, isn't that right?"
reading.cn: 电视上来了一个关于大教堂的节目。诚然，我没怎么在听。可盲人——他只能靠声音判断——在听。"你知道大教堂长什么样吗？"他问。"我听说过。它们是为了千秋万代而建的，对吧？"
reading.note: Admittedly — concessive (L78) / having only sound to go by — participial (L51) / were built to last — passive + infinitive (L79)

reading.en: I tried to describe one. I was not capable of doing it. The words I needed were not coming. "Forget it," he said. "Get me a piece of paper. We are going to draw one. I am going to put my hand on yours, and you are going to draw, and I am going to follow."
reading.cn: 我试着描述一座。我做不到。我需要的词没冒出来。"算了吧，"他说。"给我一张纸。我们要画一座。我把手放在你手上，你画，我跟着。"
reading.note: capable of doing — preposition + V-ing (L77) / are going to draw / am going to follow — future intention

reading.en: I found a paper bag. I was being instructed by a blind man on how to draw a cathedral. Admittedly, this was strange. That said, I did as he told me. He put his hand on top of mine. I drew arches, doors, windows. He felt every line being made, his fingers riding gently with the pen.
reading.cn: 我找到一个纸袋。我正被一个盲人教着怎么画大教堂。诚然，这很奇怪。话虽如此，我照他说的做了。他把手放在我的手上。我画拱门、门、窗户。他感觉到每一条线被画出来，他的手指随着笔轻轻动着。
reading.note: I was being instructed — continuous passive (L79) / Admittedly... That said — concessive (L78) / every line being made — passive participle

reading.en: "Are your eyes closed?" he asked. They were not. "Close them." I closed them. "Don't open them yet. Keep drawing." I kept drawing — flying buttresses, windows, towers. The pen was being moved as much by him now as by me.
reading.cn: "你的眼睛闭着吗？"他问。我没闭。"闭上。"我闭上了。"先别睁开。继续画。"我继续画——飞拱、窗户、塔楼。这支笔现在——是被他和我同样在推动着。
reading.note: They were not — ellipsis (L76) / The pen was being moved — continuous passive (L79)

reading.en: Then he took his hand away. "Take a look. What do you think?" I kept my eyes closed. I knew I had to. I felt I was inside something larger than my own house. I was not in any place I knew. "It is really something," I said.
reading.cn: 然后他把手拿开了。"看看吧。你觉得怎么样？"我没睁开眼。我知道我必须不睁。我感觉自己在一个比自己的家更大的东西里。我不在我认识的任何地方。"这真不一般，"我说。
reading.note: Closing — kept my eyes closed / had to / was not in any place — ellipsis chain (L76 review)

vocab.meaning: adj. 无敌的；不可战胜的

reading.en: There once lived a hare who was known to be the fastest creature in the forest. He was said to have won every race for ten years. Other animals seemed to be afraid of even challenging him.
reading.cn: 从前有一只野兔——大家都知道，他是林子里跑得最快的生物。据说他连续十年赢得了每一场比赛。别的动物似乎连挑战他都害怕。
reading.note: was known to be / was said to have won — passive + perfect/simple infinitives (KEY focus)

reading.en: A tortoise, slow and unimpressive, decided to challenge him. The hare laughed. "You appear to have lost your mind, friend. To be racing me is to have already lost."
reading.cn: 一只缓慢、毫不起眼的乌龟决定挑战他。野兔大笑。"朋友，你看起来已经发疯了。要和我比赛，就等于已经输了。"
reading.note: appear to have lost — perfect infinitive (KEY focus) / To be racing me — continuous infinitive / to have already lost — perfect infinitive (KEY focus)

reading.en: The race was set for the next morning. All the animals came. The hare seemed to have prepared for nothing — he warmed up casually, ate a carrot, even closed his eyes for a moment. The tortoise, meanwhile, was seen to be checking the path step by step.
reading.cn: 比赛定在第二天早上。所有动物都来了。野兔看起来什么也没准备——他随意热身，吃了一根胡萝卜，甚至闭眼了一会儿。而乌龟，则被人看到一步一步地查看赛道。
reading.note: seemed to have prepared — perfect infinitive (KEY focus) / was seen to be checking — passive + continuous infinitive (KEY focus)

reading.en: The race began. The hare shot ahead. Within a minute, the tortoise was already nowhere to be seen behind him. "Easy enough," the hare thought. "I deserve to be resting now." He sat down by the path under a tree.
reading.cn: 比赛开始。野兔冲了出去。一分钟之内，乌龟已经远远落在身后看不见了。"轻松，"野兔想。"我现在配休息一下。"他在路边一棵树下坐下来。
reading.note: nowhere to be seen — passive infinitive (KEY focus) / deserve to be resting — continuous infinitive after deserve

reading.en: He was, however, soon found to have fallen asleep. The tortoise, plodding past, did not even pause. He was determined not to be slowed down by the hare's tricks. He kept moving — slowly, but without stopping.
reading.cn: 然而过不久，他就被发现睡着了。乌龟踱步走过去，连停一下都没停。他下定决心不被野兔的把戏拖慢。他一直在走——慢，但不停。
reading.note: was found to have fallen — passive + perfect infinitive (KEY focus) / determined not to be slowed down — passive infinitive (KEY focus)

reading.en: The hare woke. The sun was already past noon. He was furious to have lost so much time. He started running again — fast, faster than before — but the tortoise was already to be seen at the finish line, just three steps from victory.
reading.cn: 野兔醒了。太阳已经过了正午。他气坏了，因为已经丢了这么多时间。他又开始跑——快，比之前更快——可乌龟已经能在终点线那边看到了，离胜利只差三步。
reading.note: furious to have lost — adjective + perfect infinitive (KEY focus) / was already to be seen — be + to + passive infinitive

reading.en: The tortoise crossed the line. The crowd went wild. The hare arrived a second too late. "I appear to have been outrun," he muttered. "I, who was thought to have been unbeatable."
reading.cn: 乌龟越过了终点。人群沸腾了。野兔晚了一秒到。"我看来被超过了，"他喃喃地说。"我——一个本以为不会输的人。"
reading.note: appear to have been outrun — passive perfect infinitive (KEY focus) / was thought to have been unbeatable — passive perfect infinitive (KEY focus)

reading.en: A young animal asked the tortoise the secret. "I did not start fast," he said. "But I never stopped. The hare seemed to have forgotten that to win is not to be the fastest — it is to keep moving until the end."
reading.cn: 一只小动物问乌龟秘诀。"我不是一开始就快，"他说。"但我没停过。野兔似乎忘了——所谓赢，不是最快——而是一直走到终点。"
reading.note: seemed to have forgotten — perfect infinitive / to win is not to be / it is to keep moving — to + V infinitive

reading.en: The hare, defeated, walked home alone. He had reason to be ashamed — but he also had reason, perhaps, to be grateful. To have lost was, after years of winning, the only way for him to have been forced to think at all. Some mornings, that is exactly what one needs to have happened.
reading.cn: 野兔输了，独自走回家。他有理由感到羞愧——也许还有理由感到庆幸。在赢了那么多年之后，输——可能是他唯一能被迫真正思考的方式。有些早晨，正需要这样的事发生过。
reading.note: Closing — to have lost / to have been forced — perfect infinitives / what one needs to have happened — abstract infinitive structure

reading.en: Thoreau's most famous essay was written in 1849 — a meditation on the relationship between citizen and government. The author's refusal to pay his tax had led to a single night in jail. The brevity of the imprisonment, however, was less important than the clarity of the realization it produced.
reading.cn: 梭罗最出名的散文写于1849年——是对公民与政府关系的一次沉思。作者拒交税款的行为，让他在监狱里待了一夜。然而那次监禁的短暂——并不比它带来的认识的清晰更重要。
reading.note: the relationship between... / The author's refusal / the brevity / the imprisonment / the clarity / the realization — chain of nominalizations (KEY focus)

reading.en: Thoreau's argument begins with a denial of the standard claim that 'the government governs us best which governs least.' His extension of this claim — that the best government is the one which does not govern at all — was, at the time, a startling provocation.
reading.cn: 梭罗的论证以否认一个流行的说法开始：'治理我们最好的政府是治理最少的政府。'他把这个说法推到极致——最好的政府是根本不治理的政府——这在当时是一个惊人的挑战。
reading.note: the denial / the standard claim / His extension / a startling provocation — verb→noun nominalization

reading.en: His objection was not to government as such, but to the legitimization of injustice through compliance. The American government's protection of slavery, in his view, made any taxpayer's contribution an endorsement of the system.
reading.cn: 他反对的不是政府本身，而是通过服从而对不义的合法化。在他看来，美国政府对奴隶制的保护——使任何纳税人的贡献都成为对该制度的支持。
reading.note: His objection / the legitimization / injustice through compliance / The protection / a taxpayer's contribution / an endorsement — heavy nominalization (KEY focus)

reading.en: The proper response to such a state, Thoreau insisted, was withdrawal of consent. The simplest expression of this withdrawal was the non-payment of the poll tax. The government's seizure of his body in punishment, he argued, only made the wrongness of its claim more visible.
reading.cn: 梭罗坚持说，对这样一个国家，正确的回应是撤回同意。这种撤回最简单的表达就是不交人头税。他争辩说，政府以监禁的方式抓走他的身体——只让其要求的错误更显而易见。
reading.note: The proper response / withdrawal of consent / The simplest expression / the non-payment / The seizure / the wrongness / the visibility — nominalization stack (KEY focus)

reading.en: Imprisonment, he wrote, removes the body but not the man. From the cell, his observation of the town outside was sharper than ever. The townspeople's hurry to work, their indifference to large injustices, their attachment to small comforts — all became, that night, suddenly clear.
reading.cn: 他写道：监禁带走身体，但带不走人。从牢房里，他对外面镇子的观察——比从前任何时候都更锐利。镇上人对工作的赶忙、对大的不义的漠然、对小小的舒适的执着——所有这一切，那一夜，都突然变得清楚。
reading.note: Imprisonment / his observation / The townspeople's hurry / their indifference / their attachment — nominalization (KEY focus)

reading.en: His release came the next morning, after an unknown person had paid the tax for him. His displeasure at this intervention surprised many readers — but the logic was consistent. Acceptance of the rescue would be, in effect, ratification of the system that had caused the imprisonment in the first place.
reading.cn: 第二天早上他被放了出来——因为某个不知名的人替他交了税。他对这次干预的不满让许多读者感到意外——但逻辑是一贯的。接受这种救助，实际上就是对一开始造成监禁的那个体制的批准。
reading.note: His release / His displeasure / this intervention / Acceptance of the rescue / ratification of the system / the imprisonment — sustained nominalization

reading.en: His broader argument has had a long afterlife. Gandhi's reading of Thoreau, in a Pretoria prison, contributed directly to the formation of the satyagraha movement. Martin Luther King's adoption of the same principle, almost a century later, depended on the same insight: the refusal of complicity is itself a form of action.
reading.cn: 他更广泛的论证——后世延续很久。甘地在比勒陀利亚监狱里读到梭罗——直接促成了非暴力不合作运动的形成。马丁·路德·金在将近一百年后采纳同一原则——依靠的是同一种洞察：拒绝同谋本身就是一种行动。
reading.note: His broader argument / the formation / King's adoption / The refusal / a form of action — nominalization across history

reading.en: The strength of Thoreau's essay lies less in its tactical recommendations than in its insistence on the moral awakening of the individual. Government, in this view, has no moral force of its own. Its authority rests on the daily participation of those who comply — and ends, instantly, with their refusal.
reading.cn: 梭罗这篇散文的力量——不在于它的战术建议——而在于它对个人道德觉醒的坚持。在这种观点下，政府本身没有任何道德力量。它的权威依靠每天服从者的参与——并随他们的拒绝瞬间终止。
reading.note: The strength / its tactical recommendations / its insistence / the moral awakening / authority / participation / the refusal — nominalization (KEY focus)

reading.en: His final implication is uncomfortable. Each citizen's continued payment, each citizen's continued silence, is a personal vote for whatever the government does. To pay is to ratify. To pay quietly is to ratify louder. The recognition of this fact — and the courage to act on it — has been, ever since, the test of the conscience he addressed.
reading.cn: 他最终的暗示让人不安。每个公民继续交钱、每个公民继续沉默——都是为政府所做的一切投下个人的赞成票。交钱，就是批准。沉默地交，就是更响亮地批准。承认这个事实——以及鼓起勇气去做出回应——从那以后，就成了他所诉诸的良知所要面对的考验。
reading.note: Closing — Each citizen's continued payment / silence / The recognition / the courage / the test / the conscience — final nominalization cluster

vocab.example: Hosted this dance for forty years.
Before she left for the convent.

reading.en: Gabriel Conroy and his wife Gretta had been invited to the annual Christmas dance at the Misses Morkan's. Gabriel was used to giving the after-dinner speech each year. Admittedly, the prospect of doing so always made him nervous.
reading.cn: 加布里埃尔·康罗伊和他妻子格雷塔被邀请去莫尔肯姐妹家一年一度的圣诞舞会。加布里埃尔已经习惯了每年发表餐后演说。诚然，每年想到要做这件事，他都紧张。
reading.note: had been invited — past perfect passive (L79) / used to giving — preposition + V-ing (L77) / Admittedly — concessive (L78) / the prospect of doing so — preposition + V-ing

reading.en: The Misses Morkan, his elderly aunts, were known to have hosted this dance for nearly forty years. Granted, they were no longer young. That said, they continued to be regarded by the family as the heart of every Christmas.
reading.cn: 他年长的两位姑妈莫尔肯姐妹，据说已经办了将近四十年这场舞会。诚然，她们已不年轻。话虽如此，她们仍被家族视为每个圣诞节的核心。
reading.note: were known to have hosted — passive + perfect infinitive (L81) / Granted... That said — concessive (L78) / continued to be regarded — passive infinitive (L81+L79)

reading.en: After dinner, the conversation turned to politics, music, and the dead. Mr. Browne, fond of arguing, claimed that modern singers could not be compared to those of the past. Aunt Kate, used to being interrupted, smiled patiently. The recognition of older artists, she said, was overdue.
reading.cn: 晚饭后，话题转到政治、音乐、和已故的人。布朗先生喜欢辩论，声称当今的歌手不能与过去的相提并论。姑妈凯特习惯了被打断，耐心地笑着。她说——对老一辈艺术家的认可，本就来得太晚。
reading.note: fond of arguing — preposition + V-ing (L77) / could not be compared — passive (L79) / used to being interrupted — preposition + V-ing passive / The recognition... was overdue — nominalization (L82)

reading.en: Toward the end of the night, a tenor sang a quiet, old song. Gretta stood at the top of the stairs, listening. Gabriel watched her, struck by her stillness. "What is she thinking?" he wondered. "She seems to have been transported somewhere I cannot follow."
reading.cn: 快到夜深时，一位男高音唱了一首安静的老歌。格雷塔站在楼梯顶端，听着。加布里埃尔看着她，被她的静止震住了。"她在想什么？"他想。"她似乎被带到了一个我无法跟到的地方。"
reading.note: Struck by her stillness — passive participle / seems to have been transported — perfect passive infinitive (L81+L79)

reading.en: Back at their hotel, Gabriel was surprised at finding her quiet. He had been hoping for a tender private moment. Instead, she was looking out the window. "What are you thinking of?" he asked. She admitted, then, to having loved a boy when she was young — Michael Furey, who had been seventeen, who had stood in the rain outside her window the night before she left for the convent, who had died a week later.
reading.cn: 回到他们的旅馆，加布里埃尔惊讶地发现她很安静。他本盼着一个温柔的私人时刻。可她却望着窗外。"你在想什么？"他问。她——这才承认——年轻时爱过一个男孩——迈克尔·弗雷——只有十七岁——在她进修道院前那一夜，他冒雨站在她的窗外——一周后就死了。
reading.note: surprised at finding — preposition + V-ing (L77) / had been hoping — past perfect continuous / admitted to having loved — preposition + perfect V-ing (L77+L81)

reading.en: Gabriel listened, the realization slowly arriving. He had been imagining himself, all evening, to be the central figure in his wife's life. Now he understood that the dead boy, Michael Furey, had occupied a chamber of her heart that he himself had never entered. The discovery was painful — and, admittedly, humbling.
reading.cn: 加布里埃尔听着，认识慢慢到来。整个晚上他一直把自己想成妻子生命中的主角。现在他明白了，那个死去的男孩迈克尔·弗雷——一直占据着她心里的一间小屋——他自己从来没有进过。这个发现让他痛苦——也，诚然，让他谦卑。
reading.note: the realization slowly arriving — nominalization + participle (L82) / had been imagining himself to be — perfect continuous + infinitive (L81) / The discovery — nominalization (L82) / admittedly — concessive (L78)

reading.en: When Gretta had fallen asleep, Gabriel went to the window. Snow was falling all over Ireland. The newspaper had said it would. The realization that he had never loved anyone the way the dead boy had loved his wife was the kind of recognition not easily to be undone.
reading.cn: 格雷塔睡着后，加布里埃尔走到窗前。雪正下满整个爱尔兰。报纸早已说过会下。意识到自己从未像那个死去的男孩爱过他妻子那样爱过任何人——是一种不容易被解除的认识。
reading.note: had said — past perfect / The realization that... — nominalization + that-clause (L82) / not easily to be undone — passive infinitive (L81+L79)

reading.en: He thought of the snow, falling silently — falling, indeed, on every part of Ireland: on the dark central plain, on the treeless hills, on the small graveyard on the hill where Michael Furey lay buried. His soul swooned slowly as he heard the snow falling, faintly, through the universe — falling, faintly, on all the living and the dead.
reading.cn: 他想到那雪——无声地下着——下，事实上，下在爱尔兰每一块土地上：在中部黑暗的平原、在没有树的山岗、在小小的山头墓地——迈克尔·弗雷就埋在那儿。他的灵魂——缓慢地——昏厥下去——他听到雪——隐隐约约地——下穿整个宇宙——下，隐隐约约地，下在所有活着的人和死者身上。
reading.note: Closing — falling (participle) / indeed (concessive) / where Michael Furey lay buried — relative + passive (L71+L79) / his soul swooned slowly — final image

reading.en: It is hard to be a young person, he thought. It is harder to be middle-aged. Hardest of all, perhaps, is to be alive at the moment one realizes one has lived less truly than someone who is dead.
reading.cn: 做年轻人不容易，他想。中年更难。最难的——也许——是在活着的时候意识到——自己活得不如一个死者真切。
reading.note: Hardest of all... is to be alive — superlative + infinitive / one has lived less truly than someone who is dead — comparative (L74)

reading.en: Nicholas, a small boy with a sharp mind, had been declared 'in disgrace.' How clever the adults thought themselves! What a serious crime, they said, to put a frog in one's morning bread-and-milk!
reading.cn: 尼古拉斯是个心思机敏的小男孩，他被宣布'失宠'了。大人们多么自以为是！他们说，把一只青蛙放进早晨的面包牛奶里——是多么严重的罪行啊！
reading.note: How clever the adults thought / What a serious crime — exclamation (KEY focus)

reading.en: His punishment was that, while his cousins were taken to the seaside, he was to remain home. "Such a beautiful day," his aunt announced loudly, "and yet such a naughty boy cannot enjoy it!" Nicholas, however, knew her trick.
reading.cn: 他的惩罚是：表兄妹们被带去海边，而他必须留在家里。"多么好的天气啊，"姑妈大声宣布，"可这么一个淘气的孩子却不能享受！"然而，尼古拉斯看穿了她的把戏。
reading.note: Such a beautiful day / such a naughty boy — Such + a + adj + noun

reading.en: He pretended he longed to enter the gooseberry garden, which he was forbidden to visit. So convincing was his pretence that the aunt spent the whole afternoon watching that garden — to keep him out. Meanwhile, he had quite different plans.
reading.cn: 他假装非常想进那个被禁止的醋栗园。他装得如此逼真——以至于姑妈整个下午都在盯着那个园子——防他进去。可他另有打算。
reading.note: So convincing was his pretence — emphatic inversion (KEY focus)

reading.en: Slipping into the house, he found the key to the lumber-room — a place none of the children had ever been allowed to see. How exciting it was to turn the key! What treasures lay inside!
reading.cn: 他偷偷溜进屋，找到了杂物间的钥匙——那是孩子们从来不许进的地方。转动钥匙的瞬间多么令人激动！里面又藏着什么宝贝！
reading.note: How exciting / What treasures — exclamation cluster

reading.en: The room was filled with such wonderful things that Nicholas could hardly take them in. There hung a tapestry of a hunter chasing a stag. There stood a teapot shaped like a duck. So absorbed was he that he lost track of time.
reading.cn: 屋子里装着如此美妙的东西——多到尼古拉斯都看不过来。一幅挂毯上一个猎人正追逐一头雄鹿。一只茶壶做成了鸭子的形状。他看得太入神，连时间都忘了。
reading.note: such wonderful things that / So absorbed was he that — emphatic structures (KEY focus)

reading.en: Outside, suddenly, came a frantic cry. The aunt had slipped into the rainwater-tank! "Nicholas! Come here at once!" she called. "Help me out!" How extraordinary, Nicholas thought, that grown-ups would be so foolish.
reading.cn: 外面突然传来一阵慌乱的呼喊。姑妈掉进了雨水池！"尼古拉斯！立刻过来！"她喊。"把我拉出来！"尼古拉斯想：大人居然这么愚蠢，多么不可思议啊。
reading.note: How extraordinary that — exclamation + that-clause

reading.en: "You are not my aunt," he replied calmly. "My aunt is watching the gooseberry garden. You must be the Evil One, sent to tempt me. So convincing is your imitation that, were I a less careful boy, I might be deceived. But I am not."
reading.cn: "你不是我姑妈，"他平静地回答。"我姑妈正在看着醋栗园。你一定是恶魔——派来引诱我的。你模仿得如此逼真，如果我是个不那么谨慎的孩子，可能就被骗了。但我不是。"
reading.note: So convincing is your imitation that — emphatic inversion / were I — inverted 2nd conditional

reading.en: For nearly an hour the aunt stood, soaked and humiliated, in the rainwater-tank. Such was her pride that she would not call for the maid until the last possible moment. When the kitchenmaid finally rescued her, Nicholas was already eating his bread-and-milk in perfect peace.
reading.cn: 姑妈在雨水池里站了将近一个小时，浑身湿透，颜面尽失。她的骄傲如此之深——直到不能再坚持的最后一刻才叫女仆。当厨房女仆终于把她救出来时，尼古拉斯已经在心平气和地吃他的面包牛奶了。
reading.note: Such was her pride that — Such + was + subject + that (KEY focus)

reading.en: At supper, no one spoke. The aunt looked away. The cousins, returned from a disappointing seaside, sulked. So pleasant a silence had not been heard in that house for years. And how well, Nicholas reflected, he had earned it.
reading.cn: 晚饭时，谁也不说话。姑妈别开脸。表兄妹们从扫兴的海边回来，板着脸。这屋子已经多年没有过这般令人愉快的沉默。尼古拉斯心想——他多么名副其实地挣到了这一刻。
reading.note: Closing — So pleasant a silence / how well he had earned it

vocab.example: The takings of the first week.

reading.en: Albert Edward Foreman had been verger at St. Peter's, Neville Square, for sixteen years. The dignity of the position, the cleanliness of his cassock, the regularity of his duties — these had been the foundation of his life. Such was his pride in his work that he refused to leave even on holidays.
reading.cn: 艾伯特·爱德华·福尔曼在内维尔广场圣彼得教堂当了十六年司事。这份职位的体面、白袍的整洁、职责的规律——这些是他生活的根基。他对工作的骄傲如此之深，连假期都不愿离开。
reading.note: The dignity / The cleanliness / The regularity — nominalization (L82) / Such was his pride that — emphatic inversion (L84)

reading.en: One Tuesday, the new vicar called him in. "Foreman," he said, "I have been informed that you cannot read or write. Is this true?" Albert admitted, with quiet dignity, that it was. The vicar insisted that he learn at once. He maintained that an illiterate verger was an embarrassment to the parish.
reading.cn: 一个星期二，新来的牧师把他叫进去。"福尔曼，"他说，"有人告诉我你不识字。是真的吗？"艾伯特带着平静的体面承认是的。牧师坚称他必须立刻学习。他主张——一位不识字的司事是教区的耻辱。
reading.note: I have been informed — passive (L79) / insisted that he learn / maintained that — reporting verbs + subjunctive (L66+L63)

reading.en: Albert refused. "At my age, sir, I cannot bring myself to begin." The vicar, after some thought, declared that he must, with regret, dismiss him. What a shock it was! What a cruel decision!
reading.cn: 艾伯特拒绝了。"先生，到我这年纪，我没法让自己开始学。"牧师沉思后宣布，他不得不、带着遗憾、辞退他。多么晴天霹雳啊！多么残忍的决定！
reading.note: What a shock / What a cruel decision — exclamation (L84)

reading.en: Walking home through the streets, Albert needed a cigarette. He searched all the way and found, to his surprise, that there was no tobacconist on that long, busy street. "How strange!" he thought. "How could nobody have noticed this opportunity?"
reading.cn: 艾伯特走回家的路上想抽支烟。他一路找过去，惊讶地发现这条又长又繁忙的街上居然没有一家烟铺。"多奇怪！"他想。"怎么会没人注意到这个机会？"
reading.note: How strange / How could nobody have noticed — exclamation + modal speculation (L84+L73)

reading.en: Within a month, Albert had opened his own tobacco shop on that street. The takings of the first week were astonishing. The popularity of his shop must have come, he supposed, from his attention to detail.
reading.cn: 一个月之内，艾伯特就在那条街上开起了自己的烟铺。第一周的营业额惊人。他想，店铺的火爆——一定来自他对细节的留意。
reading.note: The takings / The popularity / his attention to detail — nominalization (L82) / must have come — modal speculation (L73)

reading.en: By the third year, he had opened a second shop. By the tenth, he had ten. The growth of his small empire could only be described as remarkable. He had, by then, accumulated a fortune that would have been the envy of any man.
reading.cn: 到第三年，他开了第二家店。到第十年，他有了十家。他这个小帝国的成长——只能说非凡。到那时，他已经积累了一笔财富——任何人见了都会眼红。
reading.note: The growth / a fortune — nominalization (L82) / could only be described — passive infinitive (L81+L79)

reading.en: Once a week, Albert called at his bank. The manager, having grown fond of him, asked one day to invest the takings. Albert agreed. He was given papers to sign. "Can you read this through, Mr. Foreman?" the manager asked. Albert, with quiet dignity, replied that he could not.
reading.cn: 艾伯特每周去一次银行。经理对他渐生好感，有一天提议替他投资营业款。艾伯特同意了。有几份文件被递给他签字。"福尔曼先生，您能读一下吗？"经理问。艾伯特带着平静的体面回答——他不识字。
reading.note: having grown fond of him — perfect participle (L51) / He was given — passive (L79)

reading.en: "What!" cried the manager. "You — a man with ten shops, with thousands in the bank — you cannot read? Good Lord, sir! What would you BE now if you could?" Albert thought for a moment. So composed was he, so steady, that the answer came without hesitation.
reading.cn: "什么！"经理叫起来。"您——一位有十家店、银行里有上千的人——您不识字？老天爷啊，先生！如果您识字，现在该是什么了？"艾伯特想了一会儿。他如此沉着、如此稳定，答案毫不犹豫地出来了。
reading.note: What! — exclamation / What would you BE — modal speculation / So composed was he — emphatic inversion (L84)

reading.en: "Verger of St. Peter's, Neville Square, sir." How extraordinary, the manager thought, that a single dismissal had produced such a result. The disgrace of one Tuesday morning, it seemed, had been the foundation of an entirely better life.
reading.cn: "内维尔广场圣彼得教堂的司事，先生。"经理心想：多么不可思议——一次解雇竟造就了这样的结果。看来——某个星期二早上的耻辱——就是一段完全更好的人生的起点。
reading.note: Closing — How extraordinary that — exclamation / The disgrace / the foundation — nominalization (L82)

vocab.example: On the horizon stood a lighthouse.
vocab.example_cn: 地平线上立着一座灯塔。

vocab.example: If I am going to be drowned.

reading.en: None of them knew the colour of the sky. Their eyes glanced level at the waves that swept toward them. In a ten-foot dinghy were four men: a captain, an oiler, a cook, and a correspondent. Their ship had gone down at dawn.
reading.cn: 他们没人知道天的颜色。他们的眼睛平平地盯着扑向他们的浪。一艘十英尺长的小艇里，是四个人：船长、加油工、厨子、和一名记者。他们的船在拂晓沉了。
reading.note: In a ten-foot dinghy were four men — locative inversion (KEY focus)

reading.en: On the horizon, far away, stood a lighthouse — small, cold, indifferent. Toward this thin tower the captain steered. Wave after wave they rode. Wave after wave passed beneath them.
reading.cn: 地平线上，远远地，立着一座灯塔——小、冷、漠然。船长向这座细细的塔驶去。一波又一波的浪他们骑着过。一波又一波从他们下面涌过。
reading.note: On the horizon stood a lighthouse — locative inversion (KEY focus) / Wave after wave — topicalization

reading.en: Hardest of all was the cold. Through the night, soaked and silent, they took turns rowing. Of all the men, the oiler was the strongest — and it was he who rowed the most.
reading.cn: 最难的是寒冷。整夜，浑身湿透、沉默不语，他们轮流划桨。所有人里，加油工最壮——划得最多的也是他。
reading.note: Hardest of all was the cold — emphatic fronting (KEY focus) / it was he who — cleft (L52)

reading.en: Toward morning, exhausted, the correspondent thought: "If I am going to be drowned, why was I allowed to come thus far?" The unfairness of it struck him hard. So tired was he that he could no longer feel his hands.
reading.cn: 到清晨，筋疲力尽，那位记者想：'要是我注定要淹死——为什么当初允许我走这么远？'其中的不公狠狠地撞了他。他累得连手都感觉不到。
reading.note: So tired was he that — emphatic inversion (L84)

reading.en: Out of the south came a wind. Faint at first, then stronger, it pushed them toward the shore. "There is a man on the beach!" cried the cook. Indeed, on the sand stood a small figure, waving.
reading.cn: 从南边吹来一阵风。起初微弱，然后越来越强——把他们朝岸边推去。"岸上有人！"厨子喊。果真，沙滩上立着一个小小的身影，在挥手。
reading.note: Out of the south came a wind / on the sand stood a small figure — locative inversion (KEY focus)

reading.en: But the figure on the beach did not call for help. He waved, and waved, and walked away. "What does he mean?" the men asked. Of all answers, the simplest was the worst: there was no help; he had thought they were a fishing boat.
reading.cn: 可岸上那个人并没有叫援。他挥着手，挥着手，走开了。"他什么意思？"那些人问。所有答案里，最简单的就是最坏的：没有救援；他以为他们是一艘渔船。
reading.note: Of all answers, the simplest was the worst — Of all + noun fronting (KEY focus)

reading.en: A new wave rose. The dinghy was lifted, then thrown over. Out of the cold sea, three men climbed onto the sand. The fourth — Billie, the oiler, the strongest — was already lying still in the surf.
reading.cn: 一道新浪掀起。小艇被举高，然后翻了过去。从冰冷的海里，三个人爬上了沙滩。第四个人——比利，那个加油工，最壮的那个——已经静静地躺在浪花里了。
reading.note: Out of the cold sea, three men climbed — locative inversion (KEY focus)

reading.en: Strange it was — and Crane writes this with painful clarity — that the strongest among them was the one to die. Of all of us, said the captain quietly, he was the one we needed most.
reading.cn: 奇怪——Crane 写得带着痛苦的清晰——他们之中最强的，反而是死的那个。"我们之中，"船长平静地说，"最需要他的，正是我们。"
reading.note: Strange it was that — emphatic fronting / Of all of us... he was the one — fronting + cleft

reading.en: Late that night, by a fire on the shore, the three survivors sat. The wind had calmed. The sea, in the distance, made the only sound. They felt that they could now be interpreters of the great voice of the sea — its indifference, its rhythm, its patient power.
reading.cn: 那夜深时，岸边一堆篝火旁，三个幸存者坐着。风已经停。远处的海，是唯一的声响。他们觉得——他们现在可以成为海这个伟大声音的翻译者了——它的漠然、它的节奏、它耐心的力量。
reading.note: Closing — Late that night, by a fire on the shore, the three survivors sat — multi-fronted adverbial

vocab.meaning: adj. 酩酊大醉的（drunk 的正式说法）
vocab.example: He had been intoxicated for the winter.

vocab.meaning: adj. 压抑的；安静下来的
vocab.example: The Paris before him now seemed subdued.
vocab.example_cn: 眼前的巴黎现在显得压抑。

vocab.example: He attributed this to the crash.

vocab.meaning: v. 离去；启程（leave 的正式版）
v. 戒；克制（avoid 的正式版）

vocab.example: Marion conceded that he had reformed.
vocab.example_cn: 玛丽昂承认他改过自新了。

vocab.example: He had not yet been allowed to mourn.

reading.en: Charlie Wales returned to Paris in the autumn of 1930. Three years earlier, his wife had died of pneumonia. Two years earlier, in his grief, he had been intoxicated for almost the entire winter. Now, sober, he had come back to reclaim his daughter, Honoria, from his sister-in-law Marion.
reading.cn: 1930年秋，查理·韦尔斯回到了巴黎。三年前，他妻子死于肺炎。两年前，在悲痛中，他几乎整整一个冬天都酩酊大醉。如今，他清醒了，回来想从小姨子玛丽昂那里要回女儿奥诺莉雅。
reading.note: intoxicated (= drunk, B2→C1 upgrade) / sober / reclaim — sophisticated register (KEY focus)

reading.en: The Paris of his memory had been the city of excess — of prolonged dinners, of impulsive purchases, of mornings he could no longer recall. The Paris before him now seemed quieter, almost subdued. He attributed this partly to the crash, partly to the absence, in his own life, of those who had once accompanied him.
reading.cn: 记忆里的巴黎曾是放纵之城——漫长的晚宴、冲动的购物、他再也想不起来的清晨。眼前的巴黎现在更安静——几乎压抑。他把这一半归于股市崩盘——一半归于他自己生活中——那些曾经陪伴过他的人——的离去。
reading.note: excess / prolonged / impulsive / subdued / attributed — C1 vocabulary (KEY focus)

reading.en: He visited the Ritz bar — once his daily refuge — and was greeted by Alix, the bartender. They exchanged news. Most of the men he had once known had departed: some for America, some for the cemetery. Alix expressed mild surprise at finding him so composed.
reading.cn: 他去了里兹酒吧——曾经他每天的避风港——酒保亚历克斯招呼他。他们互通近况。他从前认识的男人大多离开了：有的回了美国，有的进了墓地。亚历克斯——温和地——惊讶于他竟如此沉着。
reading.note: refuge / departed (= left) / cemetery / composed — C1 register (KEY focus)

reading.en: At Marion's apartment, the conversation was strained. "I have been abstaining from alcohol for over a year," Charlie said. Marion was unconvinced. "How can we be certain," she asked, "that you will not lapse again?" Charlie acknowledged that no certainty was possible. He could only offer his word.
reading.cn: 在玛丽昂的公寓，谈话紧绷。"我戒酒已经一年多了，"查理说。玛丽昂不信。"我们怎么能确定——"她问，"——你不会再次故态复萌？"查理承认——确定是不可能的。他能给的，只有他的话。
reading.note: strained / abstaining / unconvinced / lapse / acknowledged — C1 register (KEY focus)

reading.en: For an hour they discussed the practical implications of Honoria's return: schools, finances, the precise terms of guardianship. Marion conceded, with reluctance, that he had reformed. Yet she insisted on a probationary period of six months, during which he was to demonstrate consistent stability.
reading.cn: 他们讨论了一个小时奥诺莉雅回来的实际事项：学校、钱、监护权的具体条款。玛丽昂带着不情愿——承认他确实改过自新。但她坚持要六个月的考察期——在这期间他要表现出持续稳定。
reading.note: implications / finances / guardianship / conceded / reformed / probationary — C1 vocabulary (KEY focus)

reading.en: That evening, Charlie dined with Honoria. Across the small table, the child looked at her father with a gravity that nearly undid him. She had inherited her mother's eyes — calm, intelligent, observant. He suppressed the rising emotion and asked, in a deliberately casual tone, what she was reading at school.
reading.cn: 那晚，查理与奥诺莉雅共进晚餐。小桌对面，孩子用一种近乎让他崩溃的庄重看着父亲。她继承了母亲的眼神——平静、聪慧、善察。他强忍住涌起的情绪——用刻意随意的语气问——她在学校读什么书。
reading.note: dined / gravity / undid / inherited / suppressed / observant — C1 register (KEY focus)

reading.en: Then, at the worst possible moment, two figures from his old life walked into the restaurant: Lorraine and Duncan, both of them already showing the effects of the afternoon's wine. They greeted him with familiar enthusiasm. Honoria watched, silent. Charlie's heart sank. Their reappearance, though brief, would prove disastrous.
reading.cn: 然后——在最不该来的时刻——他过去生活里的两个身影走进餐馆：洛琳和邓肯——两人都已经显出下午喝了酒的样子。他们用熟悉的热情招呼他。奥诺莉雅看着，没说话。查理的心沉了下去。他们的再次出现——虽然短——将被证明是灾难性的。
reading.note: figures / enthusiasm / disastrous / reappearance — B2 → C1 upgrades (KEY focus)

reading.en: Later that night, Lorraine appeared at Marion's door — drunk, loud, demanding to see Charlie. Marion, who had been on the brink of yielding the child, withdrew her consent. The decision, she said, would be reconsidered "in another six months — at the soonest."
reading.cn: 当晚晚些时候，洛琳出现在玛丽昂的门口——醉、吵、坚持要见查理。玛丽昂——本已快要交出孩子——撤回了同意。她说——这个决定要"至少再过六个月"——再考虑。
reading.note: demanding / on the brink of / yielding / withdrew her consent / reconsidered — C1 register (KEY focus)

reading.en: Charlie returned to the Ritz bar alone. He thought of Honoria's small, grave face. He thought of his wife, whom the years had not yet allowed him to mourn. He ordered a single whisky-and-soda and, to his own surprise, did not finish it. "I will get her back," he said quietly. "I have nothing else to live for."
reading.cn: 查理一个人回到里兹酒吧。他想起奥诺莉雅小小的、庄重的脸。他想起妻子——这些年他还来不及好好哀悼。他点了一杯威士忌苏打——出乎自己意料——没喝完。"我会把她要回来，"他平静地说。"除此之外，我没有什么活着的理由了。"
reading.note: Closing — mourn / surprise / quietly — controlled diction

vocab.meaning: v. 花费（spend 的正式版）
vocab.example: The sum had to be expended.

vocab.meaning: adv. 肆意地；不顾后果地
v. 询问（ask 的正式版）

reading.en: Annabel and Midge were two young stenographers in New York City. They were both in their early twenties, and lived together in a small apartment they could barely afford. On the avenues, however, they walked as if they owned the place.
reading.cn: 安娜贝尔和米奇是纽约的两位年轻速记员。她们都二十出头，合住在一间几乎付不起房租的小公寓里。然而走在大街上——她们却像这座城市是她们的。
reading.note: as if they owned the place — as if + past (L72) / however — concessive adverb (L78)

reading.en: They had invented a game they called "the Rules." Suppose, the Rules ran, an old man, a stranger to you, were to die and leave you a million dollars — on the single condition that you must spend it all on yourself. What, then, would you buy?
reading.cn: 她们发明了一种游戏，叫"规则"。规则是这样的：假设有个跟你毫无关系的老人死了，留给你一百万——条件只有一个：你必须把它全花在你自己身上。那么，你会买什么？
reading.note: Suppose ... were to die and leave — were-to inverted conditional (L53) / would buy — second conditional

reading.en: Out of this game came hours of animated discussion. By the rules, no money could be given to family, charity, or friends. The whole sum had to be expended on the self — luxuriously, recklessly, but on the self alone.
reading.cn: 这个游戏带来一小时一小时的热烈讨论。按规则，钱不能给家人、慈善机构、或朋友。这笔钱必须全部花在自己身上——奢华地、肆意地——但只能花在自己身上。
reading.note: Out of this game came hours — locative inversion (L86) / had to be expended (= spent — C1 upgrade L87)

reading.en: What a thrilling restriction it was! How free their imaginations became, once compelled to ignore everyone but themselves! Such was their devotion to the Rules that they had refined them over many afternoons of careful debate.
reading.cn: 这是多么刺激的限制！她们的想象力——一旦被迫无视除自己之外的所有人——变得多么自由！她们对规则的执着如此之深——经过许多个下午仔细辩论——已经把规则打磨得很精细了。
reading.note: What a thrilling restriction / How free / Such was their devotion that — exclamation + emphasis (L84)

reading.en: On a Wednesday afternoon, walking up Fifth Avenue, the Rules were running once more. "I would purchase," Annabel said, "an entire wardrobe of evening gowns. Of all luxuries, that is the most fundamental." Midge concurred. "I, on the other hand, would acquire a small but exquisite apartment overlooking the Park."
reading.cn: 一个星期三下午，在第五大道上散步时，规则又跑起来了。"我要买，"安娜贝尔说，"一整套晚礼服。所有奢侈里——这是最根本的。"米奇赞同。"另一方面——我会得到一间小而精致的公寓——俯瞰中央公园。"
reading.note: Of all luxuries, that is the most fundamental — fronting + cleft (L86) / purchase / acquire / exquisite — C1 upgrades (L87)

reading.en: They were just admiring a window when Midge drew Annabel's attention to a pearl necklace, displayed on a velvet stand. The pearls were enormous, regular, and lustrous — the kind of jewel one cannot, with self-respect, refrain from wanting. "Let us inquire," Annabel said suddenly. "What harm can come of it?"
reading.cn: 她们正欣赏一个橱窗，米奇让安娜贝尔注意一条放在天鹅绒架上的珍珠项链。珍珠又大又圆又亮——是那种自重的人忍不住想要的珠宝。"我们问问，"安娜贝尔突然说。"问问能有什么坏处？"
reading.note: the kind one cannot refrain from wanting — preposition + V-ing (L77) / lustrous / refrain from / inquire — C1 vocabulary (L87)

reading.en: They entered the shop. The salesman, having sized them up at a glance, treated them with the gentle condescension reserved for those visibly without money. "And how much," Annabel asked, with composed dignity, "is the necklace in the window?" The salesman replied that it was priced at two hundred and fifty thousand dollars.
reading.cn: 她们走进店。售货员一眼把她们打量过去——用一种为「明显没钱的人」保留的温和的居高临下来对待她们。"那条橱窗里的项链——"安娜贝尔带着镇定的体面问，"——多少钱？"售货员回答——标价二十五万。
reading.note: having sized them up — perfect participle (L51) / condescension / reserved / composed dignity — C1 vocabulary (L87)

reading.en: Out of the shop they walked with their dignity intact. Around the corner, however, the dignity collapsed. Annabel laughed first. Midge, after a moment, joined her. So unexpected was the price that even their imagination — that finely trained instrument — had failed to anticipate it.
reading.cn: 她们带着没受伤的体面走出店。可拐过街角——体面就垮了。安娜贝尔先笑。米奇——过了片刻——跟着笑。这价格如此出乎意料——连她们的想象力——那架训练精良的乐器——都没预料到。
reading.note: Out of the shop they walked — locative fronting (L86) / So unexpected was the price that — emphatic inversion (L84)

reading.en: They walked on, the wind in their faces. "I have, perhaps, miscalculated," Midge admitted. "Suppose, instead, the old man had left us ten million." Annabel paused. "On the same condition?" "On the same condition." "Well then. Let us proceed." And up Fifth Avenue, the Rules began again — at a higher denomination.
reading.cn: 她们继续往前走，风迎面打来。"我可能——算错了，"米奇承认。"假设，那个老人留给我们的——是一千万呢？"安娜贝尔停了一下。"同样的条件？""同样的条件。""好吧。我们继续。"——第五大道上，规则又开始了——在更高的面额上。
reading.note: Closing — Suppose ... had left us — past perfect subjunctive (L53) / a higher denomination — C1 vocabulary (L87)

vocab.meaning: adj. 不感激的（前缀 un-）

vocab.example: The medals we had been given.
My knee was in the apparatus.
It was not a small thing he was promising.
vocab.example_cn: 他承诺的——不是一件小事。

vocab.example: He had been a great fencer.
vocab.example_cn: 他曾经是个出色的击剑手。

vocab.example: They strapped it into the machine.

reading.en: In the fall, the war was always there, but we did not go to it any more. It was cold in the autumn in Milan, and the dark came very early. Then the electric lights came on, and it was pleasant — not unpleasant — along the streets, looking in the windows.
reading.cn: 秋天里——战争一直在那儿——但我们再也不去打了。米兰的秋天冷——天黑得很早。然后电灯亮起来——沿着街——望着橱窗——感觉好——不不好——感觉好。
reading.note: did not go to it any more — negation softening / not unpleasant — litotes (KEY focus, double negative for understatement)

reading.en: We were all at the hospital every afternoon. There were three of us, all wounded. We had not done anything to be brave about, but we were not ungrateful for the medals we had been given. The doctors said we would walk again. None of us, however, was entirely certain.
reading.cn: 我们每天下午都在医院。我们三个人——都是伤兵。我们没做过什么值得算勇敢的事——但我们对发给我们的勋章——也不是不感激。医生说我们会再走路。然而——我们里面没有一个人——完全确信。
reading.note: had not done anything to be brave about — understatement (we hadn't been heroic) / not ungrateful — litotes (KEY focus, = grateful) / not entirely certain — softened negation (= doubtful)

reading.en: The doctor came up to the machine where I was sitting. My knee was in the apparatus. "What did you like best to do before the war? Did you practice a sport?" — "Yes," I said, "football." — "Good," he said. "You will be able to play football again, better than ever." It was not a small thing he was promising. I was not sure he believed it.
reading.cn: 医生走到我坐着的那台机器旁。我的膝盖在器械里。"战前你最喜欢做什么？做过运动吗？"——"是的，"我说，"足球。"——"好，"他说。"你会再踢足球——比从前更好。"他承诺的——不是一件小事。我——也不确定——他相信。
reading.note: It was not a small thing — litotes (KEY focus, = a big thing) / I was not sure he believed it — understatement (KEY focus, = he probably didn't believe it)

reading.en: The major, who had been a great fencer, did not believe in the machines. He had a small hand, no bigger than a baby's. They strapped it into the apparatus that opened and closed the fingers. He looked at the machine. "I have no confidence," he said. He said this without bitterness, as if he were talking about the weather.
reading.cn: 少校——曾经是个出色的击剑手——不相信这些机器。他的一只手很小——不比婴儿的大。他们把它绑进一台开合手指的器械里。他看着机器。"我没有信心，"他说。他说这话——没有怨气——仿佛在谈天气。
reading.note: did not believe in / no bigger than a baby's — softened negation (= very small) / no confidence — direct denial / without bitterness — understatement (KEY focus, = calmly accepting loss)

reading.en: He came every day all the same. He did not believe in the machines, but he came. He thought, perhaps, that they might be of some use to others, even if not to him. It was, he said one afternoon, not unimportant to keep faith with the things one no longer believed in.
reading.cn: 他还是天天来。他不相信这些机器——可他来。也许他想——它们对别人——也许有点用——就算对他没有。一天下午他说——和你已经不再相信的东西——保持忠诚——也不是不重要的。
reading.note: did not believe... but he came — concessive negation / might be of some use — softened claim / not unimportant — litotes (KEY focus, double negation = important)

reading.en: There was a young officer who had been wounded in the face. He wore a black silk handkerchief across what had been his nose. He was a fine young man. He had been brave. The girls did not look at him in the streets. We did not, in the hospital, ask him about it.
reading.cn: 有个年轻军官——脸上受过伤。他在原来是鼻子的位置——蒙着一块黑丝手帕。他是个好青年。他曾经勇敢过。街上女孩们——不看他。在医院里——我们也不问他。
reading.note: had been wounded / had been brave — past perfect of completed states / The girls did not look at him / We did not ask — restraint (KEY focus, what is NOT done speaks louder)

reading.en: The major asked me one afternoon how I was getting along with the Italian grammar. I told him I was finding it very difficult — that there were too many irregular verbs. "Yes," he said. "Why, then, do you not take up the proper study of grammar?" — "It would be useful," I admitted, without enthusiasm.
reading.cn: 一天下午——少校问我意大利语语法学得怎么样。我告诉他——我觉得很难——不规则动词太多。"是的，"他说。"那你为什么不正式地学一下语法？"——"那会有用，"我承认——但毫无热情。
reading.note: I was finding it very difficult — direct expression / Why, then, do you not... — formal indirect command / It would be useful — modal hedge (KEY focus, = it isn't but I'm being polite) / without enthusiasm — understatement (= I really didn't want to)

reading.en: He was very angry that day. We did not, at first, understand why. Later he told me — in a voice not entirely steady — that his wife had died, quite suddenly, of pneumonia. She had been twenty-four. He had not known she was very ill until it was too late to come back. "I should not have married," he said. "I know," I said. "But you must not — " I was going to say that he must not lose hope. I did not say it. I did not, in the end, know what one should say.
reading.cn: 那天他很生气。我们一开始不明白为什么。后来他告诉我——声音不太稳——他妻子死了——很突然——肺炎。她那年二十四岁。他不知道她病得很重——等他赶回来的时候已经太晚。"我不该结婚，"他说。"我知道，"我说。"可你绝不能——"我本来想说——他绝不能失去希望。我没说出来。我——到最后——不知道——人在这种时候——该说什么。
reading.note: in a voice not entirely steady — litotes (KEY focus, = trembling) / He had not known... until — past perfect chain / I did not say it. I did not, in the end, know — repeated negation as emotional restraint (KEY focus, = unbearable)

reading.en: He came back to the machines a few days later. Three large photographs of types of wounds — before and after they had been cured by the machines — were posted on the wall. Before the major, who used the machine I used, were three photographs of hands, like his, that were completely restored. I do not know where the doctor got them. I had always understood we were the first to use the machines.
reading.cn: 几天后他回到机器旁。三张大照片——伤的种类——治好之前和之后——贴在墙上。少校——他用我用过的那台机器——前面——是三张和他一样的手——完全恢复了的——的照片。我不知道——医生从哪里弄来的。我一直以为——我们是第一批使用这些机器的人。
reading.note: Closing — were posted on the wall — passive (L79 review) / Before the major... were three photographs — locative inversion (L86 review) / I do not know where the doctor got them — quiet doubt (KEY focus, the photos may not be real)

vocab.example_cn: 一种奇怪的感觉的颠倒。

reading.en: Moths that fly by day are not, properly speaking, to be called moths; they belong rather to that company of half-creatures — half butterfly, half moth — that the daylight admits but does not entirely accept. The present specimen, however, was a true moth, hay-coloured, narrow-winged, and confined, on this particular September morning, to the windowpane through which the sun was slanting.
reading.cn: 白天飞的蛾——严格说——不该叫蛾；它们属于那一类半样生物——半像蝴蝶——半像蛾——白昼接纳它们——却又不完全接受。然而眼前这一只——是真正的蛾——干草色——窄翅膀——这个九月清晨——把自己困在阳光斜照进来的窗玻璃上。
reading.note: Moths that fly by day are not properly speaking... — fronted relative + parenthetical (CAPSTONE) / The present specimen, however, was... — discourse cohesion + appositive cluster

reading.en: Watching it for some minutes, one began to feel that life — life itself, as a substance, almost — had pressed itself, on this morning, into the body of a thing scarcely the size of a thumbnail. So small was the creature, and so vast its energy, that one could not, for a moment, decide which of the two impressions was the truer.
reading.cn: 看了几分钟之后——人开始觉得——生命——生命本身——几乎像一种实体——这天早晨——把自己——挤进了——一只小得不及拇指甲的——东西——的身体里。生灵这么小——精力这么大——人一时间——分不清——哪一个印象——更真。
reading.note: Watching it for some minutes, one began to feel — fronted participle + abstract subject / life — life itself, as a substance, almost — appositive triplet / So small was the creature, and so vast its energy, that... — So + adj inversion + that (L84 review)

reading.en: So pleasant was the September sunshine, and so vast the activity of the world outside the window — horses ploughing the field beyond, rooks circling above the elms, a child somewhere calling — that one could hardly avoid feeling, by contrast, how exceedingly narrow the moth's province had become.
reading.cn: 九月的阳光这么舒服——窗外的世界这么忙碌——田那头马在犁地——榆树上面渡鸦在盘旋——某处一个孩子在喊——人很难不感到——相比之下——这只蛾的疆域——已经变得多么狭小。
reading.note: So pleasant was the sunshine, and so vast the activity, that... — chained So + adj inversion + that (L84) / horses ploughing... rooks circling... a child calling — parallel reduced participles (L65 review) / one could hardly avoid feeling — preposition + V-ing (L77 review)

reading.en: Yet narrow as it was, the moth seemed determined to make every use of it. He flew first to one corner of the windowpane, and then, after a moment, to another. He tried his wings against the glass. He beat himself, with what looked like ardour, against a barrier he could neither break nor understand.
reading.cn: 可这疆域——再小——蛾——似乎决心——把它用到尽。他先飞到窗玻璃的一角——过一会——又飞到另一角。他用翅膀——撞玻璃。他朝着——一道他既打不破——也看不懂的——障碍——撞自己——撞得——像有热情似的。
reading.note: Yet narrow as it was — concessive inversion (KEY capstone focus) / determined to make every use — adjective + infinitive (L81 review) / first... and then... after a moment — sequential cohesion / a barrier he could neither break nor understand — neither/nor in relative clause (L76 review)

reading.en: Then, after some minutes of this brave, hopeless effort, the body of the moth — which had been trembling — grew still. The legs, formerly engaged in their small frantic running, ceased to move. He had, it seemed, come to the end of what could be done; and, in coming to it, had become — somehow — more visible than before.
reading.cn: 然后——这样勇敢、又无望地——挣扎几分钟之后——他的身体——一直在颤抖的身体——不动了。两条腿——本来在那种细小的疯狂奔跑里——停了下来。他——似乎——走到了——能做的事的尽头；而走到尽头时——却——不知怎么——比从前——更显眼了。
reading.note: after some minutes of this brave, hopeless effort — fronted PP + nominalized abstraction (L82+L86 review) / which had been trembling — non-defining relative + past perfect continuous / formerly engaged in... — reduced relative (L65 review) / He had, it seemed, come to... — inserted 'it seemed' / in coming to it, had become — preposition + V-ing (L77)

reading.en: Watching, one had a peculiar inversion of feeling. A moment ago, life had seemed enormous and the moth's effort tiny; now, suddenly, the moth's effort seemed enormous and one's own life — one had to admit — no greater. The sense of importance had shifted, quietly but completely, from one side of the windowpane to the other.
reading.cn: 看着的时候——人有一种奇怪的——感觉的颠倒。上一刻——生命显得巨大——蛾的努力很小；现在——忽然之间——蛾的努力显得巨大——而自己的生命——人不得不承认——并不更大。重要感——已经——安静却完整地——从窗玻璃的这一边——移到了——那一边。
reading.note: Watching, one had a peculiar inversion of feeling — fronted participle + abstract noun phrase (L82) / A moment ago... now, suddenly... — temporal pivot / The sense of importance had shifted, quietly but completely, from... to... — abstract subject + parenthetical adverbs + parallel from/to (CAPSTONE)

reading.en: The moth made a final movement: a tiny stretching of the wings, a final composing of the legs. Then he was still. Death, which had seemed an enormous thing, turned out to have been a small thing; or, rather, life, which had seemed enormous, turned out — when it stopped — to be also small.
reading.cn: 蛾——做了——最后一个动作：一次微小的——翅膀的——展开——一次最后的——腿的——收拢。然后——他——不动了。死亡——本来显得是件巨大的事——结果——是件小事；或者，更准确地说——生命——本来显得巨大——当它——停下来时——结果——也很小。
reading.note: a tiny stretching of the wings, a final composing of the legs — parallel nominalized phrases (L82 review) / Death, which had seemed an enormous thing, turned out to have been... — abstract subject + perfect infinitive (L81 review) / or, rather — discourse-level self-correction

reading.en: I picked up the pencil again, but I no longer felt that what I was writing of was, in itself, of any particular importance. Outside, the horses still ploughed; the children still called. The world had not, by the moth's small ending, been altered. And yet — this, I suppose, is what one means by mystery — something had moved. Something had shifted. Something, in the room, would not be the same again.
reading.cn: 我又拿起铅笔——但我不再觉得——我正在写的东西——本身——有什么特别的重要。外面——马还在犁地；孩子们还在喊。世界——并没有——因为蛾的这个小小的终结——而改变。然而——这——我猜——就是人所说的'神秘'——什么——动过了。什么——挪过了。屋子里有什么——再也不会和从前一样了。
reading.note: what I was writing of was, in itself, of any particular importance — wh-cleft (L66 review) + nominalization (L82) / The world had not, by the moth's small ending, been altered — past perfect passive + inserted PP (L79+L82) / something had moved. Something had shifted. — anaphoric repetition (CAPSTONE rhythm)

reading.en: The moth, having ceased to live, lay still on the windowpane — and seemed, in the quiet that followed, to have made his ordinary life, by his ordinary effort to keep it, into something not unlike a triumph. Of all the small things one might choose to admire, this — the unbroken determination of a creature who could not, in any sense, win — is perhaps not the least worth keeping in mind.
reading.cn: 蛾——已经停止活着——静静地躺在窗玻璃上——在随之而来的寂静里——似乎——通过他维持生命的——平平常常的努力——把他平平常常的一生——变成了——一种——和'胜利'——并非完全不同——的东西。在所有——人可以选择去敬佩的——小小的事物里面——这一件——一只生物的、永不破碎的、毫无可能赢的、决心——也许——并不是最不值得记住的。
reading.note: Closing — having ceased to live — perfect participle (L51+L65 review) / seemed, in the quiet that followed, to have made... into something — passive infinitive + abstract noun phrase / not unlike a triumph — litotes (L89 callback!) / Of all the small things one might choose to admire — fronted PP + relative (L86) / not the least worth keeping in mind — double negative litotes + reduced relative — CAPSTONE: every B2 structure in one closing sentence
